choices.text: A single central bank owned by the federal government and directed by presidential appointees
choices.textEs: A single central bank owned by the gobierno federal and directed by presidential appointees

choices.text: A network of state banks coordinated by a federal comptroller with limited regulatory authority
choices.textEs: A network of state banks coordinated by a federal comptroller with limited regulatory authority

choices.text: A private bank with a federal charter but largely independent of government supervision
choices.textEs: A private bank with a federal charter but largely independent of government supervision

choices.text: Twelve regional banks owned by member banks but governed by a presidentially appointed Federal Reserve Board
choices.textEs: Twelve regional banks owned by member banks but governed by a presidentially appointed Federal Reserve Board

items.explanation: Wilson’s Federal Reserve was structured as a hybrid system of 12 regional reserve banks overseen by a national board. A choice describing one single private bank is wrong because reformers wanted to avoid concentrating all power in one place. Its design balanced regional interests with national oversight.
items.explanationEs: Wilson’s Federal Reserve was structured as a hybrid system of 12 regional reserve banks overseen by a national board. A choice describing one single private bank is wrong because reformers wanted to avoid concentrating all power in one place. Its design balanced regional interests with national oversight.

items.stem: Direct primaries replaced party conventions for selecting candidates because —
items.stemEs: Direct primaries replaced party conventions for selecting candidates because —

choices.text: Progressive reformers believed direct elections typically produced better candidates than any other method
choices.textEs: Progressive reformers believed direct elections typically produced better candidates than any other method

choices.text: Direct primaries cost state governments less to administer than party conventions and saved on the expense of housing convention delegates
choices.textEs: Direct primaries cost gobierno estatals less to administer than party conventions and saved on the expense of housing convention delegates

choices.text: Courts ruled party conventions were unconstitutional under the 1st Amendment
choices.textEs: Courts ruled party conventions were unconstitucional under the 1st enmienda

choices.text: Party bosses in conventions chose candidates loyal to the machine rather than the voters
choices.textEs: Party bosses in conventions chose candidates loyal to the machine rather than the voters

items.explanation: Direct primaries let voters choose party nominees themselves instead of leaving that decision to party bosses in conventions. A choice saying they selected senators directly is wrong because that change came from the 17th Amendment, not the primary system itself. The reform reflected Progressive efforts to make politics more democratic and less controlled by machines.
items.explanationEs: Direct primaries let voters choose party nominees themselves instead of leaving that decision to party bosses in conventions. A choice saying they selected senators directly is wrong because that change came from the 17th enmienda, not the primary system itself. The reform reflected Progressive efforts to make politics more democrático and less controlled by machines, especially in this item's emphasis on direct primaries replaced party conventions selecting.

items.stem: The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 was a response to which concern?
items.stemEs: La Ley de Exclusión China de 1882 fue una respuesta a qué preocupación?

choices.text: Economic fears that Chinese immigrants would take American jobs
choices.textEs: Temores económicos de que los inmigrantes chinos tomaran empleos estadounidenses

choices.text: Diplomatic tensions arising from trade negotiations with China
choices.textEs: Tensiones diplomáticas surgidas de negociaciones comerciales con China

choices.text: Political concerns about Chinese influence on American elections
choices.textEs: Preocupaciones políticas sobre la influencia china en las elecciones americanas

choices.text: Cultural conflicts between Eastern and Western social traditions
choices.textEs: Conflictos culturales entre las tradiciones sociales orientales y occidentales

items.explanation: The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 grew out of anti-Chinese nativism and labor fears in the West, where many white workers blamed Chinese immigrants for low wages and job competition. A choice saying the law welcomed immigrants is wrong because it suspended Chinese immigration rather than expanding it. It was the first major federal law to ban immigration based on nationality.
items.explanationEs: La Ley de Exclusión China de 1882 fue la primera ley significativa que restringió la inmigración a los Estados Unidos. Se aprobó en respuesta al sentimiento anti-chino, particularmente en la Costa Oeste, donde los trabajadores temían que los inmigrantes chinos trabajaran por salarios más bajos y tomaran sus trabajos. Esto reflejó el aumento del nativismo y la competencia por trabajos durante la industrialización. La ley permaneció en vigor hasta 1943.

items.stem: What was the spoils system in American politics?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue el sistema de botín en la política estadounidense?

choices.text: Awarding government positions to loyal political supporters
choices.textEs: Otorgar puestos gubernamentales a partidarios políticos leales

choices.text: A competitive examination system for filling government positions
choices.textEs: Un sistema de examen competitivo para llenar puestos gubernamentales

choices.text: A progressive taxation plan for wealth redistribution
choices.textEs: Un plan de impuestos progresivos para redistribuir la riqueza

choices.text: A reform ensuring transparent and honest election procedures
choices.textEs: Una reforma que asegura procedimientos electorales transparentes y honestos

items.explanation: The spoils system gave government jobs to loyal supporters instead of the most qualified applicants, which encouraged patronage and incompetence. A choice about direct election or antitrust law is wrong because the spoils system was about political appointments, not voting reform or business regulation. Criticism of this system grew after scandals and helped lead to civil service reform in the 1880s.
items.explanationEs: El sistema de botín ("al vencedor pertenecen los despojos") fue la práctica de recompensar a los partidarios políticos con trabajos gubernamentales sin importar las calificaciones. Esto condujo a incompetencia y corrupción. Después de que el presidente James Garfield fue asesinado en 1881 por un buscador de empleo descontento, el Congreso aprobó la Ley de Servicio Civil Pendleton (1883), que estableció la contratación basada en méritos para algunos puestos federales.

items.stem: What was the main purpose of Angel Island?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue el propósito principal de Angel Island?

choices.text: An immigration processing station for Asian arrivals on the West Coast
choices.textEs: Una estación de procesamiento de inmigración para llegadas asiáticas en la Costa Oeste

choices.text: A military training facility for soldiers stationed in the Pacific region
choices.textEs: Una instalación de entrenamiento militar para soldados estacionados en el Pacífico

choices.text: A federal prison housing criminals convicted of interstate offenses
choices.textEs: Una prisión federal que albergaba criminales convictos de delitos interestatales

choices.text: A national park established to preserve California coastal environments
choices.textEs: Un parque nacional establecido para preservar ambientes costeros de California

items.explanation: Angel Island in San Francisco Bay served as a federal immigration station where many Asian immigrants, especially Chinese arrivals, were detained and questioned. A choice comparing it to Ellis Island without noting its restrictive role is wrong because Angel Island became known for long interrogations and exclusion. Its history shows that immigration policy treated different groups very differently.
items.explanationEs: Angel Island en la Bahía de San Francisco sirvió como la principal estación de inmigración para inmigrantes asiáticos (especialmente chinos) de 1910-1940. A diferencia del procesamiento relativamente rápido de Ellis Island, los inmigrantes asiáticos enfrentaron detenciones prolongadas, interrogatorios duros y trato discriminatorio debido a las leyes de exclusión. Muchos fueron retenidos durante semanas o meses, y algunos tallaron poesía en las paredes describiendo sus experiencias.

items.stem: What was the purpose of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) created in 1914?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál era el propósito de la Comisión Federal de Comercio (FTC) creada en 1914?

choices.text: To promote foreign trade agreements and boost exports
choices.textEs: Promover acuerdos de comercio exterior y aumentar exportaciones

choices.text: To regulate labor unions and resolve workplace disputes
choices.textEs: Regular sindicatos laborales y resolver disputas en el trabajo

choices.text: To enforce antitrust laws and stop unfair business acts
choices.textEs: Hacer cumplir leyes antimonopolio y detener prácticas desleales

choices.text: To collect federal income taxes and manage government funds
choices.textEs: Recaudar impuestos federales sobre la renta y gestionar fondos

items.explanation: The FTC was created to investigate companies and stop unfair methods of competition before they hardened into monopolies. A choice about controlling the money supply is wrong because that was the Federal Reserve’s job, not the FTC’s. The agency remains a key part of federal business regulation.
items.explanationEs: La Comisión Federal de Comercio fue creada junto con la Ley Clayton Antimonopolio para hacer cumplir las leyes antimonopolio, investigar prácticas comerciales desleales y proteger a los consumidores del comportamiento monopolístico.

items.stem: What was the "Wisconsin Idea" associated with Robert La Follette?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué era la "Idea de Wisconsin" asociada con Robert La Follette?

choices.text: A plan to make Wisconsin an independent nation
choices.textEs: Un plan para hacer de Wisconsin una nación independiente

choices.text: A movement to return to an agricultural economy
choices.textEs: Un movimiento para regresar a la economía agrícola

choices.text: A proposal to eliminate all state taxes
choices.textEs: Una propuesta para eliminar todos los impuestos estatales

choices.text: Using university experts to draft laws and guide government
choices.textEs: Usar expertos universitarios para redactar legislación y aplicar métodos científicos al gobierno

items.explanation: Robert La Follette’s Wisconsin Idea used university experts and state government to design practical reforms such as railroad regulation and tax changes. A choice about machine politics is wrong because the Wisconsin Idea tried to weaken party bosses through expert-led reform. It reflected Progressive confidence that knowledge and government could solve public problems.
items.explanationEs: La Idea de Wisconsin involucraba usar profesores universitarios y expertos para redactar legislación y administrar programas gubernamentales. La Follette creía que la experiencia científica debería guiar las políticas públicas, haciendo al gobierno más eficiente y efectivo.

items.stem: What was the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) created to do under Wilson?
items.stemEs: ¿Para qué fue creada la Comisión Federal de Comercio (FTC) bajo Wilson?

choices.text: Monitor and prevent unfair business practices and deceptive advertising
choices.textEs: Supervisar y prevenir prácticas comerciales desleales y publicidad engañosa

choices.text: Government should regulate banking to prevent financial crises
choices.textEs: Negociar tratados comerciales con países extranjeros en nombre de EE.UU.

choices.text: A process allowing citizens to propose new legislation through petition
choices.textEs: Fijar precios para todos los bienes de consumo vendidos en Estados Unidos

choices.text: Fighting unfair railroad rates and business practices that hurt farmers
choices.textEs: Gestionar el déficit comercial internacional del gobierno federal

items.explanation: The Federal Trade Commission was created in 1914 to investigate and prevent unfair business practices such as false advertising and other forms of unfair competition. Choice B is wrong because regulating banking crises was the job of the Federal Reserve, not the FTC. Choice D is wrong because railroad rate regulation belonged mainly to the Interstate Commerce Commission. The FTC became one of the most lasting Progressive agencies for regulating business behavior.
items.explanationEs: La Comisión Federal de Comercio (1914) fue creada para investigar y prevenir prácticas comerciales desleales, comportamiento anticompetitivo y publicidad engañosa—dando al gobierno una agencia permanente para supervisar la conducta corporativa.

items.stem: The 17th Amendment (1913), providing for direct election of U.S. senators, was a Progressive reform because —
items.stemEs: The 17th enmienda (1913), providing for direct election of U.S. senators, was a Progressive reform because —

choices.text: It gave voters a direct voice in Senate elections, replacing the system where state legislatures had selected senators
choices.textEs: It gave voters a direct voice in Senado elections, replacing the system where state legislatures had selected senators

choices.text: It required senators to maintain a legal residence in the states they represented rather than living in Washington
choices.textEs: It required senators to maintain a legal residence in the states they represented rather than living in Washington

choices.text: It shifted Senate power toward large-population states by replacing the fixed two-senator rule with a proportional representation formula
choices.textEs: It shifted Senado power toward large-population states by replacing the fixed two-senator rule with a proportional representation formula

choices.text: It transferred the Senate's role in confirming federal judges and executive officers to a newly created independent commission
choices.textEs: It transferred the Senado's role in confirming federal judges and executive officers to a newly created independent commission

items.explanation: The 17th Amendment was a Progressive reform because it gave voters a direct voice in choosing senators and reduced the influence of corrupt state legislatures. Choice B is wrong because senators already represented states and residency was not the issue the amendment addressed. Choice D is wrong because the Senate kept its role in confirming presidential appointments. The amendment reflected the Progressive belief that democracy should be more direct and less controlled by political insiders.
items.explanationEs: The 17th enmienda was a Progressive reform because it gave voters a direct voice in choosing senators and reduced the influence of corrupt state legislatures. Choice B is wrong because senators already represented states and residency was not the issue the enmienda addressed. Choice D is wrong because the Senado kept its role in confirming presidential appointments. The enmienda reflected the Progressive belief that democracia should be more direct and less controlled by political insiders.

items.stem: The 19th Amendment's ratification in 1920 was the culmination of —
items.stemEs: The 19th enmienda's ratification in 1920 was the culmination of —

choices.text: An international women's movement that the U.S. joined after observing women's suffrage in European democracies
choices.textEs: An international women's movement that the U.S. joined after observing women's sufragio in European democracies

choices.text: A 72-year campaign for women's suffrage that had begun at the Seneca Falls Convention in 1848
choices.textEs: A 72-year campaign for women's sufragio that had begun at the Seneca Falls Convention in 1848

choices.text: A constitutional mandate that all states must extend suffrage rights equally to male and female citizens
choices.textEs: A constitucional mandate that all states must extend sufragio rights equally to male and female citizens

choices.text: A 10-year Progressive Era effort begun after Theodore Roosevelt first proposed women's suffrage in 1910
choices.textEs: A 10-year Era Progresista effort begun after Theodore Roosevelt first proposed women's sufragio in 1910

items.explanation: The 19th Amendment was the result of a 72-year campaign for women's suffrage that began at Seneca Falls in 1848. Choice A is wrong because international suffrage movements mattered, but the amendment grew mainly from a long American reform struggle. Choice D is wrong because the movement did not begin in 1910 or with Theodore Roosevelt. Its ratification showed how persistence across generations could expand democratic rights.
items.explanationEs: The 19th enmienda was the result of a 72-year campaign for women's sufragio that began at Seneca Falls in 1848. Choice A is wrong because international sufragio movements mattered, but the enmienda grew mainly from a long American reform struggle. Choice D is wrong because the movement did not begin in 1910 or with Theodore Roosevelt. Its ratification showed how persistence across generations could expand democrático rights.

items.stem: The creation of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) was a compromise between Roosevelt's vision of a powerful 'trade court' and Wilson's preference for —
items.stemEs: The creation of the Federal comercio Commission (FTC) was a compromise between Roosevelt's vision of a powerful 'comercio court' and Wilson's preference for —

choices.text: An agency with broad discretion to prevent unfair competition before it became monopoly
choices.textEs: An agency with broad discretion to prevent unfair competition before it became monopolio

choices.text: A prosecutorial agency that would break up all trusts rather than regulating them
choices.textEs: A prosecutorial agency that would break up all fideicomisos rather than regulating them

choices.text: Turning antitrust enforcement largely over to the Department of Justice
choices.textEs: Turning antifideicomiso enforcement largely over to the Department of Justice

choices.text: Creating separate industry-specific regulatory commissions for each major sector
choices.textEs: Creating separate industry-specific regulatory commissions for each major sector

items.explanation: The FTC represented a compromise by creating an expert agency that could prevent unfair competition before it grew into monopoly power. Choice B is wrong because Wilson did not want a purely prosecutorial body whose only purpose was to smash all trusts. The commission became part of the long-term Progressive regulatory state.
items.explanationEs: The FTC represented a compromise by creating an expert agency that could prevent unfair competition before it grew into monopolio power. Choice B is wrong because Wilson did not want a purely prosecutorial body whose only purpose was to smash all fideicomisos. The commission became part of the long-term Progressive regulatory state.

items.stem: The Haymarket Affair of 1886 resulted in —
items.stemEs: El Asunto de Haymarket de 1886 resultó en —

choices.text: immediate passage of laws protecting all industrial workers' rights
choices.textEs: aprobación inmediata de leyes que protegen los derechos de los trabajadores

choices.text: a setback for the labor movement due to public fear of radicalism
choices.textEs: un retroceso para el movimiento laboral debido al temor al radicalismo

choices.text: widespread public support for adopting the eight-hour workday
choices.textEs: apoyo público generalizado para adoptar la jornada de ocho horas

choices.text: the formation and rapid growth of the American Federation of Labor
choices.textEs: la formación y rápido crecimiento de la Federación del Trabajo

items.explanation: The Haymarket Affair damaged the labor movement because a bomb thrown at a workers’ rally in Chicago led many Americans to associate unions with violence and radicalism. A choice saying it immediately strengthened public support for unions is wrong because the event sparked fear and backlash instead. It became a turning point in how labor activism was viewed in the late 1800s.
items.explanationEs: Cuando una bomba mató a oficiales de policía en una manifestación laboral en Chicago por la jornada de ocho horas, ocho anarquistas fueron condenados (aunque el bombardero nunca fue identificado). El incidente vinculó el activismo laboral con el anarquismo y la violencia en la mente pública, dañando a los sindicatos y a los Caballeros del Trabajo en particular.

items.stem: The Pendleton Act of 1883 reformed the civil service system by —
items.stemEs: La Ley Pendleton de 1883 reformó el sistema de servicio civil al —

choices.text: Corrupt political organizations that controlled city governments through patronage
choices.textEs: permitir que los partidos políticos controlen las decisiones de contratación

choices.text: The Social Gospel argued that Christians had a duty to address poverty and injustice
choices.textEs: dar al presidente más poder para nombrar aliados políticos

choices.text: Regulated railroad rates and practices as the first federal industry regulation
choices.textEs: eliminar todos los empleos gubernamentales por nombramiento

choices.text: requiring merit-based examinations for federal jobs instead of political patronage
choices.textEs: requerir exámenes basados en mérito para empleos federales en lugar de patronazgo político

items.explanation: The Pendleton Civil Service Act of 1883 required many federal jobs to be filled through competitive exams instead of political favoritism after President Garfield’s assassination highlighted the dangers of patronage. A choice about expanding suffrage or regulating railroads is wrong because the law targeted government hiring, not elections or transportation rates. It marked an important shift toward a more professional federal bureaucracy.
items.explanationEs: La Ley Pendleton fue aprobada después del asesinato del presidente Garfield por un buscador de cargos decepcionado. Creó la Comisión de Servicio Civil y requirió exámenes competitivos para puestos federales.

items.stem: President James Garfield's assassination in 1881 led directly to —
items.stemEs: El asesinato del presidente James Garfield en 1881 llevó directamente a —

choices.text: Farmers and rural Americans facing economic difficulties
choices.textEs: leyes de inmigración más estrictas

choices.text: The passage of the Pendleton Act for civil service reform
choices.textEs: el fin de las máquinas políticas en las ciudades estadounidenses

choices.text: passage of the Pendleton Act reforming the spoils system
choices.textEs: la aprobación de la Ley Pendleton reformando el sistema de botín

choices.text: The wealthy succeeded due to their natural superiority
choices.textEs: la destitución del vicepresidente Arthur

items.explanation: President James A. Garfield was assassinated by a disappointed office seeker in 1881, and the shock of that event pushed Congress to pass the Pendleton Civil Service Act. A choice about antitrust or labor reform is wrong because Garfield’s death was tied to patronage politics, not corporate regulation or union issues. The episode helped convince many Americans that the spoils system had become dangerous and unstable.
items.explanationEs: Charles Guiteau disparó a Garfield porque le fue negado un empleo gubernamental que sentía merecer bajo el sistema de botín. La indignación pública llevó al Congreso a aprobar la Ley Pendleton.

items.stem: Populism in the late 19th century can best be defined as —
items.stemEs: Populism in the late 19th century can best be defined as —

choices.text: A policy supporting unlimited immigration and cultural diversity
choices.textEs: A policy supporting unlimited inmigración and cultural diversity

choices.text: A political movement advocating for the rights and interests of farmers and small producers
choices.textEs: A political movement advocating for the rights and interests of farmers and small producers

choices.text: A philosophy promoting government ownership of major private industries
choices.textEs: A philosophy promoting government ownership of major private industries

choices.text: A political movement supporting the interests of wealthy
choices.textEs: A political movement supporting the interests of wealthy

items.explanation: Populism was a political movement of farmers and ordinary citizens who demanded that government curb the power of banks, railroads, and corporate monopolies. A choice describing nativism or Progressivism is wrong because Populism had a distinct rural and anti-monopoly focus. Many ideas once seen as radical Populist demands later became law.
items.explanationEs: Populism was a political movement of farmers and ordinary citizens who demanded that government curb the power of banks, railroads, and corporate monopolies. A choice describing nativism or progresismo is wrong because Populism had a distinct rural and anti-monopolio focus. Many ideas once seen as radical Populist demands later became law.

items.stem: The Federal Reserve System was created in 1913 to —
items.stemEs: The Federal Reserve System was created in 1913 to —

choices.text: Guarantee government backing for most private investments
choices.textEs: Guarantee government backing for most private investments

choices.text: Establish a single national bank controlled by the federal government
choices.textEs: Establish a single national bank controlled by the gobierno federal

choices.text: Eliminate all private banks and establish government banking as the only banking option in the country
choices.textEs: Eliminate all private banks and establish government banking as the only banking option in the country

Focus: Sinclair's book → food safety laws.
items.explanationEs: *La jungla* de Upton Sinclair (publicada el 28 de febrero de 1906) expuso las condiciones sucias en las plantas empacadoras de carne de Chicago. El Congreso respondió aprobando TANTO la Ley de Alimentos y Medicamentos Puros COMO la Ley de Inspección de Carne el 30 de junio de 1906. La Ley de Inspección de Carne abordó directamente lo que Sinclair expuso: el empaque peligroso de carne. Enfoque: el libro de Sinclair → leyes de seguridad alimentaria.

items.stem: The 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote. It was added to the Constitution in 1920. Tennessee was the final state needed to ratify (approve) this amendment. What was Tennessee's nickname when it ratified the 19th Amendment?
items.stemEs: La 19.ª Enmienda dio a las mujeres el derecho al voto. Se añadió a la Constitución en 1920. Tennessee fue el último estado necesario para ratificar (aprobar) esta enmienda. ¿Cuál fue el apodo de Tennessee cuando ratificó la 19.ª Enmienda?

choices.text: The Volunteer State
choices.textEs: El Estado Voluntario

choices.text: The Suffrage Capital
choices.textEs: La Capital del Sufragio

choices.text: The Perfect 36
choices.textEs: El 36 Perfecto

choices.text: The Key State
choices.textEs: El Estado Clave

items.dokRationale: Simple recall of Tennessee's unique role in 19th Amendment ratification — designed as a low-floor entry point for Tier 2/3 learners. Ties to TN connection in textbook.
items.explanation: Tennessee ratified the 19th Amendment on August 18, 1920 — the 36th and final state needed under the Constitution's three-fourths rule. Tennessee became known as 'The Perfect 36.' Harry Burn cast the deciding vote after his mother Febb Burn wrote him a letter urging ratification. Focus: Tennessee = 36th state = 'The Perfect 36.'
items.explanationEs: Tennessee ratificó la 19.ª Enmienda el 18 de agosto de 1920, el 36.º y último estado necesario según la regla de tres cuartos de la Constitución. Tennessee llegó a ser conocido como «El 36 Perfecto». Harry Burn emitió el voto decisivo después de que su madre Febb Burn le escribiera una carta instándolo a ratificar. Enfoque: Tennessee = 36.º estado = «El 36 Perfecto».

items.stem: What did Social Darwinists believe about wealth and poverty?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué creían los darwinistas sociales sobre la riqueza y la pobreza?

choices.text: The wealthy achieved success through their natural superiority
choices.textEs: Los ricos lograron el éxito a través de su superioridad natural

choices.text: It damaged labor by linking unions with anarchism and violence
choices.textEs: El gobierno debería redistribuir la riqueza entre todos los ciudadanos

choices.text: It was the first federal law attempting to restrict monopolies
choices.textEs: La pobreza resultó de la explotación por la clase económica alta

choices.text: They accepted all workers regardless of skill, race, or gender
choices.textEs: La sociedad debería garantizar resultados económicos iguales para todos

items.explanation: Social Darwinists argued that wealth and poverty reflected natural competition, so they saw success as proof of fitness and poverty as a sign of weakness. A choice calling for charity or government aid is wrong because Social Darwinism generally opposed helping the poor through reform programs. Industrialists used this idea to defend laissez-faire capitalism and resist regulation in the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: Los darwinistas sociales aplicaron la teoría de Charles Darwin de "supervivencia del más apto" a la sociedad humana, argumentando que las personas ricas tuvieron éxito porque eran naturalmente superiores y que la pobreza resultó de la inferioridad natural. Se opusieron a la ayuda gubernamental a los pobres, alegando que interfería con la selección natural. Esta filosofía justificó la desigualdad extrema y fue utilizada por los industriales para defender su riqueza.

items.stem: What was laissez-faire capitalism?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue el capitalismo de laissez-faire?

choices.text: a setback for the labor movement due to public fear of radicalism
choices.textEs: Una política económica basada en impuestos pesados a los ricos

choices.text: bread-and-butter issues like wages, hours, and working conditions
choices.textEs: Un sistema donde el gobierno posee y opera todos los negocios

choices.text: An economic philosophy opposing government regulation of business
choices.textEs: Una filosofía económica que se opone a la regulación gubernamental

choices.text: The unfair justice system that punished the poor but not the rich
choices.textEs: Un enfoque que requiere distribución igualitaria de la riqueza

items.explanation: Laissez-faire capitalism held that government should interfere as little as possible in the economy, leaving prices, wages, and competition to the market. A choice about strong federal regulation is wrong because that is the opposite of laissez-faire. This idea dominated much of the Gilded Age and shaped conflicts over reform.
items.explanationEs: El capitalismo de laissez-faire (francés para "dejar hacer") es la creencia de que el gobierno no debe interferir con la economía. Durante la Edad Dorada, esta filosofía dominó, permitiendo que los negocios operaran con regulación mínima. Esto llevó tanto a un rápido crecimiento industrial como a problemas serios como monopolios, explotación de trabajadores y condiciones inseguras. Los reformadores progresistas más tarde desafiaron las ideas de laissez-faire.

items.stem: How did the concept of the "melting pot" differ from actual immigrant experiences during the Gilded Age?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo difirió el concepto del "crisol de culturas" de las experiencias reales de los inmigrantes durante la Edad Dorada?

choices.text: The ideal suggested easy assimilation, but immigrants faced discrimination and formed ethnic communities
choices.textEs: El ideal sugirió asimilación fácil, pero los inmigrantes enfrentaron discriminación y formaron comunidades étnicas

choices.text: The Supreme Court interpreted the 14th Amendment narrowly, weakening federal protection of civil rights
choices.textEs: Los inmigrantes se asimilaron inmediatamente sin ningún desafío

choices.text: "Old" immigrants came from Northern/Western Europe; "new" immigrants came from Southern/Eastern Europe
choices.textEs: Nadie discutió nunca el concepto de crisol de culturas

choices.text: Establishing constitutional foundations that later civil rights movements used to fight discrimination
choices.textEs: Todos los inmigrantes rechazaron la cultura estadounidense completamente

items.explanation: The “melting pot” suggested immigrants would blend into one American culture, but in reality many newcomers faced crowded tenements, low-paying jobs, and discrimination. A choice claiming immigrants were immediately accepted as equals is wrong because nativism and ethnic prejudice were widespread. The idea of easy assimilation often hid the hardships of immigrant life in industrial cities.
items.explanationEs: La metáfora del "crisol de culturas" sugirió que los inmigrantes se mezclarían fácilmente en la sociedad estadounidense, creando una cultura unificada. En realidad, los inmigrantes enfrentaron discriminación significativa, barreras lingüísticas y explotación económica. A menudo formaron enclaves étnicos (Little Italy, Chinatown, etc.) para apoyo mutuo y preservación cultural. Los nativistas resistieron la influencia de los inmigrantes. La verdadera integración cultural fue un proceso mucho más lento y más complejo de lo que sugirió el ideal del crisol de culturas.

items.stem: How did the concept of "the Gilded Age" describe American society in the late 1800s?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo describió el concepto de "la Edad Dorada" la sociedad estadounidense a finales de 1800?

choices.text: Workers at Carnegie's steel plant clashed with Pinkerton agents hired by management
choices.textEs: No hubo crecimiento económico durante este período

choices.text: It was the first time a federal court injunction was used to break a strike
choices.textEs: Fue un tiempo de completa igualdad y justicia

choices.text: A bomb killed police officers, turning public opinion against labor unions
choices.textEs: Todo sobre la sociedad era genuinamente dorado y perfecto

choices.text: It appeared prosperous on the surface but hid serious social problems underneath
choices.textEs: Parecía próspera en la superficie pero ocultaba serios problemas sociales debajo

items.explanation: The phrase “Gilded Age” suggested that late-1800s America looked prosperous and shiny on the surface but hid corruption, inequality, and labor unrest underneath. A choice portraying the era as fully democratic and fair is wrong because many social and economic problems were concealed by the appearance of wealth. The term captures the contradiction between industrial growth and social conflict.
items.explanationEs: El término "Edad Dorada

items.stem: What was the significance of the Pendleton Civil Service Act (1883)?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue la importancia de la Ley de Servicio Civil Pendleton (1883)?

choices.text: It began replacing the spoils system with merit-based government hiring
choices.textEs: Comenzó a reemplazar el sistema de botín con contratación gubernamental basada en méritos

choices.text: To control city government and exchange services for political support
choices.textEs: Expandió el sistema de botín a más trabajos gubernamentales

choices.text: Philanthropic capitalism, where the wealthy serve as trustees for society
choices.textEs: Abolió todos los trabajos gubernamentales

choices.text: They provided essential services to immigrants in exchange for loyal votes
choices.textEs: No tuvo efecto en el empleo gubernamental

items.explanation: The Pendleton Civil Service Act of 1883 required many federal jobs to be filled through competitive exams instead of political favoritism after President Garfield’s assassination highlighted the dangers of patronage. A choice about expanding suffrage or regulating railroads is wrong because the law targeted government hiring, not elections or transportation rates. It marked an important shift toward a more professional federal bureaucracy.
items.explanationEs: La Ley Pendleton fue una reforma histórica que estableció la Comisión de Servicio Civil y requirió exámenes competitivos para algunos trabajos federales. Inicialmente cubriendo solo el 10% de los puestos federales, se expandió gradualmente. La ley representó un cambio del patrocinio político (sistema de botín) hacia un servicio gubernamental profesional basado en méritos. Se aprobó después del asesinato del presidente Garfield por un buscador de empleo decepcionado, lo que conmocionó a los estadounidenses para que apoyaran la reforma.

items.stem: The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 was significant because it —
items.stemEs: La Ley de Exclusión China de 1882 fue significativa porque —

choices.text: An immigration processing station for Asian arrivals on the West Coast
choices.textEs: terminó toda la inmigración a los Estados Unidos

choices.text: Fighting unfair railroad rates and business practices that hurt farmers
choices.textEs: dio la bienvenida a los trabajadores chinos para ayudar a construir ferrocarriles

choices.text: Increasing the money supply would raise crop prices and ease their debts
choices.textEs: otorgó ciudadanía a todos los inmigrantes chinos

choices.text: was the first federal law to restrict immigration based on nationality
choices.textEs: fue la primera ley federal en restringir la inmigración basada en nacionalidad

items.explanation: The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 grew out of anti-Chinese nativism and labor fears in the West, where many white workers blamed Chinese immigrants for low wages and job competition. A choice saying the law welcomed immigrants is wrong because it suspended Chinese immigration rather than expanding it. It was the first major federal law to ban immigration based on nationality.
items.explanationEs: La Ley de Exclusión China fue la primera ley significativa que restringió la inmigración a los Estados Unidos basada en nacionalidad. Suspendió la inmigración china por diez años y prohibió a los inmigrantes chinos convertirse en ciudadanos. Reflejaba un sentimiento anti-chino generalizado y temores de competencia laboral.

items.stem: The Pullman Strike of 1894 demonstrated that —
items.stemEs: La Huelga de Pullman de 1894 demostró que —

choices.text: A bomb killed police officers, turning public opinion against labor unions
choices.textEs: las compañías siempre negociaron justamente con los trabajadores

choices.text: the federal government would use force to break strikes affecting commerce
choices.textEs: el gobierno federal usaría la fuerza para romper huelgas que afectaran el comercio

choices.text: Industrialization created demand for labor, attracting massive immigration
choices.textEs: los sindicatos se habían vuelto demasiado poderosos

choices.text: It was the first time a federal court injunction was used to break a strike
choices.textEs: las huelgas eran una forma efectiva de lograr todas las demandas

items.explanation: The Pullman Strike showed that the federal government usually sided with business during major labor conflicts by using injunctions and troops to restore rail service. A choice claiming government was neutral is wrong because federal intervention helped break the strike. It revealed the limits of labor power in the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: Cuando la Unión Ferroviaria Americana boicoteó los vagones Pullman en todo el país, el presidente Cleveland envió tropas federales para romper la huelga, citando interferencia con la entrega de correo. Eugene V. Debs fue encarcelado. El incidente mostró la disposición del gobierno a ponerse del lado de los negocios contra los trabajadores y usar mandatos judiciales para detener huelgas.

items.stem: Samuel Gompers and the American Federation of Labor (AFL) focused on —
items.stemEs: Samuel Gompers y la Federación Americana del Trabajo (AFL) se enfocaron en —

choices.text: a setback for the labor movement due to public fear of radicalism
choices.textEs: derrocar el sistema capitalista

choices.text: bread-and-butter issues like wages, hours, and working conditions
choices.textEs: temas básicos como salarios, horas y condiciones de trabajo

choices.text: An economic philosophy opposing government regulation of business
choices.textEs: organizar trabajadores de fábrica no calificados

choices.text: The unfair justice system that punished the poor but not the rich
choices.textEs: apoyar candidatos políticos socialistas

items.explanation: Samuel Gompers founded the American Federation of Labor in 1886 and focused on practical gains such as better wages, hours, and working conditions for skilled workers. A choice naming Eugene Debs is wrong because Debs led a railroad union and later socialism, not the AFL. Gompers shaped the most durable labor organization of the era.
items.explanationEs: Bajo el liderazgo de Gompers (1886-1924), la AFL se enfocó en objetivos prácticos para trabajadores calificados: salarios más altos, horas más cortas y mejores condiciones a través de la negociación colectiva. A diferencia de los Caballeros del Trabajo, la AFL evitó causas políticas y trabajadores no calificados, haciéndola más conservadora pero también más exitosa y duradera.

items.stem: The Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 was passed to —
items.stemEs: La Ley de Comercio Interestatal de 1887 fue aprobada para —

choices.text: Awarding government positions to loyal political supporters
choices.textEs: nacionalizar la industria ferroviaria

choices.text: corrupt political machines that controlled city governments
choices.textEs: dividir todos los monopolios ferroviarios

choices.text: exposing the corruption of Boss Tweed through powerful cartoons
choices.textEs: proporcionar subsidios para la expansión ferroviaria

choices.text: regulate railroad rates and prohibit unfair pricing practices
choices.textEs: regular las tarifas ferroviarias y prohibir prácticas de precios injustas

items.explanation: The Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 created the Interstate Commerce Commission to regulate railroad practices such as unfair rates and discrimination against farmers and small shippers. A choice about breaking up all trusts is wrong because this law focused on railroads, not the entire corporate economy. It was one of the first major attempts by the federal government to regulate big business.
items.explanationEs: La Ley de Comercio Interestatal creó la Comisión de Comercio Interestatal (ICC) para regular las tarifas ferroviarias. Requería que las tarifas fueran "razonables y justas

items.stem: Political machines during the Gilded Age were characterized by —
items.stemEs: Las maquinarias políticas durante la Era Dorada se caracterizaban por —

choices.text: requiring merit-based examinations for federal jobs instead of political patronage
choices.textEs: Operaciones gubernamentales transparentes con supervisión pública de decisiones

choices.text: The Social Gospel argued that Christians had a duty to address poverty and injustice
choices.textEs: Supervisión federal de todas las elecciones y nombramientos locales

choices.text: Corrupt political organizations that controlled city governments through patronage
choices.textEs: Organizaciones políticas corruptas que controlaban los gobiernos de las ciudades a través del clientelismo

choices.text: Regulated railroad rates and practices as the first federal industry regulation
choices.textEs: Representación igualitaria para todas las clases sociales y económicas

items.explanation: Political machines were corrupt urban organizations that controlled city governments through patronage, favors, and vote trading. Choice A is wrong because merit exams were part of civil service reform, which tried to weaken machine politics. Choice D is wrong because railroad regulation was the purpose of the Interstate Commerce Act, not political machines. Their power grew in fast-changing immigrant cities where many people depended on local bosses for help.
items.explanationEs: Las maquinarias políticas eran organizaciones corruptas que controlaban los gobiernos de las ciudades a través del clientelismo.

items.stem: The assassination of President James A. Garfield in 1881 led to —
items.stemEs: El asesinato del Presidente James A. Garfield en 1881 llevó a —

choices.text: The elimination of all political appointments by presidents
choices.textEs: La eliminación de todos los nombramientos políticos por presidentes

choices.text: The expansion of the spoils system in government
choices.textEs: La expansión del sistema de botín en el gobierno

choices.text: The passage of the Pendleton Act for civil service reform
choices.textEs: La aprobación de la Ley Pendleton para la reforma del servicio civil

choices.text: The creation of more powerful political machines
choices.textEs: La creación de maquinarias políticas más poderosas

items.explanation: President James A. Garfield was assassinated by a disappointed office seeker in 1881, and the shock of that event pushed Congress to pass the Pendleton Civil Service Act. A choice about antitrust or labor reform is wrong because Garfield’s death was tied to patronage politics, not corporate regulation or union issues. The episode helped convince many Americans that the spoils system had become dangerous and unstable.
items.explanationEs: Garfield fue asesinado por un solicitante de empleo decepcionado, lo que llevó a la aprobación de la Ley de Reforma del Servicio Civil Pendleton de 1883.

items.stem: The Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 was significant because it —
items.stemEs: La Ley de Comercio Interestatal de 1887 fue significativa porque —

choices.text: Corrupt political organizations that controlled city governments through patronage
choices.textEs: Estableció los primeros parques nacionales en los Estados Unidos

choices.text: Regulated railroad rates and practices as the first federal industry regulation
choices.textEs: Reguló las tarifas y prácticas ferroviarias como la primera regulación federal de la industria

choices.text: requiring merit-based examinations for federal jobs instead of political patronage
choices.textEs: Proporcionó ayuda financiera directa a los agricultores en dificultades

choices.text: The Social Gospel argued that Christians had a duty to address poverty and injustice
choices.textEs: Creó los primeros sindicatos para trabajadores industriales

items.explanation: The Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 created the Interstate Commerce Commission to regulate railroad practices such as unfair rates and discrimination against farmers and small shippers. A choice about breaking up all trusts is wrong because this law focused on railroads, not the entire corporate economy. It was one of the first major attempts by the federal government to regulate big business.
items.explanationEs: La Ley de Comercio Interestatal fue la primera ley federal en regular la industria privada, requiriendo que las tarifas ferroviarias fueran "razonables y justas".

items.stem: The Populist Party emerged in the 1890s primarily to represent the interests of —
items.stemEs: El Partido Populista surgió en la década de 1890 principalmente para representar los intereses de —

choices.text: Farmers and rural Americans facing economic difficulties
choices.textEs: Agricultores y estadounidenses rurales enfrentando dificultades económicas

choices.text: passage of the Pendleton Act reforming the spoils system
choices.textEs: Industriales ricos promoviendo la expansión empresarial

choices.text: The passage of the Pendleton Act for civil service reform
choices.textEs: Inmigrantes recientes buscando representación política

choices.text: The wealthy succeeded due to their natural superiority
choices.textEs: Trabajadores de fábricas urbanas buscando mejores condiciones laborales

items.explanation: The Populist Party grew out of farm protest and mainly represented struggling farmers who faced debt, falling crop prices, and high railroad shipping rates. A choice centered on big business or urban political machines is wrong because Populism came from rural discontent, not corporate power. Its platform influenced later reforms such as direct election of senators and banking regulation.
items.explanationEs: El Partido Populista fue formado por agricultores que enfrentaban precios de cultivos en caída, altas tarifas ferroviarias y crédito ajustado.

items.stem: Compare Social Darwinism with the Social Gospel movement. How did their views on helping the poor differ?
items.stemEs: Compare el Darwinismo Social con el movimiento del Evangelio Social. ¿Cómo diferían sus puntos de vista sobre ayudar a los pobres?

choices.text: Herbert Spencer, who coined the phrase "survival of the fittest"
choices.textEs: El Darwinismo Social promovía la caridad; el Evangelio Social se oponía a la ayuda

choices.text: exposing the corruption of Boss Tweed through powerful cartoons
choices.textEs: Ambos movimientos acordaban que la ayuda caritativa dañaba a los pobres

choices.text: Societal Darwinism opposed aid; Societal Gospel urged Christian duty
choices.textEs: El Darwinismo Social se oponía a la ayuda; el Evangelio Social instaba al deber cristiano

choices.text: urban political machines that used corruption to maintain power
choices.textEs: Ambos movimientos apoyaban programas de bienestar del gobierno federal

items.explanation: Social Darwinism argued that aid to the poor interfered with natural competition, while the Social Gospel taught that Christians had a duty to fight poverty and injustice. Choice A is wrong because Herbert Spencer was a person linked to Social Darwinism, not the comparison itself. Choice B is wrong because Thomas Nast's cartoons dealt with political corruption, not ideas about poverty. This conflict showed how Americans disagreed over whether industrial society should reward competition or encourage reform.
items.explanationEs: Los darwinistas sociales creían que ayudar a los pobres interfería con la selección natural, mientras que el movimiento del Evangelio Social enseñaba que los cristianos tenían un deber moral de abordar los problemas sociales y ayudar a los necesitados.

items.stem: Analyze the source: Why did Upton Sinclair write "The Jungle," and what was his purpose?
items.stemEs: Analice la fuente: ¿Por qué escribió Upton Sinclair "La Jungla" y cuál era su propósito?

choices.text: Meat fell on dirty floors and moldy sausage was reprocessed
choices.textEs: Para entretener a los lectores con historias ficticias de inmigrantes

choices.text: Using university experts to draft laws and guide government
choices.textEs: Para promover la industria empacadora de carne y aumentar las ventas

choices.text: To expose dangerous conditions and push for labor reforms
choices.textEs: Para exponer condiciones peligrosas y apoyar esfuerzos de reforma laboral

choices.text: Food safety laws passed because consumers feared contamination
choices.textEs: Para defender a los dueños de fábricas contra críticas públicas injustas

items.explanation: Upton Sinclair wrote The Jungle to expose dangerous conditions in Chicago's meatpacking industry and to stir support for reform, especially for workers. Choice A is wrong because it lists evidence from the book rather than Sinclair's purpose in writing it. Choice D is wrong because it describes one result of public reaction, not the author's original goal. The novel showed how muckraking writing could turn industrial abuses into national political issues.
items.explanationEs: Sinclair escribió "La Jungla" como un exposé muckraking para revelar las terribles condiciones de trabajo y la explotación de trabajadores inmigrantes en plantas empacadoras de carne. Buscaba construir apoyo para reformas laborales, aunque el público se enfocó más en la seguridad alimentaria.

items.stem: Provide historical context: Why did the Declaration of Sentiments model itself after the Declaration of Independence?
items.stemEs: Proporcione contexto histórico: ¿Por qué la Declaración de Sentimientos se modeló después de la Declaración de Independencia?

choices.text: To argue women's rights were as fundamental as liberty
choices.textEs: Para argumentar que los derechos de las mujeres eran tan fundamentales como la independencia

choices.text: To appeal to patriotic sentiment with familiar language
choices.textEs: Para apelar al sentimiento patriótico usando lenguaje familiar

choices.text: To meet legal requirements for referencing key documents
choices.textEs: Para cumplir requisitos legales para referenciar documentos fundacionales

choices.text: To demonstrate their deep knowledge of American history
choices.textEs: Para demostrar su amplio conocimiento de la historia estadounidense

items.explanation: The Declaration of Sentiments borrowed from the Declaration of Independence so women’s rights activists could argue that denying women equality contradicted America’s own founding principles. A choice saying the document was modeled on the Constitution alone is wrong because the rhetorical parallel was specifically to the Declaration. That strategy tied women’s demands to the nation’s deepest political ideals.
items.explanationEs: Elizabeth Cady Stanton modeló deliberadamente la Declaración de Sentimientos después de la Declaración de Independencia para argumentar que los derechos de las mujeres eran tan fundamentales y "evidentes por sí mismos" como los derechos de independencia. Al cambiar "todos los hombres" a "todos los hombres y mujeres," expuso la hipocresía de negar a las mujeres derechos iguales.

items.stem: Use evidence: What specific details from "The Jungle" passage support the claim that meatpacking plants were unsanitary?
items.stemEs: Use evidencia: ¿Qué detalles específicos del pasaje de "La Jungla" apoyan la afirmación de que las plantas empacadoras de carne no eran higiénicas?

choices.text: Government inspectors monitored production and quality closely
choices.textEs: Inspectores gubernamentales monitoreaban la producción y control de calidad

choices.text: Facilities met sanitation standards and had regular inspections
choices.textEs: Las instalaciones cumplían estándares de saneamiento con limpieza regular

choices.text: Workers wore protective equipment and followed safety protocols
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores usaban equipo de protección y seguían regulaciones de salud

choices.text: Meat fell on dirty floors and moldy sausage was reprocessed
choices.textEs: La carne caía en pisos sucios y salchichas mohosas eran reprocesadas

items.explanation: Evidence such as spoiled meat, filthy machinery, contaminated floors, and unsafe handling practices supports the claim that meatpacking plants were unsanitary. A choice that mentions only long hours is wrong because the question asks specifically about food cleanliness, not labor conditions alone. These details pushed many readers to demand federal inspection of food production.
items.explanationEs: El pasaje proporciona evidencia específica de condiciones insalubres: carne que "había caído al suelo, en la suciedad y el aserrín, donde los trabajadores habían pisoteado y escupido," y salchicha vieja rechazada de Europa que estaba "mohosa y blanca" siendo reprocesada para consumo.

items.stem: Interpret: What did the creation of the Federal Reserve System reveal about Progressive Era attitudes toward government's role in the economy?
items.stemEs: Interprete: ¿Qué reveló la creación del Sistema de Reserva Federal sobre las actitudes de la Era Progresista hacia el papel del gobierno en la economía?

choices.text: Financial panics, inflexible currency, and bank power
choices.textEs: Los bancos deberían operar sin ninguna supervisión gubernamental

choices.text: Monitor and prevent unfair business practices and deceptive advertising
choices.textEs: El gobierno debería tomar control completo de todos los negocios privados

choices.text: Regulate the nation's money supply and banking system
choices.textEs: El gobierno debería evitar cualquier participación en asuntos económicos

choices.text: Government should regulate banking to prevent financial crises
choices.textEs: El gobierno debería regular la banca para prevenir pánicos financieros

items.explanation: Creating the Federal Reserve showed that Progressives believed the national government should actively manage the economy instead of waiting for the market to correct itself. A choice saying Progressives wanted no federal role in banking is wrong because the Fed represented a major expansion of that role. The reform showed how deeply faith in expertise and regulation shaped the era.
items.explanationEs: La Ley de la Reserva Federal (1913) mostró que los progresistas creían que el gobierno debería jugar un papel activo en estabilizar la economía. Veían la regulación gubernamental como necesaria para prevenir pánicos financieros y proteger el interés público, representando un cambio de la economía laissez-faire.

items.stem: Why did Populists support bimetallism (using both gold and silver as currency)?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué los populistas apoyaban el bimetalismo (usar tanto oro como plata como moneda)?

choices.text: More money in circulation would raise crop prices and ease debt
choices.textEs: Más dinero en circulación aumentaría los precios de cultivos y aliviaría deudas

choices.text: Economic fears that Chinese immigrants would take American jobs
choices.textEs: Querían hacer la moneda más escasa y aumentar su valor

choices.text: It rallied Populist and Democratic support for free silver coinage
choices.textEs: Eran dueños de minas de plata que querían aumentar ganancias

choices.text: Nativism, which favored native-born citizens over immigrants
choices.textEs: Se oponían a todas las formas de papel moneda y sistemas bancarios

items.explanation: Populists supported bimetallism and free silver because adding silver to the money supply would create inflation, making debts easier for farmers to repay and raising crop prices. A choice saying farmers wanted a stronger gold standard is wrong because tight money usually helped creditors, not debtors. Monetary policy became one of the biggest political battles of the 1890s.
items.explanationEs: Los populistas apoyaban el bimetalismo porque agregar plata a la moneda inflaría la oferta monetaria, aumentaría los precios de los cultivos y facilitaría a los agricultores endeudados pagar préstamos con dólares más baratos.

items.stem: What was the significance of Tennessee's Coal Creek labor conflict?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue la importancia del conflicto laboral de Coal Creek en Tennessee?

choices.text: It established the first minimum wage law in the United States
choices.textEs: Estableció la primera ley de salario mínimo en Estados Unidos

choices.text: It created the first successful industrial union in the nation
choices.textEs: Creó el primer sindicato industrial exitoso en el Sur

choices.text: Armed miners freed convict laborers and ended convict leasing
choices.textEs: Mineros armados liberaron a trabajadores convictos y ayudaron a terminar el arrendamiento de convictos

choices.text: It led directly to the formation of the American Federation
choices.textEs: Llevó a la formación de la Federación Americana del Trabajo

items.explanation: The Coal Creek conflict was significant because it exposed the injustice of convict leasing and showed how workers fought systems that undercut free labor. A choice about urban political machines is wrong because Coal Creek was a mining labor conflict, not a city politics issue. Tennessee’s experience reflected broader national battles over labor rights and incarceration.
items.explanationEs: Durante la Guerra de Coal Creek (1891-1892), mineros armados liberaron a trabajadores convictos que estaban siendo usados para socavar sus salarios. Este conflicto ayudó a terminar el sistema de arrendamiento de convictos de Tennessee.

items.stem: What tactics did labor unions use to pressure employers during the Gilded Age?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué tácticas usaban los sindicatos para presionar a los empleadores durante la Edad Dorada?

choices.text: Only through peaceful negotiations without any work stoppages
choices.textEs: Solo a través de negociaciones pacíficas sin ningún paro laboral

choices.text: Through strikes, boycotts, collective bargaining, and picketing
choices.textEs: A través de huelgas, boicots, negociación colectiva y piquetes

choices.text: Exclusively through voting for sympathetic pro-labor politicians
choices.textEs: Exclusivamente votando por políticos simpatizantes pro-laborales

choices.text: Only through filing formal lawsuits in the federal court system
choices.textEs: Solo a través de demandas formales en el sistema de tribunales federales

items.explanation: Labor unions used strikes, boycotts, collective bargaining, and sometimes picketing to pressure employers for better wages and conditions. A choice about trust-busting laws is wrong because that was mainly a government strategy against corporations, not a union tactic. These methods became central tools in the fight for workers’ rights.
items.explanationEs: Los sindicatos empleaban múltiples tácticas: huelgas (paros laborales), boicots (negarse a comprar productos), negociación colectiva (negociar como grupo) y piquetes (protestar fuera de los lugares de trabajo).

items.stem: How did women's work experiences differ from men's during the industrial era?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo diferían las experiencias laborales de las mujeres de las de los hombres durante la era industrial?

choices.text: Women and men received identical pay and equal conditions
choices.textEs: Las mujeres y los hombres recibían igual salario y condiciones de trabajo

choices.text: Women were legally barred from working in any factories
choices.textEs: A las mujeres se les prohibía legalmente trabajar en fábricas

choices.text: Women earned less pay and faced harassment and barriers
choices.textEs: Las mujeres ganaban menos y enfrentaban acoso y avance limitado

choices.text: Women earned higher wages for their specialized skill sets
choices.textEs: Las mujeres ganaban salarios más altos por sus habilidades textiles

items.explanation: Women in the industrial era were concentrated in lower-paying jobs such as garment work, domestic service, and clerical work, and they were often paid less than men for similar labor. A choice saying women held the same positions with equal wages is wrong because the workplace was sharply divided by gender. These inequalities helped drive women’s labor activism and reform movements.
items.explanationEs: Las mujeres típicamente ganaban 50-60% del salario de los hombres por el mismo trabajo, enfrentaban acoso sexual, tenían oportunidades de avance limitadas y a menudo trabajaban en condiciones particularmente duras en fábricas textiles y de ropa.

items.stem: How did Roosevelt distinguish between "good trusts" and "bad trusts"?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo distinguía Roosevelt entre "trusts buenos" y "trusts malos"?

choices.text: He believed all large corporations were harmful and must be dissolved
choices.textEs: Creía que todas las grandes corporaciones eran dañinas y debían disolverse

choices.text: Good trusts were efficient and fair; bad trusts abused their power
choices.textEs: Los trusts buenos eran eficientes y justos; los trusts malos abusaban de su poder de mercado

choices.text: Good trusts were Republican-owned; bad trusts were Democrat-owned
choices.textEs: Los trusts buenos eran propiedad de republicanos; los trusts malos de demócratas

choices.text: He made no distinction and supported all large business interests
choices.textEs: No hacía distinción entre trusts y apoyaba a todos los grandes negocios

items.explanation: Roosevelt saw “good trusts” as large companies that operated efficiently without abusing the public, while “bad trusts” used unfair practices to crush competition and exploit consumers. A choice saying Roosevelt wanted to break up every trust is wrong because he judged corporations by behavior, not size alone. This distinction shaped the selective trust-busting of his presidency.
items.explanationEs: Roosevelt creía que los grandes negocios no eran inherentemente malos. Distinguía entre trusts que operaban justa y eficientemente versus aquellos que abusaban de su poder mediante fijación de precios, prácticas predatorias y explotación del consumidor.

items.stem: What was significant about Roosevelt's response to the Coal Strike of 1902?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue significativo sobre la respuesta de Roosevelt a la Huelga del Carbón de 1902?

choices.text: Good trusts were efficient and fair; bad trusts abused their power
choices.textEs: Usó tropas federales para romper la huelga como presidentes anteriores

choices.text: They showed government protecting consumers from unsafe products
choices.textEs: Declaró la huelga ilegal y ordenó el arresto de líderes sindicales

choices.text: Helpful because it restored fair competition for consumers
choices.textEs: Ignoró la huelga y dejó que las fuerzas del mercado resolvieran la disputa

choices.text: He forced negotiations and became first president to back workers
choices.textEs: Forzó negociaciones y se convirtió en el primer presidente en apoyar a los trabajadores

items.explanation: Roosevelt’s response to the 1902 coal strike was significant because he intervened as a neutral broker and pressured mine owners to negotiate, rather than automatically siding with business. A choice saying he sent troops to crush the workers is wrong because his handling of this strike was unusual for the time. The episode suggested that the federal government could mediate labor disputes in the public interest.
items.explanationEs: Roosevelt se convirtió en el primer presidente en intervenir en una disputa laboral del lado de los trabajadores. Amenazó con confiscar las minas de carbón y obligó a los propietarios a negociar, demostrando su filosofía del Trato Justo de tratamiento equilibrado.

items.stem: What problems did the Federal Reserve System address?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué problemas abordó el Sistema de la Reserva Federal?

choices.text: Excessive taxation and uncontrolled government spending
choices.textEs: Altos impuestos y gasto gubernamental

choices.text: Foreign trade imbalances and declining export revenue
choices.textEs: Desequilibrios de comercio exterior

choices.text: Ongoing labor disputes and rising union organization
choices.textEs: Disputas laborales y organización sindical

choices.text: Financial panics, inflexible currency, and bank power
choices.textEs: Pánicos financieros, moneda inflexible y poder bancario concentrado

items.explanation: The Federal Reserve System was created to stabilize banking, provide an elastic currency, and reduce the financial panics that had shaken the economy. A choice about direct election reforms is wrong because the Fed dealt with money and credit, not voting procedures. It remains a core institution of the modern American economy.
items.explanationEs: La Ley de la Reserva Federal (1913) abordó problemas revelados por el Pánico de 1907: pánicos financieros recurrentes, una moneda inflexible que no podía expandirse durante crisis y poder bancario concentrado en pocas instituciones grandes.

items.stem: What role did Anne Dallas Dudley play in the women's suffrage movement?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué papel jugó Anne Dallas Dudley en el movimiento sufragista?

choices.text: Catt's campaigns and Paul's protests created combined pressure
choices.textEs: Se opuso al sufragio femenino como conservadora sureña prominente

choices.text: She founded Nashville's suffrage league and secured Tennessee's vote
choices.textEs: Fundó la liga de sufragio de Nashville y aseguró el voto de Tennessee

choices.text: The 19th Amendment doubled the electorate and changed politics
choices.textEs: Organizó la Convención de Seneca Falls en el estado de Nueva York

choices.text: They fought for suffrage but often faced racism within the movement itself
choices.textEs: Sirvió como la primera mujer electa al Congreso de EE.UU.

items.explanation: Anne Dallas Dudley was important because she helped organize Tennessee suffrage activism and build support in the state that became the crucial “Perfect 36.” A choice saying she led militant prison protests is wrong because that role fits Alice Paul more closely. Her work shows how state-level organizing was essential to winning a national amendment.
items.explanationEs: Anne Dallas Dudley, una dama de sociedad de Nashville, fundó la Liga de Sufragio Igual de Nashville y usó sus conexiones sociales para presionar por el sufragio. Sus esfuerzos fueron cruciales para asegurar el voto de Tennessee como el 36º estado en ratificar la 19ª Enmienda.

items.stem: What caused Harry Burn to change his vote and ratify the 19th Amendment in Tennessee?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué causó que Harry Burn cambiara su voto y ratificara la 19ª Enmienda en Tennessee?

choices.text: Women's wartime contributions made denying them the vote increasingly unjustifiable
choices.textEs: Recibió un soborno de líderes sufragistas

choices.text: Paul used militant tactics like hunger strikes and picketing the White House
choices.textEs: Siempre apoyó el sufragio pero fue presionado para votar en contra

choices.text: They fought for suffrage but often faced racism within the movement itself
choices.textEs: Fue amenazado con ser destituido

choices.text: He received a letter from his mother urging him to "be a good boy" and vote for suffrage
choices.textEs: Recibió una carta de su madre instándolo a "ser un buen chico" y votar por el sufragio

items.explanation: Harry Burn changed his vote after receiving a letter from his mother urging him to support ratification, and his switch helped Tennessee approve the 19th Amendment. A choice about federal court intervention is wrong because the decisive moment came from a legislative vote, not a court order. This famous episode shows how a single vote can change constitutional history.
items.explanationEs: El joven legislador Harry Burn cambió su voto después de recibir una carta de su madre, Phoebe Burn, quien escribió: "No olvides ser un buen chico y ayudar a la Sra. Catt a poner la 'rata' en ratificación." Su voto hizo de Tennessee el crucial 36º estado.

items.stem: What was the outcome of the Homestead Strike of 1892?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue el resultado de la Huelga de Homestead de 1892?

choices.text: A bomb killed police officers, turning public opinion against labor unions
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores ganaron salarios más altos y reconocimiento sindical

choices.text: Carnegie argued the wealthy had a duty to benefit society through giving
choices.textEs: El gobierno federal se puso del lado de los trabajadores

choices.text: Industrialization created demand for labor, attracting massive immigration
choices.textEs: Andrew Carnegie acordó negociar con el sindicato

choices.text: The strike was crushed after Pinkerton agents and state militia were used
choices.textEs: La huelga fue aplastada después de que se usaron agentes de Pinkerton y la milicia estatal

items.explanation: The Homestead Strike at Carnegie Steel ended in defeat for the union after violent clashes with Pinkerton guards and state militia intervention. A choice saying workers won recognition is wrong because the strike strengthened management and weakened union power at Homestead. It became one of the most famous examples of labor’s setbacks in the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: La Huelga de Homestead en Carnegie Steel fue suprimida violentamente. Después de una batalla mortal con detectives de Pinkerton que mató a trabajadores de ambos lados, se llamó a la Guardia Nacional de Pensilvania. El sindicato fue destruido y los salarios fueron reducidos.

items.stem: Why was the Great Railroad Strike of 1877 significant in American labor history?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué fue significativa la Gran Huelga Ferroviaria de 1877 en la historia laboral estadounidense?

choices.text: Labor sought social improvements including education and justice
choices.textEs: Llevó al reconocimiento sindical inmediato por todos los ferrocarriles

choices.text: The government sided with business using troops and court orders
choices.textEs: Resultó en la primera ley federal de salario mínimo

choices.text: It was the first nationwide strike showing mass organizing power
choices.textEs: Fue la primera huelga nacional y mostró que los trabajadores podían organizarse a través de industrias

choices.text: a setback for the labor movement due to public fear of radicalism
choices.textEs: Se resolvió pacíficamente a través de negociación

items.explanation: The Great Railroad Strike of 1877 was significant because it was the first major nationwide labor uprising, and it showed how quickly strikes could spread across the industrial economy. A choice saying it ended with a major union victory is wrong because federal troops and militia helped suppress it. The strike revealed growing class tension in post-Civil War America.
items.explanationEs: La Gran Huelga Ferroviaria de 1877 fue la primera huelga nacional en la historia de EE.UU. Comenzó cuando las compañías ferroviarias recortaron salarios durante una depresión. Se extendió a múltiples estados y mostró que los trabajadores podían organizarse a escala masiva, aunque se usaron tropas federales para suprimirla.

items.stem: How did the Haymarket Affair of 1886 impact the labor movement?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo impactó el Asunto de Haymarket de 1886 al movimiento laboral?

choices.text: It was the first federal law attempting to restrict monopolies
choices.textEs: Fortaleció el apoyo público a los sindicatos y llevó a reformas inmediatas

choices.text: It damaged labor by linking unions with anarchism and violence
choices.textEs: Dañó el movimiento laboral al asociar sindicatos con anarquismo y violencia

choices.text: The wealthy achieved success through their natural superiority
choices.textEs: No tuvo impacto significativo en la opinión pública

choices.text: They accepted all workers regardless of skill, race, or gender
choices.textEs: Llevó a la aprobación inmediata de la ley de jornada de ocho horas

items.explanation: The Haymarket Affair damaged the labor movement because a bomb thrown at a workers’ rally in Chicago led many Americans to associate unions with violence and radicalism. A choice saying it immediately strengthened public support for unions is wrong because the event sparked fear and backlash instead. It became a turning point in how labor activism was viewed in the late 1800s.
items.explanationEs: Cuando una bomba explotó en un mitin laboral en la Plaza Haymarket de Chicago, matando a oficiales de policía, el público se volvió contra los sindicatos. Ocho anarquistas fueron condenados (algunos ejecutados) a pesar de evidencia débil. El incidente retrasó el movimiento laboral por años.

items.stem: What triggered the Pullman Strike of 1894?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué desencadenó la Huelga Pullman de 1894?

choices.text: Workers demanded stock ownership options in the company
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores exigieron opciones de acciones en la compañía

choices.text: Railroad companies refused to hire any immigrant workers
choices.textEs: Las compañías ferroviarias se negaron a contratar trabajadores inmigrantes

choices.text: Pullman cut wages but kept rents the same in his town
choices.textEs: George Pullman recortó salarios pero no los alquileres en su ciudad empresarial

choices.text: Workers protested against new machinery replacing their jobs
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores protestaron contra el uso de nueva maquinaria

items.explanation: The Pullman Strike began after George Pullman cut workers’ wages during the depression of 1893 but did not lower rents in the company town where many employees lived. Choice A is wrong because workers were not demanding stock ownership; they were protesting wage cuts and living costs. Choice D is wrong because the immediate issue was not new machinery but the unfair treatment of Pullman workers. The strike highlighted the power imbalance between industrial employers and labor.
items.explanationEs: Durante la depresión de 1893, George Pullman recortó los salarios de los trabajadores en un 25% pero mantuvo los alquileres en su ciudad empresarial iguales. Los trabajadores que vivían en el pueblo de Pullman no tenían más opción que pagar estos altos alquileres, lo que llevó a la huelga.

items.stem: How did the federal government respond to the Pullman Strike?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo respondió el gobierno federal a la Huelga Pullman?

choices.text: It used court injunctions and troops to break the strike
choices.textEs: Usó mandatos judiciales y tropas federales para romper la huelga

choices.text: It negotiated a fair compromise between workers and owners
choices.textEs: Negoció un compromiso entre trabajadores y la compañía

choices.text: It nationalized the railroad industry to end the conflict
choices.textEs: Nacionalizó la industria ferroviaria para terminar la disputa

choices.text: It passed new labor protection laws that favored workers
choices.textEs: Aprobó nuevas leyes de protección laboral favoreciendo a los trabajadores

items.explanation: The federal government used a court injunction and then sent troops to break the Pullman Strike, claiming it had to keep the mail moving and interstate commerce open. A choice about supporting collective bargaining is wrong because Washington intervened against the strike, not for the workers. This response set a pattern of federal support for business during labor conflicts.
items.explanationEs: El presidente Grover Cleveland obtuvo un mandato judicial federal contra la huelga, alegando que interfería con la entrega de correo. Cuando los huelguistas se negaron a cumplir, envió tropas federales a Chicago. Eugene Debs fue encarcelado por violar el mandato.

items.stem: How did the American Federation of Labor (AFL) differ from the Knights of Labor in its approach to organizing?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo difería la Federación Americana del Trabajo (AFL) de los Caballeros del Trabajo en su enfoque de organización?

choices.text: A combination of companies organized to dominate an entire industry
choices.textEs: La AFL organizaba a todos los trabajadores; los Caballeros solo a artesanos calificados

choices.text: A conflict between miners and the state over convict labor in mines
choices.textEs: Ambas organizaciones tenían requisitos de membresía idénticos

choices.text: The AFL focused on skilled crafts; the Knights welcomed all workers
choices.textEs: La AFL se enfocaba en sindicatos de oficios calificados; los Caballeros daban la bienvenida a todos

choices.text: It accepted all workers regardless of race, gender, or skill level
choices.textEs: La AFL buscaba derrocar el capitalismo; los Caballeros no

items.explanation: The AFL focused mainly on skilled craft workers, while the Knights of Labor tried to include a much broader group of workers, including many unskilled laborers. Choice D is wrong because that broad membership policy describes the Knights more than the AFL. Choices A and B are wrong because they refer to a trust and the Coal Creek conflict, not union organizing strategies. The difference helps explain why the AFL became more stable while the Knights declined.
