items.explanationEs: La AFL, bajo Samuel Gompers, organizaba a trabajadores de oficios calificados (como carpinteros, cigarreros) y se enfocaba en metas prácticas como salarios y horas. Los Caballeros del Trabajo eran más inclusivos, aceptando trabajadores no calificados, mujeres y afroamericanos.

items.stem: Based on this passage, what does Gompers suggest about the broader goals of the labor movement?
items.stemEs: Basándose en este pasaje, ¿qué sugiere Gompers sobre los objetivos más amplios del movimiento laboral?

choices.text: It was the first nationwide strike showing mass organizing power
choices.textEs: El trabajo solo quería salarios más altos y horas más cortas

choices.text: The government sided with business using troops and court orders
choices.textEs: El trabajo no tenía interés en reformas sociales más allá de asuntos laborales

choices.text: a setback for the labor movement due to public fear of radicalism
choices.textEs: El trabajo quería derrocar el sistema capitalista por completo

choices.text: Labor sought social improvements including education and justice
choices.textEs: El trabajo buscaba mejoras sociales incluyendo educación y justicia

items.explanation: Gompers argued that labor was fighting not only for better pay but also for dignity, independence, and a fairer share of the wealth workers created. A choice reducing the movement to short-term wages alone is wrong because labor leaders often framed unionism as a struggle for human rights and citizenship. This broadened the meaning of labor activism beyond the workplace.
items.explanationEs: Gompers describió los objetivos del trabajo como más amplios que solo salarios—queriendo "más escuelas y menos cárceles," "más aprendizaje y menos vicio," y "más justicia y menos venganza." Esto muestra que el movimiento buscaba mejoras sociales generales.

items.stem: Why did labor unions oppose the convict lease system during this era?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué los sindicatos se oponían al sistema de arrendamiento de convictos durante esta era?

choices.text: They believed prisoners should not receive any form of training
choices.textEs: Creían que los prisioneros no deberían recibir ningún entrenamiento laboral

choices.text: Convict labor undercut free workers' wages and broke strikes
choices.textEs: El trabajo de convictos se usaba para socavar los salarios de trabajadores libres y romper huelgas

choices.text: Prisoners were treated too well compared to factory laborers
choices.textEs: Los prisioneros eran tratados demasiado bien en comparación con los trabajadores de fábricas

choices.text: Convict labor was more expensive than hiring any free workers
choices.textEs: El trabajo de convictos era más caro que contratar trabajadores libres

items.explanation: Labor unions opposed convict leasing because employers could use prison labor to replace free workers, drive down wages, and weaken bargaining power. A choice saying unions objected only for humanitarian reasons is incomplete because the system also directly threatened workers’ economic security. The issue connected labor conflict to race, punishment, and the post-Reconstruction South.
items.explanationEs: Las compañías usaban trabajo de convictos para socavar salarios y reemplazar trabajadores en huelga. En la Guerra de Coal Creek, los dueños de minas de Tennessee trajeron trabajadores convictos cuando los mineros libres exigieron mejores condiciones, provocando conflicto armado hasta que el sistema de arrendamiento de convictos fue abolido.

items.stem: What is collective bargaining, and why was it important to labor unions?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué es la negociación colectiva, y por qué era importante para los sindicatos?

choices.text: Individual workers negotiating separate contracts on their own
choices.textEs: Trabajadores individuales negociando contratos separados con empleadores

choices.text: Government officials setting wages for all workers equally
choices.textEs: Funcionarios del gobierno fijando salarios para todos los trabajadores

choices.text: Workers negotiating as a group for more bargaining power
choices.textEs: Trabajadores negociando como grupo para tener más poder contra los empleadores

choices.text: Employers setting wages based only on market supply forces
choices.textEs: Empleadores fijando salarios basados solo en condiciones del mercado

items.explanation: Collective bargaining is the process in which workers act as a group through a union to negotiate wages, hours, and working conditions with employers. A choice about individual contracts is wrong because collective bargaining depends on workers negotiating together for greater leverage. It became one of the most important principles of organized labor.
items.explanationEs: La negociación colectiva significa que los trabajadores negocian salarios, horas y condiciones como grupo en lugar de individualmente. Esto daba a los trabajadores más poder porque los empleadores no podían simplemente despedir a un trabajador y contratar a otro—enfrentarían a toda la fuerza laboral.

items.stem: What distinguished the Industrial Workers of the World (IWW) from other labor organizations?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué distinguía a los Trabajadores Industriales del Mundo (IWW) de otras organizaciones laborales?

choices.text: They only organized skilled craftsmen in the same way as the AFL
choices.textEs: Solo organizaban artesanos calificados como la AFL

choices.text: They pushed revolutionary unionism and welcomed all workers
choices.textEs: Abogaban por el sindicalismo industrial revolucionario y daban la bienvenida a todos los trabajadores

choices.text: They cooperated closely with business owners for mutual gain
choices.textEs: Cooperaban estrechamente con los dueños de negocios

choices.text: They focused exclusively on electoral politics and campaigns
choices.textEs: Se enfocaban exclusivamente en la política electoral

items.explanation: The IWW differed from more conservative unions because it aimed to organize all workers, including the unskilled, into one big union and often used a more radical language of class struggle. A choice describing skilled craft unionism is wrong because that better fits the AFL. The IWW represented the most militant wing of early 20th-century labor activism.
items.explanationEs: Los IWW ("Wobblies"), fundados en 1905, abogaban por el sindicalismo industrial revolucionario—organizando a todos los trabajadores en un gran sindicato para eventualmente tomar control de la industria. Daban la bienvenida a trabajadores inmigrantes, mujeres y minorías que otros sindicatos excluían.

items.stem: How did the Social Gospel movement differ from Social Darwinism?
items.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferenciaba el movimiento del Evangelio Social del darwinismo social?

choices.text: The Social Gospel argued that Christians had a duty to address poverty and injustice
choices.textEs: El Evangelio Social argumentaba que los cristianos tenían el deber de abordar la pobreza y la injusticia

choices.text: Corrupt political organizations that controlled city governments through patronage
choices.textEs: Ambos movimientos apoyaban el capitalismo sin restricciones ni regulación

choices.text: It provided a scientific-sounding justification for inequality and opposing regulation
choices.textEs: El Evangelio Social promovía la idea de que los pobres eran naturalmente inferiores

choices.text: requiring merit-based examinations for federal jobs instead of political patronage
choices.textEs: Ambos movimientos se oponían a la inmigración y favorecían políticas nativistas

items.explanation: The Social Gospel movement taught that Christians should fight poverty and injustice through reform, while Social Darwinism treated inequality as a natural result of competition. A choice that says both movements opposed aid to the poor is wrong because Social Gospel reformers supported settlement houses, labor reform, and charity. This debate reflected a larger argument over whether modern industrial society should be shaped by competition or social responsibility.
items.explanationEs: El movimiento del Evangelio Social, liderado por ministros como Walter Rauschenbusch, argumentaba que el cristianismo requería acción social para abordar la pobreza y la injusticia—oponiéndose directamente al enfoque de no intervención del darwinismo social.

items.stem: Why did farmers support the free coinage of silver during the Populist era?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué los agricultores apoyaron la acuñación libre de plata durante la era populista?

choices.text: Fighting unfair railroad rates and business practices that hurt farmers
choices.textEs: Las monedas de plata eran más duraderas y duraban más que las de oro

choices.text: Increasing the money supply would raise crop prices and ease their debts
choices.textEs: Aumentar la oferta monetaria elevaría los precios de los cultivos y aliviaría sus deudas

choices.text: An immigration processing station for Asian arrivals on the West Coast
choices.textEs: La minería de plata era la ocupación principal de la mayoría de los agricultores

choices.text: was the first federal law to restrict immigration based on nationality
choices.textEs: El patrón oro ya había sido abolido por el Congreso en ese momento

items.explanation: Populists supported bimetallism and free silver because adding silver to the money supply would create inflation, making debts easier for farmers to repay and raising crop prices. A choice saying farmers wanted a stronger gold standard is wrong because tight money usually helped creditors, not debtors. Monetary policy became one of the biggest political battles of the 1890s.
items.explanationEs: Los agricultores estaban ahogados en deudas por la caída de los precios de los cultivos. Aumentar la oferta monetaria mediante la acuñación de plata causaría inflación, haciendo sus deudas más fáciles de pagar y elevando los precios que recibían por los cultivos.

items.stem: What was the significance of William Jennings Bryan's "Cross of Gold" speech?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue la importancia del discurso "Cruz de Oro" de William Jennings Bryan?

choices.text: Economic fears that Chinese immigrants would take American jobs
choices.textEs: Ganó a Bryan la presidencia en la elección de 1896 contra McKinley

choices.text: It rallied Populist and Democratic support for free silver coinage
choices.textEs: Unió el apoyo populista y demócrata para la acuñación libre de plata

choices.text: More money in circulation would raise crop prices and ease debt
choices.textEs: Convenció al Congreso de adoptar inmediatamente el estándar de plata

choices.text: An immigration processing station for Asian arrivals on the West Coast
choices.textEs: Marcó el fin del movimiento populista en la política estadounidense

items.explanation: William Jennings Bryan’s “Cross of Gold” speech attacked the gold standard and argued that ordinary people should not be sacrificed to the interests of bankers and creditors. A choice saying Bryan defended gold is wrong because he wanted free silver to increase the money supply. The speech became the most famous statement of Populist-era monetary protest.
items.explanationEs: El discurso "Cruz de Oro" de Bryan en 1896 electrizó la convención demócrata al defender la plata libre y los agricultores comunes contra los intereses bancarios del este. Aunque perdió la elección, galvanizó el apoyo populista.

items.stem: How did John D. Rockefeller use horizontal integration to dominate the oil industry?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo usó John D. Rockefeller la integración horizontal para dominar la industria petrolera?

choices.text: By buying oil wells, refineries, and pipelines at every production stage
choices.textEs: Comprando pozos, refinerías y oleoductos en cada etapa de producción

choices.text: By buying out or undercutting competing oil refining companies
choices.textEs: Comprando o subcotizando a empresas competidoras de refinación de petróleo

choices.text: By investing in new technologies to replace oil with electricity
choices.textEs: Invirtiendo en nuevas tecnologías para reemplazar el petróleo con electricidad

choices.text: By forming cooperative agreements with all oil workers' unions
choices.textEs: Formando acuerdos cooperativos con todos los sindicatos de trabajadores petroleros

items.explanation: Rockefeller expanded Standard Oil mainly through horizontal integration, buying or forcing out competing oil refineries until one company dominated the market. A choice about controlling every stage of production is wrong because that describes vertical integration, not Rockefeller’s main method. This strategy helped create one of the most famous monopolies of the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: Rockefeller usó la integración horizontal—comprando o destruyendo competidores al mismo nivel de producción—para controlar más del 90% de la industria de refinación de petróleo a través de Standard Oil.

items.stem: How did the Triangle Shirtwaist fire lead to changes in labor laws?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo llevó el incendio de Triangle Shirtwaist a cambios en las leyes laborales?

choices.text: It resulted in new workplace safety regulations including fire codes and inspections
choices.textEs: Resultó en nuevas regulaciones de seguridad laboral incluyendo códigos de incendio e inspecciones

choices.text: Because families, businesses, and courts all had reasons to resist reform
choices.textEs: Llevó al Congreso a prohibir todo el trabajo fabril para mujeres permanentemente

choices.text: The Social Gospel argued that Christians had a duty to address poverty and injustice
choices.textEs: No tuvo impacto duradero en leyes laborales o regulaciones de fábricas

choices.text: He believed natural resources should be managed by the government for the public good
choices.textEs: Obligó a todas las fábricas a cerrar inmediatamente durante un año

items.explanation: The Triangle Shirtwaist Fire of 1911 killed 146 workers, many of them young immigrant women, and led to stronger factory safety laws and inspections in New York. A choice about trust regulation is wrong because the fire exposed unsafe working conditions, not monopoly practices. The disaster became a turning point in the movement for workplace reform.
items.explanationEs: El incendio provocó indignación pública y llevó a 36 nuevas leyes en el estado de Nueva York, incluyendo requisitos para escaleras de incendio, sistemas de rociadores, horas máximas de trabajo e inspecciones de edificios.

items.stem: How did Lincoln Steffens' work "The Shame of the Cities" contribute to Progressive reform?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo contribuyó la obra "La Vergüenza de las Ciudades" de Lincoln Steffens a la reforma progresista?

choices.text: It exposed urban political corruption and machine politics, fueling demand for reform
choices.textEs: Expuso la corrupción política urbana y la política de máquinas, alimentando la demanda de reforma

choices.text: Expanding democratic participation reduces corruption and increases accountability
choices.textEs: Documentó el crecimiento de los suburbios y patrones de migración rural

choices.text: It led directly to passage of food safety laws like the Pure Food and Drug Act
choices.textEs: Elogió a los gobiernos de las ciudades por su gestión eficiente de los recursos

choices.text: He believed natural resources should be managed by the government for the public good
choices.textEs: Se enfocó únicamente en mejorar los sistemas de transporte público

items.explanation: Lincoln Steffens used The Shame of the Cities to show how business interests and political machines corrupted city governments. A choice about meatpacking or child labor is wrong because Steffens focused on municipal corruption, not factories or food safety. His reporting strengthened the Progressive belief that democracy needed honest and efficient government.
items.explanationEs: Steffens expuso las alianzas corruptas entre políticos y empresas en las principales ciudades, mostrando cómo las máquinas políticas como Tammany Hall estafaban a los contribuyentes y subvertían la democracia.

items.stem: How did the Pure Food and Drug Act and Meat Inspection Act reflect Progressive goals?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo reflejaron la Ley de Alimentos y Drogas Puras y la Ley de Inspección de Carne los objetivos progresistas?

choices.text: They showed government protecting consumers from unsafe products
choices.textEs: Mostraron al gobierno protegiendo a los consumidores de productos inseguros

choices.text: He forced negotiations and became first president to back workers
choices.textEs: Eliminaron toda regulación gubernamental de la industria alimentaria

choices.text: Good trusts were efficient and fair; bad trusts abused their power
choices.textEs: Se enfocaron en aumentar las ganancias de las empresas de empaquetado de carne

choices.text: Helpful because it restored fair competition for consumers
choices.textEs: Se aprobaron para beneficiar solo a consumidores adinerados en las ciudades

items.explanation: The Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906 responded to public outrage over unsafe and mislabeled products by requiring more honest labeling and federal oversight. A choice about railroad rates is wrong because the law dealt with consumer protection, not transportation regulation. It marked a major step toward the modern regulatory state.
items.explanationEs: Estas leyes de 1906, provocadas por "La Selva" de Upton Sinclair, requirieron etiquetado preciso de alimentos y medicamentos e inspección federal de carne. Representaban la creencia progresista de que el gobierno debía proteger a los ciudadanos.

items.stem: Why was Theodore Roosevelt called a "trust-buster"?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué se llamaba a Theodore Roosevelt un "destructor de fideicomisos"?

choices.text: He used the Sherman Antitrust Act to sue large monopolies like Northern Securities
choices.textEs: Usó la Ley Antimonopolio Sherman para demandar a grandes monopolios como Northern Securities

choices.text: He believed natural resources should be managed by the government for the public good
choices.textEs: Personalmente administraba el fideicomiso más grande en Estados Unidos

choices.text: A domestic program promising fairness for workers, consumers, and businesses
choices.textEs: Creó nuevos fideicomisos para competir con los monopolios existentes

choices.text: Expanding democratic participation reduces corruption and increases accountability
choices.textEs: Abolió todas las formas de corporaciones comerciales durante su presidencia

items.explanation: Roosevelt was called a trust-buster because he used the Sherman Antitrust Act against companies like Northern Securities when he believed they abused economic power. A choice saying he opposed all corporations is wrong because he accepted large firms he thought served the public fairly. His actions expanded federal authority over big business.
items.explanationEs: Roosevelt ganó el apodo de "destructor de fideicomisos" al presentar demandas antimonopolio contra monopolios poderosos. Su caso más famoso fue contra Northern Securities Company (1902), un fideicomiso ferroviario controlado por J.P. Morgan.

items.stem: How did President Wilson's "New Freedom" program differ from Roosevelt's approach?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo se diferenció el programa "Nueva Libertad" del Presidente Wilson del enfoque de Roosevelt?

choices.text: Wilson wanted to break up monopolies entirely, while Roosevelt preferred regulating them
choices.textEs: Wilson quería desmantelar los monopolios por completo, mientras Roosevelt prefería regularlos

choices.text: He received a letter from his mother urging him to "be a good boy" and vote for suffrage
choices.textEs: Wilson se oponía a toda regulación gubernamental mientras Roosevelt la apoyaba

choices.text: It clarified illegal business practices and exempted labor unions from antitrust suits
choices.textEs: Wilson se enfocó exclusivamente en política exterior mientras Roosevelt se enfocó en doméstica

choices.text: It provided a scientific-sounding justification for inequality and opposing regulation
choices.textEs: Wilson y Roosevelt tenían plataformas y políticas progresistas idénticas

items.explanation: Wilson’s New Freedom originally sought to restore competition by breaking up concentrated power, while Roosevelt was more willing to regulate large corporations he considered useful. A choice saying Wilson opposed reform is wrong because he backed major legislation like the Federal Reserve Act and FTC. The difference shows that Progressives shared goals but not always methods.
items.explanationEs: La Nueva Libertad de Wilson buscaba eliminar monopolios y restaurar la competencia, mientras el Nuevo Nacionalismo de Roosevelt aceptaba grandes corporaciones pero quería una fuerte regulación gubernamental.

items.stem: How did Alice Paul's tactics differ from those of the mainstream suffrage movement?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo se diferenciaban las tácticas de Alice Paul de las del movimiento sufragista convencional?

choices.text: They fought for suffrage but often faced racism within the movement itself
choices.textEs: Paul se enfocó en cabildeo silencioso mientras otros organizaban marchas públicas

choices.text: Paul used militant tactics like hunger strikes and picketing the White House
choices.textEs: Paul usó tácticas militantes como huelgas de hambre y piquetes en la Casa Blanca

choices.text: Women's wartime contributions made denying them the vote increasingly unjustifiable
choices.textEs: Paul se oponía al sufragio femenino y abogaba por otros derechos de las mujeres

choices.text: She founded Nashville's suffrage league and secured Tennessee's vote
choices.textEs: Paul trabajó exclusivamente a través del Partido Demócrata para el cambio

items.explanation: Alice Paul differed from mainstream suffrage leaders by using confrontational tactics such as picketing, civil disobedience, and hunger strikes to pressure the federal government directly. A choice focused on quiet state-by-state lobbying is wrong because that was the more moderate NAWSA approach. Her methods intensified the final push for the 19th Amendment.
items.explanationEs: Alice Paul y el Partido Nacional de la Mujer usaron tácticas militantes incluyendo piquetes en la Casa Blanca, huelgas de hambre en prisión y desobediencia civil—más confrontacionales que el enfoque de cabildeo de las sufragistas convencionales.

items.stem: What role did African American women play in the suffrage movement?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué papel desempeñaron las mujeres afroamericanas en el movimiento sufragista?

choices.text: Paul used militant tactics like hunger strikes and picketing the White House
choices.textEs: Fueron incluidas igualmente en todas las organizaciones sufragistas desde el inicio

choices.text: They fought for suffrage but often faced racism within the movement itself
choices.textEs: Lucharon por el sufragio pero a menudo enfrentaron racismo dentro del movimiento mismo

choices.text: She founded Nashville's suffrage league and secured Tennessee's vote
choices.textEs: Se opusieron al sufragio femenino porque conflictuaba con la igualdad racial

choices.text: Women's wartime contributions made denying them the vote increasingly unjustifiable
choices.textEs: No tuvieron un papel significativo en el movimiento de sufragio femenino

items.explanation: African American women organized clubs, marched, spoke, and linked suffrage to racial justice, even while facing discrimination from both white society and sometimes white suffrage groups. A choice saying Black women were absent from the movement is wrong because leaders such as Ida B. Wells and Mary Church Terrell were active participants. Their role shows that the fight for the vote was also shaped by race.
items.explanationEs: Mujeres como Ida B. Wells, Mary Church Terrell y Sojourner Truth lucharon por el sufragio pero enfrentaron discriminación de sufragistas blancas que priorizaban los votos de mujeres blancas. Organizaron sus propios clubes y esfuerzos de defensa.

items.stem: What happened during the Homestead Strike of 1892?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué sucedió durante la Huelga de Homestead de 1892?

choices.text: Workers at Carnegie's steel plant clashed with Pinkerton agents hired by management
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores de la planta de acero de Carnegie chocaron con agentes de Pinkerton contratados por la gerencia

choices.text: It appeared prosperous on the surface but hid serious social problems underneath
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores ferroviarios bloquearon trenes para protestar por los bajos salarios

choices.text: Carnegie believed charity was sufficient while unions demanded structural economic change
choices.textEs: Los mineros negociaron pacíficamente salarios más altos con los dueños de las minas

choices.text: It was the first time a federal court injunction was used to break a strike
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores del gobierno fueron a la huelga contra políticas de empleo federales

items.explanation: The Homestead Strike at Carnegie Steel ended in defeat for the union after violent clashes with Pinkerton guards and state militia intervention. A choice saying workers won recognition is wrong because the strike strengthened management and weakened union power at Homestead. It became one of the most famous examples of labor’s setbacks in the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: La Huelga de Homestead (1892) estalló cuando Henry Clay Frick (administrando la planta de acero de Carnegie) recortó salarios y contrató 300 agentes de Pinkerton. Una batalla mortal entre huelguistas y Pinkertons llevó a que la milicia de Pensilvania fuera llamada, aplastando al sindicato.

items.stem: Why was the Pullman Strike of 1894 significant in labor history?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué fue significativa la Huelga Pullman de 1894 en la historia laboral?

choices.text: It was the first time a federal court injunction was used to break a strike
choices.textEs: Fue la primera vez que se usó una orden judicial federal para romper una huelga

choices.text: A bomb killed police officers, turning public opinion against labor unions
choices.textEs: Resultó en la primera ley de salario mínimo nacional

choices.text: Industrialization created demand for labor, attracting massive immigration
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores ganaron todas sus demandas y recibieron aumentos salariales importantes

choices.text: the federal government would use force to break strikes affecting commerce
choices.textEs: Estableció el derecho a la negociación colectiva a nivel nacional

items.explanation: The Pullman Strike was significant because the federal government used a court injunction and then force to help break a national labor protest tied to interstate commerce. Choice B is wrong because it describes the Haymarket Affair, not Pullman. Choice C is wrong because it explains a broad trend in industrialization, not the meaning of the 1894 strike. The strike showed how often government power favored business over labor in the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: La Huelga Pullman vio a Eugene Debs liderar un boicot nacional de vagones Pullman. El gobierno federal usó una orden judicial para terminar la huelga y envió tropas para hacerla cumplir, sentando un precedente para la intervención federal contra sindicatos.

items.stem: What was the outcome of the Haymarket Square incident of 1886?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue el resultado del incidente de la Plaza Haymarket de 1886?

choices.text: Industrialization created demand for labor, attracting massive immigration
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores ganaron una jornada de 8 horas y mejores condiciones a nivel nacional

choices.text: A bomb killed police officers, turning public opinion against labor unions
choices.textEs: Una bomba mató a oficiales de policía, volteando la opinión pública contra los sindicatos

choices.text: the federal government would use force to break strikes affecting commerce
choices.textEs: Llevó a la aprobación inmediata de la Ley Antimonopolio Sherman

choices.text: It was the first time a federal court injunction was used to break a strike
choices.textEs: El gobierno aceptó todas las demandas laborales y creó nuevos sindicatos

items.explanation: The Haymarket Affair damaged the labor movement because a bomb thrown at a workers’ rally in Chicago led many Americans to associate unions with violence and radicalism. A choice saying it immediately strengthened public support for unions is wrong because the event sparked fear and backlash instead. It became a turning point in how labor activism was viewed in the late 1800s, and this question specifically highlights outcome Haymarket Square incident 1886.
items.explanationEs: En una manifestación laboral en la Plaza Haymarket de Chicago, una bomba mató a siete oficiales de policía. Ocho anarquistas fueron condenados (a pesar de evidencia débil), y el incidente fue usado para desacreditar el movimiento laboral y los Caballeros del Trabajo.

choices.textEs: Horizontal se refiere solo a ferrocarriles; vertical se refiere a petroleras

choices.text: That educated Black leaders should guide the race toward full equality

choices.text: Horizontal means buying competitors; vertical means controlling supply

items.explanation: Andrew Carnegie used vertical integration by controlling mines, rail lines, mills, and distribution so he could manage every stage of steel production. A choice describing buying out competitors is wrong because that is horizontal integration, more closely associated with Rockefeller. Vertical integration helped large firms cut costs and dominate national markets, and this question specifically highlights difference between horizontal vertical integration.
items.explanationEs: La integración horizontal significa comprar competidores en la misma industria (como Rockefeller comprando compañías petroleras rivales). La integración vertical significa controlar todas las etapas de producción desde materias primas hasta productos terminados (como Carnegie controlando minas de hierro, ferrocarriles y acererías).

A choice saying it mainly improved labor rights is wrong because the public reacted more strongly to food safety than to Sinclair’s socialist message about workers. The book showed how exposing industrial abuse could trigger federal regulation.

items.explanation: Civil service reform was seen as necessary because the spoils system filled government jobs through patronage, which encouraged corruption and unqualified appointments. A choice about extending voting rights is wrong because reformers were trying to improve administration, not change who could vote. The issue showed how reformers wanted a more efficient and professional government.
items.explanationEs: La reforma del servicio civil fue necesaria porque el sistema de botín llenó el gobierno con partidarios políticos no calificados, llevando a incompetencia, desperdicio y corrupción. El asesinato del presidente Garfield en 1881 por un buscador de empleo decepcionado conmocionó a la nación y llevó a la Ley de Servicio Civil Pendleton (1883), que requería exámenes competitivos para algunos trabajos federales. Esto comenzó el cambio del patrocinio político a la contratación basada en méritos en el gobierno.

items.explanation: Roosevelt’s trust-busting mattered most because it established that the federal government could challenge corporate power instead of simply accepting it as inevitable. items.stem: Which statement best explains the long-term significance of Theodore Roosevelt's progressive presidency?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué afirmación describe mejor explains the long-term significance of Theodore Roosevelt's progressive presidency?

choices.text: It permanently solved most conflicts between business and labor in American industrial life
choices.textEs: It permanently solved most conflicts between business and labor in American industrial life

choices.text: It established the modern precedent for an active federal government
choices.textEs: It established the modern precedent for an active gobierno federal

choices.text: It proved that presidential power was unlimited in domestic policy
choices.textEs: It proved that presidential power was unlimited in política interna

choices.text: It demonstrated that progressive reforms were incompatible with sustained American economic growth
choices.textEs: It demonstrated that progressive reforms were incompatible with sustained American economic growth

items.explanation: The long-term significance of Theodore Roosevelt's presidency is that it helped establish the modern expectation that the federal government should actively regulate business, protect consumers, and conserve resources. Choice A is wrong because conflicts between labor and business continued long after Roosevelt left office. Choice C is wrong because Roosevelt expanded presidential leadership, but he did not prove that presidential power was unlimited. His presidency became a model for later reform-minded presidents.
items.explanationEs: The long-term significance of Theodore Roosevelt's presidency is that it helped establish the modern expectation that the gobierno federal should actively regulate business, protect consumers, and conserve resources. Choice A is wrong because conflicts between labor and business continued long after Roosevelt left office. Choice C is wrong because Roosevelt expanded presidential leadership, but he did not prove that presidential power was unlimited. His presidency became a model for later reform-minded presidents.

choices.textEs: Supported only environmental conservation, not economic reform

choices.textEs: Focused on restoring competition rather than regulating big business

choices.textEs: Opposed most forms of government regulation of business

choices.text: Emphasized international affairs over domestic reform
choices.textEs: Emphasized international affairs over domestic reform

items.explanation: Wilson differed from Roosevelt because he focused more on restoring competition by breaking up concentrated power, while Roosevelt accepted many large corporations as long as they were regulated. Choice A is wrong because Wilson cared about economic reform as well as other Progressive issues. Choice C is wrong because Wilson supported strong federal action through measures like the Federal Reserve and FTC. The contrast shows two different Progressive answers to the problem of big business.

choices.text: They permanently solved all economic and environmental problems facing the nation
choices.textEs: They permanently solved all economic and environmental problems facing the nation

choices.textEs: They were quickly reversed by subsequent administrations and had minimal long-term impact on American governance

items.explanation: Wilson's domestic reforms had lasting importance because they created institutions such as the Federal Reserve and FTC that still shape banking, business regulation, and federal policy. Choice A is wrong because those reforms were not generally seen as harmful across the long term. Choice D is wrong because many of Wilson's measures remained in place instead of disappearing quickly. His presidency helped build the modern regulatory state.

choices.text: It demonstrated that women were interested only in political rather than social or economic reform

choices.text: It proved that constitutional amendments were the most effective way to secure civil rights
choices.textEs: It proved that constitucional enmiendas were the most effective way to secure derechos civiles

items.explanation: The women's suffrage movement had a long-term impact beyond winning the vote because it trained women in organizing, lobbying, protest, and public leadership. Choice A is wrong because many suffrage activists also worked on labor reform, education, and other social issues. Choice D is wrong because the 19th Amendment did not end gender inequality. The movement expanded both democracy and women's role in public life.
items.explanationEs: The women's sufragio movement had a long-term impact beyond winning the vote because it trained women in organizing, lobbying, protest, and public leadership. Choice A is wrong because many sufragio activists also worked on labor reform, education, and other social issues. Choice D is wrong because the 19th enmienda did not end gender inigualdad. The movement expanded both democracia and women's role in public life.

choices.textEs: Western states seeking rapid resource extraction vs. Eastern conservation advocates who wanted federal lands protected from development

choices.textEs: repúblicaans who embraced scientific management of federal forests and ranges vs. Democrats who opposed federal land ownership as an unconstitucional extension of central government power

items.explanation: Progressive conservation revealed a tension between preserving nature for its own sake and using resources efficiently for human benefit. A choice saying conservation had no internal disagreements is wrong because the Muir-Pinchot split was central to the movement. That tension still shapes environmental policy debates.
items.explanationEs: Progressive conservation revealed a tension between preserving nature for its own sake and using resources efficiently for human benefit. items.explanation: The campaign against child labor reflected the broader Progressive belief that government should protect vulnerable people when the market encouraged exploitation. choices.textEs: The movement's failure to establish a federal minimum wage and maximum work hours

choices.text: The movement's failure to include African Americans and its tolerance of, or support for, racial segregation
choices.textEs: The movement's failure to include African Americans and its tolerance of, or support for, racial segregación

A choice focusing only on business regulation is wrong because the deepest limitation involved who was left out of reform’s promises. This reminds us that reform movements can be powerful and exclusionary at the same time.

choices.textEs: Roosevelt's belief that Taft had betrayed progresismo by siding with conservative repúblicaans in Congreso

items.explanation: The Republican split in 1912 came from Roosevelt's belief that Taft had abandoned Progressivism and aligned too closely with conservative Republicans. Choice B is wrong because personal conflict mattered, but the break centered on real disagreements over tariffs, conservation, and reform. Choice A is wrong because foreign policy was not the main cause of the split. The division helped Wilson win and reshaped national politics during the Progressive Era.

choices.textEs: Had bribed politicians to obtain their dominant market positions through corrupt means

A choice saying they wanted exactly the same thing is wrong because their main difference was how to handle concentrated economic power. Their debate defined two major Progressive visions of political economy.

items.stemEs: The debate over whether to repeal Prohibition illustrates which broader principle?

choices.textEs: Federal laws imposed against majority preferences will eventually be repealed when enforcement costs become politically unsustainable

choices.text: Moral reform movements can achieve constitutional changes but cannot change underlying cultural practices
choices.textEs: Moral reform movements can achieve constitucional changes but cannot change underlying cultural practices

choices.textEs: constitucional enmiendas, once ratified, are virtually impossible to reverse through the political process

choices.text: Moral reform movements can achieve constitutional changes but cannot change underlying cultural practices immediately and permanently
choices.textEs: Moral reform movements can achieve constitucional changes but cannot change underlying cultural practices immediately and permanently

items.explanation: The fight over repealing Prohibition showed that reformers had to weigh moral goals against practical results when a law produced corruption, crime, and weak enforcement. A choice saying constitutional amendments are always permanent is wrong because the 21st Amendment repealed the 18th. It demonstrated that reform movements can overreach and later be reversed.
items.explanationEs: The fight over repealing Prohibition showed that reformers had to weigh moral goals against practical results when a law produced corruption, crime, and weak enforcement. choices.textEs: Federal derechos civiles enforcement agencies created by Congreso in 1875 were reactivated after WWII

choices.textEs: Southern courts became increasingly willing to apply constitucional principles to racial cases after WWI

choices.textEs: The NAACP Legal Defense Fund pursued a careful strategy of incremental litigation over four decades

choices.textEs: International pressure during the Guerra Fría forced Southern states to voluntarily reform Jim Crow

items.explanation: Jim Crow was dismantled gradually because the NAACP Legal Defense Fund used a long, carefully planned series of court cases to weaken segregation step by step. A choice saying Southern states voluntarily gave up segregation is wrong because change usually came through sustained legal and political pressure. This strategy culminated in major civil rights victories in the mid-20th century.
items.explanationEs: Jim Crow was dismantled gradually because the NAACP Legal Defense Fund used a long, carefully planned series of court cases to weaken segregación step by step. A choice saying Southern states voluntarily gave up segregación is wrong because change usually came through sustained legal and political pressure. This strategy culminated in major derechos civiles victories in the mid-20th century.

items.stem: The Coal Creek War in Tennessee was primarily a conflict over which issue?

choices.text: Federal regulation of railroad shipping
Women's suffrage in mining communities
The use of leased convict labor in coal mines
Segregation of public schools in East Tennessee

items.explanation: The Coal Creek War of 1891-1892 in Anderson County, Tennessee, began when mine operators replaced striking free miners with convicts leased from the state; armed miners freed the convicts and burned the stockades. Choice A is wrong because railroad rate regulation was a national issue handled by the Interstate Commerce Commission. Choice D is wrong because school segregation was not the dispute. The conflict helped end Tennessee's convict-lease system in 1896, one of the earliest such repeals in the South.

items.stem: How did Social Darwinism justify the enormous wealth inequality of the Gilded Age?

choices.text: It argued that wealthy individuals had a moral obligation to give away their fortunes to improve society as a whole
It applied Darwin's theory of natural selection to human society, claiming the wealthy succeeded through superior traits and that poverty was natural
It proposed that government regulation of business would accelerate economic competition and speed social progress
It maintained that only property-owning citizens had the mental capacity to govern democratic institutions effectively

items.explanation: Social Darwinism, popularized by Herbert Spencer and William Graham Sumner, applied Darwin's biological 'survival of the fittest' to economics, arguing that the wealthy were naturally superior and that poverty was the just result of individual failure — opposing government intervention to address inequality.

items.stem: How did the Social Gospel movement challenge the Social Darwinist justifications for poverty in the late 1800s?

choices.text: It applied Christian ethics to social problems, insisting that society had a collective religious duty to address poverty through reform
It argued that poverty was a sign of moral failure and that only personal religious conversion could improve the condition of the poor
It maintained that industrialists should replace political machines as the primary providers of social welfare services
It proposed that churches should invest their endowments in worker cooperatives to compete with industrial corporations

items.explanation: The Social Gospel movement, associated with figures like Walter Rauschenbusch and Jane Addams, argued that Christian teachings demanded social justice and that poverty was a structural problem requiring collective societal action — directly countering Social Darwinism's 'natural order' justification for inequality.

items.stem: Why did farmers in the late 1800s form the Granger movement and later support the Populist Party?

choices.text: Farmers organized to demand that the federal government pay direct subsidies to agricultural producers to compete with industrial wages
Farmers organized politically because rising crop prices were making agricultural land too expensive for new farmers to purchase
Farmers organized to resist the economic power of railroad monopolies, banks, and middlemen who controlled prices and transportation costs at farmers' expense
Farmers organized to oppose the influx of immigrant agricultural workers who were accepting lower wages on large commercial farms

items.explanation: Farmers faced a devastating combination of falling crop prices, high railroad freight rates, expensive credit from eastern banks, and manipulation by grain elevator operators — conditions that drove the cooperative Granger movement and the political Populist Party demanding railroad regulation and currency reform.

items.stem: How did management and government responses to labor strikes in the late 1800s typically affect workers' efforts to organize unions?

choices.text: Management and government consistently supported workers' right to strike, which strengthened union membership and collective bargaining power
Government officials mediated most major strikes through binding arbitration, which gave unions legal standing for future contract negotiations
Management responded by offering profit-sharing plans that satisfied workers' demands without the need for formal union contracts
Management used lockouts and private guards while governments deployed troops and issued court injunctions, weakening unions and suppressing strikes

items.explanation: The Pullman Strike (1894) and Homestead Strike (1892) exemplify the era's pattern: management hired Pinkerton agents and used lockouts, while the federal government secured court injunctions and sent troops to break strikes, consistently prioritizing capital over organized labor.

items.stem: How did the formation of trusts and monopolies in the late 1800s affect consumers and small businesses?

choices.text: Trusts reduced prices for consumers by achieving economies of scale that smaller businesses could not match
Trusts created employment opportunities for skilled workers by requiring specialized labor that small businesses could not afford to hire
Trusts standardized product quality across industries, benefiting consumers through more reliable and safer goods
Trusts eliminated competition, allowing large corporations to raise prices, reduce quality, and drive small businesses out of markets

items.explanation: The Sherman Antitrust Act (1890) was passed specifically because trusts used their market dominance to engage in predatory pricing against smaller competitors, fix prices for consumers, and use railroad rebates to squeeze out rivals — the opposite of competitive market benefit.

items.stem: Why were women and children a significant portion of the industrial workforce in the late 1800s and early 1900s?

choices.text: Employers hired women and children because they could be paid lower wages than men and had fewer legal protections, reducing production costs
Women and children preferred factory work because it offered more social interaction than domestic service or farm labor
Federal laws required factories to employ a minimum percentage of women and children to ensure economic opportunity for vulnerable populations
Women and children worked in factories because male workers refused to perform certain dangerous tasks, leaving those positions unfilled

items.explanation: Industrial employers specifically targeted women and children as a cheap labor supply: women earned 50-60% of male wages for identical work and children even less, with minimal legal protections — maximizing profit margins at the expense of the most vulnerable workers.

items.stem: How did muckraker journalism, as practiced by writers like Ida Tarbell and Upton Sinclair, contribute to Progressive Era reform?

choices.text: Muckrakers served as official investigators for the federal government and their findings were automatically converted into legislation
Muckrakers exposed corporate abuses and political corruption to the public, creating popular demand that made Progressive reform legislation politically possible
Muckrakers provided legal representation for workers and consumers harmed by corporate misconduct, winning landmark reform court cases
Muckrakers organized consumer boycotts of major corporations that directly forced companies to reform their practices without government intervention

items.explanation: Tarbell's exposé of Standard Oil's predatory practices and Sinclair's The Jungle horrified a mass reading public, generating the political pressure that made trust-busting and food safety legislation (Pure Food and Drug Act, 1906) not just possible but politically necessary.

items.stem: How did the goals of Samuel Gompers's American Federation of Labor (AFL) differ from the broader aims of Eugene Debs and the industrial union movement?

choices.text: Gompers focused on skilled craft workers and practical wage improvements while Debs sought to organize all workers and fundamentally restructure the economic system
Gompers advocated for the violent overthrow of industrial capitalism while Debs pursued gradual reforms through the existing political process
Gompers worked to organize unskilled immigrant workers while Debs focused exclusively on protecting the wages of native-born skilled craftsmen
Gompers supported government ownership of major industries while Debs believed workers should negotiate directly with private employers

items.explanation: The AFL under Gompers pursued 'bread and butter' unionism — better wages, hours, and conditions for already-organized skilled craft workers — while Debs envisioned industrial unionism that would unite all workers to challenge capitalism's fundamental power structure.

items.stem: How did the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire of 1911 change public attitudes toward working conditions for women and children in American factories?

choices.text: It demonstrated that factory owners voluntarily improved safety conditions when given financial incentives by state governments
It proved that the federal government already had sufficient workplace safety regulations that only needed stronger enforcement
It showed that women workers preferred factory employment despite known dangers because wages were higher than in domestic service
It revealed that dangerous conditions for women workers resulted from employer negligence and inadequate regulations, generating demand for workplace safety laws

items.explanation: The Triangle Shirtwaist fire killed 146 garment workers, mostly young immigrant women, when locked exits trapped them — graphically demonstrating the deadly consequences of inadequate workplace safety laws and generating massive public pressure for fire safety codes, labor inspection laws, and workers' compensation in New York and nationally.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Seventeenth Amendment shall not abridge the right of citizens of the United States to vote, in direct election, for their United States Senators." — 17th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, 1913

Which of the following best describes the progressive reform achieved by the 17th Amendment?

choices.text: It established term limits for U.S. Senators, preventing them from serving more than two consecutive terms.
It increased the size of the Senate by adding two senators from each newly admitted state.
It required that U.S. Senators be elected directly by the voters of each state rather than chosen by state legislatures.
It gave women the right to vote in U.S. Senate elections for the first time.

items.explanation: The 17th Amendment (1913) established the direct election of U.S. Senators by popular vote, replacing the original constitutional provision that had senators chosen by state legislatures. Progressives argued that state legislatures were corrupt and dominated by party bosses and corporate interests, and that direct election would make the Senate more responsive to the people. Option A is incorrect because the 17th Amendment changed how senators were selected, not term limits. Option B is incorrect because the Senate size is set by law, not changed by this amendment. Option D is incorrect because giving women the right to vote was the 19th Amendment (1920).

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The right of citizens of the United States to vote shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of sex." — 19th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, 1920

Which of the following best describes the long-term significance of the 19th Amendment?

choices.text: It formally recognized women as full political participants, representing the largest expansion of voting rights in American history up to that point.
It granted women the right to vote only in federal elections, leaving states free to maintain restrictions on women in state elections.
It also guaranteed women equal pay and workplace protections, transforming both political and economic rights simultaneously.
Its passage immediately led to women winning seats in Congress and state legislatures across the country in the 1920 elections.

items.explanation: The 19th Amendment (1920) granted women the right to vote, representing the culmination of more than 70 years of suffrage activism. It was the largest single expansion of voting rights in American history, doubling the eligible electorate. Its long-term significance includes the formal recognition of women as full political participants and citizens, and the beginning of women's organized political participation in American democracy. Option B is incorrect because the 19th Amendment affected federal and state elections. Option C is incorrect because women's economic rights (equal pay, workplace protections) required additional legislation. Option D is incorrect because the amendment was about voting rights, not elected office participation.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The income tax is the most just and equitable form of taxation. Each man pays according to his means, and the wealthiest bear the greatest share of the public burden." — Senator Robert La Follette, Senate Speech, 1913

Which of the following constitutional amendments established the federal income tax that La Follette is describing?

choices.text: The 14th Amendment, which established equal protection under the law for all American citizens.
The 15th Amendment, which prohibited racial discrimination in voting and tax collection.
The 17th Amendment, which provided Congress with new revenue powers to fund progressive reforms.
The 16th Amendment, which granted Congress the power to levy a federal income tax based on individual income.

items.explanation: The 16th Amendment (1913) granted Congress the power to levy a federal income tax based on income regardless of state population. This was a major progressive era reform that allowed the federal government to shift the tax burden toward the wealthy and fund expanded government programs. Option A is incorrect because the 14th Amendment (1868) dealt with citizenship and equal protection, not taxes. Option B is incorrect because the 15th Amendment (1870) dealt with voting rights for Black men. Option C is incorrect because the 17th Amendment (1913) established direct election of senators.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph, taken around 1902, shows a group of immigrants arriving at the Ellis Island immigration station in New York Harbor. The individuals carry bundles and luggage and appear to be waiting in line for processing.

(Photograph, c. 1902. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.)

Which factor BEST explains why millions of immigrants like those in this photograph traveled to the United States during this period?
items.stemEs:
Usa la fotografía para responder la pregunta.

¿Qué factor explica MEJOR por qué millones de inmigrantes viajaron a los Estados Unidos durante este período?

choices.text: The United States government actively recruited workers from European nations
Steamship companies forced passengers to relocate to America permanently
American labor unions encouraged immigration to increase their membership numbers
Economic hardship and limited opportunity in home countries combined with the promise of jobs in American industry

items.explanation: The combination of push factors (religious persecution, political instability, poverty) and pull factors (industrial jobs, economic opportunity, freedom) drove the massive wave of immigration in the late 1800s and early 1900s.
items.explanationEs: La combinación de factores de empuje y atracción impulsó la ola masiva de inmigración.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows Ida Tarbell, whose investigative reporting on Standard Oil exposed the company's monopolistic business practices.

(Photograph, c. 1904. Public Domain.)

How did the work of journalists like Ida Tarbell contribute to Progressive Era reforms?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo contribuyó el trabajo de periodistas como Ida Tarbell a las reformas de la Era Progresista?

choices.text: Their writing entertained the public but had no effect on government policy
Their exposés informed public opinion and created pressure for government regulation of big business
They worked directly with corporations to develop voluntary reform programs
Their reporting focused exclusively on political corruption and ignored economic issues

items.explanation: Tarbell's detailed exposé on Standard Oil's predatory practices helped build public support for antitrust action. Her work contributed to the 1911 Supreme Court decision to break up Standard Oil and supported broader Progressive Era efforts to regulate corporate power.
items.explanationEs: La exposición de Tarbell ayudó a construir apoyo público para la acción antimonopolio y la regulación del poder corporativo.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows the women's suffrage parade in Washington, D.C., March 3, 1913.

(Photograph, 1913. Public Domain.)

How did public demonstrations like the one shown in this photograph help advance the women's suffrage movement?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo ayudaron las manifestaciones públicas como esta a avanzar el movimiento sufragista?

choices.text: They had no impact because the public already supported women's voting rights
They convinced President Wilson to immediately sign a suffrage law
They led to violence that turned public opinion against the suffrage movement
They drew national media attention, built public sympathy, and increased political pressure on elected officials

items.explanation: The 1913 parade attracted enormous media coverage, especially after spectators attacked marchers and police failed to protect them. The resulting public outrage generated sympathy for the suffrage cause and intensified pressure on Congress to act, contributing to the eventual passage of the 19th Amendment in 1920.
items.explanationEs: El desfile atrajo cobertura mediática y generó simpatía pública que intensificó la presión sobre el Congreso.

items.stem: The creation of the National Park System in the early twentieth century reflected which broader Progressive Era goal?

choices.text: Limiting federal authority over public lands
Conserving natural resources and public lands for future generations
Promoting unrestricted commercial use of natural resources
Privatizing federally owned western territories

items.explanation: Setting aside national parks and creating a federal agency to run them expressed the Progressive conservation goal of managing natural resources and public lands in the long-term public interest rather than leaving them to unrestricted private exploitation. Choice A is wrong because the park system enlarged federal authority over public land. Choice C is wrong because conservation limited commercial use rather than promoting it without restriction. The period also revealed the split between conservationists like Gifford Pinchot, who favored managed use, and preservationists like John Muir, who favored leaving wilderness untouched.

items.stem: Why was Tennessee's ratification vote in August 1920 historically significant?

choices.text: It was the first state to ratify the 19th Amendment
It introduced a separate state-level women's suffrage amendment
It rejected the 19th Amendment, blocking its ratification
It provided the 36th and final state needed to add the 19th Amendment to the Constitution

items.explanation: Tennessee's ratification on August 18, 1920, was the thirty-sixth state approval, meeting the three-fourths requirement and putting the Nineteenth Amendment into the Constitution. Choice A is wrong because Tennessee was the last state needed, not the first to ratify. Choice C is wrong because the state approved rather than rejected the amendment. The vote turned on a single legislator, Harry Burn, who changed his position after a letter from his mother.

items.stem: How did Theodore Roosevelt's trust-busting policy differ from a complete opposition to all big business?

choices.text: Roosevelt supported breaking up all large corporations regardless of their business practices or economic impact
Roosevelt opposed all private enterprise and sought to replace major industries with government-owned public monopolies
Roosevelt's trust-busting focused exclusively on foreign corporations that competed unfairly with American domestic businesses
Roosevelt distinguished between 'good trusts' that benefited the public and 'bad trusts' that engaged in unfair practices, targeting only the latter

items.explanation: Roosevelt's 'Square Deal' framework held that large corporations were a natural economic development, but those that used their power to harm consumers, workers, or competitors warranted federal action — leading him to prosecute Northern Securities while leaving other large firms untouched.

items.stem: How did Woodrow Wilson's Federal Reserve Act of 1913 address the economic instability caused by the nation's banking system?

choices.text: It nationalized all private banks and placed them under direct federal ownership and management to prevent financial panics
It created a system of regional federal banks with a central board to regulate currency, interest rates, and banking practices
It established a flat federal tax on all bank profits to fund a national emergency financial reserve available to all states
It required all banks to back their loans with gold reserves equal to 100 percent of the money they lent to customers

items.explanation: The Federal Reserve Act created twelve regional Federal Reserve Banks overseen by a Board of Governors, giving the federal government tools to stabilize the money supply, set interest rates, and serve as a lender of last resort during banking panics — addressing the instability exposed by the Panic of 1907.

items.stem: Why was Tennessee's ratification of the 19th Amendment in 1920 described as the 'Perfect 36' moment in the women's suffrage movement?

choices.text: Tennessee's suffrage supporters won a 36-vote majority in the state legislature, overcoming a tie that had deadlocked the ratification vote for months
Tennessee became the 36th and final state needed to ratify the 19th Amendment, providing the three-fourths majority required for it to become law
Tennessee was the 36th state to introduce a women's suffrage bill in its legislature, completing a milestone in the campaign's national history
Tennessee's governor was the 36th governor to sign a state suffrage bill, meaning all states had approved women's voting in state elections

items.explanation: The U.S. Constitution requires 3/4 of states to ratify an amendment; in 1920 there were 48 states, making 36 the required threshold. Tennessee's ratification on August 18, 1920 — decided by 24-year-old legislator Harry Burn's last-minute vote change — provided exactly the 36th state needed.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The war has brought together nations of different races, creeds, and cultures, all fighting under one banner for one cause — the liberation of Europe from tyranny. The map of the world has been redrawn in blood." — Woodrow Wilson, Address to Congress, 1917

Which of the following best describes the geographic consequence of World War I referenced in this excerpt?

choices.text: The United States gained new colonial territories in Europe following the war.
European colonial empires expanded significantly into Africa and Asia after the war.
The war led to the dissolution of empires and the creation of new nations across Europe and the Middle East.
Germany was eliminated as a nation and its territory absorbed into France and Britain.

items.explanation: Wilson's reference to the map of the world being 'redrawn' points to the major territorial reorganization that followed WWI, especially in Europe and the Middle East. The dissolution of empires (Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian, German, Russian) and the creation of new nations was one of the most significant geographic consequences of the war. Option A is incorrect because the U.S. did not acquire significant overseas territory from WWI. Option B is incorrect because colonialism persisted after WWI. Option D is incorrect because Germany retained its mainland territory, losing primarily overseas colonies.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Treaty of Versailles has stripped Germany of its colonies, its merchant ships, its foreign investments, and has imposed upon it a burden of reparations which must crush its industry for generations." — John Maynard Keynes, The Economic Consequences of the Peace, 1919

Which of the following geographic changes imposed by the Treaty of Versailles does this excerpt most directly describe?

choices.text: Germany lost its overseas colonial territories, which were redistributed as League of Nations mandates.
Germany was forced to return Alsace-Lorraine to the United States.
Germany was divided into four occupation zones controlled by the Allied powers.
Germany was required to cede the Rhineland to France as a permanent territory.

items.explanation: Keynes criticizes the Versailles settlement's economic and territorial terms, specifically the loss of colonies — a major geographic consequence. Germany lost all of its overseas colonies, which were redistributed as League of Nations mandates. Option B is incorrect because Alsace-Lorraine was a continental, not colonial, territory. Option C is incorrect as Germany was not partitioned after WWI (that happened after WWII). Option D is incorrect because the Rhineland was demilitarized but remained German territory.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"Millions of men have left their villages, their farms, and their cities to fight in lands they have never seen. The trenches of France, the deserts of Mesopotamia, and the seas of the Pacific have become the new geography of this war." — British War Office Report, 1916

Based on this excerpt, which of the following best describes a geographic impact of World War I on the soldiers who fought in it?

choices.text: The war accelerated European immigration to the United States by opening new trade routes.
The war was fought across multiple distant geographic theaters, drawing soldiers far from their home regions.
The war immediately created dozens of new independent nations across Africa and Asia.
Industrial cities shrank as war production shifted from urban centers to rural factories.

items.explanation: The excerpt highlights how WWI was fought across multiple distant theaters of war — France, the Middle East (Mesopotamia), and the seas. This illustrates that the war's geographic scope pulled men from their home regions to fight in unfamiliar and distant territories across multiple continents. Option A is incorrect because immigration patterns were disrupted, not accelerated, during the war. Option C is incorrect because new nations were not yet created during the fighting itself. Option D is incorrect because industrial cities grew, not shrank, during the war.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Ottoman Empire's collapse has created a vacuum in the Middle East. The Sykes-Picot Agreement, drawn in secret, has divided Arab lands between Britain and France, drawing borders that bear no resemblance to the cultural or tribal boundaries of the people who live there." — T.E. Lawrence, 1919

Which of the following geographic consequences of WWI does this passage most directly address?

choices.text: The collapse of Austria-Hungary led to the reorganization of Balkan states under Ottoman supervision.
The United States received the territories of Palestine and Iraq as compensation for its wartime contributions.
Britain and France directly annexed all former Ottoman territories, eliminating Arab political identity.
European powers divided Middle Eastern lands according to their own interests rather than the cultural boundaries of local peoples.

items.explanation: T.E. Lawrence criticizes the Sykes-Picot Agreement, which divided former Ottoman territories in the Middle East between Britain and France without regard for the existing ethnic, religious, or tribal boundaries of the local populations. This is a direct reference to the imposition of arbitrary colonial borders on the Middle East following WWI. Option A is incorrect because Austria-Hungary, not the Ottoman Empire, controlled the Balkans. Option B is incorrect because the U.S. did not receive Middle Eastern territories. Option C is incorrect because the League of Nations mandate system, not annexation, was used.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Austro-Hungarian Empire, once a great power stretching from the Alps to the Adriatic, no longer exists. In its place, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia, Hungary, and Austria have emerged — each struggling to define its borders and its people." — Paris Peace Conference Summary, 1919

Which of the following best summarizes the geographic impact described in this excerpt?

choices.text: The collapse of the Austro-Hungarian Empire resulted in the creation of several new independent nations in Central Europe.
Germany was divided into smaller republics that replaced the dissolved Austro-Hungarian Empire.
The League of Nations took direct administrative control over the newly formed Central European states.
The Austro-Hungarian Empire merged with Russia to form the Soviet Union after the war.

items.explanation: The excerpt describes the fragmentation of the Austro-Hungarian Empire following WWI and the creation of several new states in its place. This reflects the principle of national self-determination promoted at the Paris Peace Conference, which led to the geographic reorganization of Central Europe. Option B is incorrect because Germany was not absorbed into new states. Option C is incorrect because the League of Nations did not govern Central European states directly. Option D is incorrect because Russia, not Austria-Hungary, formed the Soviet Union.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The great migration has begun. Hundreds of thousands of Black Americans are leaving the fields of Mississippi and Alabama for the factories of Chicago and Detroit, drawn by wages and the promise of freedom from Jim Crow." — Chicago Defender, 1917

Which of the following best describes the geographic change referenced in this excerpt as a consequence of World War I?

choices.text: European immigrants flooded into Southern cities to fill agricultural jobs vacated by Black farmers.
The federal government relocated Black Americans to Northern cities as part of a wartime labor mandate.
Large numbers of Black Americans migrated from the rural South to Northern industrial cities in search of economic opportunity and greater freedom.
The war caused Black Americans to leave Northern cities and return to Southern farms to meet increased agricultural demand.

items.explanation: The excerpt from the Chicago Defender describes the Great Migration — the massive movement of Black Americans from the rural South to Northern industrial cities, accelerated by WWI's demand for factory labor. This was one of the most significant internal geographic shifts in U.S. history during the WWI era. Option A is incorrect because this describes foreign immigration, not internal migration. Option B is incorrect because the military did not mandate relocation. Option D is incorrect because Black Americans moved toward, not away from, cities.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"Spain's empire in the Caribbean and the Pacific is crumbling. The United States must decide whether it will fill the vacuum created by Spanish weakness, or stand aside while other powers — Germany, Japan — move in." — Senator Henry Cabot Lodge, 1898

Which of the following best describes the imperialist argument Lodge is making in this excerpt?

choices.text: The United States should maintain strict neutrality and allow Spain's colonies to become independent.
The United States must expand its strategic presence in the Caribbean and Pacific to prevent rival powers from filling the void left by Spain.
The United States had a humanitarian obligation to liberate Spanish colonies from oppressive rule.
The United States should seek trade agreements with Spain's former colonies rather than acquiring territory.

items.explanation: Lodge's argument reflects the imperialist position that the U.S. must expand its territorial and strategic presence or risk having rival powers like Germany and Japan fill the vacuum left by Spain's declining empire. This reflects the competitive-imperialism rationale used to justify U.S. expansion in the Caribbean and Pacific following the Spanish-American War. Option A is incorrect because Lodge was advocating for expansion, not isolationism. Option C is incorrect because Lodge's argument was strategic and geopolitical, not primarily humanitarian. Option D is incorrect because Lodge wanted the U.S. to acquire territory, not simply trade rights.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"We cannot fly under the flag of anti-imperialism and then proceed to annex Puerto Rico and the Philippines. Either we are a republic that respects the rights of all peoples, or we are an empire." — Mark Twain, Anti-Imperialist League Statement, 1899

Which of the following best describes the argument made by anti-imperialists like Mark Twain?

choices.text: American imperialism contradicted the nation's founding principles of self-governance and consent of the governed.
The economic costs of maintaining overseas colonies would outweigh any commercial benefits.
The United States lacked the military strength needed to defend distant territories like the Philippines.
Colonized peoples should be given full U.S. citizenship rights before their territories could be annexed.

items.explanation: Twain and the Anti-Imperialist League argued that American imperialism contradicted the nation's founding principles of self-governance and consent of the governed. By colonizing Puerto Rico and the Philippines, the U.S. was imposing its rule on people who had not consented — the very thing the American Revolution was fought against. This was a contradiction of American democratic ideals. Option B is incorrect because Twain opposed imperialism, regardless of economic benefits. Option C is incorrect because the argument was about principles, not military capacity. Option D is incorrect because Twain was not arguing for racial segregation at home.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Pacific Ocean is the ocean of commerce and of the future. The nation that controls Hawaii controls the Pacific, and the nation that controls the Pacific controls the trade of the world." — Alfred Thayer Mahan, The Influence of Sea Power upon History, 1890

Which of the following best explains Mahan's argument for American expansion in the Pacific?

choices.text: The United States should acquire Hawaii to protect native Hawaiian peoples from European colonial powers.
The United States should remain neutral in Pacific affairs and allow Asian nations to control regional trade.
Control of strategically located territories like Hawaii was essential for naval power and dominance of global trade routes.
Hawaii's large population would provide a valuable source of workers for American industries.

items.explanation: Mahan's geostrategic argument held that national power depended on naval supremacy, and naval supremacy required overseas bases and coaling stations. Hawaii's location made it essential to control the Pacific and, through it, global trade. This argument directly influenced U.S. policy makers like Theodore Roosevelt and Henry Cabot Lodge and contributed to the annexation of Hawaii in 1898. Option A is incorrect because Mahan's argument was strategic, not humanitarian. Option B is incorrect because Mahan was advocating expansion, not neutrality. Option D is incorrect because Mahan's argument was not about immigration.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Platt Amendment gives the United States the right to intervene in Cuban affairs when necessary to preserve Cuban independence and maintain a government adequate for protecting life, property, and individual liberty." — Platt Amendment, 1901

Which of the following best describes the impact of the Platt Amendment on Cuban sovereignty?

choices.text: It formally transferred Cuban sovereignty from Spain to the United States, making Cuba an official U.S. territory.
It granted Cuba full independence and required the United States to withdraw all military forces immediately.
It required Cuba to give the United States permanent ownership of the Guantanamo Bay naval base.
It gave the United States the right to intervene in Cuban affairs, making Cuba effectively a U.S. protectorate despite nominal independence.

items.explanation: The Platt Amendment severely restricted Cuban sovereignty by giving the United States the right to intervene in Cuban affairs, requiring Cuba to lease bases to the U.S. (resulting in Guantanamo Naval Base), and limiting Cuba's ability to sign treaties or take on debt without U.S. approval. While Cuba was technically independent, the Platt Amendment made it essentially a U.S. protectorate. Option A is incorrect because Cuba gained independence from Spain, not the U.S. — the Platt Amendment restricted that independence. Option B is incorrect because the amendment actually limited Cuban freedom of action. Option C is incorrect because Guantanamo Bay was leased, not given, to the U.S.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The canal is the greatest engineering achievement in American history. It connects two oceans and transforms the geography of global trade. Ships that once had to navigate the treacherous passage around Cape Horn can now pass through in hours." — President Theodore Roosevelt, Remarks at Panama Canal, 1906

Which of the following best describes the economic and strategic significance of the Panama Canal?
