choices.text: It dramatically shortened shipping routes between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, giving the United States a major strategic and commercial advantage.
It gave Colombia control over a critical waterway, which Colombia then leased to the United States for annual payments.
It created a free international waterway that all nations could use without restriction, improving global diplomatic relations.
It restricted the U.S. Navy's ability to move ships between oceans because of its narrow width and complex lock system.

items.explanation: The Panama Canal, completed in 1914, dramatically shortened shipping routes between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, eliminating the need for the dangerous voyage around Cape Horn at the southern tip of South America. This reduced shipping times and costs, benefiting American trade and Navy. It gave the U.S. both an economic and military-strategic advantage — the Navy could move its fleet rapidly between oceans. Option B is incorrect because Colombia initially controlled the land — Panama declared independence with U.S. backing. Option C is incorrect because the Canal was not free to use. Option D is incorrect because the Canal benefited the U.S. Navy by allowing rapid fleet movement, not restricting it.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"I took the Canal Zone and let Congress debate, and while the debate goes on, the canal does also." — President Theodore Roosevelt, Lecture at University of California, 1911

Which of the following best describes the controversy surrounding Roosevelt's acquisition of the Panama Canal Zone?

choices.text: Roosevelt seized the Canal Zone from France, which had originally agreed to sell it to the United States but then backed out.
Roosevelt used U.S. taxpayer money to pay other nations to build the canal without congressional authorization.
The U.S. supported Panama's revolution against Colombia to obtain the canal rights, bypassing Colombia's rejection of the treaty.
Panama declared independence from Spain with U.S. support specifically to gain the economic benefits of the canal.

items.explanation: Roosevelt's boastful admission that he 'took' the Canal Zone without waiting for Congress refers to the U.S. role in supporting Panama's revolution against Colombia. When Colombia refused to ratify the canal treaty, the U.S. encouraged Panamanian independence, recognized Panama immediately, and signed a favorable canal treaty. Critics argued this was an illegal use of presidential power and violated Colombia's sovereignty. Option A is incorrect because France originally attempted to build the canal, not Colombia. Option B is incorrect because the canal was not paid for by other nations. Option D is incorrect because Panama gained independence from Colombia, not from Spain.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Roosevelt Corollary: In the Western Hemisphere, chronic wrongdoing may force the United States to the exercise of an international police power." — President Theodore Roosevelt, Annual Message to Congress, 1904

Which of the following best describes the significance of the Roosevelt Corollary to the Monroe Doctrine?

choices.text: It limited U.S. military intervention in Latin America by requiring congressional approval before any deployment.
It expanded the Monroe Doctrine by asserting the U.S. right to intervene militarily in Latin American countries experiencing instability or debt crises.
It extended American authority to intervene in any nation worldwide when U.S. business interests were threatened.
It replaced military intervention with a system of peaceful economic mediation to resolve Latin American disputes.

items.explanation: The Roosevelt Corollary expanded the Monroe Doctrine from a statement warning European powers to stay out of the Western Hemisphere to an assertion that the U.S. had the right — and duty — to intervene in Latin American countries that failed to maintain order or meet their financial obligations. This transformed the Monroe Doctrine from a defensive posture into an interventionist policy, justifying repeated U.S. military interventions in Central America and the Caribbean. Option A is incorrect because the Corollary expanded, not limited, U.S. intervention. Option C is incorrect because the Corollary specifically applied to the Western Hemisphere, not globally. Option D is incorrect because Roosevelt was justifying intervention, not proposing peaceful mediation.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The construction of the canal required the labor of tens of thousands of workers — Jamaicans, Barbadians, Spanish workers — in brutal tropical conditions. Yellow fever and malaria killed thousands before Dr. Gorgas brought the diseases under control." — David McCullough, The Path Between the Seas, 1977

Which of the following best describes a major challenge that had to be overcome to complete the Panama Canal?

choices.text: The engineers had to redirect four major rivers that flooded the construction site annually.
The project faced a severe labor shortage because American workers refused to work in tropical conditions.
The lack of adequate explosives technology meant engineers had to rely entirely on hand-dug excavations.
Tropical diseases, particularly yellow fever and malaria, killed thousands of workers until a mosquito eradication campaign brought them under control.

items.explanation: One of the greatest obstacles to building the Panama Canal was tropical disease — particularly yellow fever and malaria, which killed thousands of French workers in the earlier failed attempt. Dr. William Gorgas implemented a massive mosquito eradication campaign based on the theory that mosquitoes spread disease (then a new scientific understanding), which dramatically reduced the death rate and made the construction feasible. Option A is incorrect because the engineering challenge was the mountainous terrain, not river flooding (though landslides were a problem). Option B is incorrect because labor was plentiful — it was disease, not shortage of workers, that was the main challenge. Option C is incorrect because dynamite was readily available — the explosive used was a technological advance, not a limitation.

items.stem: Why were political machines able to gain power in rapidly growing cities during the Gilded Age?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué las máquinas políticas pudieron ganar poder en ciudades de rápido crecimiento durante la Edad Dorada?

choices.text: Philanthropic capitalism, where the wealthy serve as trustees for society
choices.textEs: Fueron ordenadas por enmiendas constitucionales aprobadas después de la guerra

choices.text: It began replacing the spoils system with merit-based government hiring
choices.textEs: Operaron como los gobiernos municipales más transparentes y responsables

choices.text: They provided essential services to immigrants in exchange for loyal votes
choices.textEs: Proporcionaron servicios esenciales a inmigrantes a cambio de votos leales

choices.text: To control city government and exchange services for political support
choices.textEs: No enfrentaron oposición de movimientos de reforma o partidos rivales

items.explanation: Political machines gained power in fast-growing cities because many immigrants needed jobs, housing, and help from local officials at a time when city governments provided few services. A choice claiming cities were already well managed is wrong because machine power expanded where institutions were weak and corruption was common. Their success revealed the strains that immigration and urbanization placed on American democracy.
items.explanationEs: Las máquinas políticas prosperaron porque llenaron un vacío crucial en ciudades en rápida industrialización. Con inmigración masiva y sin sistema de bienestar gubernamental, las máquinas proporcionaron servicios esenciales—trabajos, asistencia de vivienda, comida, ayuda legal—a cambio de votos. Este sistema de patrocinio era corrupto pero efectivo. Jefes como William Tweed controlaron Tammany Hall al construir lealtad entre las comunidades inmigrantes que dependían del apoyo de la máquina.

items.stem: How did the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 contradict American ideals?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo contradijo la Ley de Exclusión China de 1882 los ideales estadounidenses?
items.correctAnswer: The Chinese Exclusion Act contradicted American ideals of equality, opportunity, and "Give me your tired, your poor" immigration principles. It was the first law to ban immigration based solely on race/nationality, violating principles of equal treatment and creating a racial hierarchy that designated Chinese people as undesirable. This contradicted the American dream narrative of the U.S. as a welcoming land of opportunity for all.
items.explanation: The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 banned immigration from China on the basis of nationality, making it the first major federal law to exclude a group by race and ethnicity. A strong response should explain how that policy conflicted with ideals of equality, opportunity, and the image of the United States as a welcoming nation for immigrants, using specific evidence such as discrimination at the border or the law’s unequal treatment of Chinese laborers. This question matters because it shows how immigration policy could clash with American democratic ideals even during a period of rapid economic growth.
items.explanationEs: Las respuestas fuertes deben identificar al menos dos formas en que la ley contradijo los valores estadounidenses: igualdad, oportunidad para todos los inmigrantes, no discriminación, los ideales de la Estatua de la Libertad o el concepto de crisol de culturas. Las respuestas deben explicar la contradicción, no solo declarar hechos sobre la ley.

items.stem: Why were "robber barons" criticized despite their contributions to economic growth?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué fueron criticados los "barones ladrones" a pesar de sus contribuciones al crecimiento económico?

choices.text: They paid their workers excessive wages that hurt business profits
choices.textEs: Pagaron a sus trabajadores salarios excesivos que dañaron ganancias

choices.text: They donated too much money to charitable causes and foundations
choices.textEs: Donaron demasiado dinero a causas caritativas y fundaciones

choices.text: They built monopolies, exploited workers, and corrupted government
choices.textEs: Construyeron monopolios, explotaron trabajadores y corrompieron al gobierno

choices.text: They actively supported labor unions and collective bargaining rights
choices.textEs: Apoyaron activamente a los sindicatos y derechos de negociación colectiva

items.explanation: The label “robber barons” criticized industrialists who used ruthless tactics such as price-fixing, rebates, and political influence to build fortunes. A choice praising them only as inventors is incomplete because the term specifically pointed to exploitative business behavior. The phrase reflected public anger at the concentration of wealth during the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: Mientras los industriales como Rockefeller, Carnegie y J.P. Morgan contribuyeron al crecimiento económico, fueron llamados "barones ladrones" porque: (1) Crearon monopolios que eliminaron la competencia y fijaron precios, (2) Explotaron trabajadores con salarios bajos, largas horas y condiciones peligrosas, (3) Usaron sobornos y corrupción para influir en políticos, (4) Aplastaron sindicatos laborales violentamente, (5) Acumularon enorme riqueza mientras millones vivían en pobreza. Esta crítica llevó a las reformas de la Era Progresista.

items.stem: How did the philosophy of Social Darwinism justify both industrial capitalism and opposition to labor unions?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo justificó la filosofía del Darwinismo Social tanto el capitalismo industrial como la oposición a los sindicatos laborales?

choices.text: Ellis Island processed European immigrants more efficiently while Angel Island detained Asian immigrants longer
choices.textEs: No tuvo conexión con políticas económicas

choices.text: It states "All persons born or naturalized in the United States... are citizens" and guarantees equal protection
choices.textEs: Apoyó la regulación gubernamental de negocios y fuertes protecciones laborales

choices.text: The ideal suggested easy assimilation, but immigrants faced discrimination and formed ethnic communities
choices.textEs: Promovió la distribución equitativa de la riqueza

choices.text: It argued that economic competition was natural selection and unions interfered with survival of the fittest
choices.textEs: Argumentó que la competencia económica era selección natural y los sindicatos interferían con la supervivencia del más apto

items.explanation: Social Darwinism justified big business by claiming winners in the marketplace were naturally superior, and it opposed unions by portraying aid to weaker workers as interference with competition. A choice supporting government protection for unions is wrong because Social Darwinists usually rejected that kind of intervention. The ideology linked economic inequality to a broader defense of laissez-faire society.
items.explanationEs: El Darwinismo Social aplicó el "supervivencia del más apto" de Darwin a la economía: los empresarios exitosos eran naturalmente superiores y merecían riqueza; los pobres eran naturalmente inferiores y merecían pobreza. Esta ideología justificó: (1) Capitalismo de laissez-faire - el gobierno no debería interferir con la competencia económica natural; (2) Oposición a los sindicatos - la negociación colectiva interfería con la selección natural y recompensaba a los "no aptos"; (3) Rechazo del bienestar - ayudar a los pobres debilitaba a la sociedad al permitir que los "no aptos" sobrevivieran. Los industriales como Andrew Carnegie usaron el Darwinismo Social para defender la desigualdad extrema, aunque irónicamente Carnegie más tarde abrazó la filantropía a través de su Evangelio de la Riqueza.

items.stem: Evaluate the effectiveness of Thomas Nast's political cartoons in combating political corruption —
items.stemEs: Evalúe la efectividad de las caricaturas políticas de Thomas Nast en el combate a la corrupción política —

choices.text: They successfully exposed corruption and helped turn public opinion against corrupt officials
choices.textEs: Expusieron exitosamente la corrupción y ayudaron a cambiar la opinión pública contra los funcionarios corruptos

choices.text: Machines provided jobs and services to immigrants in exchange for political loyalty and votes
choices.textEs: Solo influyeron en estadounidenses ricos que podían comprar periódicos

choices.text: It provided a scientific-sounding justification for inequality and opposing regulation
choices.textEs: Aumentaron el apoyo a las maquinarias políticas haciéndolas parecer más poderosas

choices.text: The Social Gospel argued that Christians had a duty to address poverty and injustice
choices.textEs: Tuvieron poco impacto porque la mayoría de los estadounidenses no podían leer periódicos

items.explanation: Thomas Nast exposed Boss Tweed and Tammany Hall through powerful political cartoons in Harper’s Weekly that helped turn public opinion against corruption. A choice about labor organizing or yellow journalism is wrong because Nast was best known for anti-corruption cartoons, not union leadership or sensational newspapers. His work showed how the press could become a major force for reform during the Gilded Age and Progressive Era.
items.explanationEs: Las caricaturas de Thomas Nast en Harper's Weekly fueron muy efectivas para exponer la corrupción de Boss Tweed.

items.stem: Analyze cause and effect: What reforms resulted from "The Jungle," and why did they focus on food safety rather than labor conditions?
items.stemEs: Analice causa y efecto: ¿Qué reformas resultaron de "La Jungla" y por qué se enfocaron en la seguridad alimentaria en lugar de las condiciones laborales?

choices.text: Labor unions gained strength but food regulations were blocked
choices.textEs: Los sindicatos ganaron fuerza pero nunca resultaron regulaciones alimentarias

choices.text: The book raised awareness but Congress took no action on reform
choices.textEs: El libro aumentó la conciencia pero el Congreso no tomó acción legislativa

choices.text: Food safety laws passed because consumers feared contamination
choices.textEs: Las leyes de seguridad alimentaria pasaron porque los consumidores temían la contaminación

choices.text: Meatpacking companies voluntarily improved safety on their own
choices.textEs: Las compañías empacadoras mejoraron voluntariamente sus estándares de seguridad

items.explanation: The Jungle helped lead to food safety laws because readers were horrified by the idea of contaminated meat reaching their own tables. Choice A is wrong because the biggest immediate reforms were not union gains but the Meat Inspection Act and Pure Food and Drug Act. Choice B is wrong because Congress did take action in 1906. The response showed that consumer fear often moved lawmakers faster than concern for workers' labor conditions.
items.explanationEs: Mientras Sinclair pretendía exponer la explotación de trabajadores, el público reaccionó fuertemente a las descripciones repugnantes de contaminación de alimentos. Esto llevó a la Ley de Alimentos y Drogas Puras y la Ley de Inspección de Carne (1906). Sinclair dijo famosamente que "apuntó al corazón del público y le dio en el estómago."

items.stem: Make an argument: Was Theodore Roosevelt's trust-busting more helpful or harmful to the economy? Support your claim.
items.stemEs: Haga un argumento: ¿La disolución de trusts de Theodore Roosevelt fue más útil o dañina para la economía? Apoye su afirmación.

choices.text: He managed resources for both development and protection
choices.textEs: Dañino porque desalentó el crecimiento empresarial y la eficiencia

choices.text: Helpful because it restored fair competition for consumers
choices.textEs: Útil porque restauró la competencia y protegió a los consumidores

choices.text: They showed government protecting consumers from unsafe products
choices.textEs: Neutral porque las fuerzas del mercado solas deberían determinar la competencia

choices.text: He forced negotiations and became first president to back workers
choices.textEs: Dañino porque dio al gobierno control excesivo sobre los negocios

items.explanation: Roosevelt’s trust-busting was more helpful to many reformers because it warned corporations that the federal government could act against abuses of monopoly power. A choice saying it had no effect at all is wrong because the Northern Securities case and similar actions clearly expanded federal oversight. At the same time, the debate shows that Progressives disagreed over regulation versus unrestricted growth.
items.explanationEs: La disolución de trusts de Roosevelt, aunque controvertida, ayudó a restaurar la competencia en industrias dominadas por monopolios. Al dividir compañías como Standard Oil y Northern Securities, protegió a los consumidores del fijado de precios y dio a negocios más pequeños oportunidades de competir. Esto promovió una economía más saludable y competitiva.

items.stem: Evaluate: Which Progressive Era reform had the most significant long-term impact on American democracy?
items.stemEs: Evalúe: ¿Qué reforma de la Era Progresista tuvo el impacto más significativo a largo plazo en la democracia estadounidense?

choices.text: Catt's campaigns and Paul's protests created combined pressure
choices.textEs: La Ley Sherman Antimonopolio fue más importante que el sufragio

choices.text: She founded Nashville's suffrage league and secured Tennessee's vote
choices.textEs: La Ley de Alimentos y Drogas Puras tuvo el mayor impacto democrático

choices.text: The 19th Amendment doubled the electorate and changed politics
choices.textEs: La 19ª Enmienda duplicó el electorado y transformó la política

choices.text: To argue women's rights were as fundamental as liberty
choices.textEs: Los esfuerzos de conservación expandieron más los derechos ciudadanos

items.explanation: The 19th Amendment had an enormous long-term impact because it doubled the potential electorate and made women full participants in constitutional democracy. Choice A is wrong because it describes a suffrage strategy, not the reform itself. Choice B is wrong because Anne Dallas Dudley was important in Tennessee but did not create the broadest democratic change by herself. Expanding the electorate changed politics far beyond the Progressive Era itself.
items.explanationEs: Aunque todas las reformas progresistas fueron significativas, la 19ª Enmienda tuvo el impacto democrático más profundo. Otorgar a las mujeres el derecho al voto duplicó el electorado potencial, cambió la naturaleza de las campañas políticas y abrió caminos para la participación de las mujeres en todos los niveles de gobierno. Esto transformó fundamentalmente la democracia estadounidense.

items.stem: Analyze how the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire revealed the failures of laissez-faire policies toward workplace safety.
items.stemEs: Analice cómo el incendio de Triangle Shirtwaist reveló los fracasos de las políticas de laissez-faire hacia la seguridad laboral.

choices.text: Without oversight, owners neglected safety causing 146 deaths
choices.textEs: Sin supervisión, los propietarios descuidaron la seguridad, causando 146 muertes prevenibles

choices.text: The fire showed that government regulations were far too strict
choices.textEs: El incendio mostró que las regulaciones gubernamentales ya eran demasiado estrictas

choices.text: Excessive government interference in business caused the fire
choices.textEs: El incendio fue causado por la interferencia excesiva del gobierno en los negocios

choices.text: Existing safety regulations were adequate but poorly enforced
choices.textEs: Las regulaciones de seguridad existentes eran adecuadas pero los trabajadores las ignoraron

items.explanation: The Triangle Shirtwaist Fire of 1911 killed 146 workers, many of them young immigrant women, and led to stronger factory safety laws and inspections in New York. A choice about trust regulation is wrong because the fire exposed unsafe working conditions, not monopoly practices. The disaster became a turning point in the movement for workplace reform.
items.explanationEs: El Incendio de Triangle mostró que sin regulaciones de seguridad gubernamentales, los propietarios priorizaban las ganancias sobre la seguridad de los trabajadores. Salidas cerradas, sin rociadores y escaleras de incendios inadecuadas llevaron a 146 muertes, demostrando que el cumplimiento voluntario era insuficiente.

items.stem: Analyze the source: What argument was Eugene Debs making about the relationship between labor and capital?
items.stemEs: Analice la fuente: ¿Qué argumento estaba haciendo Eugene Debs sobre la relación entre el trabajo y el capital?

choices.text: Workers and owners should cooperate as equal partners in trade
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores y los propietarios deberían cooperar como socios iguales

choices.text: Government regulation alone can protect all workers' rights
choices.textEs: La regulación gubernamental sola puede proteger los derechos de los trabajadores

choices.text: Individual workers can succeed without any union organization
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores individuales pueden tener éxito sin organización sindical

choices.text: Workers must unite because capital is organized against them
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores deben unirse porque el capital está organizado en su contra

items.explanation: Debs argued that labor created wealth while capital controlled it, so the interests of workers and big business were fundamentally in conflict. A choice saying labor and capital naturally wanted the same things is wrong because Debs emphasized class tension, not harmony. His language reflected the growing radical critique of industrial capitalism.
items.explanationEs: Debs argumentaba que los trabajadores habían perdido batallas porque carecían de unidad, mientras que "el capital está organizado al máximo grado." Creía que solo uniéndose en "una gran organización" los trabajadores podrían lograr la "emancipación de la esclavitud asalariada."

items.stem: What was Mother Jones criticizing in her statement about the man who stole shoes versus a railroad?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué estaba criticando Mother Jones en su declaración sobre el hombre que robó zapatos versus un ferrocarril?

choices.text: The unfair justice system that punished the poor but not the rich
choices.textEs: La injusticia de un sistema de justicia que castigaba a los pobres mientras recompensaba a criminales ricos

choices.text: a setback for the labor movement due to public fear of radicalism
choices.textEs: La necesidad de leyes más estrictas contra todas las formas de robo

choices.text: An economic philosophy opposing government regulation of business
choices.textEs: La importancia de las medidas de seguridad ferroviaria

choices.text: bread-and-butter issues like wages, hours, and working conditions
choices.textEs: Su oposición al Senado de EE.UU. como institución

items.explanation: Mother Jones was a fiery labor organizer known for mobilizing miners, textile workers, and even children to protest exploitation. A choice presenting her as a business reformer is wrong because she was famous for labor activism, not corporate management. She became one of the most recognizable voices for workers in the early 1900s.
items.explanationEs: Mother Jones destacó la desigualdad de clase en el sistema de justicia—un hombre pobre va a prisión por robar zapatos, mientras que los industriales ricos que participaban en prácticas corruptas (metafóricamente "robando un ferrocarril") se convertían en senadores poderosos en lugar de enfrentar castigo.

items.stem: Analyze the pattern: How did the federal government typically respond to major strikes during the Gilded Age?
items.stemEs: Analice el patrón: ¿Cómo respondía típicamente el gobierno federal a las huelgas importantes durante la Edad Dorada?

choices.text: The government remained neutral and let disputes resolve on their own
choices.textEs: El gobierno permanecía neutral y dejaba que las disputas se resolvieran naturalmente

choices.text: The government forced businesses to negotiate with labor unions
choices.textEs: El gobierno obligaba a los negocios a negociar con los sindicatos

choices.text: The government consistently supported the workers' right to strike
choices.textEs: El gobierno consistentemente apoyaba el derecho de los trabajadores a la huelga

choices.text: The government sided with business using troops and court orders
choices.textEs: El gobierno típicamente se ponía del lado de los negocios, usando tropas y mandatos contra los huelguistas

items.explanation: The federal government usually responded to major strikes by siding with employers through injunctions, troops, and the language of law and order. A choice claiming Washington regularly protected unions is wrong because that rarely happened in the late 1800s. This pattern explains why labor organizing was so difficult during the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: Durante la Edad Dorada, el gobierno federal consistentemente intervenía a favor de los dueños de negocios. Las tropas federales rompieron la Gran Huelga Ferroviaria (1877) y la Huelga Pullman (1894). Los tribunales emitían mandatos contra los huelguistas, y líderes sindicales como Eugene Debs fueron encarcelados.

items.stem: What lasting impact did the labor movement of the Gilded Age have on American society?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué impacto duradero tuvo el movimiento laboral de la Edad Dorada en la sociedad estadounidense?

choices.text: It laid groundwork for later labor protections and reforms
choices.textEs: Sentó las bases para protecciones laborales posteriores y la jornada de ocho horas

choices.text: It had no lasting impact because all unions were fully destroyed
choices.textEs: No tuvo impacto duradero ya que todos los sindicatos fueron destruidos permanentemente

choices.text: It resulted in immediate passage of comprehensive labor laws
choices.textEs: Resultó en la aprobación inmediata de leyes laborales integrales

choices.text: It ended the use of strikes as a labor tactic going forward
choices.textEs: Terminó el uso de huelgas como táctica laboral permanentemente

items.explanation: Even though many early strikes failed, the labor movement left a lasting impact by keeping issues like hours, wages, child labor, and workplace safety in the national debate. A choice saying the movement had no legacy is wrong because later reforms built on those earlier struggles. Gilded Age labor activism helped lay the foundation for 20th-century workers’ rights.
items.explanationEs: Aunque la mayoría de las huelgas de la Edad Dorada fracasaron, el movimiento laboral estableció sindicatos, desarrolló tácticas de organización y aumentó la conciencia sobre las condiciones de los trabajadores. Esto sentó las bases para las reformas de la Era Progresista y protecciones posteriores del New Deal como la jornada de 8 horas y los derechos de negociación colectiva.

items.stem: How did Social Darwinism serve the interests of wealthy industrialists during the Gilded Age?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo sirvió el darwinismo social a los intereses de los industriales adinerados durante la Edad Dorada?

choices.text: The Social Gospel argued that Christians had a duty to address poverty and injustice
choices.textEs: Animó a los industriales a donar todas sus ganancias a la caridad

choices.text: It provided a scientific-sounding justification for inequality and opposing regulation
choices.textEs: Proporcionó una justificación de sonido científico para la desigualdad y oponerse a la regulación

choices.text: Corrupt political organizations that controlled city governments through patronage
choices.textEs: Llevó directamente a la creación de programas gubernamentales de bienestar

choices.text: requiring merit-based examinations for federal jobs instead of political patronage
choices.textEs: Promovió la distribución igualitaria de la riqueza entre todas las clases sociales

items.explanation: Social Darwinism appealed to many industrialists because it portrayed their wealth as the natural reward for superior ability and treated government regulation or labor demands as interference with progress. A choice emphasizing aid to the poor is wrong because that view fit the Social Gospel, not Social Darwinism. The idea gave moral cover to the extreme inequality of the Gilded Age.
items.explanationEs: El darwinismo social dio a los industriales una justificación pseudocientífica para la desigualdad extrema, argumentando que los ricos merecían su riqueza por superioridad natural y que la intervención gubernamental perturbaría las leyes económicas naturales.

items.stem: Why was it difficult to pass child labor laws during the Gilded Age?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué fue difícil aprobar leyes de trabajo infantil durante la Edad Dorada?

choices.text: It resulted in new workplace safety regulations including fire codes and inspections
choices.textEs: Porque los niños preferían trabajar a asistir a la escuela

choices.text: Because families, businesses, and courts all had reasons to resist reform
choices.textEs: Porque familias, empresas y tribunales todos tenían razones para resistir la reforma

choices.text: Without oversight, owners neglected safety causing 146 deaths
choices.textEs: Porque no había organizaciones que abogaran por los derechos de los niños

choices.text: Textile mills, coal mines, glass factories, and large farms
choices.textEs: Porque todos los estadounidenses creían que el trabajo infantil era moralmente aceptable

items.explanation: Child labor laws were hard to pass because many families depended on children’s wages, employers wanted cheap labor, and courts often resisted broad government regulation of the economy. A choice claiming everyone already agreed child labor was wrong is inaccurate because business interests strongly opposed reform. The fight showed the limits of Progressive reform before the New Deal.
items.explanationEs: La reforma del trabajo infantil enfrentó múltiples obstáculos: las familias pobres dependían de los salarios de los niños, los industriales dependían de mano de obra barata, los tribunales anularon leyes como interferencia inconstitucional con la libertad de contratación.

items.stem: How did Roosevelt's approach to conservation reflect Progressive values?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo reflejó el enfoque de Roosevelt hacia la conservación los valores progresistas?

choices.text: He believed natural resources should be managed by the government for the public good
choices.textEs: Creía que los recursos naturales deberían ser administrados por el gobierno para el bien público

choices.text: He used the Sherman Antitrust Act to sue large monopolies like Northern Securities
choices.textEs: Vendió todas las tierras federales a empresas privadas para desarrollo

choices.text: A domestic program promising fairness for workers, consumers, and businesses
choices.textEs: Se opuso a todas las formas de regulación gubernamental del uso de la tierra

choices.text: It exposed urban political corruption and machine politics, fueling demand for reform
choices.textEs: Creía que la conservación solo era importante para terratenientes adinerados

items.explanation: Roosevelt’s conservation policy reflected Progressive values because it used expert management and federal action to solve problems of resource waste and public stewardship. A choice saying he left all resource decisions to private companies is wrong because Roosevelt believed the national government had to act. Conservation showed how Progressives linked science, efficiency, and reform.
items.explanationEs: Roosevelt reservó 230 millones de acres de tierras públicas, creando parques nacionales, bosques y monumentos. Reflejaba la creencia progresista de que el gobierno debía administrar los recursos para todos los ciudadanos, no solo para el beneficio corporativo.

items.stem: President Theodore Roosevelt distinguished between "good trusts" and "bad trusts." Explain this distinction using specific examples, and evaluate whether this approach was effective in addressing the problems of monopoly power.
items.stemEs: El presidente Theodore Roosevelt distinguía entre "trusts buenos" y "trusts malos." Explique esta distinción usando ejemplos específicos y evalúe si este enfoque fue efectivo para abordar los problemas del poder monopólico.
items.correctAnswer: Roosevelt believed "good trusts" like U.S. Steel operated efficiently and served consumers, while "bad trusts" like Northern Securities used unfair practices to eliminate competition. He pursued selective antitrust action rather than breaking up all large corporations. This approach was partially effective — it established federal authority to regulate business — but critics argued it gave the president too much discretion and left many monopolies intact.
items.explanation: Roosevelt called some corporations “good trusts” when they operated efficiently under public oversight, but he labeled “bad trusts” as companies that crushed competition through unfair practices, as in the Northern Securities case. A strong response should use specific examples like US Steel or Northern Securities and then evaluate whether Roosevelt’s selective trust-busting actually reduced monopoly power or mainly expanded presidential authority to regulate business. This debate connects to a larger Progressive Era question about whether government should regulate big business or break it apart.
items.explanationEs: Los estudiantes deben analizar una distinción histórica, aplicarla con evidencia específica y evaluar la efectividad.

items.stem: The debate between Social Darwinism and Social Gospel in the late 19th century was fundamentally a debate about —
items.stemEs: The debate between Social Darwinism and Social Gospel in the late 19th century was fundamentally a debate about —

choices.text: The moral obligations of a society to its most vulnerable members
choices.textEs: The moral obligations of a society to its most vulnerable members

choices.text: Whether churches should support labor unions and progressive political candidates
choices.textEs: Whether churches should support sindicatos and progressive political candidates

choices.text: Whether evolution or creation explained human origins
choices.textEs: Whether evolution or creation explained human origins

choices.text: The proper interpretation of the U.S. Constitution's commerce clause
choices.textEs: The proper interpretation of the U.S. Constitución's commerce clause

items.explanation: The disagreement between Social Darwinism and the Social Gospel centered on whether society should accept inequality as natural or try to reduce it through moral action and reform. A choice limited only to church doctrine is wrong because the debate shaped views on labor, poverty, and the role of government. This conflict captured a core argument of the industrial era: competition versus reform.
items.explanationEs: The disagreement between Social Darwinism and the Social Gospel centered on whether society should accept inigualdad as natural or try to reduce it through moral action and reform. A choice limited only to church doctrine is wrong because the debate shaped views on labor, poverty, and the role of government. This conflict captured a core argument of the industrial era: competition versus reform.

items.stem: The defeat of William Jennings Bryan in 1896 marked the end of Populism as a major force because —
items.stemEs: The defeat of William Jennings Bryan in 1896 marked the end of Populism as a major force because —

choices.text: Bryan's free silver platform was too economically radical for the majority of American voters, who were persuaded by Republican sound-money arguments
choices.textEs: Bryan's free silver platform was too economically radical for the majority of American voters, who were persuaded by repúblicaan sound-money arguments

choices.text: Populist leaders in Kansas and Georgia were arrested and prosecuted for organizing farmers' boycotts and cooperative marketing schemes against railroad interests
choices.textEs: Populist leaders in Kansas and Georgia were arrested and prosecuted for organizing farmers' boycotts and cooperative marketing schemes against railroad interests

choices.text: Northern industrial workers did not share farmers' interest in inflation, and McKinley's Republicans successfully portrayed Bryan's silver campaign as a threat to factory wages and urban living standards
choices.textEs: Northern industrial workers did not share farmers' interest in inflación, and McKinley's repúblicaans successfully portrayed Bryan's silver campaign as a threat to factory wages and urban living standards

choices.text: The Supreme Court ruled key Populist economic proposals — including the subtreasury plan and railroad rate regulations — unconstitutional infringements on interstate commerce
choices.textEs: The Corte Suprema ruled key Populist economic proposals — including the subtreasury plan and railroad rate regulations — unconstitucional infringements on interstate commerce

items.explanation: Populism declined after 1896 because many of its supporters were absorbed into the Democratic Party behind William Jennings Bryan, and economic conditions changed after the depression eased. A choice saying farmers suddenly stopped facing problems is wrong because rural distress continued even after the party weakened. Although the party faded, its reform ideas survived in later Progressive legislation.
items.explanationEs: Populism declined after 1896 because many of its supporters were absorbed into the democrático Party behind William Jennings Bryan, and economic conditions changed after the depresión eased. A choice saying farmers suddenly stopped facing problems is wrong because rural distress continued even after the party weakened. Although the party faded, its reform ideas survived in later Progressive legislación, especially in this item's emphasis on defeat William Jennings Bryan 1896 marked.

items.stem: The Populist movement's lasting significance for American history was that it —
items.stemEs: The Populist movement's lasting significance for American history was that it —

choices.text: Demonstrated that ordinary citizens could organize mass political movements challenging concentrated economic power
choices.textEs: Demonstrated that ordinary citizens could organize mass political movements challenging concentrated economic power

choices.text: Permanently transformed the Democratic Party into a vehicle for agricultural interests
choices.textEs: Permanently transformed the democrático Party into a vehicle for agricultural interests

choices.text: Proved that third parties could successfully challenge the two-party system in America
choices.textEs: Proved that third parties could successfully challenge the two-party system in America

choices.text: Created the foundation for the labor movement of the 20th century
choices.textEs: Created the foundation for the labor movement of the 20th century

items.explanation: Populism had a lasting impact because reforms once dismissed as radical, such as direct election of senators and stronger regulation of business and banking, later became part of mainstream policy. A choice saying Populism disappeared without influence is wrong because many Progressive reforms echoed Populist demands. The movement showed how protest politics can reshape the major parties even after a third party declines.
items.explanationEs: Populism had a lasting impact because reforms once dismissed as radical, such as direct election of senators and stronger regulation of business and banking, later became part of mainstream policy. A choice saying Populism disappeared without influence is wrong because many Progressive reforms echoed Populist demands. The movement showed how protest politics can reshape the major parties even after a third party declines, especially in this item's emphasis on populist movement s lasting significance American.

items.stem: The labor movement's struggle for recognition in the late 19th century demonstrated that —
items.stemEs: The labor movement's struggle for recognition in the late 19th century demonstrated that —

choices.text: Without legal protection for organizing and collective bargaining, corporations could deploy economic sanctions, private security forces, and court injunctions to destroy union locals before they gained a permanent foothold
choices.textEs: Without legal protection for organizing and collective bargaining, corporations could deploy economic sanctions, private security forces, and court injunctions to destroy union locals before they gained a permanent foothold

choices.text: The federal government consistently allied with employers against striking workers, dispatching troops and issuing injunctions that effectively ended major strikes before workers could win concessions
choices.textEs: The gobierno federal consistently allied with employers against striking workers, dispatching troops and issuing injunctions that effectively ended major huelgas before workers could win concessions

choices.text: Most workers genuinely preferred individual negotiation with supervisors over the adversarial collective bargaining model that union organizers promoted
choices.textEs: Most workers genuinely preferred individual negotiation with supervisors over the adversarial collective bargaining model that union organizers promoted

choices.text: Strike tactics consistently failed to produce lasting wage gains because employers could always replace strikers with newly arrived immigrants willing to work at lower wages
choices.textEs: huelga tactics consistently faicondujo a produce lasting wage gains because employers could always replace huelgars with newly arrived immigrants willing to work at lower wages

items.explanation: The labor movement showed that without legal protection for unions, employers could use money, private guards, court injunctions, and state force to crush worker organization. Choice B is wrong because the federal government usually sided with business in major strikes during the late 1800s. Choice D is wrong because strikes sometimes won gains, even though many were defeated. These struggles helped convince later reformers that labor rights needed federal protection.
items.explanationEs: The labor movement showed that without legal protection for unions, employers could use money, private guards, court injunctions, and state force to crush worker organization. Choice B is wrong because the gobierno federal usually sided with business in major huelgas during the late 1800s. Choice D is wrong because huelgas sometimes won gains, even though many were defeated. These struggles helped convince later reformers that labor rights needed federal protection.

items.stem: Progressive Era reform was primarily driven by which social class and why?
items.stemEs: Era Progresista reform fue principalmente driven by which social class and why?

choices.text: Upper class — industrial elites who wanted to stabilize capitalism against socialist revolution
choices.textEs: Upper class — industrial elites who wanted to stabilize capitalismo against socialist revolution

choices.text: Working class — they were most directly harmed by industrial capitalism's abuses
choices.textEs: Working class — they were most directly harmed by industrial capitalismo's abuses

choices.text: Middle class — educated professionals who believed in scientific management and were alarmed by both plutocracy and radicalism
choices.textEs: Middle class — educated professionals who believed in scientific management and were alarmed by both plutocracy and radicalism

choices.text: Rural farmers — they had organized through the Populist movement and maintained political influence
choices.textEs: Rural farmers — they had organized through the Populist movement and maintained political influence

items.explanation: Much Progressive reform was led by the urban middle class, whose members used education, journalism, and professional expertise to attack corruption and social problems. A choice saying reform came mainly from industrial tycoons is wrong because many reformers were criticizing corporate power, not representing it. That background shaped both the strengths and limits of Progressive reform.
items.explanationEs: Much Progressive reform was led by the urban middle class, whose members used education, journalism, and professional expertise to attack corruption and social problems. A choice saying reform came mainly from industrial tycoons is wrong because many reformers were criticizing corporate power, not representing it. That background shaped both the strengths and limits of Progressive reform.

items.stem: The Progressive Era saw three presidents — Roosevelt, Taft, and Wilson — each pursue different approaches to reform. Compare their reform philosophies and methods, using specific legislation and actions as evidence. Then evaluate which president's approach had the most lasting impact on the role of the federal government in American life.
items.stemEs: La Era Progresista vio a tres presidentes — Roosevelt, Taft y Wilson — cada uno perseguir enfoques diferentes de reforma. Compare sus filosofías y métodos de reforma, usando legislación y acciones específicas como evidencia. Luego evalúe qué enfoque presidencial tuvo el impacto más duradero en el rol del gobierno federal.
items.correctAnswer: Strong responses should: (1) Describe each president's reform philosophy with specific examples, (2) Compare approaches systematically, (3) Make an evidence-based argument about lasting impact. Roosevelt: "Square Deal" — selective trust-busting (Northern Securities), consumer protection (Meat Inspection Act, Pure Food and Drug Act), conservation (150 million acres of forest reserves). Taft: more aggressive trust-busting (90 suits vs. Roosevelt's 44) but politically clumsy (Payne-Aldrich Tariff, Ballinger-Pinchot controversy). Wilson: "New Freedom" — Federal Reserve Act (1913), Clayton Antitrust Act (1914), FTC, graduated income tax (16th Amendment). Wilson's reforms arguably had the most lasting structural impact because the Federal Reserve and income tax became permanent foundations of modern governance.
items.explanation: A strong response should compare Roosevelt’s Square Deal, Taft’s aggressive but politically divisive antitrust actions, and Wilson’s New Freedom using specific evidence such as the Northern Securities case, the Payne-Aldrich Tariff and Ballinger-Pinchot controversy, and the Federal Reserve Act or Clayton Antitrust Act. The best essays do more than list reforms: they explain how each president viewed federal power and make a clear argument about which approach had the most lasting effect on the role of government. This matters because the Progressive Era helped define the modern expectation that the federal government should shape the economy and protect the public.
items.explanationEs: Este ítem DOK 4 requiere síntesis a través de tres administraciones, comparación de filosofías y métodos, y argumento evaluativo sobre significado duradero.

items.stem: Analyze how American imperialism in the late 1800s reflected BOTH idealistic and self-interested motivations. Use evidence from at least THREE specific events or policies (e.g., Spanish-American War, annexation of Hawaii, Open Door Policy, Panama Canal, Philippine-American War). Then evaluate whether imperialism ultimately strengthened or weakened American democratic ideals.
items.stemEs: Analice cómo el imperialismo americano a fines del siglo XIX reflejó motivaciones TANTO idealistas como interesadas. Use evidencia de al menos TRES eventos o políticas específicas. Luego evalúe si el imperialismo finalmente fortaleció o debilitó los ideales democráticos americanos.
items.correctAnswer: Strong responses should identify both idealistic motivations (spreading democracy, "civilizing mission") and self-interested ones (economic markets, strategic military bases, national prestige) in specific events, then make a nuanced evaluative argument. The Spanish-American War combined genuine sympathy for Cuban independence with yellow journalism and commercial interests. Hawaiian annexation served naval strategy (Pearl Harbor) while overthrowing a sovereign government. The Philippine-American War exposed the contradiction between liberation rhetoric and colonial violence (200,000+ Filipino deaths).
items.explanation: A strong response should show that American imperialism mixed idealistic language about spreading liberty or “civilization” with self-interested goals such as new markets, naval bases, and national prestige. It should use at least three specific examples, such as the Spanish-American War, annexation of Hawaii, the Open Door Policy, the Panama Canal, or the Philippine-American War, and then judge whether those actions strengthened or weakened democratic ideals. This prompt is important because it asks students to weigh American expansion against the nation’s stated commitment to self-government.
items.explanationEs: Este ítem DOK 4 exige síntesis de múltiples eventos, análisis de motivaciones competidoras y un argumento evaluativo extendido.

items.stem: A student argues: "World War I marked the end of American isolationism." Write a well-supported response that either agrees, disagrees, or modifies this claim, using evidence from U.S. entry into WWI, wartime domestic policy, and postwar foreign policy decisions.
items.stemEs: Un estudiante argumenta: "La Primera Guerra Mundial marcó el fin del aislacionismo americano." Escriba una respuesta bien fundamentada que esté de acuerdo, en desacuerdo o modifique esta afirmación.
items.correctAnswer: The strongest response modifies the claim: WWI temporarily ended isolationism but the Senate's rejection of the Treaty of Versailles and the return to "normalcy" in the 1920s showed that isolationist sentiment remained powerful. Evidence should include: Wilson's shift from neutrality to war, the Espionage and Sedition Acts domestically, Senate rejection of the League, and 1920s immigration restrictions and tariffs.
items.explanation: The strongest response will probably modify the claim by showing that World War I pushed the United States into world affairs but did not fully end isolationist thinking. A strong answer should use evidence such as Wilson’s move from neutrality to war, wartime laws like the Espionage and Sedition Acts, the Senate’s rejection of the Treaty of Versailles and League of Nations, and the return to restrictionist policies in the 1920s. This issue matters because it shows that US foreign policy often shifts between international involvement and withdrawal rather than moving in a straight line.
items.explanationEs: Este ítem DOK 4 requiere que los estudiantes evalúen una afirmación histórica y construyan una tesis matizada.

items.stem: Compare and contrast the strategies of Carrie Chapman Catt and Alice Paul. How did their different approaches contribute to the success of women's suffrage?
items.stemEs: Compare y contraste las estrategias de Carrie Chapman Catt y Alice Paul. ¿Cómo contribuyeron sus diferentes enfoques al éxito del sufragio femenino?

choices.text: Both leaders used identical militant tactics to pressure Congress
choices.textEs: Ambas líderes usaron tácticas militantes idénticas para presionar al Congreso

choices.text: Catt's campaigns and Paul's protests created combined pressure
choices.textEs: Las campañas políticas de Catt y las protestas de Paul crearon presión complementaria

choices.text: They opposed each other and their conflict delayed ratification
choices.textEs: Se opusieron mutuamente y su conflicto retrasó significativamente la ratificación

choices.text: Only Catt's approach worked while Paul's tactics hurt the cause
choices.textEs: Solo el enfoque de Catt fue efectivo mientras las tácticas de Paul dañaron la causa

items.explanation: Carrie Chapman Catt’s “Winning Plan” combined state-level suffrage campaigns with a coordinated push for a federal constitutional amendment. A choice about militant picketing is wrong because that tactic is more closely associated with Alice Paul and the National Woman’s Party. Catt’s strategy helped unify the final drive for the 19th Amendment.
items.explanationEs: La NAWSA de Catt usó campañas organizadas estado por estado y el "Plan Ganador

items.stem: Evaluate: Why did most strikes during the Gilded Age fail to achieve their goals?
items.stemEs: Evalúe: ¿Por qué la mayoría de las huelgas durante la Edad Dorada no lograron sus objetivos?

choices.text: Workers had strong legal protections that made strikes pointless
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores tenían fuertes protecciones legales que hacían las huelgas innecesarias

choices.text: Public opinion overwhelmingly supported the striking workers
choices.textEs: La opinión pública apoyaba abrumadoramente a los trabajadores en huelga

choices.text: Workers were too well-paid to sustain strikes for very long
choices.textEs: Los trabajadores estaban demasiado bien pagados para mantener huelgas por mucho tiempo

choices.text: Government, courts, and military all sided with business owners
choices.textEs: El gobierno, los tribunales y el ejército apoyaban a los dueños contra los trabajadores

items.explanation: Most Gilded Age strikes failed because employers could rely on courts, state militias, federal troops, Pinkerton guards, and replacement workers to defeat unions. Choice A is wrong because workers did not have strong legal protections; courts often issued injunctions against them. Choice B is wrong because public opinion often turned against labor after violence or business propaganda. These repeated defeats showed how much political and economic power still rested with industrial capital.
items.explanationEs: Las huelgas a menudo fracasaban porque toda la estructura de poder se oponía a los trabajadores: los tribunales emitían mandatos haciendo las huelgas ilegales, las tropas federales rompían huelgas, los detectives de Pinkerton proporcionaban rompehuelgas y violencia, y la cobertura de prensa a menudo retrataba a los huelguistas como radicales peligrosos.

items.stem: How did World War I contribute to the passage of the 19th Amendment?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo contribuyó la Primera Guerra Mundial a la aprobación de la Enmienda 19?

choices.text: Women's wartime contributions made denying them the vote increasingly unjustifiable
choices.textEs: Las contribuciones de las mujeres en tiempos de guerra hicieron cada vez más injustificable negarles el voto

choices.text: He received a letter from his mother urging him to "be a good boy" and vote for suffrage
choices.textEs: La guerra causó que toda oposición al sufragio femenino desapareciera inmediatamente

choices.text: Paul used militant tactics like hunger strikes and picketing the White House
choices.textEs: Las naciones europeas obligaron a EE.UU. a dar a las mujeres derechos de voto como condición de paz

choices.text: They fought for suffrage but often faced racism within the movement itself
choices.textEs: La guerra no tuvo impacto significativo en el movimiento de sufragio femenino

items.explanation: World War I helped the 19th Amendment pass because women’s wartime service strengthened the argument that they had earned full political citizenship. A choice saying the war distracted voters away from suffrage forever is wrong because wartime service actually increased support. The amendment shows how national emergencies can reshape ideas about citizenship.
items.explanationEs: Las contribuciones vitales de las mujeres durante la Primera Guerra Mundial—trabajando en fábricas, sirviendo como enfermeras y apoyando el esfuerzo bélico—hicieron más difícil argumentar que no eran aptas para votar. El Presidente Wilson finalmente respaldó el sufragio.

items.stem: Why did the Populist movement ultimately decline despite its widespread support among farmers?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué decayó el movimiento populista a pesar de su amplio apoyo entre los agricultores?

choices.text: Bryan's 1896 loss, economic recovery, and Democratic absorption weakened it
choices.textEs: La derrota de Bryan en 1896, la recuperación económica y la absorción demócrata lo debilitaron

choices.text: Increasing the money supply would raise crop prices and ease their debts
choices.textEs: Todos los agricultores se volvieron ricos y ya no necesitaban representación política

choices.text: Fighting unfair railroad rates and business practices that hurt farmers
choices.textEs: La Corte Suprema declaró inconstitucional al Partido del Pueblo

choices.text: An immigration processing station for Asian arrivals on the West Coast
choices.textEs: Las ideas populistas fueron completamente rechazadas por ambos partidos principales

items.explanation: Populism declined after 1896 because many of its supporters were absorbed into the Democratic Party behind William Jennings Bryan, and economic conditions changed after the depression eased. A choice saying farmers suddenly stopped facing problems is wrong because rural distress continued even after the party weakened. Although the party faded, its reform ideas survived in later Progressive legislation.
items.explanationEs: Después de la derrota de Bryan en 1896, la economía mejoró con descubrimientos de oro, reduciendo la urgencia del tema de la plata. Muchas ideas populistas (impuesto sobre la renta, elección directa de senadores) fueron adoptadas más tarde por los progresistas.

items.stem: Why did the women's suffrage movement take more than 70 years (1848-1920) to achieve the 19th Amendment?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué the women's sufragio movement take more than 70 years (1848-1920) to achieve the 19th enmienda?

choices.text: Congress had raised the constitutional threshold for amendments in 1868, requiring three-fourths of states to ratify, making the suffrage amendment far harder to pass than earlier amendments
choices.textEs: Congreso had raised the constitucional threshold for enmiendas in 1868, requiring three-fourths of states to ratify, making the sufragio enmienda far harder to pass than earlier enmiendas

choices.text: Multiple overlapping obstacles — liquor industry lobbying, Southern white fears that Black women would demand the vote, and anti-suffrage arguments about women's domestic sphere — combined to block the amendment for decades
choices.textEs: Multiple overlapping obstacles — liquor industry lobbying, Southern white fears that Black women would demand the vote, and anti-sufragio arguments about women's domestic sphere — combined to block the enmienda for decades

choices.text: Women's suffrage organizations lacked the financial resources and professional political staff needed to sustain a decades-long national lobbying campaign against well-funded opposition
choices.textEs: Women's sufragio organizations lacked the financial resources and professional political staff needed to sustain a decades-long national lobbying campaign against well-funded opposition

choices.text: National anti-suffrage organizations successfully pressured congressional leaders to table the Nineteenth Amendment bill through procedural motions until the wartime political climate forced a vote
choices.textEs: National anti-sufragio organizations successfully pressured Congresoional leaders to table the Nineteenth enmienda bill through procedural motions until the wartime political climate forced a vote

items.explanation: Women’s suffrage took more than 70 years because activists faced entrenched gender norms, political resistance, movement divisions, and the slow challenge of winning support state by state before a national amendment passed. A choice saying women lacked any organization is wrong because suffragists built strong national movements, but opposition remained powerful. The long struggle shows how difficult it can be to expand democratic rights.
items.explanationEs: Women’s sufragio took more than 70 years because activists faced entrenched gender norms, political resistance, movement divisions, and the slow challenge of winning support state by state before a national enmienda passed. A choice saying women lacked any organization is wrong because suffragists built strong national movements, but opposition remained powerful. The long struggle shows how difficult it can be to expand democrático rights.

items.stem: Social Darwinism was used by many Gilded Age industrialists to justify economic inequality. Which of the following best explains why this application of Darwin's ideas was fundamentally flawed as a social theory?
items.stemEs: El darwinismo social fue utilizado por muchos industrialistas de la Era Dorada para justificar la desigualdad económica. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor por qué esta aplicación de las ideas de Darwin era fundamentalmente defectuosa como teoría social?

choices.text: Darwin himself publicly rejected any application of his theories to human economic competition.
choices.textEs: El propio Darwin rechazó públicamente cualquier aplicación de sus teorías a la competencia económica humana.

choices.text: Social Darwinism was rejected immediately by most Americans because it conflicted with religious beliefs.
choices.textEs: El darwinismo social fue rechazado inmediatamente por la mayoría de los estadounidenses porque contradecía las creencias religiosas.

choices.text: Natural selection operates through biological inheritance over generations, not through economic choices or moral virtue within a single lifetime.
choices.textEs: La selección natural opera mediante la herencia biológica a lo largo de generaciones, no a través de decisiones económicas o virtud moral dentro de una sola vida.

choices.text: The theory was flawed because it incorrectly predicted that industrial monopolies would eventually collapse without government intervention.
choices.textEs: La teoría era defectuosa porque predijo incorrectamente que los monopolios industriales eventualmente colapsarían sin intervención gubernamental.

items.explanation: Darwin's theory of natural selection described biological processes operating over vast timescales in response to environmental pressures, not moral worth or economic virtue. Social Darwinists misapplied 'survival of the fittest' — a phrase coined by Herbert Spencer — to human society, ignoring that wealth accumulation depended heavily on inherited privilege, legal structures, and exploitation rather than innate fitness. This conflation rationalized suffering as natural and inevitable, shielding the wealthy from accountability. It also contradicted the Social Gospel response, which held that human society could and should be deliberately improved through collective moral action.
items.explanationEs: La teoría de Darwin sobre la selección natural describía procesos biológicos que ocurren durante vastos períodos de tiempo en respuesta a presiones ambientales, no el mérito moral o la virtud económica. Los darwinistas sociales aplicaron erróneamente la 'supervivencia del más apto' —frase acuñada por Herbert Spencer— a la sociedad humana, ignorando que la acumulación de riqueza dependía en gran medida del privilegio heredado, las estructuras legales y la explotación más que de una aptitud innata. Esta confusión racionalizó el sufrimiento como algo natural e inevitable, protegiendo a los ricos de rendir cuentas. También contradecía la respuesta del Evangelio Social, que sostenía que la sociedad humana podía y debía mejorarse deliberadamente mediante la acción moral colectiva.

items.stem: The Social Gospel movement and Social Darwinism both emerged in response to the conditions of industrialization, yet they reached opposite conclusions about the role of society in addressing poverty. Which of the following best evaluates why the Social Gospel movement represented a more effective foundation for Progressive Era reform?
items.stemEs: El movimiento del Evangelio Social y el darwinismo social surgieron en respuesta a las condiciones de la industrialización, pero llegaron a conclusiones opuestas sobre el papel de la sociedad para abordar la pobreza. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor por qué el movimiento del Evangelio Social representó una base más efectiva para las reformas de la Era Progresista?

choices.text: The Social Gospel treated poverty as a systemic injustice requiring collective action, creating an ideological basis for government and civic reform.
choices.textEs: El Evangelio Social trató la pobreza como una injusticia sistémica que requería acción colectiva, creando una base ideológica para la reforma gubernamental y cívica.

choices.text: The Social Gospel was more effective because it was supported by wealthy industrialists who funded settlement houses and labor unions.
choices.textEs: El Evangelio Social fue más efectivo porque contaba con el apoyo de ricos industrialistas que financiaban casas de asentamiento y sindicatos.

choices.text: Unlike Social Darwinism, the Social Gospel was accepted by both major political parties as the official basis for economic policy.
choices.textEs: A diferencia del darwinismo social, el Evangelio Social fue aceptado por ambos partidos políticos principales como base oficial para la política económica.

choices.text: The Social Gospel was more scientifically rigorous, providing empirical data that Social Darwinism lacked.
choices.textEs: El Evangelio Social era más científicamente riguroso, proporcionando datos empíricos que el darwinismo social carecía.

items.explanation: The Social Gospel held that poverty was a systemic problem caused by unjust social structures, not individual moral failure — an analysis that directly justified legislative reform, settlement houses, and labor protections. Social Darwinism, by contrast, treated inequality as natural and inevitable, actively discouraging intervention. Progressive Era reformers needed an ideological framework that demanded collective responsibility; the Social Gospel provided precisely that theological and moral mandate. Its emphasis on human dignity and community obligation translated into concrete policy advocacy in ways that Social Darwinism structurally could not.
items.explanationEs: El Evangelio Social sostenía que la pobreza era un problema sistémico causado por estructuras sociales injustas, no por un fracaso moral individual —un análisis que justificaba directamente la reforma legislativa, las casas de asentamiento y las protecciones laborales. El darwinismo social, por el contrario, trataba la desigualdad como natural e inevitable, desalentando activamente la intervención. Los reformistas de la Era Progresista necesitaban un marco ideológico que exigiera responsabilidad colectiva; el Evangelio Social proporcionó exactamente ese mandato teológico y moral. Su énfasis en la dignidad humana y la obligación comunitaria se tradujo en una defensa concreta de políticas de maneras que el darwinismo social estructuralmente no podía lograr.

items.stem: Andrew Carnegie's 'Gospel of Wealth' combined elements of both Social Darwinism and the Social Gospel. Which of the following best analyzes an internal contradiction within Carnegie's philosophy?
items.stemEs: El 'Evangelio de la Riqueza' de Andrew Carnegie combinó elementos tanto del darwinismo social como del Evangelio Social. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones analiza mejor una contradicción interna en la filosofía de Carnegie?

choices.text: Carnegie's philosophy was contradictory because he endowed thousands of public libraries while simultaneously opposing municipal tax increases that would have funded public education and social services
choices.textEs: La filosofía de Carnegie se contradecía porque construyó bibliotecas mientras simultáneamente se oponía al financiamiento de la educación pública.

choices.text: Carnegie claimed that disciplined individual effort was the true basis of legitimate wealth, yet he had relied heavily on family connections and borrowed capital to finance his early business ventures
choices.textEs: Carnegie afirmaba que el trabajo arduo garantizaba la riqueza, pero había heredado su capital empresarial inicial de su padre.

choices.text: Carnegie publicly invoked Social Darwinism to justify breaking the Amalgamated union at Homestead, yet his earlier Pittsburgh mills had operated under collective bargaining agreements with the same union
choices.textEs: Carnegie usó el darwinismo social para oponerse a todos los sindicatos laborales, pero luego contrató trabajadores sindicalizados en sus acerías.

choices.text: Carnegie invoked Social Darwinism to justify unlimited accumulation, yet his Gospel of Wealth's duty to redistribute surplus wealth contradicted the principle that natural competition alone should determine the social distribution of resources
choices.textEs: Carnegie usó el darwinismo social para justificar la acumulación ilimitada de riqueza, pero su deber filantrópico contradecía la idea de que la competencia natural debería determinar los resultados sociales.

items.explanation: Carnegie argued that Social Darwinism validated the right of talented individuals to accumulate vast wealth, yet he simultaneously argued that the wealthy had a moral obligation to redistribute that wealth through philanthropy. This is contradictory: if inequality is natural and reflects the fitness of the winner, then redistributing wealth through charity undermines the very competitive process that Social Darwinism claims produces social progress. The contradiction reveals that Carnegie was selectively applying theory — using Social Darwinism to justify acquisition and a diluted Social Gospel to manage his public image and legacy.
items.explanationEs: Carnegie argumentó que el darwinismo social validaba el derecho de los individuos talentosos a acumular grandes riquezas, pero simultáneamente argumentó que los ricos tenían una obligación moral de redistribuir esa riqueza mediante la filantropía. Esto es contradictorio: si la desigualdad es natural y refleja la aptitud del ganador, entonces redistribuir la riqueza mediante la caridad socava el mismo proceso competitivo que el darwinismo social afirma que produce progreso social. La contradicción revela que Carnegie aplicaba la teoría de forma selectiva, usando el darwinismo social para justificar la adquisición y un Evangelio Social diluido para gestionar su imagen pública y su legado.

items.stem: A historian argues that Social Darwinism was less a scientific theory and more a political ideology that served the interests of industrial elites. Which of the following types of evidence would most strongly support this interpretation?
items.stemEs: Un historiador argumenta que el darwinismo social era menos una teoría científica y más una ideología política que servía a los intereses de las élites industriales. ¿Cuál de los siguientes tipos de evidencia apoyaría más fuertemente esta interpretación?

choices.text: Evidence that biologists in the 1880s publicly endorsed the application of natural selection to economic competition.
choices.textEs: Evidencia de que los biólogos en la década de 1880 respaldaron públicamente la aplicación de la selección natural a la competencia económica.

choices.text: Evidence that industrialists funded Social Darwinist publications while lobbying against labor laws and antitrust regulation.
choices.textEs: Evidencia de que los industrialistas financiaron publicaciones darwinistas sociales mientras hacían lobby contra las leyes laborales y la regulación antimonopolio.

choices.text: Evidence that Social Darwinism was taught in public schools as part of the science curriculum by the 1890s.
choices.textEs: Evidencia de que el darwinismo social se enseñaba en las escuelas públicas como parte del currículo de ciencias en la década de 1890.

choices.text: Evidence that most Progressive Era reformers had previously studied and accepted Social Darwinist ideas before rejecting them.
choices.textEs: Evidencia de que la mayoría de los reformistas de la Era Progresista habían estudiado y aceptado previamente las ideas darwinistas sociales antes de rechazarlas.

items.explanation: If Social Darwinism was genuinely a scientific theory applied neutrally, one would expect it to be used consistently — including against the wealthy when their businesses failed. Instead, the theory was selectively invoked to protect accumulated wealth and block worker protections, while ignoring structural advantages that helped elites succeed. Evidence that major industrialists funded the promotion of Social Darwinism while simultaneously lobbying against regulations would demonstrate that the 'theory' functioned as ideological cover for political and economic interests, not as disinterested scientific inquiry.
items.explanationEs: Si el darwinismo social fuera genuinamente una teoría científica aplicada de forma neutral, se esperaría que se usara de manera consistente, incluso contra los ricos cuando sus negocios fracasaban. En cambio, la teoría se invocaba selectivamente para proteger la riqueza acumulada y bloquear las protecciones laborales, ignorando las ventajas estructurales que ayudaban a las élites a tener éxito. La evidencia de que los principales industrialistas financiaban la promoción del darwinismo social mientras simultáneamente hacían lobby contra las regulaciones demostraría que la 'teoría' funcionaba como cobertura ideológica para intereses políticos y económicos, no como una investigación científica desinteresada.

items.stem: Which of the following scenarios would most directly challenge the core premises of Social Darwinism as applied to American economic life in the late 19th century?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál de los siguientes escenarios desafiaría más directamente las premisas centrales del darwinismo social aplicado a la vida económica estadounidense a finales del siglo XIX?

choices.text: A company achieves total market dominance not through superior products but by using political connections to block competitors and control prices.
choices.textEs: Una empresa logra un dominio total del mercado no a través de productos superiores, sino utilizando conexiones políticas para bloquear a los competidores y controlar los precios.

choices.text: A large corporation fails to compete internationally and must shut down several factories, laying off thousands of workers.
choices.textEs: Una gran corporación no logra competir internacionalmente y debe cerrar varias fábricas, despidiendo a miles de trabajadores.

choices.text: A first-generation immigrant builds a successful business by working longer hours than established competitors in the same industry.
choices.textEs: Un inmigrante de primera generación construye un negocio exitoso trabajando más horas que los competidores establecidos en la misma industria.

choices.text: An economic depression causes widespread business failures among small firms while large corporations survive by cutting wages.
choices.textEs: Una depresión económica provoca quiebras masivas entre las pequeñas empresas mientras las grandes corporaciones sobreviven recortando salarios.

items.explanation: Social Darwinism claimed that economic success reflected personal fitness and that competitive markets naturally rewarded the most capable individuals. The existence of monopolies — where a single company eliminates all competition through legal manipulation, political influence, and predatory pricing — fundamentally contradicts this premise. When market dominance is achieved by crushing competition rather than through superior fitness, the 'natural selection' metaphor breaks down entirely. This is exactly the scenario that justified Progressive Era antitrust legislation: the market was not self-correcting through fair competition.
items.explanationEs: El darwinismo social afirmaba que el éxito económico reflejaba la aptitud personal y que los mercados competitivos recompensaban naturalmente a los individuos más capaces. La existencia de monopolios, donde una sola empresa elimina toda la competencia mediante la manipulación legal, la influencia política y los precios predatorios, contradice fundamentalmente esta premisa. Cuando el dominio del mercado se logra aplastando la competencia en lugar de a través de una aptitud superior, la metáfora de la 'selección natural' se desmorona por completo. Este es exactamente el escenario que justificó la legislación antimonopolio de la Era Progresista: el mercado no se autocorregía mediante la competencia justa.

items.stem: The Social Gospel movement drew its inspiration from Christian theology but pursued goals that aligned with secular Progressive reform. Which of the following best explains how the Social Gospel was able to bridge the divide between religious and secular reformers?
items.stemEs: El movimiento del Evangelio Social se inspiró en la teología cristiana pero persiguió metas que se alineaban con la reforma progresista secular. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor cómo el Evangelio Social pudo tender un puente entre reformadores religiosos y seculares?

choices.text: The Social Gospel required all reformers to convert to Protestant Christianity as a precondition for joining reform coalitions.
choices.textEs: El Evangelio Social requería que todos los reformistas se convirtieran al protestantismo como condición previa para unirse a las coaliciones de reforma.
