choices.textEs: La mejora agrícola resultó del aumento de los precios de los productos básicos globales, la reforma regulatoria parcial y los partidos principales que absorbieron las demandas populistas, revelando que los terceros partidos a menudo fracasan organizativamente pero tienen éxito en cambiar las agendas de los partidos principales, y que los efectos de la reforma son a menudo difusos e interrelacionados con factores no políticos.

choices.text: Farm improvement from 1896 to 1920 was entirely the result of Populist political advocacy: the threat of continued third-party organization forced both major parties to enact the agricultural reforms that produced improved conditions.
choices.textEs: La mejora agrícola de 1896 a 1920 fue enteramente el resultado de la defensa política populista: la amenaza de la organización continua de terceros partidos forzó a ambos partidos principales a promulgar las reformas agrícolas que produjeron mejores condiciones.

choices.text: Farm conditions improved despite the failure of Populism, not because of it: the improvement came from technological innovations in agriculture that the Populist movement had actually opposed because they benefited large farm operations over small family farms.
choices.textEs: Las condiciones agrícolas mejoraron a pesar del fracaso del populismo, no a causa de él: la mejora provino de innovaciones tecnológicas en la agricultura que el movimiento populista en realidad había opuesto porque beneficiaban a las grandes operaciones agrícolas sobre las pequeñas granjas familiares.

choices.text: Farm improvement reveals that Populism was not necessary for agrarian reform: the conditions that drove farm distress in the 1880s and 1890s would have been resolved by normal market adjustments without any political intervention.
choices.textEs: La mejora agrícola revela que el populismo no era necesario para la reforma agraria: las condiciones que impulsaron la angustia agrícola en las décadas de 1880 y 1890 se habrían resuelto mediante ajustes de mercado normales sin ninguna intervención política.

items.explanation: Farm conditions improved after 1896 for multiple reasons: rising commodity prices as global demand for American agricultural products grew, some genuine Progressive regulatory reform (ICC rate regulation, railroad safety laws), and the absorption of some Populist demands into both major parties' platforms. This multi-factor improvement reveals an important dynamic in American reform history: third parties often fail organizationally but succeed in shifting the policy agenda of major parties, which then adopt modified versions of third-party demands once they become politically unavoidable. The improvement also came partly from external economic factors (rising prices) unrelated to political reform, which makes it difficult to attribute farm improvement solely to reform advocacy. This complexity suggests that reform's effects are often diffuse, delayed, and intertwined with non-political factors.
items.explanationEs: Las condiciones agrícolas mejoraron después de 1896 por múltiples razones: el aumento de los precios de los productos básicos a medida que crecía la demanda global de productos agrícolas estadounidenses, algunas reformas regulatorias progresistas genuinas (regulación de tarifas de la ICC, leyes de seguridad ferroviaria) y la absorción de algunas demandas populistas en las plataformas de ambos partidos principales. Esta mejora multifactorial revela una dinámica importante en la historia de reforma estadounidense: los terceros partidos a menudo fracasan organizativamente pero tienen éxito en cambiar la agenda política de los partidos principales, que luego adoptan versiones modificadas de las demandas de terceros partidos una vez que se vuelven políticamente inevitables. La mejora también provino en parte de factores económicos externos (precios crecientes) no relacionados con la reforma política, lo que hace difícil atribuir la mejora agrícola únicamente a la defensa de la reforma. Esta complejidad sugiere que los efectos de la reforma son a menudo difusos, retrasados e interrelacionados con factores no políticos.

items.stem: The labor movement's use of the strike as its primary weapon created an ongoing tension between worker rights and public order. Which of the following best evaluates how the Progressive Era attempted to resolve this tension?
items.stemEs: El uso del movimiento laboral de la huelga como su arma principal creó una tensión continua entre los derechos de los trabajadores y el orden público. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor cómo la Era Progresista intentó resolver esta tensión?

choices.text: The Progressive Era fully resolved the tension by establishing clear legal rules that protected all strike activity as constitutional free speech while strictly prohibiting any use of violence or property damage during labor disputes.
choices.textEs: La Era Progresista resolvió completamente la tensión estableciendo reglas legales claras que protegían toda actividad huelguística como libre expresión constitucional mientras prohibían estrictamente cualquier uso de violencia o daño a la propiedad durante las disputas laborales.

choices.text: The Progressive Era partially addressed the tension through procedural institutionalization — creating mediation, collective bargaining recognition, and partial antitrust exemption — but continued military intervention in major strikes showed the tension was far from resolved.
choices.textEs: La Era Progresista abordó parcialmente la tensión a través de la institucionalización procedimental, creando mediación, reconocimiento de la negociación colectiva y exención parcial del antimonopolio, pero la intervención militar continua en las huelgas principales mostró que la tensión estaba lejos de resolverse.

choices.text: The Progressive Era resolved the tension entirely in favor of management by clearly establishing that any strike action that disrupted interstate commerce or caused property damage was illegal, eliminating strikes as a viable labor tactic.
choices.textEs: La Era Progresista resolvió la tensión enteramente a favor de la gerencia al establecer claramente que cualquier acción huelguística que interrumpiera el comercio interestatal o causara daños a la propiedad era ilegal, eliminando las huelgas como táctica laboral viable.

choices.text: The Progressive Era resolved the tension entirely in favor of labor by establishing that workers had an absolute constitutional right to strike in any sector of the economy without government interference regardless of public impact.
choices.textEs: La Era Progresista resolvió la tensión enteramente a favor del trabajo al establecer que los trabajadores tenían un derecho constitucional absoluto a la huelga en cualquier sector de la economía sin interferencia gubernamental independientemente del impacto público.

items.explanation: The Progressive Era did not fully resolve the tension between strike rights and public order — it reframed it through a procedural approach that recognized collective bargaining rights while maintaining restrictions on strike tactics that threatened essential services or used violence. The Clayton Act attempted to exempt union activity from antitrust prosecution; the Department of Labor (created 1913) provided mediation services; some states created arbitration boards. But courts continued to issue injunctions against strikes, and the government continued to intervene militarily in major disputes (Colorado Coalfield War, 1913-1914). The Progressive approach was to institutionalize labor-management conflict within regulated channels rather than either suppressing labor rights entirely or allowing unlimited strike action — a partial resolution that satisfied neither side fully and that remained contested until the New Deal's National Labor Relations Act of 1935.
items.explanationEs: La Era Progresista no resolvió completamente la tensión entre los derechos de huelga y el orden público, sino que la reenmarcó a través de un enfoque procedimental que reconocía los derechos de negociación colectiva mientras mantenía restricciones sobre las tácticas de huelga que amenazaban los servicios esenciales o usaban violencia. La Ley Clayton intentó eximir la actividad sindical del enjuiciamiento antimonopolio; el Departamento de Trabajo (creado en 1913) proporcionó servicios de mediación; algunos estados crearon juntas de arbitraje. Pero los tribunales continuaron emitiendo mandatos contra las huelgas, y el gobierno continuó interviniendo militarmente en disputas importantes (Guerra de los Campos de Carbón de Colorado, 1913-1914). El enfoque progresista fue institucionalizar el conflicto trabajo-gerencia dentro de canales regulados en lugar de suprimir los derechos laborales por completo o permitir acción huelguística ilimitada, una resolución parcial que no satisfizo completamente a ninguna de las partes y que permaneció controvertida hasta la Ley Nacional de Relaciones Laborales del New Deal de 1935.

items.stem: Women reformers in the Progressive Era were simultaneously excluded from formal political participation (before the 19th Amendment) and central to major reform achievements. Which of the following best explains how women exercised political influence without the formal right to vote?
items.stemEs: Las reformadoras de la Era Progresista fueron simultáneamente excluidas de la participación política formal (antes de la 19.ª Enmienda) y centrales en los principales logros de reforma. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor cómo las mujeres ejercieron influencia política sin el derecho formal al voto?

choices.text: Women exercised political influence primarily through their husbands and male relatives who voted according to women's guidance, creating an informal proxy voting system that gave women significant electoral influence without formal voting rights.
choices.textEs: Las mujeres ejercieron influencia política principalmente a través de sus maridos y parientes masculinos que votaban según la guía de las mujeres, creando un sistema informal de voto por representación que daba a las mujeres influencia electoral significativa sin derechos de voto formales.

choices.text: Women had no meaningful political influence before the 19th Amendment because all formal political power was held exclusively by male voters and elected officials who consistently ignored women's reform demands.
choices.textEs: Las mujeres no tenían influencia política significativa antes de la 19.ª Enmienda porque todo el poder político formal era sostenido exclusivamente por votantes masculinos y funcionarios electos que ignoraban consistentemente las demandas de reforma de las mujeres.

choices.text: Women exercised political influence exclusively through the courts by filing lawsuits challenging laws that discriminated against women, using judicial victories to create legal precedents that compelled legislative reform.
choices.textEs: Las mujeres ejercieron influencia política exclusivamente a través de los tribunales presentando demandas que desafiaban las leyes que discriminaban a las mujeres, usando victorias judiciales para crear precedentes legales que obligaban a la reforma legislativa.

choices.text: Women used settlement houses, women's clubs, and reform networks as institutional bases for research, lobbying, legislation drafting, and coalition-building — expanding influence in policy areas defined as maternal expertise (child welfare, public health) without requiring formal voting rights.
choices.textEs: Las mujeres usaron casas de asentamiento, clubes de mujeres y redes de reforma como bases institucionales para la investigación, el lobby, la redacción de legislación y la construcción de coaliciones, expandiendo la influencia en áreas de política definidas como experiencia maternal (bienestar infantil, salud pública) sin requerir derechos de voto formales.

items.explanation: Women exercised political influence through multiple channels that did not require formal voting rights: settlement houses provided women reformers with institutional bases for research, advocacy, and coalition-building; women's clubs and suffrage organizations built grassroots organizational capacity and lobbying skills; women dominated the settlement house network that conducted social research and provided the empirical evidence that reformers used to make the case for specific legislation; women activists like Florence Kelley were centrally involved in writing model legislation for child labor and maximum hours laws; and women reformers cultivated relationships with male politicians who controlled legislative outcomes. The Progressive Era's expansion of the public sphere to include maternal concerns (child welfare, public health, housing) created political space for women's influence precisely in areas defined as women's particular expertise.
items.explanationEs: Las mujeres ejercieron influencia política a través de múltiples canales que no requerían derechos de voto formales: las casas de asentamiento proporcionaban a las reformadoras bases institucionales para la investigación, la defensa y la construcción de coaliciones; los clubes de mujeres y las organizaciones sufragistas construyeron capacidad organizativa de base y habilidades de lobby; las mujeres dominaron la red de casas de asentamiento que realizaba investigación social y proporcionaba la evidencia empírica que los reformistas usaban para argumentar a favor de legislación específica; activistas mujeres como Florence Kelley estaban centralmente involucradas en la redacción de legislación modelo para el trabajo infantil y las leyes de horas máximas; y las reformadoras cultivaban relaciones con políticos masculinos que controlaban los resultados legislativos. La expansión de la Era Progresista de la esfera pública para incluir preocupaciones maternales (bienestar infantil, salud pública, vivienda) creó espacio político para la influencia de las mujeres precisamente en áreas definidas como la experiencia particular de las mujeres.

items.stem: The Sherman Antitrust Act's application to labor unions was finally addressed by the Clayton Act in 1914. However, the Duplex Printing Press Co. v. Deering (1921) Supreme Court decision significantly limited the Clayton Act's labor protections. Which of the following best evaluates the significance of this pattern for understanding judicial power in the American political system?
items.stemEs: La aplicación de la Ley Sherman Antimonopolio a los sindicatos laborales fue finalmente abordada por la Ley Clayton en 1914. Sin embargo, la decisión de la Corte Suprema en Duplex Printing Press Co. v. Deering (1921) limitó significativamente las protecciones laborales de la Ley Clayton. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor el significado de este patrón para comprender el poder judicial en el sistema político estadounidense?

choices.text: The pattern reveals that the Supreme Court had the constitutional authority to veto any labor legislation it opposed, making legislative reform of labor law impossible without first changing the Court's composition.
choices.textEs: El patrón revela que la Corte Suprema tenía la autoridad constitucional de vetar cualquier legislación laboral que se opusiera, haciendo imposible la reforma legislativa de la ley laboral sin cambiar primero la composición de la Corte.

choices.text: The pattern reveals that Congress was insincere in its labor protection intentions and deliberately wrote ambiguous statutory language knowing that courts would narrow the protections to satisfy the corporate interests that controlled both branches.
choices.textEs: El patrón revela que el Congreso fue insincero en sus intenciones de protección laboral y deliberadamente escribió lenguaje estatutario ambiguo sabiendo que los tribunales reducirían las protecciones para satisfacer los intereses corporativos que controlaban ambas ramas.

choices.text: The pattern reveals that statutory change alone cannot guarantee reformed outcomes — judicial interpretation shapes how statutes are applied in practice, and a judiciary whose culture favors property rights will narrow labor protections even when statutory text seems clear.
choices.textEs: El patrón revela que el cambio estatutario solo no puede garantizar resultados reformados: la interpretación judicial da forma a cómo los estatutos se aplican en la práctica, y un poder judicial cuya cultura favorece los derechos de propiedad reducirá las protecciones laborales incluso cuando el texto estatutario parece claro.

choices.text: The pattern is insignificant because the Duplex decision was quickly reversed by Congress through new legislation, showing that American democracy's self-correcting mechanisms effectively responded to judicial overreach within the Progressive Era.
choices.textEs: El patrón es insignificante porque la decisión Duplex fue rápidamente revertida por el Congreso mediante nueva legislación, mostrando que los mecanismos de autocorrección de la democracia estadounidense respondieron efectivamente a los excesos judiciales dentro de la Era Progresista.

items.explanation: The pattern of Congress passing labor-protective legislation followed by judicial narrowing through interpretation reveals a fundamental feature of American constitutional politics: legislative majorities can pass reform statutes, but judicial interpretation shapes how those statutes are actually applied in practice. Courts do not simply apply neutral legal text — they interpret ambiguous statutory language according to frameworks reflecting their own institutional culture, precedent, and in the early 20th century, a strong judicial culture favorable to property rights and skeptical of labor power. The Clayton Act clearly stated that labor was not a commodity and that unions were not combinations in restraint of trade, but the Court in Duplex interpreted these provisions narrowly by finding ways to characterize the specific union activity at issue as outside the exemption. This reveals that statutory change alone cannot guarantee reformed outcomes without a judiciary willing to implement congressional intent.
items.explanationEs: El patrón del Congreso aprobando legislación protectora del trabajo seguida de la reducción judicial mediante interpretación revela una característica fundamental de la política constitucional estadounidense: las mayorías legislativas pueden aprobar leyes de reforma, pero la interpretación judicial da forma a cómo esas leyes se aplican realmente en la práctica. Los tribunales no simplemente aplican texto legal neutro: interpretan el lenguaje estatutario ambiguo de acuerdo con marcos que reflejan su propia cultura institucional, precedentes y, a principios del siglo XX, una fuerte cultura judicial favorable a los derechos de propiedad y escéptica del poder laboral. La Ley Clayton declaraba claramente que el trabajo no era una mercancía y que los sindicatos no eran combinaciones en restricción del comercio, pero el Tribunal en Duplex interpretó estas disposiciones estrechamente encontrando maneras de caracterizar la actividad sindical específica en cuestión como fuera de la exención. Esto revela que el cambio estatutario solo no puede garantizar resultados reformados sin un poder judicial dispuesto a implementar la intención del Congreso.

items.stem: Between 1877 and 1920, the number of women employed in the paid labor force more than doubled. Which of the following best analyzes the relationship between this demographic shift and the growth of the women's suffrage movement?
items.stemEs: Entre 1877 y 1920, el número de mujeres empleadas en la fuerza laboral remunerada se más que duplicó. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones analiza mejor la relación entre este cambio demográfico y el crecimiento del movimiento por el sufragio femenino?

choices.text: Women's growing labor force participation created new, self-interested constituencies for suffrage — women subject to workplace legislation they couldn't influence through voting — while building organizational capacities and strengthening the civic contribution argument for political representation.
choices.textEs: La creciente participación de las mujeres en la fuerza laboral creó nuevas circunscripciones con intereses propios para el sufragio, mujeres sujetas a legislación laboral que no podían influir a través del voto, mientras construía capacidades organizativas y fortalecía el argumento de la contribución cívica para la representación política.

choices.text: Women's labor force participation weakened the suffrage movement by convincing many women that economic equality could be achieved without political rights, reducing their incentive to organize and advocate for voting rights.
choices.textEs: La participación de las mujeres en la fuerza laboral debilitó el movimiento sufragista al convencer a muchas mujeres de que la igualdad económica podía lograrse sin derechos políticos, reduciendo su incentivo para organizarse y abogar por los derechos de voto.

choices.text: Women's labor force participation was largely unrelated to the suffrage movement because most female workers were uneducated immigrants who opposed suffrage on cultural and religious grounds, creating a constituency that suffrage leaders actively avoided mobilizing.
choices.textEs: La participación de las mujeres en la fuerza laboral era en gran medida no relacionada con el movimiento sufragista porque la mayoría de las trabajadoras eran inmigrantes sin educación que se oponían al sufragio por razones culturales y religiosas, creando una circunscripción que los líderes del sufragio evitaban activamente movilizar.

choices.text: Women's labor force participation created a constituency for suffrage that suffrage organizations deliberately rejected because working-class women's demands for labor rights conflicted with the middle-class suffrage movement's focus on voting rights alone.
choices.textEs: La participación de las mujeres en la fuerza laboral creó una circunscripción para el sufragio que las organizaciones sufragistas deliberadamente rechazaron porque las demandas de las mujeres de clase trabajadora por los derechos laborales conflictuaban con el enfoque del movimiento sufragista de clase media únicamente en los derechos de voto.

items.explanation: The growth of women's paid labor force participation created new constituencies for suffrage and new arguments for it simultaneously. Women working in factories and offices were directly subject to legislation regulating wages, hours, and working conditions — but had no vote to influence that legislation. This made the case for suffrage concrete and immediately self-interested rather than abstract: women needed political representation to have voice in laws that directly governed their daily working lives. The experience of organized work also built organizational skills, solidarity, and civic consciousness — qualities that supported suffrage organizing. Women workers also demonstrated through their economic contribution that they were full participants in civic society, strengthening the civic contribution argument for suffrage. The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire galvanized precisely this connection between working women's conditions and political power.
items.explanationEs: El crecimiento de la participación de las mujeres en la fuerza laboral remunerada creó simultáneamente nuevas circunscripciones para el sufragio y nuevos argumentos a favor de él. Las mujeres que trabajaban en fábricas y oficinas estaban directamente sujetas a la legislación que regulaba los salarios, las horas y las condiciones de trabajo, pero no tenían voto para influir en esa legislación. Esto hizo que el caso para el sufragio fuera concreto e inmediatamente de interés propio en lugar de abstracto: las mujeres necesitaban representación política para tener voz en las leyes que gobernaban directamente sus vidas laborales diarias. La experiencia del trabajo organizado también construyó habilidades organizativas, solidaridad y conciencia cívica, cualidades que apoyaron la organización del sufragio. Las mujeres trabajadoras también demostraron a través de su contribución económica que eran participantes plenas en la sociedad cívica, fortaleciendo el argumento de la contribución cívica para el sufragio. El incendio de la fábrica Triangle Shirtwaist galvanizó precisamente esta conexión entre las condiciones de las mujeres trabajadoras y el poder político.

items.stem: Progressive Era reformers frequently invoked 'the public interest' as justification for regulatory intervention. Which of the following best evaluates the difficulty of defining 'the public interest' and how this difficulty shaped the practice of Progressive regulation?
items.stemEs: Los reformistas de la Era Progresista frecuentemente invocaban 'el interés público' como justificación para la intervención regulatoria. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la dificultad de definir 'el interés público' y cómo esta dificultad moldeó la práctica de la regulación progresista?

choices.text: The difficulty of defining 'the public interest' had no practical impact on Progressive regulation because expert commissioners could objectively determine public interest through scientific analysis without reference to political considerations.
choices.textEs: La dificultad de definir el 'interés público' no tuvo impacto práctico en la regulación progresista porque los comisionados expertos podían determinar objetivamente el interés público mediante análisis científico sin referencia a consideraciones políticas.

choices.text: 'The public interest' is inherently contested since regulatory decisions always distribute benefits and burdens among different groups — agencies claiming to serve it were inevitably making contested political choices that their expert, neutral framing obscured rather than eliminated.
choices.textEs: El 'interés público' es inherentemente contestado ya que las decisiones regulatorias siempre distribuyen beneficios y cargas entre diferentes grupos: las agencias que afirmaban servirlo inevitablemente tomaban decisiones políticas controvertidas que su encuadre experto y neutral oscurecía en lugar de eliminar.

choices.text: Progressive reformers resolved the difficulty of defining 'the public interest' through democratic processes: regulatory agencies held public hearings in which all affected groups could participate equally, ensuring that final decisions genuinely reflected broader public preferences.
choices.textEs: Los reformistas progresistas resolvieron la dificultad de definir el 'interés público' a través de procesos democráticos: las agencias reguladoras celebraban audiencias públicas en las que todos los grupos afectados podían participar igualmente, asegurando que las decisiones finales reflejaran genuinamente las preferencias públicas más amplias.

choices.text: The difficulty of defining 'the public interest' caused Progressive regulation to collapse entirely by the 1920s, as agencies abandoned the concept in favor of explicit partisan advocacy for the groups their commissioners were drawn from.
choices.textEs: La dificultad de definir el 'interés público' causó que la regulación progresista colapsara por completo para la década de 1920, ya que las agencias abandonaron el concepto a favor de la defensa partidista explícita de los grupos de los que provenían sus comisionados.

items.explanation: The concept of 'the public interest' is inherently contested — different groups in society have genuinely different interests, and regulatory policy inevitably benefits some groups more than others. When a railroad rate commission sets freight rates, it simultaneously determines income distribution between railroads, farmers, consumers, and railroad workers. Claiming to serve 'the public interest' obscures these distributional conflicts without resolving them. Progressive regulatory agencies that claimed to serve 'the public interest' were inevitably making contested political choices about whose interests to prioritize — choices that often reflected the class biases of expert commissioners, the lobbying power of organized interests, and the political pressures of the moment. The concept of 'the public interest' thus served simultaneously as genuine reform motivation and as ideological cover for politically contested distributional choices.
items.explanationEs: El concepto de 'interés público' es inherentemente contestado: diferentes grupos en la sociedad tienen intereses genuinamente diferentes, y la política regulatoria inevitablemente beneficia a algunos grupos más que a otros. Cuando una comisión de tarifas ferroviarias establece las tarifas de flete, simultáneamente determina la distribución del ingreso entre los ferrocarriles, los agricultores, los consumidores y los trabajadores ferroviarios. Afirmar que se sirve al 'interés público' oscurece estos conflictos distributivos sin resolverlos. Las agencias reguladoras progresistas que afirmaban servir al 'interés público' inevitablemente tomaban decisiones políticas controvertidas sobre qué intereses priorizar, decisiones que a menudo reflejaban los sesgos de clase de los comisionados expertos, el poder de lobby de los intereses organizados y las presiones políticas del momento. El concepto de 'interés público' servía así simultáneamente como motivación de reforma genuina y como cobertura ideológica para elecciones distributivas políticamente controvertidas.

items.stem: The Populist movement's Omaha Platform demanded that government ownership or control of railroads. Compare this to the Progressive Era's actual approach of regulatory commissions. Which of the following best evaluates what this difference in approach reveals about the limits of American reform?
items.stemEs: La Plataforma de Omaha del movimiento populista demandaba propiedad o control gubernamental de los ferrocarriles. Compara esto con el enfoque real de la Era Progresista de comisiones reguladoras. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor qué revela esta diferencia de enfoque sobre los límites de la reforma estadounidense?

choices.text: The difference reveals that the Populist demand for government ownership was economically unsound while Progressive regulatory commissions were economically sophisticated — reformers simply learned from Populist mistakes and adopted a more effective approach.
choices.textEs: La diferencia revela que la demanda populista de propiedad gubernamental era económicamente insostenible mientras que las comisiones reguladoras progresistas eran económicamente sofisticadas: los reformistas simplemente aprendieron de los errores populistas y adoptaron un enfoque más efectivo.

choices.text: The difference reveals that Progressive reformers were personally opposed to government ownership of industry for ideological reasons, whereas Populists were philosophically committed to it — the shift reflected a genuine change in reform movement ideology, not political constraints.
choices.textEs: La diferencia revela que los reformistas progresistas se oponían personalmente a la propiedad gubernamental de la industria por razones ideológicas, mientras que los populistas estaban filosóficamente comprometidos con ella: el cambio reflejó un cambio genuino en la ideología del movimiento de reforma, no restricciones políticas.

choices.text: The regulatory compromise reveals that American reform operates within the constraint of capitalist property relations — government ownership directly threatened private property rights that neither major party would challenge, while regulation preserved those rights while adding public oversight.
choices.textEs: El compromiso regulatorio revela que la reforma estadounidense opera dentro de la restricción de las relaciones de propiedad capitalistas: la propiedad gubernamental amenazaba directamente los derechos de propiedad privada que ninguno de los dos partidos principales desafiaría, mientras que la regulación preservaba esos derechos mientras añadía supervisión pública.

choices.text: The difference between Populist and Progressive approaches to railroads reveals that the two movements were in fundamental philosophical opposition with no continuity between them, and that Progressive reformers deliberately rejected the Populist legacy as too radical to be useful.
choices.textEs: La diferencia entre los enfoques populista y progresista de los ferrocarriles revela que los dos movimientos estaban en oposición filosófica fundamental sin continuidad entre ellos, y que los reformistas progresistas rechazaron deliberadamente el legado populista como demasiado radical para ser útil.

items.explanation: The gap between Populist demands for government ownership and the Progressive Era's actual regulatory solution reveals a fundamental constraint of American reform: the boundaries of politically achievable change within capitalist property relations. Government ownership of railroads directly threatened private property rights — a constitutional and cultural threshold that neither major party was willing to cross because it would have required confronting the entire capitalist class. Regulatory commissions, by contrast, preserved private ownership while imposing public oversight — a compromise that left private property rights and profit-making intact. This pattern (regulation rather than nationalization) has recurred throughout American history and reflects both constitutional constraints (protection of private property under due process) and the ideological dominance of market capitalism as the framework within which American politics operates.
items.explanationEs: La brecha entre las demandas populistas de propiedad gubernamental y la solución regulatoria real de la Era Progresista revela una restricción fundamental de la reforma estadounidense: los límites del cambio políticamente alcanzable dentro de las relaciones de propiedad capitalistas. La propiedad gubernamental de los ferrocarriles amenazaba directamente los derechos de propiedad privada, un umbral constitucional y cultural que ninguno de los dos partidos principales estaba dispuesto a cruzar porque habría requerido confrontar a toda la clase capitalista. Las comisiones reguladoras, por el contrario, preservaron la propiedad privada mientras imponían supervisión pública, un compromiso que dejó intactos los derechos de propiedad privada y la obtención de ganancias. Este patrón (regulación en lugar de nacionalización) se ha repetido a lo largo de la historia estadounidense y refleja tanto las restricciones constitucionales (protección de la propiedad privada bajo el debido proceso) como el dominio ideológico del capitalismo de mercado como el marco dentro del cual opera la política estadounidense.

items.stem: The Populist and Progressive movements both emerged partly in response to the economic dislocations of industrialization. Which of the following best evaluates the fundamental difference in how each movement understood the relationship between economic problems and political solutions?
items.stemEs: Los movimientos populista y progresista surgieron en parte en respuesta a las disrupciones económicas de la industrialización. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la diferencia fundamental en cómo cada movimiento entendía la relación entre los problemas económicos y las soluciones políticas?

choices.text: Both movements understood economic problems as requiring the same type of political solution; the difference was only in which specific policies they pursued, not in any fundamental difference in economic or political theory.
choices.textEs: Ambos movimientos entendían los problemas económicos como que requerían el mismo tipo de solución política; la diferencia era solo en qué políticas específicas perseguían, no en ninguna diferencia fundamental en teoría económica o política.

choices.text: Populists understood economic problems as moral failings of individual industrialists that could be corrected by reforming those individuals' character, while Progressives understood them as structural problems requiring institutional reform.
choices.textEs: Los populistas entendían los problemas económicos como fracasos morales de los industrialistas individuales que podían corregirse reformando el carácter de esos individuos, mientras que los progresistas los entendían como problemas estructurales que requerían reforma institucional.

choices.text: Progressives understood economic problems as requiring greater popular democratic control over the economy, while Populists preferred expert-managed solutions that insulated economic policy from direct democratic pressure.
choices.textEs: Los progresistas entendían los problemas económicos como que requerían mayor control democrático popular sobre la economía, mientras que los populistas preferían soluciones gestionadas por expertos que aislaban la política económica de la presión democrática directa.

choices.text: Populism understood economic problems as structural power relationships requiring direct democratic control of key economic institutions; Progressivism understood them as dysfunction within a basically sound system that expert-managed reform could correct while preserving market capitalism.
choices.textEs: El populismo entendía los problemas económicos como relaciones de poder estructurales que requerían control democrático directo de las instituciones económicas clave; el progresismo los entendía como disfunción dentro de un sistema básicamente sólido que la reforma gestionada por expertos podía corregir mientras preservaba el capitalismo de mercado.

items.explanation: Populism understood economic problems as rooted in structural power relationships — monopoly control of money, credit, and transportation — that required direct democratic political power to overcome. Populists sought to give democratic majorities direct control over key economic institutions (government ownership of railroads, government credit through the subtreasury) as the solution. Progressivism understood economic problems as rooted in ignorance, inefficiency, and institutional capture that expert-managed reform could correct while preserving the basic structure of market capitalism. Progressives sought to bring technical knowledge to bear on specific dysfunction within the existing system rather than transforming the fundamental relationship between economic power and political power. This is why Populism was fundamentally more radical than Progressivism despite both responding to similar economic grievances.
items.explanationEs: El populismo entendía los problemas económicos como enraizados en relaciones de poder estructurales, el control monopólico del dinero, el crédito y el transporte, que requerían poder político democrático directo para superarse. Los populistas buscaban dar a las mayorías democráticas control directo sobre instituciones económicas clave (propiedad gubernamental de los ferrocarriles, crédito gubernamental a través de la subtesorería) como solución. El progresismo entendía los problemas económicos como enraizados en la ignorancia, la ineficiencia y la captura institucional que la reforma gestionada por expertos podía corregir mientras preservaba la estructura básica del capitalismo de mercado. Los progresistas buscaban aplicar conocimiento técnico a disfunciones específicas dentro del sistema existente en lugar de transformar la relación fundamental entre el poder económico y el poder político. Por eso el populismo era fundamentalmente más radical que el progresismo a pesar de que ambos respondían a quejas económicas similares.

items.stem: Roosevelt's position in this excerpt is best described as supporting —

choices.text: The complete elimination of all large corporations
A return to small-scale, pre-industrial production
Government regulation while preserving large corporations
Federal ownership of all major industries

items.explanation: Theodore Roosevelt argued that large corporations were an efficient product of modern industry and should be regulated by a strong federal government rather than broken up on principle — his distinction between 'good' and 'bad' trusts. Choice A is wrong because he did not seek to eliminate large corporations as such. Choice D is wrong because he sought federal supervision, not federal ownership. Roosevelt's position became the New Nationalism he ran on in 1912.

items.stem: Ida B. Wells wrote this pamphlet primarily to —

choices.text: Defend the policies of segregation in the South
Promote the migration of African Americans to Liberia
Document and oppose the practice of lynching in the United States
Support women's suffrage at the federal level

items.explanation: Ida B. Wells investigated lynchings and published the evidence in Southern Horrors and A Red Record, showing that the charges used to justify mob killings were usually false and that lynching was a tool of racial and economic control. Choice A is wrong because Wells attacked segregation rather than defending it. Choice B is wrong because emigration to Liberia was a different movement she did not lead. Her data-driven journalism became a model for later civil rights advocacy.

items.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the data in the table?

choices.text: Rural population grew faster than urban population during the period
Most Americans lived in cities throughout the entire period shown
Urban population declined sharply after 1900
The U.S. population became increasingly urban between 1870 and 1920

items.explanation: The table shows the urban share of the population rising steadily between 1870 and 1920, the span in which the census first recorded more Americans living in cities and towns than in rural areas. Choice A is wrong because urban growth outpaced rural growth across the period. Choice B is wrong because a majority did not live in cities for the whole period — that crossover happened near its end. Industrial jobs and immigration were the main drivers of the shift.

items.stem: The transcontinental railroad's completion in 1869 simultaneously drove continental economic integration and catastrophic disruption of Plains Indian nations. Which statement most accurately analyzes the structural relationship between these two consequences rather than treating them as separate phenomena?

choices.text: The railroad created enormous investment wealth for Eastern capitalists while destroying the bison herds Plains tribes depended on for survival, making it both a symbol of industrial progress and an instrument of cultural destruction operating through separate and unconnected mechanisms.

The railroad accelerated western settlement and continental economic integration, but did so by displacing Native nations, facilitating the bison slaughter, and undermining treaty agreements — revealing that industrial development and Indigenous dispossession were structurally inseparable rather than coincidental processes.

The railroad's primary historical significance was economic, generating profits for investors and markets for western agricultural goods, while its effects on Native peoples were largely unintended consequences rather than structural features of the federal land grant and military protection policies tied to its construction.

The transcontinental railroad ultimately failed to deliver promised economic benefits to most western settlers because of monopolistic freight pricing, meaning its primary legacy was the destruction of Native cultures rather than the continental economic transformation its promoters advertised.

items.explanation: The transcontinental railroad required Native dispossession through federal land grants, military protection of construction, government-supported bison extermination, and the settlement wave that followed, making the two processes structurally linked rather than incidentally connected.

items.stem: The Knights of Labor reached peak membership of approximately 700,000 in 1886 then rapidly collapsed after the Haymarket affair, while the American Federation of Labor grew steadily through craft unionism into the 1890s. What does this divergent pattern reveal about the conditions necessary for sustainable labor organization in the Gilded Age industrial economy?

choices.text: The pattern demonstrates that workers preferred craft-based unions because they could achieve wage gains through collective bargaining without the political radicalism that made the Knights of Labor a target of employer campaigns and government repression.

The Knights' collapse showed that unskilled workers lacked the economic leverage to sustain a national labor organization, making craft unionism the only structurally viable strategy for achieving labor gains in the rapidly industrializing late-19th-century economy.

Broad-based inclusive unionism faced structural vulnerabilities in an environment of employer hostility and anti-labor public opinion, while narrowly focused craft unions proved more resilient by concentrating bargaining leverage among skilled workers whose specialized labor was difficult for employers to replace during strikes.

The Haymarket affair's association with anarchism permanently discredited all forms of radical labor organizing, ensuring that any union that pursued political transformation rather than pure wage improvement would inevitably fail regardless of its organizational structure or membership base.

items.explanation: The AFL's strategy of organizing skilled workers in autonomous craft unions provided structural resilience: skilled craftsmen possessed irreplaceable expertise giving them genuine strike leverage, while the Knights' diverse membership including easily replaceable unskilled workers left them vulnerable to employer strikebreaking.

items.stem: Congress passed the Chinese Exclusion Act in 1882 even though Chinese immigrants constituted a tiny fraction of the total American population. What does the intensity of the political response to this relatively small immigrant group most reveal about the forces driving nativist legislation in the Gilded Age?

choices.text: The Chinese Exclusion Act was a proportionate response to genuine labor market displacement in California, where Chinese workers had systematically driven white miners and railroad workers out of available jobs by accepting wages that native-born workers could not survive on.

American nativism in the 1880s was principally driven by racial science theories popularized by academic institutions, which gave working-class voters a scientific vocabulary for expressing what were fundamentally biological fears about Chinese immigrants.

The exclusion act demonstrated that Congress was willing to abandon constitutional equal protection commitments when confronted with sustained regional political pressure from Western states, showing that geographic intensity of political demand could override abstract national legal principles.

The act reveals that nativist politics were driven less by actual economic or demographic impact of Chinese immigration than by racial anxieties, economic insecurity among white workers, and politicians' willingness to scapegoat a legally vulnerable minority group for broader dislocations produced by industrial capitalism.

items.explanation: The disproportionality between the Chinese American population size and the legislative response points toward racial anxiety and political scapegoating as the primary drivers — Chinese immigrants were targeted because they were racially visible, politically powerless, and could serve as convenient symbols of economic anxiety.

items.stem: The People's Party platform of 1892 demanded a graduated income tax, government ownership of railroads and telegraphs, and the direct election of senators. Given that several of these demands were enacted during the Progressive Era, how should the Populists' historical significance most accurately be assessed?

choices.text: The Populists articulated a systemic critique of industrial capitalism that was ahead of its political time — their specific reform demands, though defeated in the 1890s, became the policy template the Progressive movement adopted once middle-class reformers recognized the structural problems the Populists had first diagnosed.

The Populists succeeded primarily in permanently shifting the Democratic Party leftward, as evidenced by William Jennings Bryan's three presidential campaigns, which forced Republicans to address agrarian grievances they might otherwise have ignored until social unrest reached crisis levels.

The rapid adoption of Populist policy ideas by Progressive-era reformers demonstrates that the Populist movement failed on its own terms, since its most important reforms only became law after the movement disbanded and its constituency was absorbed into mainstream party coalitions.

The Populist Party's significance was primarily ideological rather than practical, since Progressives who later enacted similar measures drew intellectual inspiration from European socialist movements rather than from the American agrarian tradition the Populists represented.

items.explanation: The Populists identified the core problems of Gilded Age capitalism and proposed specific remedies that became law within two decades, making their platform both a diagnostic framework and a practical policy road map that shaped the entire Progressive Era reform agenda.

items.stem: How did the outcomes of the Spanish-American War of 1898 most significantly alter the direction of United States foreign policy?

choices.text: The United States adopted a policy of strict neutrality to prevent future entanglement in conflicts involving European colonial powers.
The United States shifted from continental expansion to acquiring overseas territories and projecting power beyond its borders.
The United States abandoned the Monroe Doctrine to pursue cooperative security arrangements with European colonial empires.
The United States prioritized economic treaties over military interventions as a strategy for expanding international influence.

items.explanation: The acquisition of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines, plus the assertion of influence over Cuba, marked a decisive shift from the continental expansion of Manifest Destiny to overseas imperialism and naval power projection.

items.stem: Which best explains why the United States initially maintained neutrality when World War I began in Europe in 1914? H A significant portion of the American population had ethnic and cultural ties to both sides of the conflict, making full support for either alliance politically divisive. B. Most Americans had strong cultural and economic ties to Germany and the Central Powers that made opposing them politically unpopular. C. President Wilson believed the United States military was too unprepared to fight a major European land war. D. Congress had passed binding legislation requiring the United States to remain neutral in all conflicts between European nations. CORRECT ANSWER

choices.text: A significant portion of the American population had ethnic and cultural ties to both sides of the conflict, making full support for either alliance politically divisive.
Most Americans had strong cultural and economic ties to Germany and the Central Powers that made opposing them politically unpopular.
President Wilson believed the United States military was too unprepared to fight a major European land war.
Congress had passed binding legislation requiring the United States to remain neutral in all conflicts between European nations.

items.explanation: Wilson explicitly cited the diverse ethnic loyalties of the American population in calling for neutrality 'in thought as well as deed.' German Americans, Irish Americans, and Anglo Americans all had competing sympathies that made alignment with either side politically untenable.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph, taken around 1902, shows a group of immigrants arriving at the Ellis Island immigration station in New York Harbor. The individuals carry bundles and luggage and appear to be waiting in line for processing.

(Photograph, c. 1902. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.)

How did the wave of immigration depicted in this photograph contribute to BOTH economic growth and social tension in the United States?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo contribuyó la ola de inmigración representada en esta fotografía TANTO al crecimiento económico como a la tensión social?

choices.text: Immigrants provided an essential industrial labor force while also provoking nativist movements that demanded immigration restrictions
Immigrants immediately gained political power through voting, which caused resentment among established political parties
Immigrants refused to adopt American customs, which forced the government to create separate legal systems for different ethnic groups
Immigrants competed primarily with enslaved workers for agricultural jobs, which increased sectional tensions

items.explanation: Mass immigration provided cheap labor that fueled industrial expansion while simultaneously provoking nativist backlash, leading to restrictive legislation like the Chinese Exclusion Act (1882) and the Immigration Act of 1924.
items.explanationEs: La inmigración masiva proporcionó mano de obra barata que impulsó la expansión industrial y provocó reacciones nativistas.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows Ida Tarbell, author of The History of the Standard Oil Company (1904).

(Photograph, c. 1904. Public Domain.)

To what extent did muckraking journalism reshape the relationship between the federal government and big business during the Progressive Era?
items.stemEs: ¿En qué medida el periodismo muckraker reconfiguró la relación entre el gobierno federal y las grandes empresas?

choices.text: Muckrakers' investigations provided evidence that enabled landmark legislation such as the Sherman and Clayton Antitrust Acts and the creation of the Federal Trade Commission
Muckraking had no lasting impact because the government continued to support monopolies throughout the twentieth century
Muckrakers replaced the government as the primary regulator of business practices
Their work only affected the oil industry and did not extend to other sectors of the economy

items.explanation: Muckraking journalism fundamentally changed federal-business relations by documenting abuses that demanded government response. Tarbell's Standard Oil exposé supported antitrust enforcement; Upton Sinclair's The Jungle led to the Pure Food and Drug Act (1906); Lincoln Steffens exposed municipal corruption. Together, these investigations built the case for the regulatory state.
items.explanationEs: El periodismo muckraker cambió las relaciones gobierno-empresa documentando abusos que exigieron respuesta federal.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows the 1913 women's suffrage parade in Washington, D.C.

(Photograph, 1913. Public Domain.)

Analyze how the strategies used by the women's suffrage movement, as illustrated by this photograph, reflected broader patterns of Progressive Era reform.
items.stemEs: Analice cómo las estrategias del movimiento sufragista reflejaron patrones más amplios de la reforma de la Era Progresista.

choices.text: The suffrage movement was unrelated to other Progressive Era reforms and operated in isolation
Progressive reformers opposed women's suffrage because they believed reform should focus only on economic issues
Like other Progressive movements, suffragists used public demonstrations, media campaigns, and political lobbying to build grassroots support for democratic reforms
The suffrage movement relied entirely on court decisions and never engaged in public protest

items.explanation: The suffrage movement exemplified Progressive Era reform strategies: grassroots organizing, public demonstrations, investigative journalism, and legislative lobbying. Like temperance advocates, labor organizers, and civil rights activists, suffragists combined moral arguments with practical political action. Their success with the 19th Amendment (1920) demonstrated how sustained public pressure could achieve constitutional change.
items.explanationEs: El movimiento sufragista ejemplificó las estrategias de reforma progresista: organización popular, manifestaciones y cabildeo legislativo.

items.stem: Jane Addams co-founded Hull House in Chicago in 1889 as a residential reform center embedded within an immigrant working-class neighborhood. How does the settlement house movement's methodology of living among the poor represent a theoretically significant departure from traditional charitable organization approaches to urban poverty?

choices.text: The settlement house approach was primarily significant for its political outputs, since it created a dense network of reform-minded residents who could lobby state legislatures for labor and housing regulations more effectively than geographically dispersed charitable organizations.

By training college-educated women for professional social work careers, settlement houses uniquely addressed middle-class female unemployment while targeting urban poverty, creating an institution that benefited two marginalized groups through a single organizational structure.

The settlement house model challenged the dominant charity framework's assumption that poverty resulted from individual moral failure by embedding reformers within poor communities, systematically gathering empirical data on structural causes, and using that evidence to advocate for legislative remedies rather than individual moral improvement.

Settlement houses were primarily significant as spaces where immigrant communities could preserve cultural traditions and native languages while assimilating at their own pace, making cultural mediation rather than structural poverty reform their primary social contribution.

items.explanation: Hull House and similar settlements challenged the moral reform tradition by treating poverty as a structural condition shaped by unsafe housing, exploitative labor, and inadequate public services — a methodological shift from individual charity to social science investigation that laid the foundation for Progressive Era reform legislation. Unit 3: Imperialism & World War I, 1890–1920 (US.19–US.27)

items.stem: Which best explains why Tennessee's ratification of the 19th Amendment in August 1920 was historically decisive?

choices.text: Tennessee was the first Southern state to support women's suffrage, signaling that Progressive-era reform had penetrated the Deep South.
Tennessee's vote resolved a constitutional dispute over whether a state legislature could reverse a prior rejection of a federal amendment.
Tennessee's ratification confirmed that women's suffrage had broad bipartisan support across all regions of the country.
Tennessee provided the 36th and final ratification required to add the amendment to the Constitution, making it the deciding vote.

items.explanation: Three-fourths of states (36 of 48) were required for ratification. Tennessee's vote, cast by Harry T. Burn after his mother's letter urging him to 'be a good boy,' provided the exact threshold needed to add the 19th Amendment to the Constitution.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from Andrew Carnegie's essay "The Gospel of Wealth" (1889), published in the North American Review (available through the Library of Congress digital collections):

"The problem of our age is the proper administration of wealth, so that the ties of brotherhood may still bind together the rich and poor in harmonious relationship. The conditions of human life have not only been changed, but revolutionized, within the past few hundred years. In former days there was little difference between the dwelling, dress, food, and environment of the chief and those of his retainers... Today the world obtains commodities of excellent quality at prices which even the generation preceding this would have deemed incredible. The poor enjoy what the rich could not before afford. What were the luxuries have become the necessaries of life."
— Andrew Carnegie, "The Gospel of Wealth," North American Review, June 1889

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of the Gilded Age economy (US.08) and the rise of industrial monopolies (US.12), write a constructed response that:
1. States a clear CLAIM about whether Carnegie's argument adequately justifies the extreme concentration of industrial wealth in the hands of a few individuals.
2. Provides at least TWO pieces of specific EVIDENCE — one drawn from the excerpt and one from your knowledge of Carnegie's business practices, vertical integration, or the broader conditions of Gilded Age workers — to support your claim.
3. Offers REASONING that explains how your evidence connects to your claim AND addresses the long-term consequences of industrial consolidation for American workers, consumers, and democratic governance.

Your response should be one to two well-developed paragraphs synthesizing both the primary source and your historical knowledge.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del ensayo de Andrew Carnegie "El Evangelio de la Riqueza" (1889), publicado en la North American Review (disponible en las colecciones digitales de la Biblioteca del Congreso):

"El problema de nuestra época es la correcta administración de la riqueza, de modo que los lazos de fraternidad aún puedan unir al rico y al pobre en una relación armoniosa. Las condiciones de vida humana no solo han cambiado, sino que han sido revolucionadas en los últimos cientos de años. En tiempos pasados había poca diferencia entre la vivienda, el vestido, la comida y el entorno del jefe y los de sus subordinados... Hoy el mundo obtiene artículos de excelente calidad a precios que incluso la generación anterior a esta habría considerado increíbles. Los pobres disfrutan lo que los ricos no podían permitirse antes. Lo que eran lujos se han convertido en necesidades de vida."
— Andrew Carnegie, "El Evangelio de la Riqueza," North American Review, junio de 1889

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la economía de la Era Dorada (US.08) y el surgimiento de los monopolios industriales (US.12), escribe una respuesta construida que:
1. Establezca un ARGUMENTO claro sobre si el razonamiento de Carnegie justifica adecuadamente la extrema concentración de riqueza industrial en manos de unos pocos.
2. Proporcione al menos DOS piezas de EVIDENCIA específica — una del fragmento y una de tu conocimiento sobre las prácticas comerciales de Carnegie, la integración vertical, o las condiciones generales de los trabajadores de la Era Dorada — para apoyar tu argumento.

items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response states a clear claim — such as: Carnegie's argument is fundamentally self-serving and fails to account for the structural exploitation that made his wealth possible. The student uses the excerpt's claim that industrialization benefits "the poor" as evidence Carnegie framed exploitation as philanthropy, then counters with knowledge-based evidence: Carnegie Steel's 12-hour workdays, the 1892 Homestead Strike (in which Carnegie used Pinkerton agents against striking workers), or his use of vertical integration to eliminate competition and suppress wages. Strong reasoning connects these facts to the claim by explaining that the "harmonious relationship" Carnegie described was structurally impossible when one party controlled wages, working conditions, and prices. The response concludes by noting long-term consequences: the Sherman Antitrust Act (1890), Progressive-era trust-busting, and ongoing debates about corporate power in democracy.

Read the following excerpt from the Report of the Factory Investigating Commission of the State of New York (1912), established in the aftermath of the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire of March 25, 1911 (available through the New York State Library and the National Archives):

"The fire at the Triangle Waist Company demonstrated beyond all question that the present system of factory inspection is wholly inadequate for the protection of those employed in manufacturing establishments... In this fire 146 persons lost their lives, nearly all of them young women and girls employed in garment-making. Exit doors were found locked. Fire escapes were inadequate. No sprinkler system existed. The owners had given no fire drills. The investigation has shown that this tragedy was not an accident — it was the predictable result of unchecked industrial power operating without legislative constraint."
— New York Factory Investigating Commission, Preliminary Report, 1912

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of the labor movement (US.11) and government regulation of industry (US.13), write a constructed response that:
1. States a CLAIM about whether the labor movement or government regulation was the more effective force for protecting American workers during the Progressive Era.
2. Provides at least TWO pieces of specific EVIDENCE — one from the excerpt and one from your knowledge of labor unions, strikes, or legislative reforms — to support your claim.
3. Offers REASONING that explains the relationship between labor organizing and government action, addressing why one mechanism proved more durable than the other in protecting worker rights.

Your response should be one to two well-developed paragraphs.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del Informe de la Comisión de Investigación de Fábricas del Estado de Nueva York (1912), establecida tras el incendio de la fábrica Triangle Shirtwaist el 25 de marzo de 1911 (disponible en la Biblioteca del Estado de Nueva York y los Archivos Nacionales):

"El incendio en Triangle Waist Company demostró sin lugar a dudas que el sistema actual de inspección de fábricas es completamente inadecuado para proteger a los empleados en establecimientos manufactureros... En este incendio perdieron la vida 146 personas, casi todas mujeres jóvenes y niñas empleadas en la confección de prendas. Se encontraron puertas de salida cerradas con llave. Las escaleras de incendios eran inadecuadas. No existía sistema de rociadores. Los propietarios no habían realizado simulacros de incendio. La investigación ha demostrado que esta tragedia no fue un accidente — fue el resultado predecible del poder industrial no controlado que operaba sin restricciones legislativas."
— Comisión de Investigación de Fábricas de Nueva York, Informe Preliminar, 1912

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento del movimiento obrero (US.11) y la regulación gubernamental de la industria (US.13), escribe una respuesta construida que:
1. Establezca un ARGUMENTO sobre si el movimiento obrero o la regulación gubernamental fue la fuerza más efectiva para proteger a los trabajadores estadounidenses durante la Era Progresista.
2. Proporcione al menos DOS piezas de EVIDENCIA específica — una del fragmento y una de tu conocimiento sobre sindicatos laborales, huelgas o reformas legislativas.
3. Ofrezca RAZONAMIENTO que explique la relación entre la organización laboral y la acción gubernamental, abordando por qué un mecanismo resultó más duradero que el otro.

Tu respuesta debe ser de uno a dos párrafos bien desarrollados.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response might claim that government regulation ultimately proved more durable because labor organizing alone was vulnerable to suppression, while legislation created structural protections. The student uses the commission report's conclusion — that the disaster was "the predictable result of unchecked industrial power operating without legislative constraint" — as evidence that the absence of regulation (not worker organization) was the primary failure. Outside knowledge evidence might include: the International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union (ILGWU) organizing drives; the 1909 "Uprising of the 20,000" shirtwaist workers' strike; and the post-fire passage of New York labor laws (1911-1913) that became a national model. Strong reasoning explains that the AFL and early unions could not compel employers to improve safety conditions without legal backing, and that the Triangle fire galvanized political will for state intervention, demonstrating that labor action and government regulation were complementary rather than competing forces.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from Theodore Roosevelt, "The New Nationalism" speech delivered at Osawatomie, Kansas, August 31, 1910, and published by the National Archives:

"The man who wrongly holds that every human right is secondary to his profit must now give way to the advocate of human welfare, who rightly maintains that every man holds his property subject to the general right of the community to regulate its use to whatever degree the public welfare may require it. The New Nationalism puts the national need before sectional or personal advantage. It is impatient of the utter confusion that results from local legislatures attempting to treat national issues as local issues. It is still more impatient of the impotence which springs from overdivision of governmental powers, the impotence which makes it possible for local selfishness or for legal cunning, hired by wealthy special interests, to bring national activities to a deadlock."
— Theodore Roosevelt, "The New Nationalism," Osawatomie, Kansas, August 31, 1910

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of Theodore Roosevelt's progressivism (US.18) and government regulation of industry (US.13), write a constructed response that:
1. States a CLAIM about the extent to which Roosevelt's "New Nationalism" represented a genuine expansion of federal regulatory power or was primarily rhetorical positioning.
2. Provides at least TWO pieces of specific EVIDENCE — one from the excerpt and one from your knowledge of Roosevelt's specific regulatory actions as president or the legislative legacy of his progressivism — to support your claim.
3. Provides REASONING that evaluates the long-term tension between expanded federal authority and constitutional limits on executive power, connecting Roosevelt's vision to specific outcomes during or after his presidency.

Your response should be one to two well-developed paragraphs.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del discurso de Theodore Roosevelt, "El Nuevo Nacionalismo," pronunciado en Osawatomie, Kansas, el 31 de agosto de 1910, y publicado por los Archivos Nacionales:

"El hombre que sostiene erróneamente que cada derecho humano es secundario a su ganancia debe ahora ceder el paso al defensor del bienestar humano, quien mantiene correctamente que cada hombre posee su propiedad sujeta al derecho general de la comunidad de regular su uso hasta el grado que el bienestar público pueda requerirlo. El Nuevo Nacionalismo antepone la necesidad nacional a la ventaja sectorial o personal. Es impaciente con la total confusión que resulta de las legislaturas locales que intentan tratar los asuntos nacionales como asuntos locales. Es aún más impaciente con la impotencia que surge de la excesiva división de los poderes gubernamentales, la impotencia que hace posible que el egoísmo local o la astucia legal, contratada por intereses especiales adinerados, paralice las actividades nacionales."
— Theodore Roosevelt, "El Nuevo Nacionalismo," Osawatomie, Kansas, 31 de agosto de 1910

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento del progresismo de Theodore Roosevelt (US.18) y la regulación gubernamental de la industria (US.13), escribe una respuesta construida que:
1. Establezca un ARGUMENTO sobre en qué medida el "Nuevo Nacionalismo" de Roosevelt representó una expansión genuina del poder regulador federal o fue principalmente un posicionamiento retórico.

Tu respuesta debe ser de uno a dos párrafos bien desarrollados.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response claims that Roosevelt's New Nationalism was both substantive and rhetorical — it built on real regulatory precedents from his presidency but also signaled an ambition that exceeded what his actual record achieved. The student uses the excerpt's argument that property rights are "subject to the general right of the community" as evidence that Roosevelt articulated a genuinely expansive theory of federal authority. Outside knowledge evidence includes: the Bureau of Corporations (1903), the Hepburn Act (1906) strengthening ICC railroad regulation, the Pure Food and Drug Act (1906), the dissolution of Northern Securities Company (1902) as the first major trust-bust, and the designation of 150 million acres of national forest reserves. Strong reasoning notes the tension between Roosevelt's rhetoric and constitutional constraints: the Supreme Court and Congress limited regulatory expansion, and Roosevelt's inability to translate New Nationalism into legislation in 1912 (his Progressive Party campaign) revealed the limits of executive progressivism without legislative backing.

Read the following excerpt from Jane Addams, Twenty Years at Hull-House (1910), available in the public domain through the Library of Congress and Project Gutenberg:

"Hull-House was established not as a social experiment, but because of the sincere conviction that the first step toward meeting the social problem of the city required that its workers should live in the neighborhood... We were neighbors to these immigrants; it was as neighbors that we tried to understand them. In those early years I saw daily the contrast between the industrial claim upon workers — the twelve and even fourteen hours a day in the shop — and the claim of the city upon its children — the swarms of children in the streets, the obvious need for kindergartens and playgrounds and boys' clubs. I saw that the modern city was obliged to perform the functions for which families and neighborhoods had formerly been responsible."
— Jane Addams, Twenty Years at Hull-House, 1910

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of urbanization challenges (US.10) and the labor movement (US.11), write a constructed response that:

3. Provides REASONING that evaluates the settlement house model as a reform strategy and connects it to the larger debate about whether Progressive Era reform was fundamentally structural or palliative.

Your response should be one to two well-developed paragraphs.

"Hull-House se estableció no como un experimento social, sino por la convicción sincera de que el primer paso hacia la resolución del problema social de la ciudad requería que sus trabajadores vivieran en el vecindario... Éramos vecinos de estos inmigrantes; fue como vecinos que intentamos comprenderlos. En esos primeros años vi diariamente el contraste entre la exigencia industrial sobre los trabajadores — las doce e incluso catorce horas al día en el taller — y la exigencia de la ciudad sobre sus hijos — los enjambres de niños en las calles, la obvia necesidad de jardines de infantes y parques de juegos y clubes para chicos. Vi que la ciudad moderna estaba obligada a realizar las funciones de las que antes eran responsables las familias y los vecindarios."
— Jane Addams, Veinte Años en Hull-House, 1910

items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response takes a nuanced position: the settlement house movement was both palliative and structurally oriented, but its structural impact was ultimately limited by class dynamics and the priorities of middle-class reformers. The response connects to the broader Progressive Era debate: reform that provided services without addressing structural economic power left the fundamental causes of poverty in place.

items.stem:
DOCUMENT-BASED QUESTION

Directions: The following question is based on the three documents below. Analyze each document using the HIPP framework (Historical context, Intended audience, Purpose, Point of view). Then construct a well-organized argument in response to the prompt.

PROMPT: Using all three documents and your knowledge of the Gilded Age, evaluate the following claim: "The rapid industrialization of the United States between 1877 and 1900 created prosperity for some Americans while systematically exploiting others, and the mechanisms workers and government used to respond were fundamentally inadequate to address the structural inequality industrialization produced."

Construct an argument that agrees, disagrees, or qualifies this claim using evidence from all three documents and at least two additional pieces of outside historical knowledge. Your response should address the perspectives of at least two groups — industrial workers, industrialists, or policymakers — and evaluate the effectiveness of their strategies.

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT 1
Source: Andrew Carnegie, "The Gospel of Wealth," North American Review, June 1889. Available through the Library of Congress digital collections.

"The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced. Such, in my opinion, is the true Gospel concerning Wealth, obedient to which is the duty of the man of Wealth: First, to set an example of modest, unostentatious living, shunning display or extravagance; to provide moderately for the legitimate wants of those dependent upon him; and after doing so to consider all surplus revenues which come to him simply as trust funds, which he is called upon to administer, and strictly bound as a matter of duty to administer in the manner which, in his judgment, is best calculated to produce the most beneficial results for the community."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT 2
Source: Samuel Gompers, Report to the American Federation of Labor Convention, December 1890. Available through the Library of Congress, American Memory collection.

"There is not a man here who has not felt the degradation of being compelled to work more hours than human endurance can well bear, and at wages insufficient to maintain himself and his family in anything approaching comfort and decency. The American Federation of Labor declares that the eight-hour workday is not a demand of idleness — it is a demand for life. A man who works twelve or fourteen hours has no time to be a citizen, a father, or a human being. We do not demand charity from the rich. We demand justice from the system."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT 3
Source: Sherman Antitrust Act, Section 1, United States Congress, July 2, 1890. Available through the National Archives and Records Administration.

"Every contract, combination in the form of trust or otherwise, or conspiracy, in restraint of trade or commerce among the several States, or with foreign nations, is declared to be illegal. Every person who shall make any contract or engage in any combination or conspiracy hereby declared to be illegal shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, on conviction thereof, shall be punished by fine not exceeding five thousand dollars, or by imprisonment not exceeding one year, or by both said punishments, in the discretion of the court."

─────────────────────────────────────────

Remember to: (1) Apply HIPP analysis to each document. (2) Construct a clear argument that responds to the prompt. (3) Use evidence from all three documents. (4) Incorporate at least two outside historical facts not mentioned in the documents.
