Tu respuesta debe: (1) presentar una afirmación defendible sobre el debate de la justificación; (2) usar evidencia específica de la campaña del Pacífico, el costo proyectado de la Operación Downfall y las condiciones en el momento del bombardeo; (3) razonar a través de las consecuencias a largo plazo — la carrera armamentística nuclear de la Guerra Fría, el principio de disuasión y los esfuerzos internacionales para controlar las armas nucleares. Sintetiza a través de US.55 y US.59 (Guerra Fría).
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response will: (1) Claim: A defensible claim (either direction) — e.g., The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, while militarily effective in ending the Pacific war without a land invasion, opened a nuclear era whose long-term costs — arms race, proliferation, deterrence doctrine — arguably outweighed the short-term military savings. OR: The bombings were justified given the projected casualties of Operation Downfall and Japan's demonstrated willingness to fight to the last. The response must argue a position, not merely describe both sides. (2) Evidence: Manhattan Project — $2 billion, 130,000 workers, Los Alamos; Trinity test (July 16, 1945); Hiroshima (August 6, ~80,000 immediate dead); Nagasaki (August 9, ~40,000 immediate dead); Japan's surrender (August 15); Operation Downfall projections (500,000–1 million U.S. casualties); Soviet entry into the Pacific war (August 8) as alternative factor; Truman's framing of Hiroshima as 'Army base' (not civilian city). (3) Reasoning: Truman's announcement frames the bomb as a military weapon against a military target — but Hiroshima was a city of 350,000 civilians. Long-term: Soviet atomic test (1949) began the nuclear arms race (US.59); deterrence doctrine shaped Cold War strategy for 45 years; nuclear non-proliferation treaty (1968) as international response.

Rhetorical analysis of Truman's address present (e.g., 'Army base' framing). Cross-standard synthesis (US.55 → US.59) demonstrated.

items.stem:
Analyze the following three primary source excerpts and write a document-based essay that argues whether the policy of appeasement and American isolationism made World War II inevitable.

DOCUMENT A: Excerpt from the Atlantic Charter, signed by FDR and Winston Churchill, August 14, 1941 (National Archives, public domain):
"First, their countries seek no aggrandizement, territorial or other; Second, they desire to see no territorial changes that do not accord with the freely expressed wishes of the peoples concerned; Third, they respect the right of all peoples to choose the form of government under which they will live..."

DOCUMENT B: Excerpt from the Neutrality Act of 1937, U.S. Congress (Avalon Project, Yale Law School, public domain):
"Whenever the President shall find that there exists a state of war between, or among, two or more foreign states, the President shall proclaim such fact, and it shall thereafter be unlawful to export, or attempt to export, or cause to be exported, arms, ammunition, or implements of war from any place in the United States to any belligerent state..."

DOCUMENT C: Excerpt from FDR's 'Arsenal of Democracy' Fireside Chat, December 29, 1940 (Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library; public domain government record):
"The Nazi masters of Germany have made it clear that they intend not only to dominate all life and thought in their own country, but also to enslave the whole of Europe, and then to use the resources of Europe to dominate the rest of the world... If Great Britain goes down, the Axis powers will control the continents of Europe, Asia, Africa... and they will be in a position to bring enormous military and naval resources against this hemisphere."

Using HIPP (Historical context, Intended audience, Purpose, Point of view) analysis for each document and your knowledge of U.S. foreign policy from 1935 to 1941, construct an argument that evaluates the relationship between American isolationism, the failure of international response to fascist aggression, and the conditions that made a global war both predictable and avoidable. Address how FDR's evolving rhetoric in Documents A and C contrasts with the formal neutrality of Document B.
items.stemEs:
Analiza los siguientes tres extractos de fuentes primarias y escribe un ensayo basado en documentos que argumente si la política de apaciguamiento y el aislacionismo americano hicieron inevitable la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

DOCUMENTO A: Extracto de la Carta del Atlántico, firmada por FDR y Winston Churchill, 14 de agosto de 1941 (Archivo Nacional, dominio público):
"Primero, sus países no buscan agrandamiento, territorial ni de otro tipo; Segundo, desean no ver cambios territoriales que no concuerden con los deseos libremente expresados de los pueblos interesados; Tercero, respetan el derecho de todos los pueblos a elegir la forma de gobierno bajo la cual vivirán..."

DOCUMENTO B: Extracto de la Ley de Neutralidad de 1937, Congreso de EE.UU. (Proyecto Avalon, Escuela de Derecho de Yale, dominio público):
"Cuando el Presidente considere que existe un estado de guerra entre dos o más estados extranjeros, proclamará tal hecho, y desde entonces será ilegal exportar, o intentar exportar, o hacer exportar, armas, municiones o implementos de guerra desde cualquier lugar de los Estados Unidos a cualquier estado beligerante..."

DOCUMENTO C: Extracto del Chat de Chimenea de FDR 'Arsenal de la Democracia', 29 de diciembre de 1940 (Biblioteca Presidencial de Franklin D. Roosevelt; registro gubernamental de dominio público):
"Los maestros nazis de Alemania han dejado en claro que pretenden no solo dominar toda vida y pensamiento en su propio país, sino también esclavizar a toda Europa, y luego usar los recursos de Europa para dominar el resto del mundo... Si Gran Bretaña cae, las potencias del Eje controlarán los continentes de Europa, Asia, África... y estarán en posición de traer enormes recursos militares y navales contra este hemisferio."

Usando el análisis HIPP (Contexto histórico, Audiencia prevista, Propósito, Punto de vista) para cada documento y tu conocimiento de la política exterior de EE.UU. de 1935 a 1941, construye un argumento que evalúe la relación entre el aislacionismo americano, el fracaso de la respuesta internacional a la agresión fascista y las condiciones que hicieron que una guerra mundial fuera tanto predecible como evitable. Aborda cómo la retórica evolutiva de FDR en los Documentos A y C contrasta con la neutralidad formal del Documento B.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score (6/6) response will: THESIS: Present a historically defensible claim that goes beyond restating the documents — e.g., 'American isolationism, while reflecting genuine public sentiment after WWI, functionally enabled fascist aggression by removing the credible threat of U.S. military intervention, making the war highly likely though not formally inevitable.' DOCUMENT ANALYSIS (all three with HIPP): Doc A (Atlantic Charter) — Historical context: U.S. still formally neutral but increasingly aligned; Audience: Allied nations and U.S. public; Purpose: articulate shared democratic values to justify growing U.S. involvement; POV: FDR and Churchill as leaders of threatened democracies. Doc B (Neutrality Act 1937) — Context: U.S. domestic isolationist sentiment post-WWI and during Depression; Audience: Congress and American voters; Purpose: legally prohibit arms sales to belligerents; POV: isolationist-dominated Congress. Doc C (Arsenal of Democracy) — Context: Britain under Blitz, France fallen; Audience: American radio audience; Purpose: shift public opinion toward intervention without declaring war; POV: FDR urgently warning of strategic threat. EVIDENCE BEYOND DOCS: Munich Agreement (1938); Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact (1939); Germany's invasion of Poland; Lend-Lease (1941); America First movement. SYNTHESIS: The three documents together reveal the tension within U.S. policy — formal neutrality (Doc B) vs. ideological alignment (Docs A, C) — showing a policy that was internally inconsistent and increasingly untenable.

SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Sophisticated historically defensible thesis. All three documents analyzed using HIPP with accuracy — historical context, audience, purpose, and point of view for each. At least three pieces of outside evidence (beyond the documents). Demonstrates why isolationism enabled aggression AND engages with the counterargument (could war have been avoided). Synthesizes across all documents and outside knowledge. Writing is organized, precise, and historically specific.
5 - Advanced: Clear thesis. All three documents analyzed with at least three HIPP elements each. Two pieces of outside evidence. Addresses the tension between documents A/C and B. Mostly organized.
4 - Proficient: Clear thesis. Two documents analyzed with HIPP. One to two pieces of outside evidence. Argument present but some analytical gaps. Organized.
3 - Adequate: Thesis present but vague. One to two documents analyzed, HIPP partially applied. One piece of outside evidence. Argument partially developed.
2 - Developing: Minimal thesis. Documents described but not analyzed. Little outside evidence. Argument not fully developed.
1 - Beginning: No thesis or off-topic thesis. One document mentioned. No HIPP analysis. No outside evidence.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Doc A — HIPP reveals FDR's ideological commitment to democratic principles before formal war entry; Doc B — HIPP reveals domestic political constraints on executive action; Doc C — HIPP reveals FDR's rhetorical strategy of strategic self-interest argument (not idealism) to shift isolationist public.
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Munich Agreement (September 1938); Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact (August 1939); German invasion of Poland (September 1939); Fall of France (June 1940); Lend-Lease Act (March 1941); America First Committee; Pearl Harbor (December 1941).
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: Tesis sofisticada y históricamente defendible. Los tres documentos analizados usando HIPP con precisión — contexto histórico, audiencia, propósito y punto de vista para cada uno. Al menos tres piezas de evidencia externa (más allá de los documentos). Demuestra por qué el aislacionismo habilitó la agresión Y aborda el contraargumento (¿podría haberse evitado la guerra?). Sintetiza a través de todos los documentos y el conocimiento externo. La escritura es organizada, precisa e históricamente específica.
5 - Avanzado: Tesis clara. Los tres documentos analizados con al menos tres elementos HIPP cada uno. Dos piezas de evidencia externa. Aborda la tensión entre los documentos A/C y B. Mayormente organizado.
4 - Competente: Tesis clara. Dos documentos analizados con HIPP. Una a dos piezas de evidencia externa. Argumento presente pero con algunas lagunas analíticas. Organizado.
3 - Adecuado: Tesis presente pero vaga. Uno a dos documentos analizados, HIPP parcialmente aplicado. Una pieza de evidencia externa. Argumento parcialmente desarrollado.
2 - En desarrollo: Tesis mínima. Documentos descritos pero no analizados. Poca evidencia externa. Argumento no completamente desarrollado.
1 - Inicial: Sin tesis o tesis fuera del tema. Un documento mencionado. Sin análisis HIPP. Sin evidencia externa.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EXPECTATIVAS DE ANÁLISIS DE DOCUMENTOS: Doc A — HIPP revela el compromiso ideológico de FDR con los principios democráticos antes de la entrada formal en la guerra; Doc B — HIPP revela las restricciones políticas internas sobre la acción ejecutiva; Doc C — HIPP revela la estrategia retórica de FDR del argumento de interés estratégico propio (no idealismo) para cambiar al público aislacionista.
EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Acuerdo de Múnich (septiembre de 1938); Pacto Molotov-Ribbentrop (agosto de 1939); invasión alemana de Polonia (septiembre de 1939); caída de Francia (junio de 1940); Ley de Préstamo y Arriendo (marzo de 1941); Comité America First; Pearl Harbor (diciembre de 1941).

items.stem:
Analyze the following two primary source excerpts and construct a document-based argument evaluating the decision to use atomic weapons against Japan in August 1945.

DOCUMENT A: Excerpt from President Harry S. Truman's radio address to the nation, August 6, 1945 (Public Papers of the Presidents, 1945; public domain):
"Sixteen hours ago an American airplane dropped one bomb on Hiroshima, an important Japanese Army base. That bomb had more power than 20,000 tons of T.N.T... The Japanese began the war from the air at Pearl Harbor. They have been repaid many fold. And the end is not yet. With this bomb we have now added a new and revolutionary increase in destruction to supplement the growing power of our armed forces."

DOCUMENT B: Excerpt from the Potsdam Declaration, issued by the United States, United Kingdom, and Republic of China, July 26, 1945 (U.S. Department of State, 1945; National Archives, public domain):
"We call upon the government of Japan to proclaim now the unconditional surrender of all Japanese armed forces... The alternative for Japan is prompt and utter destruction... Following are our terms. We will not deviate from them. There are no alternatives. We shall brook no delay."

Using HIPP analysis for each document and your knowledge of the Pacific Theater and the atomic bomb decision, construct an argument evaluating whether the atomic bombings were militarily justified and morally defensible. Your argument must address: (1) what each document reveals about the strategic and rhetorical framing of the atomic decision; (2) what the Potsdam Declaration's ultimatum reveals about Japan's perceived options before the bombings; (3) the long-term consequences — the nuclear arms race, deterrence doctrine, and international efforts to limit nuclear weapons. Include at least two pieces of outside evidence.
items.stemEs:
Analiza los siguientes dos extractos de fuentes primarias y construye un argumento basado en documentos que evalúe la decisión de usar armas atómicas contra Japón en agosto de 1945.

DOCUMENTO A: Extracto del discurso radial del presidente Harry S. Truman a la nación, 6 de agosto de 1945 (Documentos Públicos de los Presidentes, 1945; dominio público):
"Hace dieciséis horas, un avión estadounidense lanzó una bomba sobre Hiroshima, una importante base del ejército japonés. Esa bomba tenía más potencia que 20.000 toneladas de T.N.T... Los japoneses comenzaron la guerra desde el aire en Pearl Harbor. Han sido recompensados muchas veces. Y el final aún no ha llegado. Con esta bomba hemos añadido ahora un nuevo y revolucionario aumento en la destrucción para complementar el creciente poder de nuestras fuerzas armadas."

DOCUMENTO B: Extracto de la Declaración de Potsdam, emitida por los Estados Unidos, el Reino Unido y la República de China, 26 de julio de 1945 (Departamento de Estado de EE.UU., 1945; Archivo Nacional, dominio público):
"Hacemos un llamado al gobierno de Japón para que proclame ahora la rendición incondicional de todas las fuerzas armadas japonesas... La alternativa para Japón es la destrucción inmediata y total... Los siguientes son nuestros términos. No nos desviaremos de ellos. No hay alternativas. No toleraremos ningún retraso."

Usando el análisis HIPP para cada documento y tu conocimiento del Teatro del Pacífico y la decisión de la bomba atómica, construye un argumento que evalúe si los bombardeos atómicos estaban militarmente justificados y eran moralmente defendibles. Tu argumento debe abordar: (1) qué revela cada documento sobre el encuadre estratégico y retórico de la decisión atómica; (2) qué revela el ultimátum de la Declaración de Potsdam sobre las opciones percibidas de Japón antes de los bombardeos; (3) las consecuencias a largo plazo — la carrera armamentística nuclear, la doctrina de disuasión y los esfuerzos internacionales para limitar las armas nucleares. Incluye al menos dos piezas de evidencia externa.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score (6/6) response will: THESIS: A defensible and sophisticated claim — e.g., 'The pairing of the Potsdam Declaration and Truman's announcement reveals the atomic decision as both a military calculation (ending the Pacific war without a land invasion) and a strategic communication act — but Truman's framing of Hiroshima as a "military base" rather than a city of civilians exposed the moral evasion at the heart of the justification, an evasion whose long-term cost was a nuclear arms race that shaped the next half-century.' HIPP — Doc A: Context: war in Pacific, Japan refusing to surrender after Potsdam; Audience: American public; Purpose: justify atomic use as military retaliation (Pearl Harbor framing) and industrial achievement; POV: Truman as war president managing public perception — notably calls Hiroshima 'an important Japanese Army base' not a city. HIPP — Doc B: Context: two weeks before bombings, war ongoing; Audience: Japanese government and public; Purpose: offer final ultimatum before using atomic bomb; POV: Allied powers warning of 'prompt and utter destruction' — deliberately vague about the nature of that destruction. OUTSIDE EVIDENCE: Iwo Jima (6,800 U.S. dead in 36 days); Operation Downfall projections; Soviet entry into Pacific (August 8); Japan's surrender (August 15); Soviet atomic test (1949) beginning arms race; NPT (1968). SYNTHESIS: Potsdam (Doc B) was the last diplomatic step; Truman's announcement (Doc A) was the first step in nuclear age justification. Together they reveal the transition from WWII military decision to Cold War strategic paradigm.

Long-term consequences addressed (arms race, deterrence, NPT). Synthesis connects the two documents as a before-and-after of the atomic decision.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Doc A — Truman frames Hiroshima as 'Army base': critical HIPP should question this framing. Doc B — Potsdam Declaration issued July 26 but did not specify atomic bomb; Japan's government saw it as Allied propaganda. Both documents require analysis of what they omit as much as what they say.
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Iwo Jima casualties (February–March 1945); Operation Downfall projections; Soviet entry (August 8, 1945); Hiroshima (~80,000 immediate dead) and Nagasaki (~40,000); Japan's surrender (August 15); Soviet atomic test (1949); NPT (1968).

GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: Tesis sofisticada que toma una posición defendible sobre la justificación. Ambos documentos analizados con HIPP completo, incluyendo lectura crítica del encuadre de 'base del ejército' de Truman y la amenaza vaga deliberadamente de 'destrucción total' de Potsdam. Dos o más piezas de evidencia externa. Consecuencias a largo plazo abordadas (carrera armamentística, disuasión, TNP). EXPECTATIVAS DE ANÁLISIS DE DOCUMENTOS: Doc A — Truman encuadra Hiroshima como 'base del ejército': el HIPP crítico debe cuestionar este encuadre. Doc B — La Declaración de Potsdam emitida el 26 de julio pero no especificó la bomba atómica; el gobierno japonés la vio como propaganda aliada. Ambos documentos requieren análisis de lo que omiten tanto como de lo que dicen.

items.stem:
Analyze the following two primary source excerpts and construct a document-based argument about how the Yalta and Potsdam Conferences shaped the postwar world order and planted the seeds of the Cold War.

DOCUMENT A: Excerpt from the Yalta Conference communiqué, February 11, 1945 (U.S. Department of State, Foreign Relations of the United States, 1945; National Archives, public domain):
"The Premier of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, and the President of the United States have consulted with each other in the common interests of the peoples of their countries... It is their purpose that Germany be disarmed and demilitarized and that all German industry used for military production shall be eliminated or controlled; all Nazi and militarist influences shall be eliminated from public offices and from the cultural and economic life of the German people... The Conference agreed that the question of the government of Poland was discussed."

DOCUMENT B: Excerpt from the Potsdam Declaration, July 26, 1945 (U.S. Department of State, 1945; National Archives, public domain):
"We call upon the government of Japan to proclaim now the unconditional surrender of all Japanese armed forces... The following are our terms. We will not deviate from them... Japan shall be permitted to maintain such industries as will sustain her economy and permit the exaction of just reparations in kind, but not those which would enable her to re-arm for war."

Using HIPP analysis for each document and your knowledge of the wartime conferences and postwar transition, construct an argument that evaluates how the decisions made at Yalta and Potsdam created the framework for postwar Europe and the Pacific — and how those decisions contained the contradictions that would become the Cold War. Your argument should address the ambiguity in Yalta's Poland discussion, what the Potsdam Declaration reveals about Allied strategy for Japan, and connect both to the emerging U.S.-Soviet rivalry. Include at least two pieces of outside evidence.
items.stemEs:
Analiza los siguientes dos extractos de fuentes primarias y construye un argumento basado en documentos sobre cómo las Conferencias de Yalta y Potsdam moldearon el orden mundial de posguerra y sembraron las semillas de la Guerra Fría.

DOCUMENTO A: Extracto del comunicado de la Conferencia de Yalta, 11 de febrero de 1945 (Departamento de Estado de EE.UU., Relaciones Exteriores de los Estados Unidos, 1945; Archivo Nacional, dominio público):
"El Primer Ministro de la Unión de Repúblicas Socialistas Soviéticas, el Primer Ministro del Reino Unido y el Presidente de los Estados Unidos se han consultado entre sí en los intereses comunes de los pueblos de sus países... Su propósito es que Alemania sea desarmada y desmilitarizada y que toda la industria alemana utilizada para la producción militar sea eliminada o controlada; todas las influencias nazis y militaristas serán eliminadas de los cargos públicos y de la vida cultural y económica del pueblo alemán... La Conferencia acordó que se discutió la cuestión del gobierno de Polonia."

DOCUMENTO B: Extracto de la Declaración de Potsdam, 26 de julio de 1945 (Departamento de Estado de EE.UU., 1945; Archivo Nacional, dominio público):
"Hacemos un llamado al gobierno de Japón para que proclame ahora la rendición incondicional de todas las fuerzas armadas japonesas... Los siguientes son nuestros términos. No nos desviaremos de ellos... A Japón se le permitirá mantener las industrias que puedan sostener su economía y permitir el pago de reparaciones justas en especie, pero no aquellas que le permitan rearmarse para la guerra."

Usando el análisis HIPP para cada documento y tu conocimiento de las conferencias de guerra y la transición de posguerra, construye un argumento que evalúe cómo las decisiones tomadas en Yalta y Potsdam crearon el marco para la Europa de posguerra y el Pacífico — y cómo esas decisiones contenían las contradicciones que se convertirían en la Guerra Fría. Tu argumento debe abordar la ambigüedad en la discusión de Polonia en Yalta, lo que la Declaración de Potsdam revela sobre la estrategia aliada para Japón, y conectar ambas con la rivalidad emergente entre EE.UU. y la URSS. Incluye al menos dos piezas de evidencia externa.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score (6/6) response will: THESIS: E.g., 'The Yalta and Potsdam agreements reflected the last moment of Allied unity — and revealed simultaneously the unresolved tensions over spheres of influence in Europe and Asia that would crystallize into the Cold War within two years.' HIPP — Doc A (Yalta): Context: war nearly over in Europe, February 1945, FDR declining; Audience: Allied publics and postwar policymakers; Purpose: announce Allied cooperation on postwar Germany; POV: Allied leaders managing competing interests — Stalin seeking Eastern European buffer states, FDR and Churchill seeking democratic self-determination. Note: 'the question of the government of Poland was discussed' — deliberately vague, concealing deep disagreement. HIPP — Doc B (Potsdam): Context: Germany defeated, atomic bomb about to be used, Japan still fighting; Audience: Japanese government and public; Purpose: ultimatum demanding unconditional surrender; POV: Truman, Attlee, Chiang Kai-shek — notably excluding Stalin from Pacific theater decisions while Stalin was present at Potsdam for European discussions. OUTSIDE EVIDENCE: Soviet occupation of Eastern Europe (violating Yalta self-determination terms); Berlin Blockade (1948); Truman Doctrine (1947) — responding to Soviet expansion; Marshall Plan (1947); NATO (1949). SYNTHESIS: Yalta's ambiguity about Poland became the fault line for postwar U.S.-Soviet conflict; Potsdam's exclusion of Stalin from Japan's surrender terms accelerated the nuclear rivalry that defined the Cold War.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.56, US.57 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Sophisticated thesis about Allied unity/Cold War seeds. Both documents with full HIPP including critical analysis of Yalta's Poland ambiguity and Potsdam's strategic exclusions. Two or more outside evidence pieces. Synthesis connects wartime conferences to Cold War onset. Cross-era synthesis (US.56 → US.59) demonstrated.
5 - Advanced: Clear thesis. Both documents with mostly complete HIPP. Cold War connection present. Two outside pieces.
4 - Proficient: Clear thesis. Both documents with three+ HIPP elements. One outside piece. Some Cold War connection.
3 - Adequate: Thesis present. One document fully analyzed. Some outside evidence. Partial Cold War connection.
2 - Developing: Minimal thesis. Documents described. Little analysis or Cold War connection.
1 - Beginning: No thesis. One document referenced without analysis.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Yalta — 'Poland was discussed' is the most significant phrase; its deliberate vagueness concealed Stalin's intention to install a Soviet-controlled government. Potsdam — Truman's exclusion of the Soviet Union from Japan surrender terms showed the alliance fracturing in real time.
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Yalta agreements on Poland (and subsequent Soviet violation); Soviet expansion into Eastern Europe (1945–1948); Berlin Blockade (1948–1949); Truman Doctrine (1947); Marshall Plan (1947); NATO (1949); Soviet atomic test (1949).
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: Tesis sofisticada sobre la unidad aliada/semillas de la Guerra Fría. Ambos documentos con HIPP completo, incluyendo análisis crítico de la ambigüedad de Polonia en Yalta y las exclusiones estratégicas de Potsdam. Dos o más piezas de evidencia externa. La síntesis conecta las conferencias de guerra con el inicio de la Guerra Fría. Síntesis entre eras (US.56 → US.59) demostrada.
5 - Avanzado: Tesis clara. Ambos documentos con HIPP mayormente completo. Conexión con la Guerra Fría presente. Dos piezas externas.
4 - Competente: Tesis clara. Ambos documentos con tres o más elementos HIPP. Una pieza externa. Alguna conexión con la Guerra Fría.
3 - Adecuado: Tesis presente. Un documento completamente analizado. Alguna evidencia externa. Conexión parcial con la Guerra Fría.
2 - En desarrollo: Tesis mínima. Documentos descritos. Poco análisis o conexión con la Guerra Fría.
1 - Inicial: Sin tesis. Un documento referenciado sin análisis.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EXPECTATIVAS DE ANÁLISIS DE DOCUMENTOS: Yalta — 'se discutió Polonia' es la frase más significativa; su deliberada vaguedad ocultó la intención de Stalin de instalar un gobierno controlado por los soviéticos. Potsdam — la exclusión de la Unión Soviética de los términos de rendición de Japón por parte de Truman mostró la alianza fracturándose en tiempo real.
EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Acuerdos de Yalta sobre Polonia (y posterior violación soviética); expansión soviética hacia Europa Oriental (1945–1948); Bloqueo de Berlín (1948–1949); Doctrina Truman (1947); Plan Marshall (1947); OTAN (1949); prueba atómica soviética (1949).

items.stem:
Using your knowledge of the European Theater of World War II and the Allied wartime conferences, write an extended response using the CER framework (Claim, Evidence, Reasoning) that answers the following question:

How did the military decisions made in the European Theater — particularly D-Day (Operation Overlord) and the Battle of the Bulge — both reflect and shape the political agreements reached at the Yalta and Potsdam Conferences? To what extent did military outcomes determine the postwar political order in Europe?

Your response must: (1) Advance a clear claim about the relationship between military success in the European Theater and the diplomatic leverage each Allied power held at Yalta and Potsdam; (2) Use specific evidence from at least two major military operations and at least two conference decisions to support your argument; (3) Reason through how the military geography of Europe in May 1945 — which armies were where — directly determined the political boundaries that would define the Cold War. Synthesize across US.48 (European Theater) and US.56 (Allied Conferences).
items.stemEs:
Usando tu conocimiento del Teatro Europeo de la Segunda Guerra Mundial y las conferencias aliadas en tiempos de guerra, escribe una respuesta extendida usando el marco CER que responda la siguiente pregunta:

¿Cómo las decisiones militares tomadas en el Teatro Europeo — particularmente el Día D (Operación Overlord) y la Batalla de las Ardenas — reflejaron y dieron forma a los acuerdos políticos alcanzados en las Conferencias de Yalta y Potsdam? ¿En qué medida los resultados militares determinaron el orden político de posguerra en Europa?

Tu respuesta debe: (1) Plantear una afirmación clara sobre la relación entre el éxito militar en el Teatro Europeo y la influencia diplomática que cada potencia aliada mantenía en Yalta y Potsdam; (2) Usar evidencia específica de al menos dos operaciones militares importantes y al menos dos decisiones de conferencias; (3) Razonar sobre cómo la geografía militar de Europa en mayo de 1945 — qué ejércitos estaban dónde — determinó directamente las fronteras políticas que definirían la Guerra Fría. Sintetiza entre US.48 (Teatro Europeo) y US.56 (Conferencias Aliadas).
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response will: CLAIM — A thesis such as: 'Military success in the European Theater, particularly the rapid Allied advance after D-Day and Soviet advances from the East, determined each power's negotiating position at Yalta and Potsdam — ultimately creating a postwar Europe divided along the lines of where armies stood when Germany surrendered.' EVIDENCE — (1) D-Day (June 6, 1944): opening the Western Front gave Western Allies leverage but also created a race with the Soviet advance; Eisenhower's decision not to race to Berlin (leaving it to the Soviets) had profound political consequences. (2) Battle of the Bulge (December 1944-January 1945): Germany's last offensive delayed the Western advance, giving Soviet forces more time to push further into Eastern Europe. (3) Yalta (February 1945): Stalin's strong negotiating position — Soviet armies were already in Poland — allowed him to extract ambiguous promises about 'free elections' that he never intended to honor. (4) Potsdam (July 1945): Germany defeated, new U.S. president (Truman), U.S. atomic bomb tested — Truman deliberately withheld full atomic details from Stalin; the wartime partnership was already fracturing. REASONING — The military map of Europe in May 1945 became the political map of Europe for the next 45 years. Soviet occupation of Eastern Europe was a military fact before it became a political one.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.48, US.56, US.59 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Sophisticated claim connecting military outcomes to diplomatic leverage. Specific evidence from D-Day, Battle of the Bulge, Yalta, and Potsdam with precise details. Reasoning explicitly argues that military geography determined political geography — the DOK 4 synthesis connecting US.48 → US.56 → US.59 (Cold War origins). Engages with Eisenhower's decision not to race to Berlin.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim. Evidence from two military campaigns and one or two conferences. Reasoning connects military and political outcomes with some cross-era Cold War connection.
2 - Developing: Claim present. Evidence from one military campaign and one conference. Limited causal reasoning.
1 - Beginning: Vague claim. Some mention of D-Day or Yalta without analytical connection.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: D-Day landings — 156,000 Allied troops, Operation Market Garden (failure), V-E Day May 8, 1945; Battle of the Bulge — 75,000 American casualties; Yalta — 'Declaration on Liberated Europe,' Poland borders, Soviet entry into Pacific War; Potsdam — Germany divided into four occupation zones, atomic bomb testing, Truman-Stalin friction.
SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: Must connect US.48 (military operations) + US.56 (conferences) forward to the Cold War division of Europe (US.59). A strong response will note that Yalta's ambiguity about Poland became the first major U.S.-Soviet confrontation.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Afirmación sofisticada que conecta los resultados militares con el poder diplomático. Evidencia específica del Día D, la Batalla de las Ardenas, Yalta y Potsdam. El razonamiento argumenta explícitamente que la geografía militar determinó la geografía política — síntesis DOK 4 conectando US.48 → US.56 → US.59.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara. Evidencia de dos campañas militares y una o dos conferencias. El razonamiento conecta resultados militares y políticos.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación presente. Evidencia de una campaña y una conferencia. Razonamiento causal limitado.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga. Alguna mención del Día D o Yalta sin conexión analítica.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Día D — 156,000 tropas aliadas; Batalla de las Ardenas — 75,000 bajas estadounidenses; Yalta — 'Declaración sobre Europa Liberada,' fronteras de Polonia; Potsdam — Alemania dividida en cuatro zonas de ocupación.
EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: Debe conectar US.48 + US.56 hacia US.59 (Guerra Fría).

items.stem:
Using your knowledge of the Allied wartime conferences (US.56) and the GI Bill of Rights/Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944 (US.57), write an extended response using the CER framework (Claim, Evidence, Reasoning) that addresses the following question:

The Yalta and Potsdam Conferences (1945) shaped the international postwar order, while the GI Bill (1944) shaped the domestic postwar order. To what extent did the decisions made at Yalta and Potsdam and the policies embodied in the GI Bill collectively define the United States' postwar trajectory — internationally as a superpower and domestically as a mass middle-class society — and what contradictions or failures did each produce?

Your response must: (1) Advance a defensible claim about how wartime decisions at both the international and domestic levels set the conditions for postwar American society; (2) Use specific evidence from at least two conference decisions and at least two provisions of the GI Bill and their real-world outcomes; (3) Reason through the contradictions each produced — Yalta's ambiguity breeding the Cold War, the GI Bill's racial exclusions widening the wealth gap — and argue whether these outcomes were inevitable or the result of specific choices. Synthesize across US.56 and US.57.
items.stemEs:
Usando tu conocimiento de las conferencias aliadas en tiempos de guerra (US.56) y la Ley de Reajuste de los Militares en Servicio de 1944 / GI Bill (US.57), escribe una respuesta extendida usando el marco CER que aborde la siguiente pregunta:

Las Conferencias de Yalta y Potsdam (1945) dieron forma al orden internacional de posguerra, mientras que el GI Bill (1944) dio forma al orden doméstico de posguerra. ¿En qué medida las decisiones tomadas en Yalta y Potsdam y las políticas del GI Bill definieron colectivamente la trayectoria de posguerra de los Estados Unidos — internacionalmente como superpotencia y domésticamente como sociedad de clase media masiva — y qué contradicciones o fracasos produjo cada una?

Tu respuesta debe: (1) Plantear una afirmación defendible sobre cómo las decisiones en tiempos de guerra a nivel internacional y doméstico establecieron las condiciones para la sociedad estadounidense de posguerra; (2) Usar evidencia específica de al menos dos decisiones de conferencias y al menos dos disposiciones del GI Bill; (3) Razonar sobre las contradicciones que produjo cada una. Sintetiza entre US.56 y US.57.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response will: CLAIM — A thesis connecting both levels of postwar ordering and their contradictions: e.g., 'The Yalta and Potsdam Conferences and the GI Bill together created the architecture of postwar America — a superpower committed to democratic internationalism abroad and a mass middle class at home — but both were undermined by their own contradictions: Yalta's ambiguity fueled the Cold War, and the GI Bill's racial exclusions deepened domestic inequality.' EVIDENCE — Yalta: 'Declaration on Liberated Europe' (free elections pledged, later violated); Poland borders; Soviet entry into Pacific War (Manchuria, August 1945); UN framework agreed. Potsdam: Germany into four occupation zones; Japanese surrender ultimatum; Truman's oblique mention of the atomic bomb to Stalin; the beginning of superpower friction. GI Bill: college enrollment doubled; the postwar suburban boom (Levittown) funded by VA loans; 8 million veterans went to college by 1956; Veterans Administration hospitals. GI Bill contradictions: Black veterans excluded from college loans (HBCUs overcrowded), from VA home loans in white suburbs, from small business loans through discriminatory local banks. REASONING — The GI Bill built the white middle class and the suburban landscape while simultaneously denying Black veterans the same ladder — this is not an oversight but a structural feature of how the New Deal and WWII-era federal programs interacted with Jim Crow institutions. Yalta's contradiction: Soviet sphere in Eastern Europe was already a military fact; Yalta ratified it with ambiguous language that the U.S. could interpret as a promise of democracy and the USSR could interpret as a sphere-of-influence agreement.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.56, US.57 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Sophisticated thesis connecting Yalta/Potsdam (international) and the GI Bill (domestic) as parallel architects of the postwar order, with full engagement with each policy's contradictions. Specific evidence from conference proceedings and GI Bill provisions/outcomes. Reasoning identifies the structural origins of the Cold War and the racial wealth gap as consequences of specific decisions, not inevitable outcomes. Cross-era synthesis connecting to the Cold War (US.59) and Civil Rights (US.71) demonstrates DOK 4.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim connecting both policies to the postwar order. Evidence from conferences and GI Bill with accurate details. Reasoning acknowledges contradictions in each.
2 - Developing: Claim present. Evidence from one policy area (either conferences or GI Bill) with some accuracy. Limited synthesis across both standards.
1 - Beginning: Vague claim. One policy mentioned with minimal evidence. No synthesis.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Yalta agreements — 'Declaration on Liberated Europe,' Poland; Potsdam — occupation zones, atomic decision; GI Bill provisions — education, home loans, business loans, VA hospitals; college enrollment growth; Levittown and suburbanization; racial exclusions — HBCU capacity, restrictive covenants, discriminatory VA offices; GI Bill racial gap's persistence into 21st century.
SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: US.56 (Yalta/Potsdam) → US.59 (Cold War); US.57 (GI Bill) → US.71 (Civil Rights) and US.78 (social change). Both chains of causation must be present for DOK 4 credit.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Tesis sofisticada que conecta Yalta/Potsdam (internacional) y el GI Bill (doméstico) como arquitectos paralelos del orden de posguerra, con participación completa en las contradicciones de cada política. Evidencia específica. El razonamiento identifica los orígenes estructurales de la Guerra Fría y la brecha racial de riqueza. Síntesis entre eras.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara. Evidencia de conferencias y GI Bill. El razonamiento reconoce las contradicciones.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación presente. Evidencia de un área de política. Síntesis limitada.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga. Una política mencionada con evidencia mínima.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Yalta — 'Declaración sobre Europa Liberada'; Potsdam — zonas de ocupación; GI Bill — educación, préstamos de vivienda, hospitales VA; Levittown; exclusiones raciales; brecha de riqueza racial.
EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: US.56 → US.59; US.57 → US.71 y US.78.

items.stem: What was the Cold War?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: A period of geopolitical tension between the U.S. and USSR without direct fighting
choices.textEs: Un período de tensión geopolítica entre EE.UU. y URSS sin combate directo

choices.text: Allied leaders planned post-WWII Europe, setting the stage for Cold War divisions
choices.textEs: Los líderes aliados planificaron la Europa de la posguerra de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, sentando las bases para las divisiones de la Guerra Fría

choices.text: Both sides used media, culture, and information to promote their ideology worldwide
choices.textEs: Una competencia económica entre Estados Unidos y aliados de Europa Occidental

choices.text: A July 1945 meeting where tensions between Truman and Stalin revealed a growing rift
choices.textEs: Un conjunto de negociaciones diplomáticas entre potencias Aliadas tras la Segunda Guerra Mundial

items.explanation: The Cold War was a period of geopolitical tension between the United States and the Soviet Union in which the two superpowers avoided direct war but competed through alliances, propaganda, and proxy conflicts. Choice B is wrong because it describes allied leaders planned post-WWII Europe, setting the stage for Cold War divisions, not period of geopolitical tension between the U.S. and USSR without direct fighting. These developments defined the Cold War as a global struggle over power, ideology, and influence.
items.explanationEs: La Guerra Fría (1947-1991) fue un período de tensión geopolítica entre Estados Unidos y la Unión Soviética caracterizado por conflicto ideológico, carrera armamentista y guerras proxy, pero sin confrontación militar directa entre las superpotencias.

items.stem: What was the Berlin Wall?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue el Muro de Berlín?

choices.text: A temporary checkpoint created to manage trade between East and West Berlin
choices.textEs: Un punto de control temporal creado para administrar comercio entre Berlín Este y Oeste

choices.text: A defensive fortification constructed by Western Allies to protect West Berlin
choices.textEs: Una fortificación defensiva construida por Aliados Occidentales para proteger Berlín Occidental

choices.text: A boundary line established by Allied forces during the occupation of Germany
choices.textEs: Una línea fronteriza establecida por fuerzas Aliadas durante la ocupación de Alemania

choices.text: A barrier built by East Germany in 1961 to prevent citizens from fleeing west
choices.textEs: Una barrera construida por Alemania Oriental en 1961 para evitar que ciudadanos huyeran al oeste

items.explanation: The Berlin Wall was built by communist East Germany in 1961 to stop people from escaping into democratic West Berlin. Choice A is wrong because it describes temporary checkpoint created to manage trade between East and West Berlin, not barrier built by East Germany in 1961 to prevent citizens from fleeing west. These developments defined the Cold War as a global struggle over power, ideology, and influence.
items.explanationEs: El Muro de Berlín fue construido en 1961 por la Alemania Oriental comunista para detener el flujo de refugiados que escapaban a Berlín Occidental democrático. Se convirtió en el símbolo más visible de la Cortina de Hierro que dividía Europa.

items.stem: What was the Korean War?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue la Guerra de Corea?

choices.text: A 1950-1953 conflict in which the United States declined to intervene militarily on the peninsula
choices.textEs: Un conflicto de 1952-1955 involucrando invasión militar china de la nación coreana unificada

choices.text: A 1945-1948 territorial dispute between Japan and the newly divided Korean peninsula
choices.textEs: Una disputa territorial de 1945-1948 entre Japón y la recientemente dividida península coreana

choices.text: A 1948-1950 civil war between democratic and communist factions within South Korea
choices.textEs: Una guerra civil de 1948-1950 entre facciones democráticas y comunistas dentro de Corea del Sur

choices.text: A 1950-1953 conflict where North Korea invaded South Korea, prompting U.S. action
choices.textEs: Un conflicto de 1950-1953 donde Corea del Norte invadió Corea del Sur, provocando acción de EE.UU.

items.explanation: The Korean War was a 1950-1953 conflict where North Korea invaded South Korea, prompting U.S. action. Choice A is wrong because it describes 1952-1955 conflict involving Chinese military invasion of the unified Korean nation, not 1950-1953 conflict where North Korea invaded South Korea, prompting U.S. action. Korea made containment a military commitment and showed how limited wars could become long, costly stalemates.
items.explanationEs: La Guerra de Corea (1950-1953) ocurrió cuando Corea del Norte (respaldada por China y la Unión Soviética) invadió Corea del Sur, llevando a intervención de EE.UU. para contener el comunismo. Terminó en armisticio con Corea permaneciendo dividida en el paralelo 38.

items.stem: Which countries directly supported North Korea during the Korean War?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué países apoyaron directamente a Corea del Norte durante la Guerra de Corea?

choices.text: Japan and Taiwan supplied weapons and economic assistance to the north
choices.textEs: Japón y Taiwán suministraron armas y asistencia económica al norte

choices.text: China and the Soviet Union provided military and material support
choices.textEs: China y la Unión Soviética proporcionaron apoyo militar y material

choices.text: Great Britain and France contributed troops and equipment to the conflict
choices.textEs: Gran Bretaña y Francia contribuyeron tropas y equipo al conflicto

choices.text: India and Indonesia offered diplomatic recognition and financial backing
choices.textEs: India e Indonesia ofrecieron reconocimiento diplomático y respaldo financiero

items.explanation: China and the Soviet Union provided military and material support fit this question because they were the key nations involved. Choice A is wrong because Japan and Taiwan supplied weapons and economic assistance to the north were not the actual countries involved in this agreement or conflict. Korea made containment a military commitment and showed how limited wars could become long, costly stalemates.
items.explanationEs: Corea del Norte fue apoyada por las potencias comunistas China y Unión Soviética, con China enviando cientos de miles de tropas después de que fuerzas de la ONU se acercaran a la frontera china.

items.stem: When did the Korean War begin?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuándo comenzó la Guerra de Corea?

choices.text: November 11, 1918, when the armistice ended the First World War
choices.textEs: 11 de noviembre de 1918, cuando el armisticio terminó la Primera Guerra Mundial

choices.text: December 7, 1941, when Japan attacked the U.S. at Pearl Harbor
choices.textEs: 7 de diciembre de 1941, cuando Japón atacó a EE.UU. en Pearl Harbor

choices.text: May 8, 1945, when Germany surrendered ending the European war
choices.textEs: 8 de mayo de 1945, cuando Alemania se rindió terminando la guerra europea

choices.text: June 25, 1950, when North Korea crossed the 38th parallel
choices.textEs: 25 de junio de 1950, cuando Corea del Norte cruzó el paralelo 38

items.explanation: the Korean War began in June 25, 1950, when North Korea crossed the 38th parallel. Choice A is wrong because it describes november 11, 1918, when the armistice ended the First World War, not june 25, 1950, when North Korea crossed the 38th parallel. Korea made containment a military commitment and showed how limited wars could become long, costly stalemates.
items.explanationEs: La Guerra de Corea comenzó el 25 de junio de 1950, cuando fuerzas norcoreanas cruzaron el paralelo 38 e invadieron Corea del Sur, provocando respuesta inmediata de EE.UU. y ONU.

items.stem: What was brinksmanship?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue la política al borde del abismo?

choices.text: The Soviet shootdown of a U.S. spy plane, exposing surveillance and causing a crisis
choices.textEs: El derribo soviético de un avión espía de los EE.UU., lo que expuso la vigilancia y provocó una crisis

choices.text: A policy pledging U.S. aid to Middle Eastern countries resisting communist aggression
choices.textEs: Una política de hacer pequeñas concesiones económicas para evitar desacuerdos comerciales mayores

choices.text: A strategy of pushing dangerous situations to the edge to force opponents to retreat
choices.textEs: Una estrategia de llevar situaciones peligrosas al borde para forzar a oponentes a retroceder

choices.text: A competition between the U.S. and USSR to build superior nuclear weapons arsenals
choices.textEs: Un plan para participar en conversaciones diplomáticas prolongadas para retrasar confrontación

items.explanation: Brinksmanship was the Cold War strategy of pushing crises to the edge of war to force the other side to back down. Choice A is wrong because it describes soviet shootdown of a U.S. spy plane, exposing surveillance and causing a crisis, not strategy of pushing dangerous situations to the edge to force opponents to retreat. Nuclear weapons changed global strategy by making deterrence and crisis management central to superpower relations.
items.explanationEs: La política al borde del abismo fue la estrategia de la Guerra Fría de llevar situaciones peligrosas al borde del desastre para forzar a un oponente a retroceder, especialmente respecto a armas nucleares bajo el Presidente Eisenhower.

items.stem: What was the arms race during the Cold War?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue la carrera armamentista durante la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: A competition between the U.S. and USSR to build superior nuclear weapons arsenals
choices.textEs: Una competencia entre EE.UU. y URSS para construir arsenales de armas nucleares superiores

choices.text: A program to develop conventional military equipment and train larger ground forces
choices.textEs: Un programa para desarrollar equipamiento militar convencional y entrenar fuerzas terrestres más grandes

choices.text: A series of athletic competitions used to demonstrate national superiority publicly
choices.textEs: Una serie de competencias atléticas usadas para demostrar superioridad nacional públicamente

choices.text: A set of trade embargo programs designed to weaken opposing economic structures
choices.textEs: Un conjunto de programas de embargo comercial diseñados para debilitar estructuras económicas opuestas

items.explanation: The arms race during the Cold War was a competition between the U.S. and USSR to build superior nuclear weapons arsenals. Choice B is wrong because it describes program to develop conventional military equipment and train larger ground forces, not competition between the U.S. and USSR to build superior nuclear weapons arsenals. These developments defined the Cold War as a global struggle over power, ideology, and influence.
items.explanationEs: La carrera armamentista fue la competencia de la Guerra Fría entre superpotencias para desarrollar armas nucleares y sistemas de entrega cada vez más poderosos, creando arsenales masivos capaces de destruir el mundo muchas veces.

items.stem: What was "massive retaliation" policy under Eisenhower designed to prevent?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fue diseñada a prevenir la política de "represalia masiva" bajo Eisenhower?

choices.text: It created weapons far more powerful than atomic bombs, escalating the arms race
choices.textEs: Inmigración de países comunistas, fortaleciendo medidas de seguridad fronteriza

choices.text: The doctrine that nuclear war would destroy both sides, deterring its actual use
choices.textEs: Competencia económica de Europa, imponiendo restricciones comerciales estrictas en el exterior

choices.text: Soviet aggression, by threatening an overwhelming nuclear response to any attack

Choice A is wrong because 1960 is too late — McCarthy had already been censured by the Senate in 1954 and died in 1957. Choices B and C are wrong because 1945 and 1955 fall outside the speech's documented date. Las opciones B y C son incorrectas porque 1945 y 1955 quedan fuera de la fecha documentada del discurso. El discurso de Wheeling encendió el Segundo Susto Rojo y convirtió a McCarthy en el cruzado anticomunista más prominente de la época.
