items.stem: Clinton's impeachment in 1998 by the House of Representatives was only the second presidential impeachment in American history. The Senate ultimately acquitted him. What were the specific charges on which he was impeached?
items.stemEs: Clinton's juicio político in 1998 by the Cámara de Representantes was only the second presidential juicio político in American history. The Senado ultimately acquitted him. What were the specific charges on which he was impeached?

choices.text: Bribery and abuse of power related to the Whitewater real estate investigation
choices.textEs: Soborno y abuso de poder relacionados con la investigación inmobiliaria de Whitewater

choices.text: Campaign finance violations related to illegal contributions from foreign governments
choices.textEs: Violaciones de financiación de campaña relacionadas con contribuciones ilegales de gobiernos extranjeros

choices.text: Perjury (lying under oath) and obstruction of justice related to the Monica Lewinsky scandal
choices.textEs: Perjurio (mentir bajo juramento) y obstrucción de la justicia relacionados con el escándalo Mónica Lewinsky

choices.text: Abuse of power and contempt of Congress related to Whitewater document subpoenas
choices.textEs: Abuso de poder y desacato al Congreso relacionados con citaciones judiciales de documentos de Whitewater

items.explanation: Perjury (lying under oath) and obstruction of justice related to the Monica Lewinsky scandal. Choice A is wrong because it describes bribery and abuse of power related to the Whitewater real estate investigation, not perjury (lying under oath) and obstruction of justice related to the Monica Lewinsky scandal. These battles intensified partisan polarization and changed how Congress and the presidency confronted each other.
items.explanationEs: Perjurio (mentir bajo juramento) y obstrucción de la justicia relacionados con el escándalo Mónica Lewinsky. La opción A es incorrecta porque describe soborno y abuso de poder relacionados con la investigación Whitewater, no perjurio y obstrucción de la justicia. El juicio político de Clinton intensificó la guerra partidista y dejó al presidente políticamente debilitado pero en el cargo.

items.stem: The Paris Peace Accords, signed in January 1973, ended —
items.stemEs: Los Acuerdos de Paz de París, firmados en enero de 1973, pusieron fin a —

choices.text: The war between North and South Vietnam permanently, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development
choices.textEs: La guerra entre Vietnam del Norte y Vietnam del Sur de manera permanente, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo

choices.text: Direct U.S. military involvement in Vietnam, requiring withdrawal of U.S. forces while leaving North Vietnamese troops in the South
choices.textEs: La participación militar directa de los Estados Unidos en Vietnam, que exigió la retirada de las fuerzas estadounidenses dejando tropas norvietnamitas en el Sur

choices.text: All combat operations in Southeast Asia including Cambodia and Laos, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development
choices.textEs: Todas las operaciones de combate en el Sudeste Asiático, incluidos Camboya y Laos, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo

choices.text: The war between the United States and China over Vietnam, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development
choices.textEs: La guerra entre los Estados Unidos y China por Vietnam, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo

items.explanation: Direct U.S. military involvement in Vietnam, requiring withdrawal of U.S. forces while leaving North Vietnamese troops in the South — a ceasefire that most observers recognized would not hold. Choice A is wrong because it describes war between North and South Vietnam permanently, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development, not direct U.S. military involvement in Vietnam, requiring withdrawal of U.S. forces while leaving North Vietnamese troops in the South — a ceasefire that most observers recognized would not hold. The Vietnam era deepened the credibility gap and made Americans more skeptical of presidential war-making.
items.explanationEs: La participación militar directa de los Estados Unidos en Vietnam, que exigió la retirada de las fuerzas estadounidenses dejando tropas norvietnamitas en el Sur — un alto el fuego que la mayoría de los observadores reconoció que no se sostendría. La opción A es incorrecta porque describe la guerra entre Vietnam del Norte y Vietnam del Sur de manera permanente, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo, no la participación militar directa de los Estados Unidos en Vietnam. La era de Vietnam profundizó la brecha de credibilidad e hizo a los estadounidenses más escépticos respecto al uso de la guerra por parte del poder ejecutivo.

items.stem: The Fall of Saigon (April 30, 1975) occurred when —
items.stemEs: La Caída de Saigón (30 de abril de 1975) ocurrió cuando —

choices.text: South Vietnamese forces repelled the North Vietnamese attack with U.S. air support, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development
choices.textEs: Las fuerzas survietnamitas repelieron el ataque norvietnamita con apoyo aéreo de los EE.UU., lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo

choices.text: U.S. forces withdrew in good order after completing their mission, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development
choices.textEs: Las fuerzas de los EE.UU. se retiraron en orden después de cumplir su misión, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo

choices.text: A negotiated peace allowed both governments to share power, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development
choices.textEs: Una paz negociada permitió a ambos gobiernos compartir el poder, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo

choices.text: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon two years after the U.S. withdrawal, completing their conquest of South Vietnam and unifying the country under communist rule
choices.textEs: Las fuerzas de Vietnam del Norte tomaron Saigón dos años después de la retirada de los EE.UU., completando su conquista de Vietnam del Sur

items.explanation: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon two years after the U.S. withdrawal, completing their conquest of South Vietnam and unifying the country under communist rule — the final collapse of the South Vietnamese government. Choice A is wrong because it describes south Vietnamese forces repelled the North Vietnamese attack with U.S. air support, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development, not north Vietnamese forces captured Saigon two years after the U.S. withdrawal, completing their conquest of South Vietnam and unifying the country under communist rule — the final collapse of the South Vietnamese government. The Vietnam era deepened the credibility gap and made Americans more skeptical of presidential war-making.
items.explanationEs: Las fuerzas de Vietnam del Norte tomaron Saigón dos años después de la retirada de los EE.UU., completando su conquista de Vietnam del Sur. La opción A es incorrecta porque describe que las fuerzas survietnamitas repelieron el ataque norvietnamita con apoyo aéreo de los EE.UU., lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo. La era de Vietnam profundizó la brecha de credibilidad e hizo a los estadounidenses más escépticos respecto al uso de la guerra por parte del poder ejecutivo.

items.stem: The 26th Amendment (1971) lowered the voting age from 21 to 18. The primary argument for this change was —
items.stemEs: La 26.ª Enmienda (1971) redujo la edad para votar de 21 a 18 años. El argumento principal para este cambio fue —

choices.text: Young Americans drafted to fight in Vietnam were old enough to vote for the leaders who sent them to war
choices.textEs: Los jóvenes estadounidenses reclutados para luchar en Vietnam tenían edad suficiente para votar por los líderes que los enviaban a combatir

choices.text: All major Western democracies had already lowered their voting ages to 18 by the mid-1960s
choices.textEs: Todas las principales democracias occidentales ya habían reducido su edad para votar a 18 años a mediados de los sesenta

choices.text: 18-year-olds had demonstrated exceptional civic maturity and educational attainment compared to prior generations
choices.textEs: Los jóvenes de 18 años habían demostrado una madurez cívica y un nivel educativo excepcionales en comparación con generaciones anteriores

choices.text: The Supreme Court had ruled that the existing voting age was unconstitutional under the 26th Amendment
choices.textEs: La Corte Suprema había resuelto que la edad para votar vigente era inconstitucional bajo la 26.ª Enmienda

items.explanation: Young Americans who were old enough to be drafted and die in Vietnam were old enough to vote for the leaders who sent them. Choice B is wrong because it describes all Western democracies had already lowered their voting ages to 18, not young Americans who were old enough to be drafted and die in Vietnam were old enough to vote for the leaders who sent them. The Vietnam era deepened the credibility gap and made Americans more skeptical of presidential war-making.
items.explanationEs: Los jóvenes estadounidenses que tenían edad suficiente para ser reclutados y morir en Vietnam tenían edad suficiente para votar por los líderes que los enviaban a combatir. La opción B es incorrecta porque describe que todas las principales democracias occidentales ya habían reducido su edad para votar a 18 años a mediados de los sesenta, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo. La 26.ª Enmienda representó la expansión más reciente del derecho al sufragio en la historia constitucional estadounidense.

items.stem: Operation Eagle Claw (April 1980) was —
items.stemEs: La Operación Eagle Claw (abril de 1980) fue —

choices.text: A military airstrike on Iranian nuclear facilities, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development
choices.textEs: Un ataque aéreo contra instalaciones nucleares iraníes, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo

choices.text: A naval blockade of Iranian ports designed to force hostage release, which was not the primary driver of this historical change
choices.textEs: Un bloqueo naval de los puertos iraníes diseñado para forzar la liberación de los rehenes, lo cual no fue el principal motivo de este desarrollo

choices.text: A failed military rescue attempt that ended when helicopters malfunctioned in the Iranian desert, killing eight U.S. servicemen and humiliating the Carter administration
choices.textEs: Un fallido intento de rescate militar que terminó cuando los helicópteros sufrieron fallas mecánicas en el desierto iraní, matando a ocho militares de los EE.UU.

choices.text: A successful rescue mission that freed the American hostages, which was not the primary driver of this historical change
choices.textEs: Una exitosa misión de rescate que liberó a los rehenes estadounidenses, lo cual no fue el principal motivo de este desarrollo

items.explanation: A failed military rescue attempt that ended when helicopters malfunctioned in the Iranian desert, killing eight U.S. servicemen and humiliating the Carter administration. Choice A is wrong because it describes military airstrike on Iranian nuclear facilities, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development, not failed military rescue attempt that ended when helicopters malfunctioned in the Iranian desert, killing eight U.S. servicemen and humiliating the Carter administration. The hostage crisis fed the image of American weakness abroad and helped set the stage for Reagan's victory in 1980.
items.explanationEs: Un fallido intento de rescate militar que terminó cuando los helicópteros sufrieron fallas mecánicas en el desierto iraní, matando a ocho militares de los EE.UU. La opción A es incorrecta porque describe un ataque aéreo contra instalaciones nucleares iraníes, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo. El fracaso de la Operación Eagle Claw contribuyó a la percepción de debilidad de Carter.

items.stem: The 'Contract with America,' which Gingrich and House Republicans signed in 1994, pledged to —
items.stemEs: The 'Contract with America,' which Gingrich and House repúblicaans signed in 1994, pledged to:

choices.text: Pass a specific list of legislation within the first 100 days of the new Congress
choices.textEs: Pass a specific list of legislación within the first 100 days of the new Congreso

choices.text: Cut all government spending by 50% in the first year
choices.textEs: Recortar todo el gasto gubernamental en un 50% durante el primer año

choices.text: Impeach President Clinton regardless of the evidence
choices.textEs: Someter a juicio político al presidente Clinton independientemente de las pruebas

choices.text: Withdraw the United States from all international organizations
choices.textEs: Retirar a los Estados Unidos de todas las organizaciones internacionales

items.explanation: Pass a specific list of legislation within the first 100 days of the new Congress. Choice B is wrong because it describes cut all government spending by 50% in the first year, not pass a specific list of legislation within the first 100 days of the new Congress. These battles intensified partisan polarization and changed how Congress and the presidency confronted each other.
items.explanationEs: Pass a specific list of legislación within the first 100 days of the new Congreso. Choice B is wrong because it describes cut all government spending by 50% in the first year, not pass a specific list of legislación within the first 100 days of the new Congreso. These battles intensified partisan polarization and changed how Congreso and the presidency confronted each other.

items.stem: President Clinton was impeached by the House of Representatives in December 1998 on charges of —
items.stemEs: President Clinton was impeached by the Cámara de Representantes in December 1998 on charges of:

choices.text: Treason and accepting illegal foreign campaign contributions from a hostile foreign power
choices.textEs: Traición y aceptación de contribuciones ilegales de campaña de una potencia extranjera hostil

choices.text: Abuse of power and bribery in connection with federal contracts and government appointments
choices.textEs: Abuso de poder y soborno en relación con contratos federales y nombramientos gubernamentales

choices.text: Perjury (lying under oath about his affair with Monica Lewinsky) and obstruction of justice in the Paula Jones case
choices.textEs: Perjurio (mentir bajo juramento sobre su relación con Mónica Lewinsky) y obstrucción de la justicia en el caso Paula Jones

choices.text: Violating the War Powers Act and conducting unauthorized covert foreign policy through back channels
choices.textEs: Violating the War Powers Act and conducting unauthorized covert política exterior through back channels

items.explanation: Perjury (lying under oath to a federal grand jury about his affair with Monica Lewinsky) and obstruction of justice (attempting to influence witnesses in the Paula Jones sexual harassment lawsuit). Choice A is wrong because it describes treason and accepting foreign campaign contributions, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development, not perjury (lying under oath to a federal grand jury about his affair with Monica Lewinsky) and obstruction of justice (attempting to influence witnesses in the Paula Jones sexual harassment lawsuit). The Vietnam era deepened the credibility gap and made Americans more skeptical of presidential war-making.
items.explanationEs: Perjurio (mentir bajo juramento ante un gran jurado federal sobre su relación con Mónica Lewinsky) y obstrucción de la justicia (intentar encubrir la relación). La opción A es incorrecta porque describe traición y aceptación de contribuciones ilegales de campaña de una potencia extranjera hostil, no perjurio y obstrucción de la justicia. El juicio político intensificó la guerra partidista.

items.stem: After the House voted to impeach Clinton, the Senate —
items.stemEs: Después de que la Cámara votara para someter a juicio político a Clinton, el Senado —

choices.text: Voted to censure Clinton rather than conducting a formal impeachment trial, a lesser penalty
choices.textEs: Voted to censure Clinton rather than conducting a formal juicio político trial, a lesser penalty

choices.text: Referred the matter to the Supreme Court for final adjudication on presidential misconduct
choices.textEs: Remitió el asunto a la Corte Suprema para la adjudicación final sobre la mala conducta presidencial

choices.text: Acquitted Clinton — the prosecution fell well short of the two-thirds majority required for conviction
choices.textEs: Absolvió a Clinton — la acusación quedó muy lejos de la mayoría de dos tercios requerida para la condena

choices.text: Convicted Clinton and removed him from office after a strict party-line Senate vote found him guilty
choices.textEs: Condenó a Clinton y lo destituyó del cargo tras una votación estrictamente partidista en el Senado

items.explanation: Acquitted Clinton — the prosecution fell well short of the two-thirds majority required for conviction, with most Democrats voting not guilty and even some Republicans voting to acquit. Choice A is wrong because it describes voted to censure Clinton rather than conduct a full trial, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development, not acquitted Clinton — the prosecution fell well short of the two-thirds majority required for conviction, with most Democrats voting not guilty and even some Republicans voting to acquit. These battles intensified partisan polarization and changed how Congress and the presidency confronted each other.
items.explanationEs: Acquitted Clinton — the prosecution fell well short of the two-thirds majority required for conviction, with most Democrats voting not guilty and even some repúblicaans voting to acquit. Choice A is wrong because it describes voted to censure Clinton rather than conduct a full trial, which historians consider a secondary factor in this development, not acquitted Clinton — the prosecution fell well short of the two-thirds majority required for conviction, with most Democrats voting not guilty and even some repúblicaans voting to acquit. These battles intensified partisan polarization and changed how Congreso and the presidency confronted each other.

items.stem: The collapse of the Soviet Union in December 1991 left the United States as —
items.stemEs: El colapso de la Unión Soviética en diciembre de 1991 dejó a los Estados Unidos como —

choices.text: The world's sole remaining superpower
choices.textEs: La única superpotencia mundial restante

choices.text: Obligated by treaty to maintain a permanent military presence in Europe
choices.textEs: Obligados por tratado a mantener una presencia militar permanente en Europa

choices.text: One of two remaining superpowers alongside China
choices.textEs: Una de las dos superpotencias restantes junto a China

choices.text: A declining power rapidly being overtaken by Japan and Germany economically
choices.textEs: Una potencia en declive que Japón y Alemania estaban superando rápidamente en el ámbito económico

items.explanation: The world's sole remaining superpower. Choice C is wrong because it describes one of two remaining superpowers alongside China, not world's sole remaining superpower. Post-Cold War events forced the United States to define how far its power and responsibilities should reach in a one-superpower world.
items.explanationEs: The world's sole remaining superpower. Choice C is wrong because it describes one of two remaining superpowers alongside China, not world's sole remaining superpower. Post-Guerra Fría events forced the United States to define how far its power and responsibilities should reach in a one-superpower world.

items.stem: The Paris Peace Accords (1973) resulted in —
items.stemEs: The Paris Peace Accords (1973) resultó en:

choices.text: International supervision of free elections throughout Vietnam
choices.textEs: La supervisión internacional de elecciones libres en todo Vietnam

choices.text: A ceasefire and the withdrawal of U.S. combat forces from Vietnam
choices.textEs: Un alto el fuego y la retirada de las fuerzas de combate de los EE.UU. de Vietnam

choices.text: An immediate withdrawal of all North Vietnamese forces from South Vietnam
choices.textEs: Una retirada inmediata de todas las fuerzas de Vietnam del Norte de Vietnam del Sur

choices.text: South Vietnam being partitioned into two independent nations permanently
choices.textEs: La división permanente de Vietnam del Sur en dos naciones independientes

items.explanation: A ceasefire and the withdrawal of U.S. combat forces from Vietnam. Choice C is wrong because it describes immediate withdrawal of all North Vietnamese forces from South Vietnam, not ceasefire and the withdrawal of U.S. combat forces from Vietnam. The Vietnam era deepened the credibility gap and made Americans more skeptical of presidential war-making.
items.explanationEs: Un alto el fuego y la retirada de las fuerzas de combate de los EE.UU. de Vietnam. La opción C es incorrecta porque describe la retirada inmediata de todas las fuerzas de Vietnam del Norte de Vietnam del Sur, no un alto el fuego y una retirada estadounidense. La era de Vietnam profundizó la brecha de credibilidad.

items.stem: President Nixon's policy of "Vietnamization" for the Vietnam War meant —
items.stemEs: La política de 'Vietnamización' del presidente Nixon para la Guerra de Vietnam significó —

choices.text: Expanding the war into Cambodia and Laos to cut North Vietnamese supply lines
choices.textEs: Expandir la guerra hacia Camboya y Laos para cortar las líneas de suministro de Vietnam del Norte

choices.text: Gradually transferring combat responsibility to South Vietnamese forces while withdrawing U.S. troops
choices.textEs: Transferir gradualmente la responsabilidad del combate a las fuerzas survietnamitas mientras se retiraban las tropas de los EE.UU.

choices.text: Negotiating a neutralist government acceptable to both North and South Vietnam
choices.textEs: Negociar un gobierno neutralista aceptable tanto para Vietnam del Norte como para Vietnam del Sur

choices.text: Increasing U.S. troop levels to decisively defeat North Vietnam
choices.textEs: Aumentar los efectivos de los EE.UU. para derrotar decisivamente a Vietnam del Norte

items.explanation: Gradually transferring combat responsibility to South Vietnamese forces while withdrawing U.S. troops. Choice D is wrong because it describes increasing U.S. troop levels to decisively defeat North Vietnam, not gradually transferring combat responsibility to South Vietnamese forces while withdrawing U.S. troops. The Vietnam era deepened the credibility gap and made Americans more skeptical of presidential war-making.
items.explanationEs: La transferencia gradual de la responsabilidad del combate a las fuerzas survietnamitas mientras se retiraban las tropas de los EE.UU. La opción D es incorrecta porque describe el aumento de los efectivos de los EE.UU. para derrotar decisivamente a Vietnam del Norte, no la Vietnamización. La era de Vietnam profundizó la brecha de credibilidad.

items.stem: The Pentagon Papers, leaked by Daniel Ellsberg in 1971, revealed that —
items.stemEs: Los Papeles del Pentágono, filtrados por Daniel Ellsberg en 1971, revelaron que —

choices.text: Nixon had secretly negotiated with North Vietnam before his election in 1968
choices.textEs: Nixon había negociado secretamente con Vietnam del Norte antes de su elección en 1968

choices.text: CIA operatives had conducted illegal operations against antiwar protesters in the United States
choices.textEs: Agentes de la CIA habían llevado a cabo operaciones ilegales contra manifestantes antibelicistas en los Estados Unidos

choices.text: Multiple administrations had systematically misled the public about the prospects for victory in Vietnam
choices.textEs: Múltiples administraciones habían engañado sistemáticamente al público sobre las perspectivas de victoria en Vietnam

choices.text: The Gulf of Tonkin incidents were substantially fabricated by the Johnson administration
choices.textEs: Los incidentes del Golfo de Tonkín fueron sustancialmente fabricados por la administración Johnson

items.explanation: Multiple administrations had systematically misled the public about the prospects for victory in Vietnam. Choice A is wrong because it describes nixon had secretly negotiated with North Vietnam before his election in 1968, not multiple administrations had systematically misled the public about the prospects for victory in Vietnam. The Vietnam era deepened the credibility gap and made Americans more skeptical of presidential war-making.
items.explanationEs: Múltiples administraciones habían engañado sistemáticamente al público sobre las perspectivas de victoria en Vietnam. La opción A es incorrecta porque describe que Nixon había negociado secretamente con Vietnam del Norte antes de su elección en 1968, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo. La era de Vietnam profundizó la brecha de credibilidad e hizo a los estadounidenses más escépticos respecto al uso de la guerra por parte del poder ejecutivo.

items.stem: Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 prohibited —
items.stemEs: El Título IX de las Enmiendas a la Ley de Educación de 1972 prohibió —

choices.text: Sex discrimination in any educational program receiving federal financial assistance
choices.textEs: Sex discriminación in any educational program receiving federal financial assistance

choices.text: Age discrimination in college admissions at federally funded institutions
choices.textEs: Age discriminación in college admissions at federally funded institutions

choices.text: Racial segregation in any school receiving federal funding
choices.textEs: Racial segregación in any school receiving federal funding

choices.text: Religious instruction in public schools funded by the federal government
choices.textEs: La instrucción religiosa en las escuelas públicas financiadas por el gobierno federal

items.explanation: Sex discrimination in any educational program receiving federal financial assistance. Choice C is wrong because it describes racial segregation in any school receiving federal funding, not sex discrimination in any educational program receiving federal financial assistance. The 1970s brought new arguments about rights, energy, gender, and diplomacy that reshaped politics after the early Cold War.
items.explanationEs: Sex discriminación in any educational program receiving federal financial assistance. Choice C is wrong because it describes racial segregación in any school receiving federal funding, not sex discriminación in any educational program receiving federal financial assistance. The 1970s brought new arguments about rights, energy, gender, and diplomacia that reshaped politics after the early Guerra Fría.

items.stem: The 1980 U.S. Olympic boycott was a response to —
items.stemEs: El boicot olímpico de los EE.UU. en 1980 fue una respuesta a —

choices.text: Cuban military involvement in Angola and other African nations
choices.textEs: La intervención militar cubana en Angola y otras naciones africanas

choices.text: Iran's refusal to release American hostages before the opening of the Moscow games
choices.textEs: La negativa de Irán a liberar a los rehenes estadounidenses antes de la apertura de los Juegos de Moscú

choices.text: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979
choices.textEs: La invasión soviética de Afganistán en diciembre de 1979

choices.text: East German and Soviet athletes' use of performance-enhancing drugs
choices.textEs: El uso de sustancias dopantes por parte de atletas alemanes orientales y soviéticos

items.explanation: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979. Choice D is wrong because it describes east German and Soviet athletes' use of performance-enhancing drugs, not soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979. This issue helped shape the political, social, and foreign policy debates of modern U.S. history.
items.explanationEs: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979. Choice D is wrong because it describes east German and Soviet athletes' use of performance-enhancing drugs, not soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979. This issue helped shape the political, social, and política exterior debates of modern U.S. history.

items.stem: The Iranian revolution of 1979 replaced the Shah's government with —
items.stemEs: La revolución iraní de 1979 reemplazó el gobierno del Sha con —

choices.text: A secular democratic republic modeled on European parliamentary systems
choices.textEs: A secular democrático república modeled on European parliamentary systems

choices.text: A military junta aligned with the Soviet Union
choices.textEs: Una junta militar aliada con la Unión Soviética

choices.text: An Islamic theocracy led by Ayatollah Khomeini
choices.textEs: Una teocracia islámica dirigida por el Ayatolá Jomeini

choices.text: A constitutional monarchy under the Shah's son
choices.textEs: Una monarquía constitucional bajo el hijo del Sha

items.explanation: An Islamic theocracy led by Ayatollah Khomeini. Choice D is wrong because it describes constitutional monarchy under the Shah's son, not islamic theocracy led by Ayatollah Khomeini. The hostage crisis fed the image of American weakness abroad and helped set the stage for Reagan's victory in 1980.
items.explanationEs: Una teocracia islámica dirigida por el Ayatolá Jomeini. La opción D es incorrecta porque describe una monarquía constitucional bajo el hijo del Sha, no una teocracia islámica. La revolución iraní estableció un modelo de gobierno islamista que influyó en la política regional durante décadas.

items.stem: Jerry Falwell Sr.'s Moral Majority, founded in 1979, was primarily concerned with —
items.stemEs: La Mayoría Moral del pastor Jerry Falwell, fundada en 1979, se preocupaba principalmente por —

choices.text: Opposing détente with the Soviet Union on grounds that communism was morally incompatible with American values
choices.textEs: Opposing détente with the Soviet Union on grounds that comunismo was morally incompatible with American values

choices.text: Reducing government spending and cutting taxes for working-class Americans
choices.textEs: Reducir el gasto gubernamental y recortar los impuestos para los estadounidenses de clase trabajadora

choices.text: Mobilizing Evangelical Christian voters around issues like abortion, school prayer, and traditional family values
choices.textEs: Movilizar a los votantes evangélicos en torno a temas como el aborto, la oración en las escuelas y los valores tradicionales

choices.text: Promoting school choice and opposition to federal control of education
choices.textEs: Promover la elección de escuelas y la oposición al control federal de la educación

items.explanation: Mobilizing Evangelical Christian voters around issues like abortion, school prayer, and traditional family values. Choice A is wrong because it describes opposing détente with the Soviet Union on grounds that communism was morally incompatible with American values, not mobilizing Evangelical Christian voters around issues like abortion, school prayer, and traditional family values. These debates helped define the conservative turn in American politics during the 1980s.
items.explanationEs: Mobilizing Evangelical Christian voters around issues like abortion, school prayer, and traditional family values. Choice A is wrong because it describes opposing détente with the Soviet Union on grounds that comunismo was morally incompatible with American values, not mobilizing Evangelical Christian voters around issues like abortion, school prayer, and traditional family values. These debates helped define the conservative turn in American politics during the 1980s.

items.stem: The Reagan Doctrine committed the United States to —
items.stemEs: La Doctrina Reagan comprometió a los Estados Unidos a —

choices.text: Providing support to anti-communist resistance movements seeking to overthrow Soviet-backed governments
choices.textEs: Proporcionar apoyo a los movimientos de resistencia anticomunistas que buscaban derrocar a los gobiernos respaldados por la Unión Soviética

choices.text: Countering Soviet expansionism through diplomatic pressure and economic sanctions
choices.textEs: Contrarrestar el expansionismo soviético mediante presión diplomática y sanciones económicas

choices.text: Negotiating arms reductions as the primary method of reducing Cold War tensions
choices.textEs: Negotiating arms reductions as the primary method of reducing Guerra Fría tensions

items.explanation: Senator Joseph McCarthy is best known for leading public investigations and accusations of communist infiltration in U.S. government and society. From his February 9, 1950, Wheeling speech through the 1954 Army-McCarthy hearings, he charged hundreds of officials, intellectuals, and entertainers with disloyalty using little or no evidence. Choice B is wrong because McCarthy supported, not opposed, U.S. NATO commitments. Choice D is wrong because civil-rights legislation came primarily through the Eisenhower, Kennedy, and Johnson administrations, not McCarthy's subcommittee. McCarthy's tactics defined the broader Second Red Scare phenomenon now called McCarthyism.
items.explanationEs: El senador Joseph McCarthy es más conocido por liderar investigaciones públicas y acusaciones de infiltración comunista en el gobierno y la sociedad de EE. UU. Desde su discurso del 9 de febrero de 1950 en Wheeling hasta las audiencias Ejército-McCarthy de 1954, acusó a cientos de funcionarios, intelectuales y artistas de deslealtad con poca o ninguna evidencia. La opción B es incorrecta porque McCarthy apoyó, no se opuso, a los compromisos de EE. UU. con la OTAN. La opción D es incorrecta porque la legislación de derechos civiles llegó principalmente a través de los gobiernos de Eisenhower, Kennedy y Johnson, no del subcomité de McCarthy. Las tácticas de McCarthy definieron el fenómeno más amplio del Segundo Susto Rojo, hoy llamado macartismo.

items.explanation: The March on the Pentagon in October 1967 was one of the largest antiwar demonstrations of the Vietnam War era, organized by the National Mobilization Committee to End the War in Vietnam. The presence of armed military police and the Pentagon location make the context clear. Choices B, C, and D describe other historical protest movements unrelated to this event.

La presencia de policía militar armada y la ubicación en el Pentágono hacen el contexto evidente. Las opciones B, C y D describen otros movimientos de protesta históricos no relacionados con este evento.

items.explanation: Arms limitation agreements that capped nuclear weapons between superpowers. Choice D is wrong because it describes it eliminated an entire class of nuclear missiles and built mutual trust, not arms limitation agreements that capped nuclear weapons between superpowers. Nuclear weapons changed global strategy by making deterrence and crisis management central to superpower relations.
items.explanationEs: Los Tratados de Limitación de Armas Estratégicas (SALT I en 1972, SALT II en 1979) pusieron límites al número de misiles nucleares y lanzadores que cada superpotencia podía poseer. Estos fueron acuerdos históricos en la reducción del riesgo de guerra nuclear durante la distención.

items.stem: What were the SALT Treaties and why were they significant?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué fueron los Tratados SALT y por qué fueron significativos?

choices.text: Arms limitation agreements that froze the number of nuclear weapons each side could have
choices.textEs: Acuerdos de limitación de armas que congelaron el número de armas nucleares que cada lado podía tener

choices.text: A period of reduced tensions and increased diplomacy between the U.S. and Soviet Union
choices.textEs: Acuerdos comerciales que abrieron los mercados soviéticos a los negocios estadounidenses

choices.text: College deferments meant wealthier young men could avoid service while poorer men could not
choices.textEs: Programas de intercambio cultural que enviaban estudiantes entre los dos países

choices.text: Graphic footage of combat in living rooms turned public opinion against the war
choices.textEs: Tratados ambientales para reducir la contaminación en ambas naciones

items.explanation: Arms limitation agreements that froze the number of nuclear weapons each side could have. Choice C is wrong because it describes college deferments meant wealthier young men could avoid service while poorer men could not, not arms limitation agreements that froze the number of nuclear weapons each side could have. Nuclear weapons changed global strategy by making deterrence and crisis management central to superpower relations.
items.explanationEs: Las Conversaciones sobre Limitación de Armas Estratégicas (SALT I en 1972, SALT II en 1979) fueron los primeros acuerdos entre EE.UU. y la URSS para limitar el crecimiento de arsenales nucleares.

items.stem: What was the long-term impact of the Korean War on U.S. foreign policy?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál fue el impacto a largo plazo de la Guerra de Corea en la política exterior de EE.UU.?

choices.text: It established U.S. willingness to fight limited wars to contain communism without full war
choices.textEs: Estableció disposición de EE.UU. de pelear guerras limitadas para contener comunismo sin guerra total

choices.text: A mutual defense alliance formed by the Soviet Union and Eastern European communist nations
choices.textEs: Llevó a retiro completo de EE.UU. de todos asuntos asiáticos y compromisos militares

choices.text: MacArthur's dismissal for wanting to expand war and the stalemate outcome show clear limits
choices.textEs: Terminó todas alianzas militares y cooperación con naciones asiáticas por varias décadas

choices.text: It showed the difficulty of achieving clear victory while avoiding escalation to world war
choices.textEs: Causó paz inmediata y duradera entre Estados Unidos y la Unión Soviética

items.explanation: The long-term impact of the Korean War on U.S. foreign policy was It established U.S. willingness to fight limited wars to contain communism without full war. Choice B is wrong because it describes mutual defense alliance formed by the Soviet Union and Eastern European communist nations, not it established U.S. willingness to fight limited wars to contain communism without full war. Korea made containment a military commitment and showed how limited wars could become long, costly stalemates.
items.explanationEs: La Guerra de Corea demostró el compromiso de EE.UU. con la contención a través de guerras limitadas y conflictos proxy en lugar de confrontación directa con potencias nucleares, estableciendo el patrón para intervenciones de la Guerra Fría.

items.stem: According to Eisenhower's Farewell Address, what dangers did he see in the military-industrial complex?
items.stemEs: Según el Discurso de Despedida de Eisenhower, ¿qué peligros veía en el complejo militar-industrial?

choices.text: Only informed citizens could hold government accountable and prevent excessive military power
choices.textEs: Una peligrosa falta de cooperación entre establecimiento militar e industria de defensa

choices.text: National security requires strong military, but that same partnership could threaten democracy
choices.textEs: Gasto militar insuficiente que dejaba la nación vulnerable a ataque soviético directo

choices.text: Unwarranted influence over government that could endanger liberties and democratic processes
choices.textEs: Influencia injustificada sobre gobierno que podría poner en peligro libertades y procesos democráticos

choices.text: Total war between superpowers became suicidal, leading to proxy wars and indirect rivalry
choices.textEs: La guerra total entre las superpotencias se volvió suicida, lo que condujo a guerras por delegación y a la rivalidad indirecta

items.explanation: Unwarranted influence over government that could endanger liberties and democratic processes. Choice A is wrong because it describes only informed citizens could hold government accountable and prevent excessive military power, not unwarranted influence over government that could endanger liberties and democratic processes. Nuclear weapons changed global strategy by making deterrence and crisis management central to superpower relations.
items.explanationEs: Eisenhower advirtió que el complejo militar-industrial podría ganar influencia injustificada sobre política gubernamental, potencialmente poniendo en peligro procesos democráticos y libertades civiles a través de gasto militar excesivo y cabildeo.

items.stem: What paradox did Eisenhower identify in his military-industrial complex warning?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué paradoja identificó Eisenhower en su advertencia sobre el complejo militar-industrial?

choices.text: National security requires strong military, but that same partnership could threaten democracy
choices.textEs: Seguridad nacional requiere ejército fuerte, pero esa misma asociación podría amenazar democracia

choices.text: Only informed citizens could hold government accountable and prevent excessive military power
choices.textEs: El ejército era simultáneamente tanto demasiado fuerte como demasiado débil para necesidades de defensa

choices.text: Yes, subsequent decades showed military spending influenced policy and contractors gained power
choices.textEs: Gasto de defensa ayudó la economía general pero también dañó crecimiento económico al mismo tiempo

choices.text: Unwarranted influence over government that could endanger liberties and democratic processes
choices.textEs: Lograr paz requería prepararse para guerra pero guerra era ahora completamente imposible de ganar

items.explanation: National security requires strong military, but that same partnership could threaten democracy. Choice B is wrong because it describes only informed citizens could hold government accountable and prevent excessive military power, not national security requires strong military, but that same partnership could threaten democracy. Nuclear weapons changed global strategy by making deterrence and crisis management central to superpower relations.
items.explanationEs: Eisenhower reconoció que aunque defensa fuerte era necesaria para seguridad, la estrecha relación entre ejército, contratistas de defensa y gobierno podría llevar a influencia excesiva sobre política y amenazar valores democráticos que se suponía proteger.

items.stem: The hostage crisis had which of the following long-term effects on U.S.-Iranian relations?
items.stemEs: The hostage crisis had ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones long-term effects on U.S.-Iranian relations?

choices.text: It produced a mutual defense agreement with Iraq, which the U.S. viewed as a counterweight to Iran
choices.textEs: Produjo un acuerdo de defensa mutua con Irak, al que los EE.UU. veían como contrapeso frente a Irán

choices.text: It hardened American public attitudes toward Iran, contributing to decades of hostility between the two nations
choices.textEs: Endureció las actitudes del público estadounidense hacia Irán, contribuyendo a décadas de hostilidad entre las dos naciones

choices.text: It led the U.S. to impose an oil embargo on Iran that caused economic collapse
choices.textEs: Llevó a los EE.UU. a imponer un embargo petrolero a Irán que causó el colapso económico de ese país

choices.text: It permanently ended diplomatic relations between the U.S. and Iran, which were rarely fully restored
choices.textEs: Puso fin permanentemente a las relaciones diplomáticas entre los EE.UU. e Irán, que raramente se restauraron plenamente

items.explanation: It hardened American public attitudes toward Iran, contributing to decades of hostility between the two nations. Choice D is wrong because it describes it permanently ended diplomatic relations between the U.S. and Iran, which were rarely fully restored, not it hardened American public attitudes toward Iran, contributing to decades of hostility between the two nations. The hostage crisis fed the image of American weakness abroad and helped set the stage for Reagan's victory in 1980.
items.explanationEs: Endureció las actitudes públicas estadounidenses hacia Irán, contribuyendo a décadas de hostilidad entre las dos naciones. La opción A es incorrecta porque describe que produjo un acuerdo de defensa mutua con Irak, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo. Las consecuencias de la crisis de los rehenes configuraron las relaciones EE.UU.-Irán durante décadas.

items.stem: The savings and loan crisis of the late 1980s and early 1990s is historically significant because it demonstrated —
items.stemEs: La crisis de las instituciones de ahorro y préstamo de finales de los años ochenta y principios de los noventa es históricamente significativa porque ilustró —

choices.text: That small banks were more vulnerable to financial crises than large commercial banks
choices.textEs: Que los bancos pequeños eran más vulnerables a las crisis financieras que los grandes bancos comerciales

choices.text: That Reaganomics had failed to produce sustained economic growth in the financial sector
choices.textEs: Que reaganomics no había logrado generar un crecimiento económico sostenido en el sector financiero

choices.text: How deregulation without adequate oversight could lead to widespread financial fraud and costly taxpayer bailouts
choices.textEs: Cómo la desregulación sin supervisión adecuada puede conducir a fraudes financieros generalizados y costosos rescates con dinero de los contribuyentes

choices.text: The need for the Federal Reserve to actively regulate interest rates during economic downturns
choices.textEs: La necesidad de que la Reserva Federal regulara activamente las tasas de interés durante las recesiones económicas

items.explanation: How deregulation without adequate oversight could lead to widespread financial fraud and costly taxpayer bailouts. Choice A is wrong because it describes that small banks were more vulnerable to financial crises than large commercial banks, not how deregulation without adequate oversight could lead to widespread financial fraud and costly taxpayer bailouts. These debates helped define the conservative turn in American politics during the 1980s.
items.explanationEs: Cómo la desregulación sin supervisión adecuada podía conducir a un fraude financiero generalizado y costosos rescates financiados por los contribuyentes. La opción A es incorrecta porque describe que los bancos pequeños eran más vulnerables a las crisis financieras que los grandes bancos comerciales, lo cual los historiadores consideran un factor secundario en este desarrollo. La crisis de las instituciones de ahorro y préstamo fue una de las peores catástrofes financieras en la historia de los EE.UU.

items.stem: The militia movement of the 1990s reflected —
items.stemEs: El movimiento de milicias de los años noventa reflejó —

choices.text: Domestic anti-Communist investigations and loyalty programs
choices.textEs: Las investigaciones anticomerciales internas y los programas de lealtad

choices.text: Widespread opposition to the Brady Bill and assault weapons ban that had been passed in 1993-94
choices.textEs: La amplia oposición a la Ley Brady y a la prohibición de armas de asalto aprobadas en 1993-94

choices.text: A rational response to genuine threats to constitutional rights from overreaching federal enforcement
choices.textEs: Una respuesta racional a amenazas genuinas a los derechos constitucionales por parte de una aplicación federal extralimitada

choices.text: Anti-government ideology fueled by events at Ruby Ridge and Waco that cast federal agents as tyrannical
choices.textEs: Ideología antiestatal alimentada por los eventos en Ruby Ridge y Waco que presentaron a los agentes federales como tiranos

items.explanation: Both A and B contributed to the militia movement's growth in the 1990s. Choice B is wrong because it describes widespread opposition to the Brady Bill and assault weapons ban that had been passed in 1993-94, not both A and B contributed to the militia movement's growth in the 1990s. Post-Cold War events forced the United States to define how far its power and responsibilities should reach in a one-superpower world.
items.explanationEs: Both A and B contribuyó a the militia movement's growth in the 1990s. Choice B is wrong because it describes widespread opposition to the Brady Bill and assault weapons ban that had been passed in 1993-94, not both A and B contribuyó a the militia movement's growth in the 1990s. Post-Guerra Fría events forced the United States to define how far its power and responsibilities should reach in a one-superpower world.

items.stem: The Korean War (1950-1953) is best understood as which type of conflict?
items.stemEs: ¿La Guerra de Corea (1950-1953) se entiende mejor como qué tipo de conflicto?

choices.text: A conflict between rival European colonial powers
choices.textEs: Un conflicto entre potencias coloniales europeas rivales

choices.text: A war for Korean independence from Japanese colonial rule
choices.textEs: Una guerra por la independencia coreana del dominio colonial japonés

choices.text: A civil war fought entirely without foreign involvement
choices.textEs: Una guerra civil librada completamente sin participación extranjera

choices.text: A proxy war between U.S.-led and Soviet/Chinese-backed forces during the Cold War
choices.textEs: Una guerra por delegación entre fuerzas lideradas por EE. UU. y fuerzas respaldadas por la Unión Soviética y China durante la Guerra Fría

items.explanation: The Korean War (June 25, 1950 - July 27, 1953) is best understood as a proxy war between U.S.-led United Nations forces and Soviet/Chinese-backed North Korean and Chinese forces during the Cold War. After North Korea invaded South Korea, the U.N. Security Council authorized military intervention; the U.S. provided the bulk of U.N. forces, while China entered in October 1950 and the Soviet Union provided air support and materiel. Choice A is wrong because European colonial powers were not principal combatants. Choice B is wrong because Japan's colonial rule of Korea ended in 1945, five years before the war. Choice C is wrong because foreign involvement was central to the conflict. The war ended in armistice — not a peace treaty — at the 38th parallel, leaving Korea divided to this day.
items.explanationEs: La Guerra de Corea (25 de junio de 1950 - 27 de julio de 1953) se entiende mejor como una guerra subsidiaria entre las fuerzas de las Naciones Unidas lideradas por EE. UU. y las fuerzas norcoreanas y chinas respaldadas por la Unión Soviética y China durante la Guerra Fría. Tras la invasión de Corea del Sur por Corea del Norte, el Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU autorizó la intervención militar; EE. UU. aportó la mayor parte de las fuerzas de la ONU, mientras que China entró en octubre de 1950 y la Unión Soviética proporcionó apoyo aéreo y material bélico. La opción A es incorrecta porque las potencias coloniales europeas no fueron combatientes principales. La opción B es incorrecta porque el dominio colonial japonés sobre Corea terminó en 1945, cinco años antes de la guerra. La opción C es incorrecta porque la participación extranjera fue central en el conflicto. La guerra terminó con un armisticio — no un tratado de paz — en el paralelo 38, dejando a Corea dividida hasta hoy.

items.stem: How did Senator Joseph McCarthy's tactics during the Second Red Scare affect civil liberties in the United States?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo afectaron las tácticas del senador Joseph McCarthy durante el Segundo Miedo Rojo a las libertades civiles en Estados Unidos?

choices.text: McCarthy's investigations were limited to military personnel and had little effect on the broader American public
choices.textEs: Las investigaciones de McCarthy se limitaron al personal militar y tuvieron poco efecto en el público estadounidense en general

choices.text: McCarthy worked through the courts to overturn First Amendment protections for suspected communists
choices.textEs: McCarthy actuó a través de los tribunales para derogar las protecciones de la Primera Enmienda para presuntos comunistas

choices.text: McCarthy used congressional hearings and public accusations to create an atmosphere of fear that led to blacklisting and silenced political dissent
choices.textEs: McCarthy utilizó audiencias del Congreso y acusaciones públicas para crear una atmósfera de miedo que condujo a listas negras y silenció la disidencia política

choices.text: McCarthy coordinated with the Supreme Court to permanently ban the Communist Party from participating in elections
choices.textEs: McCarthy coordinó con la Corte Suprema para prohibir permanentemente al Partido Comunista participar en elecciones

items.explanation: McCarthy's Senate hearings weaponized accusation without due process, producing widespread blacklisting in government and entertainment and chilling free speech across American society.
items.explanationEs: Las audiencias en el Senado de McCarthy convirtieron las acusaciones sin debido proceso en un arma, produciendo listas negras generalizadas en el gobierno y el entretenimiento, e inhibiendo la libertad de expresión en toda la sociedad estadounidense.

items.stem: Why did the United States intervene in the Korean War rather than allowing North Korea to unify the peninsula by force?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué intervino Estados Unidos en la Guerra de Corea en lugar de permitir que Corea del Norte unificara la península por la fuerza?

choices.text: The United States had a formal treaty obligation to defend South Korea as a member of NATO
choices.textEs: Estados Unidos tenía una obligación formal de tratado de defender a Corea del Sur como miembro de la OTAN

choices.text: The United Nations ordered the United States to send troops, leaving American leaders no choice in the matter
choices.textEs: Las Naciones Unidas ordenaron a Estados Unidos enviar tropas, sin dejar a los líderes estadounidenses ninguna opción en el asunto

choices.text: The United States intervened primarily to protect its oil interests in the Korean peninsula
choices.textEs: Estados Unidos intervino principalmente para proteger sus intereses petroleros en la península coreana

choices.text: The domino theory led U.S. policymakers to believe that allowing communist expansion in Korea would encourage further communist aggression elsewhere
choices.textEs: La teoría del dominó llevó a los responsables de la política de EE. UU. a creer que permitir la expansión comunista en Corea fomentaría una mayor agresión comunista en otros lugares

items.explanation: The domino theory — the belief that communist victory in one country would trigger communist takeovers in neighboring nations — was the central rationale for U.S. intervention in Korea.
items.explanationEs: La teoría del dominó —la creencia de que la victoria comunista en un país desencadenaría tomas comunistas en las naciones vecinas— fue la justificación central para la intervención de EE. UU. en Corea.

items.stem: How did Eisenhower's policy of 'brinksmanship' differ from Truman's approach to containing Soviet expansion?
items.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferenciaba la política de «brinksmanship» (política al borde del abismo) de Eisenhower del enfoque de Truman para contener la expansión soviética?

choices.text: Brinksmanship relied on massive nuclear retaliation threats rather than costly conventional military buildups, making deterrence cheaper
choices.textEs: El brinksmanship se basó en amenazas de represalia nuclear masiva en lugar de costosas acumulaciones militares convencionales, lo que hizo la disuasión más económica

choices.text: Brinksmanship involved direct military confrontations with Soviet forces across Europe and Asia
choices.textEs: El brinksmanship implicó confrontaciones militares directas con las fuerzas soviéticas en toda Europa y Asia

choices.text: Eisenhower abandoned containment entirely and pursued a policy of rollback to liberate Soviet-controlled territories
choices.textEs: Eisenhower abandonó completamente la contención y aplicó una política de retroceso para liberar los territorios controlados por los soviéticos

choices.text: Brinksmanship reduced defense spending by establishing a formal peace treaty with the Soviet Union
choices.textEs: El brinksmanship redujo el gasto en defensa al establecer un tratado de paz formal con la Unión Soviética

items.explanation: Eisenhower's 'New Look' defense policy paired brinksmanship — threatening massive nuclear retaliation — with cuts to expensive conventional forces, relying on nuclear deterrence as a cost-effective containment strategy.
items.explanationEs: La política de «Nueva Mirada» de Eisenhower combinó el brinksmanship —amenazando con una represalia nuclear masiva— con recortes a las costosas fuerzas convencionales, apoyándose en la disuasión nuclear como estrategia de contención más rentable.

This image shows Bert the Turtle from the 1951 civil defense film "Duck and Cover," which instructed American schoolchildren to take cover under their desks in the event of a nuclear attack.

(Still from "Duck and Cover," 1951. U.S. Federal Civil Defense Administration.)

What does this civil defense campaign reveal about American society during the early Cold War?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué revela esta campaña de defensa civil sobre la sociedad estadounidense durante la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: Americans were unconcerned about nuclear weapons because they trusted government protection
choices.textEs: Los estadounidenses no se preocupaban por las armas nucleares porque confiaban en la protección del gobierno

choices.text: Fear of nuclear conflict permeated daily life, including the education of young children
choices.textEs: El miedo al conflicto nuclear permeó la vida cotidiana, incluida la educación de los niños pequeños

choices.text: The U.S. government believed nuclear war was impossible but created the film for entertainment
choices.textEs: El gobierno de EE. UU. creía que la guerra nuclear era imposible, pero creó el filme con fines de entretenimiento

choices.text: Schools independently developed emergency plans without any government involvement
choices.textEs: Las escuelas desarrollaron planes de emergencia de manera independiente sin ninguna participación del gobierno

items.explanation: The 'Duck and Cover' campaign reflects how deeply nuclear anxiety penetrated American society, reaching into elementary school classrooms and shaping the daily experiences of Cold War-era children.
items.explanationEs: La campaña refleja cómo la ansiedad nuclear penetró profundamente en la sociedad estadounidense.

This photograph shows American soldiers during the Korean War, c. 1950.

(U.S. Army photograph, c. 1950. Public Domain.)

How did the Korean War, in which the soldiers shown in this photograph fought, demonstrate the global nature of the Cold War?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo demostró la Guerra de Corea la naturaleza global de la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: The conflict involved forces from the U.S., UN allies, China, and the Soviet Union fighting over the political future of a divided Asian nation
choices.textEs: El conflicto involucró fuerzas de EE. UU., aliados de la ONU, China y la Unión Soviética disputándose el futuro político de una nación asiática dividida

choices.text: The war was a purely internal Korean affair with no outside involvement
choices.textEs: La guerra fue un asunto puramente interno coreano sin participación exterior

choices.text: The conflict was limited to a naval blockade and never involved ground troops
choices.textEs: El conflicto se limitó a un bloqueo naval y nunca involucró tropas terrestres

choices.text: The Korean War ended communism in Asia permanently
choices.textEs: La Guerra de Corea puso fin permanentemente al comunismo en Asia

items.explanation: The Korean War demonstrated that the Cold War was global: the U.S. and UN allies fought to defend South Korea, while China sent hundreds of thousands of troops to support North Korea, and the Soviet Union provided military equipment and advisors. The conflict showed that superpower rivalry could produce devastating proxy wars far from Europe.
items.explanationEs: La Guerra de Corea demostró que la rivalidad de la Guerra Fría podía producir guerras por poderes devastadoras lejos de Europa.

This photograph shows Sputnik 1, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957.

(Photograph, 1957. Public Domain.)

How did the launch of Sputnik influence domestic policy in the United States?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo influyó el lanzamiento del Sputnik en la política interna de Estados Unidos?

choices.text: It had no effect on domestic policy because the satellite was seen as a military, not civilian, issue
choices.textEs: No tuvo ningún efecto en la política interna porque el satélite se consideró un asunto militar y no civil

choices.text: Congress reduced education spending to redirect funds toward military defense
choices.textEs: El Congreso redujo el gasto en educación para redirigir fondos hacia la defensa militar

choices.text: Congress passed the National Defense Education Act to increase funding for science, math, and foreign language education
choices.textEs: El Congreso aprobó la Ley de Defensa Nacional para la Educación con el fin de aumentar el financiamiento para la educación en ciencias, matemáticas y lenguas extranjeras

choices.text: The government closed all public schools and replaced them with military academies
choices.textEs: El gobierno cerró todas las escuelas públicas y las reemplazó por academias militares

items.explanation: The Sputnik crisis directly led to the National Defense Education Act (NDEA) of 1958, which provided federal funding for education in science, mathematics, and foreign languages. It also led to the creation of NASA and the Advanced Research Projects Agency (ARPA, later DARPA), demonstrating how Cold War competition drove domestic policy changes.
items.explanationEs: La crisis del Sputnik llevó a la Ley Nacional de Educación para la Defensa (1958) y la creación de la NASA.

This U.S. reconnaissance photograph shows Soviet missile installations in Cuba, October 1962.

(U.S. Department of Defense photograph, 1962. Public Domain.)

How did President Kennedy respond to the threat documented in this photograph?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo respondió el presidente Kennedy a la amenaza documentada en esta fotografía?

choices.text: He immediately ordered a full-scale military invasion of Cuba
choices.textEs: Ordenó de inmediato una invasión militar a gran escala de Cuba

choices.text: He imposed a naval blockade (quarantine) of Cuba and demanded the removal of Soviet missiles
choices.textEs: Impuso un bloqueo naval (cuarentena) a Cuba y exigió la retirada de los misiles soviéticos

choices.text: He negotiated a military alliance with the Soviet Union to share control of the missiles
choices.textEs: Negoció una alianza militar con la Unión Soviética para compartir el control de los misiles

choices.text: He ignored the intelligence and took no action against the missile installations
choices.textEs: Ignoró la información de inteligencia y no tomó ninguna medida contra las instalaciones de misiles

items.explanation: Kennedy imposed a naval quarantine around Cuba to prevent additional Soviet military shipments, while demanding the removal of missiles already in place. After 13 tense days of negotiation, the Soviet Union agreed to remove the missiles in exchange for a U.S. pledge not to invade Cuba and the secret removal of U.S. Jupiter missiles from Turkey.
items.explanationEs: Kennedy impuso un bloqueo naval de Cuba y exigió la remoción de los misiles soviéticos.

This photograph shows Buzz Aldrin on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission, July 20, 1969.

(NASA photograph, 1969. Public Domain.)

How did the Moon landing, shown in this photograph, serve the strategic goals of the United States during the Cold War?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo sirvió el alunizaje a los objetivos estratégicos de EE.UU. durante la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: It demonstrated American technological superiority over the Soviet Union and served as a powerful propaganda victory in the Space Race
choices.textEs: Demostró la superioridad tecnológica de EE. UU. sobre la Unión Soviética y sirvió como una poderosa victoria propagandística en la Carrera Espacial

choices.text: It ended the Cold War because the Soviet Union conceded defeat after the landing
choices.textEs: Puso fin a la Guerra Fría porque la Unión Soviética reconoció su derrota tras el alunizaje

choices.text: The Moon landing was a purely scientific mission with no political significance
choices.textEs: El alunizaje fue una misión puramente científica sin ninguna importancia política

choices.text: It was conducted jointly with the Soviet Union as a sign of cooperation
choices.textEs: Se realizó conjuntamente con la Unión Soviética como señal de cooperación

items.explanation: The Apollo 11 Moon landing was a decisive Cold War victory. After years of Soviet firsts (Sputnik, Gagarin), the Moon landing demonstrated that American science, technology, and the capitalist system could achieve humanity's greatest exploration feat, restoring U.S. prestige and validating Kennedy's vision of American leadership.
items.explanationEs: El alunizaje fue una victoria decisiva de la Guerra Fría que demostró la superioridad tecnológica estadounidense.
