(U.S. Department of Defense photograph, 1962. Public Domain.)

Which statement best analyzes how the Cuban Missile Crisis influenced the trajectory of U.S.-Soviet relations during the Cold War?
items.stemEs:
Utiliza la fotografía para responder la pregunta.

Esta fotografía de reconocimiento aéreo muestra instalaciones soviéticas de misiles en Cuba, octubre de 1962.

(Fotografía del Departamento de Defensa de los Estados Unidos, 1962. Dominio público.)

¿Cuál enunciado analiza mejor cómo la Crisis de los Misiles en Cuba influyó en la trayectoria de las relaciones entre Estados Unidos y la Unión Soviética durante la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: The crisis ended the Cold War immediately as both sides agreed to permanent disarmament
choices.textEs: La crisis puso fin inmediatamente a la Guerra Fría cuando ambas partes acordaron un desarme permanente

choices.text: The crisis had no lasting impact because tensions returned to pre-crisis levels within weeks
choices.textEs: La crisis no tuvo un impacto duradero porque las tensiones volvieron a los niveles previos a la crisis en pocas semanas

choices.text: The crisis led to a complete breakdown in communication between the two superpowers
choices.textEs: La crisis condujo a una ruptura total de la comunicación entre las dos superpotencias

choices.text: The near-catastrophe prompted both superpowers to establish communication channels and pursue arms control agreements, including the Nuclear Test Ban Treaty and the Moscow-Washington hotline
choices.textEs: El casi catastrófico evento llevó a ambas superpotencias a establecer canales de comunicación y a buscar acuerdos de control de armamentos, incluido el Tratado de Prohibición Parcial de Pruebas Nucleares y la línea directa Moscú-Washington

items.explanation: The Cuban Missile Crisis was a turning point in Cold War relations. The terrifying proximity to nuclear war motivated both sides to improve communication (Moscow-Washington hotline, 1963), pursue arms control (Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty, 1963), and eventually move toward détente. The crisis demonstrated that direct confrontation risked mutual destruction, pushing both superpowers toward diplomatic management of their rivalry.
items.explanationEs: La crisis motivó a ambas superpotencias a mejorar la comunicación y buscar el control de armamentos, sentando las bases para la distensión.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows the Apollo 11 Moon landing, July 20, 1969.

(NASA photograph, 1969. Public Domain.)

Which statement best evaluates the extent to which the Space Race served as both a scientific achievement and a tool of Cold War competition?
items.stemEs:
Utiliza la fotografía para responder la pregunta.

Esta fotografía muestra el alunizaje del Apollo 11, el 20 de julio de 1969.

(Fotografía de la NASA, 1969. Dominio público.)

¿Cuál enunciado evalúa mejor en qué medida la carrera espacial sirvió tanto como logro científico como instrumento de la competencia durante la Guerra Fría?

choices.text: The Space Race was entirely a scientific endeavor that had no connection to Cold War politics
choices.textEs: La Carrera Espacial fue completamente un esfuerzo científico que no tuvo ninguna conexión con la política de la Guerra Fría

choices.text: While producing genuine scientific breakthroughs, the Space Race was fundamentally driven by superpower rivalry, with each achievement framed as evidence of systemic superiority
choices.textEs: Si bien produjo genuinos avances científicos, la Carrera Espacial fue impulsada fundamentalmente por la rivalidad entre superpotencias, con cada logro enmarcado como evidencia de la superioridad sistémica

choices.text: The Space Race produced no lasting scientific benefits and was purely a military competition
choices.textEs: La Carrera Espacial no produjo beneficios científicos duraderos y fue puramente una competencia militar

choices.text: Both superpowers agreed to share all space technology to advance human knowledge
choices.textEs: Ambas superpotencias acordaron compartir toda la tecnología espacial para avanzar en el conocimiento humano

items.explanation: The Space Race produced extraordinary scientific achievements — satellite communications, weather monitoring, computing advances, materials science — while simultaneously serving as a stage for ideological competition. Each milestone was celebrated not just as science but as proof of systemic superiority. The dual nature is reflected in NASA's mission: advancing human knowledge while demonstrating American capability to the world.
items.explanationEs: La Carrera Espacial produjo logros científicos extraordinarios mientras servía simultáneamente como escenario de competencia ideológica.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph from October 21, 1967, shows anti-Vietnam War protesters confronting military police at the Pentagon during the March on the Pentagon.

(U.S. Government photograph, 1967. Public Domain.)

Which statement best evaluates how antiwar protests like the one shown contributed to shifts in U.S. policy toward the Vietnam War?
items.stemEs:
Observe la fotografía para responder la pregunta.

Esta fotografía del 21 de octubre de 1967 muestra a manifestantes contra la Guerra de Vietnam enfrentándose a la policía militar frente al Pentágono durante la Marcha sobre el Pentágono. Jóvenes hombres y mujeres se encuentran frente a filas de soldados armados con cascos y rifles. Los manifestantes parecen ser civiles de pie muy cerca de la línea militar, lo que ilustra la dramática oposición interna a la participación de EE. UU. en la Guerra de Vietnam que había crecido a fines de la década de 1960.

(Fotografía de la protesta antibelicista en el Pentágono, 21 de octubre de 1967. Biblioteca del Congreso, División de Impresas y Fotografías.)

Analice cómo el movimiento de protesta antibelicista mostrado en esta fotografía influyó en la política del gobierno de EE. UU. con respecto a la Guerra de Vietnam.

choices.text: Antiwar protests directly and immediately caused President Johnson to withdraw all U.S. troops from Vietnam in 1967
choices.textEs: Las protestas antibelicistas causaron directa e inmediatamente que el presidente Johnson retirara todas las tropas de EE. UU. de Vietnam en 1967

choices.text: Antiwar protests had no measurable influence on government policy because elected officials consistently ignored public opinion on military matters
choices.textEs: Las protestas antibelicistas no tuvieron ninguna influencia medible en la política del gobierno porque los funcionarios electos ignoraron sistemáticamente la opinión pública en asuntos militares

choices.text: Antiwar protests caused the government to escalate military operations in Vietnam to demonstrate strength and resolve to protesters
choices.textEs: Las protestas antibelicistas hicieron que el gobierno intensificara las operaciones militares en Vietnam para demostrar fortaleza y determinación ante los manifestantes

choices.text: Antiwar protests contributed to a political climate that pressured President Johnson not to seek re-election, influenced the Nixon administration's Vietnamization strategy, and helped build Congressional opposition that eventually cut off war funding
choices.textEs: Las protestas antibelicistas contribuyeron a un clima político que presionó al presidente Johnson a no buscar la reelección, influyeron en la estrategia de vietnamización de la administración Nixon y ayudaron a construir la oposición del Congreso que eventualmente cortó el financiamiento de la guerra

items.explanation: The antiwar movement had a complex, indirect influence on Vietnam policy. Protest activity contributed to the political climate in which President Johnson announced in March 1968 that he would not seek re-election and initiated peace talks, demonstrating that domestic opposition had real political consequences. The movement also influenced the Nixon administration's 'Vietnamization' strategy — transferring combat responsibility to South Vietnamese forces while withdrawing American troops — and contributed to Congress's eventual 1973 refusal to fund further military operations in Southeast Asia. However, the war continued for years after protests began, and some historians argue protests may have hardened some policymakers' positions. Choice A overstates direct causation. Choice B unduly minimizes effect. Choice C inverts the actual policy direction.
items.explanationEs: El movimiento antibelicista tuvo una influencia compleja e indirecta en la política de Vietnam. La actividad de protesta contribuyó al clima político en que el presidente Johnson anunció en marzo de 1968 que no buscaría la reelección e inició conversaciones de paz, lo que demostró que la oposición interna tenía consecuencias políticas reales. El movimiento también influyó en la estrategia de «vietnamización» de la administración Nixon —transferir la responsabilidad del combate a las fuerzas survietnamitas mientras se retiraban las tropas estadounidenses— y contribuyó a la eventual negativa del Congreso en 1973 a financiar más operaciones militares en el Sudeste Asiático. Sin embargo, la guerra continuó durante años después de que comenzaran las protestas, y algunos historiadores argumentan que las protestas pueden haber endurecido las posiciones de algunos responsables de las políticas. La opción A sobreestima la causalidad directa. La opción B minimiza indebidamente el efecto. La opción C invierte la dirección real de la política.

items.stem: What did the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution authorize the President to do?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué autorizó al presidente a hacer la Resolución del Golfo de Tonkin?

choices.text: Open formal diplomatic relations with North Vietnam
choices.textEs: Establecer relaciones diplomáticas formales con Vietnam del Norte

choices.text: Withdraw all U.S. troops from Vietnam immediately
choices.textEs: Retirar de inmediato todas las tropas de EE. UU. de Vietnam

choices.text: Use armed force in Southeast Asia without a formal declaration of war
choices.textEs: Usar la fuerza armada en el Sudeste Asiático sin una declaración formal de guerra

choices.text: End the military draft for the duration of the Vietnam conflict
choices.textEs: Poner fin al servicio militar obligatorio durante el conflicto de Vietnam

items.explanation: The Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, Public Law 88-408 enacted August 10, 1964, authorized the President to use armed force in Southeast Asia without a formal declaration of war. Passed by Congress 416-0 in the House and 88-2 in the Senate after reported North Vietnamese attacks on U.S. destroyers, the resolution gave President Johnson broad latitude to escalate U.S. military involvement, ultimately to over 500,000 troops by 1968. Choice A is wrong because the resolution authorized force, not diplomacy. Choice B is wrong because the resolution authorized escalation, not withdrawal. Choice D is wrong because the draft continued until 1973 under the Selective Service System. The resolution was repealed in January 1971 amid growing congressional concern over executive war-making.
items.explanationEs: La Resolución del Golfo de Tonkín, Ley Pública 88-408 promulgada el 10 de agosto de 1964, autorizó al Presidente a usar la fuerza armada en el Sudeste Asiático sin una declaración formal de guerra. Aprobada por el Congreso 416-0 en la Cámara y 88-2 en el Senado tras los reportados ataques norvietnamitas contra destructores estadounidenses, la resolución otorgó al presidente Johnson amplia libertad para escalar la participación militar de EE. UU., llegando finalmente a más de 500.000 tropas para 1968. La opción A es incorrecta porque la resolución autorizó el uso de la fuerza, no la diplomacia. La opción B es incorrecta porque la resolución autorizó la escalada, no la retirada. La opción D es incorrecta porque el reclutamiento continuó hasta 1973 bajo el Sistema de Servicio Selectivo. La resolución fue derogada en enero de 1971 en medio de la creciente preocupación del Congreso por la conducción ejecutiva de la guerra.

items.stem: The War Powers Resolution was passed primarily to —
items.stemEs: La Resolución de Poderes de Guerra fue aprobada principalmente para —

choices.text: Expand the President's authority to wage war without congressional input
choices.textEs: Ampliar la autoridad del presidente para llevar a cabo una guerra sin aportación del Congreso

choices.text: Limit presidential power to commit U.S. forces without congressional approval
choices.textEs: Limitar el poder presidencial para comprometer fuerzas de EE. UU. sin la aprobación del Congreso

choices.text: Authorize the President to declare war unilaterally
choices.textEs: Autorizar al presidente a declarar la guerra unilateralmente

choices.text: Require all military spending to be approved by the Supreme Court
choices.textEs: Requerir que todo el gasto militar fuera aprobado por la Corte Suprema

items.explanation: The War Powers Resolution, Public Law 93-148 enacted November 7, 1973, over President Nixon's veto, was passed primarily to limit presidential power to commit U.S. forces without congressional approval. The law requires the president to notify Congress within 48 hours of deploying forces and prohibits forces from remaining in hostilities longer than 60 days (with a 30-day withdrawal period) without congressional authorization. Choice A is wrong because the law restricts, not expands, presidential war powers. Choice C is wrong because Article I, Section 8 of the Constitution reserves the power to declare war to Congress. Choice D is wrong because the Supreme Court does not approve military spending — that authority belongs to Congress under the appropriations clause. The resolution emerged directly from concerns over Vietnam-era escalation.
items.explanationEs: La Resolución de Poderes de Guerra, Ley Pública 93-148 promulgada el 7 de noviembre de 1973 sobre el veto del presidente Nixon, fue aprobada principalmente para limitar el poder presidencial de comprometer fuerzas estadounidenses sin la aprobación del Congreso. La ley exige que el presidente notifique al Congreso dentro de las 48 horas posteriores al despliegue de fuerzas y prohíbe que las fuerzas permanezcan en hostilidades más de 60 días (con un período de retirada de 30 días) sin autorización del Congreso. La opción A es incorrecta porque la ley restringe, no amplía, los poderes presidenciales de guerra. La opción C es incorrecta porque el Artículo I, Sección 8 de la Constitución reserva al Congreso el poder de declarar la guerra. La opción D es incorrecta porque la Corte Suprema no aprueba el gasto militar — esa autoridad corresponde al Congreso bajo la cláusula de asignaciones. La resolución surgió directamente de las preocupaciones sobre la escalada en la era de Vietnam.

items.stem: Nixon's 1972 visit to China and the SALT I agreement with the Soviet Union represented a fundamental strategic shift for a president who had built his entire political career on fierce anti-communist positions. Which argument provides the most analytically complete explanation for why Nixon was uniquely positioned to pursue détente with communist powers?
items.stemEs: La visita de Nixon a China en 1972 y el acuerdo SALT I con la Unión Soviética representaron un cambio estratégico fundamental para un presidente que había construido toda su carrera política en posiciones ferozmente anticomunistas. ¿Cuál argumento proporciona la explicación analíticamente más completa de por qué Nixon estaba en una posición única para buscar la distensión con las potencias comunistas?

choices.text: Nixon's anti-communist record was always more strategic theater than genuine conviction — designed to accumulate political capital he could spend on realist diplomacy once in power — revealing that most prominent Cold War ideologues privately held pragmatic views they could not express publicly before achieving executive authority.
choices.textEs: El historial anticomunista de Nixon siempre fue más un teatro estratégico que una convicción genuina —diseñado para acumular capital político que pudiera gastar en diplomacia realista una vez en el poder— revelando que la mayoría de los ideólogos prominentes de la Guerra Fría mantuvieron en privado puntos de vista pragmáticos que no podían expresar públicamente antes de alcanzar la autoridad ejecutiva.

choices.text: American military setbacks in Vietnam and the growing power of Western Europe and Japan had so weakened U.S. relative power by 1969 that any president would have pursued accommodation with China and the Soviet Union, making Nixon's specific ideological history irrelevant to the policy outcomes.
choices.textEs: Los reveses militares estadounidenses en Vietnam y el creciente poder de Europa Occidental y Japón habían debilitado tanto el poder relativo de EE. UU. para 1969 que cualquier presidente habría buscado un acuerdo con China y la Unión Soviética, haciendo irrelevante la historia ideológica específica de Nixon para los resultados de la política.

choices.text: Nixon pursued détente primarily because Henry Kissinger's realist foreign policy philosophy dominated administration decision-making, with Nixon's principal contribution being political cover for Kissinger's strategic vision rather than independent strategic initiative of his own.
choices.textEs: Nixon buscó la distensión principalmente porque la filosofía de política exterior realista de Henry Kissinger dominó la toma de decisiones de la administración, siendo la contribución principal de Nixon la cobertura política para la visión estratégica de Kissinger más que la iniciativa estratégica independiente propia.

choices.text: Nixon's established anti-communist credentials provided domestic political protection against charges of appeasement that would have been politically fatal for a liberal president, while his strategic realism and Kissinger's exploitation of the Sino-Soviet split simultaneously provided both the motive and the opportunity for opening to China — making his decades of ideological positioning a strategic asset that enabled
choices.textEs: Las credenciales anticomunistas establecidas de Nixon le proporcionaron protección política doméstica frente a las acusaciones de apaciguamiento que habrían sido políticamente fatales para un presidente liberal, mientras que su realismo estratégico y la explotación por parte de Kissinger de la ruptura sino-soviética proporcionaron simultáneamente tanto el motivo como la oportunidad para la apertura hacia China —haciendo de sus décadas de posicionamiento ideológico un activo estratégico que posibilitó la iniciativa.

items.explanation: The 'only Nixon could go to China' analysis is grounded in real strategic logic: a liberal Democratic president who opened to Beijing would have faced devastating domestic attacks from the Republican anti-communist right that could have derailed the initiative politically — Nixon's specific partisan and ideological history created a domestic political insulation that made the diplomatic opening achievable in ways it would not have been for any president without his particular record. Unit 8: A Nation in Transition, 1950s–1963 (US.71–US.77)
items.explanationEs: El análisis de que «solo Nixon podía ir a China» se basa en una lógica estratégica real: un presidente demócrata liberal que abriera relaciones con Pekín habría enfrentado devastadores ataques domésticos de la derecha anticomunista republicana que podrían haber descarrilado la iniciativa políticamente —el historial partisan e ideológico específico de Nixon creó un aislamiento político doméstico que hizo posible la apertura diplomática de maneras en que no lo habría sido para ningún presidente sin su historial particular.

items.stem: Which best explains why communist governments across Eastern Europe collapsed so rapidly between 1989 and 1991?
items.stemEs: ¿Cuál explica mejor por qué los gobiernos comunistas en toda Europa del Este colapsaron tan rápidamente entre 1989 y 1991?

choices.text: Reagan's military buildup forced the Soviet Union to spend so heavily on defense that it could no longer provide the economic support Eastern European governments required.
choices.textEs: El aumento de gasto militar de Reagan obligó a la Unión Soviética a gastar tanto en defensa que ya no podía proporcionar el apoyo económico que requerían los gobiernos de Europa del Este.

choices.text: NATO military pressure created internal divisions within Eastern European communist parties that led to their peaceful dissolution.
choices.textEs: La presión militar de la OTAN creó divisiones internas dentro de los partidos comunistas de Europa del Este que llevaron a su pacífica disolución.

choices.text: Gorbachev's reforms signaled that the Soviet Union would no longer use military force to preserve Eastern European communist governments, removing the threat that had suppressed popular opposition for decades.
choices.textEs: Las reformas de Gorbachev señalaron que la Unión Soviética ya no usaría la fuerza militar para preservar los gobiernos comunistas de Europa del Este, eliminando la amenaza que había suprimido la oposición popular durante décadas.

choices.text: Economic integration with Western Europe had already transformed Eastern European economies, making communist central planning unsustainable by 1989.
choices.textEs: La integración económica con Europa Occidental ya había transformado las economías de Europa del Este, haciendo insostenible la planificación central comunista para 1989.

items.explanation: The Brezhnev Doctrine had guaranteed Soviet military intervention to preserve communist governments (as in Hungary 1956 and Czechoslovakia 1968). When Gorbachev signaled through glasnost and perestroika that he would not repeat this, popular opposition movements — which had always existed — could act without fear of Soviet tanks, producing rapid collapse.
items.explanationEs: La Doctrina Brezhnev había garantizado la intervención militar soviética para preservar los gobiernos comunistas (como en Hungría en 1956 y Checoslovaquia en 1968). Cuando Gorbachev señaló a través del glasnost y la perestroika que no repetiría esto, los movimientos de oposición popular —que siempre habían existido— pudieron actuar sin temor a los tanques soviéticos, produciendo un colapso rápido.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The détente policy seeks to reduce the dangers of direct confrontation by establishing areas of cooperation — trade, arms control, diplomacy — with the Soviet Union while maintaining the fundamental competition between our systems." — Henry Kissinger, Senate Testimony, 1974

Evaluate Kissinger's détente strategy. Which of the following best analyzes the key tension in the détente approach to U.S.-Soviet relations?
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento.

«La política de distensión busca reducir los peligros de la confrontación directa estableciendo áreas de cooperación —comercio, control de armamentos, diplomacia— con la Unión Soviética, al tiempo que mantiene la competencia fundamental entre nuestros sistemas.» — Henry Kissinger, Testimonio ante el Senado, 1974

Evalúe la estrategia de distensión de Kissinger. ¿Cuál de los siguientes analiza mejor la tensión clave en el enfoque de la distensión para las relaciones entre EE. UU. y la Unión Soviética?

choices.text: Détente sought to cooperate with the Soviet Union on practical matters while maintaining the fundamental ideological competition — a strategy critics attacked from both right (too soft on communism) and left (not committed enough to peace).
choices.textEs: La distensión buscó cooperar con la Unión Soviética en asuntos prácticos mientras mantenía la competencia ideológica fundamental —una estrategia que los críticos atacaron tanto desde la derecha (demasiado blanda con el comunismo) como desde la izquierda (no suficientemente comprometida con la paz)—.

choices.text: Détente resolved the ideological competition between the U.S. and Soviet Union by establishing that neither system was superior.
choices.textEs: La distensión resolvió la competencia ideológica entre EE. UU. y la Unión Soviética al establecer que ninguno de los sistemas era superior.

choices.text: Détente required that both the U.S. and Soviet Union gradually abandon their opposing political and economic systems.
choices.textEs: La distensión requirió que tanto EE. UU. como la Unión Soviética abandonaran gradualmente sus sistemas políticos y económicos opuestos.

choices.text: Détente was designed to ignore the fundamental tensions between the superpowers and focus only on avoiding direct military conflict.
choices.textEs: La distensión fue diseñada para ignorar las tensiones fundamentales entre las superpotencias y centrarse únicamente en evitar el conflicto militar directo.

items.explanation: Kissinger's détente strategy tried to manage a fundamental tension: the U.S. and Soviet Union were locked in an ideological competition (capitalism vs. communism, democracy vs. authoritarianism) while also sharing an interest in avoiding nuclear war. Détente tried to cooperate on practical matters (trade, arms control) while acknowledging that the underlying competition continued. Critics from the right argued détente legitimized Soviet power and abandoned human rights; critics from the left argued it didn't go far enough toward peace. Option B is incorrect because détente explicitly acknowledged continued competition, not ending it. Option C is incorrect because détente did not require one side to abandon its system. Option D is incorrect because détente was specifically designed to reduce tensions, not ignore them.
items.explanationEs: La estrategia de distensión de Kissinger intentó manejar una tensión fundamental: EE. UU. y la Unión Soviética estaban atrapados en una competencia ideológica (capitalismo frente a comunismo, democracia frente a autoritarismo) al mismo tiempo que compartían un interés en evitar una guerra nuclear. La distensión intentó cooperar en asuntos prácticos (comercio, control de armamentos) reconociendo al mismo tiempo que la competencia subyacente continuaba. Los críticos de la derecha argumentaron que la distensión legitimaba el poder soviético y abandonaba los derechos humanos; los críticos de la izquierda argumentaron que no iba lo suficientemente lejos hacia la paz. La opción B es incorrecta porque la distensión reconoció explícitamente la competencia continua, no su fin. La opción C es incorrecta porque la distensión no requería que ninguno de los lados abandonara su sistema. La opción D es incorrecta porque la distensión fue diseñada específicamente para reducir las tensiones, no para ignorarlas.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Helsinki Accords recognize the sovereignty of all European states, including those in Eastern Europe. But in exchange for this recognition, the Soviets must accept human rights provisions that we can use to hold them accountable." — National Security Advisor Brent Scowcroft, 1975

Analyze the strategic value of the 1975 Helsinki Accords for U.S. policy. Which of the following best evaluates the long-term consequences of the human rights provisions?
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento.

«Los Acuerdos de Helsinki reconocen la soberanía de todos los estados europeos, incluidos los de Europa del Este. Pero a cambio de este reconocimiento, los soviéticos deben aceptar disposiciones de derechos humanos que podemos usar para exigirles responsabilidades.» — Asesor de Seguridad Nacional Brent Scowcroft, 1975

Analice el valor estratégico de los Acuerdos de Helsinki de 1975 para la política de EE. UU. ¿Cuál de los siguientes evalúa mejor las consecuencias a largo plazo de las disposiciones de derechos humanos?

choices.text: The Soviets immediately liberalized their human rights practices after signing the Accords, demonstrating the success of détente.
choices.textEs: Los soviéticos liberalizaron de inmediato sus prácticas de derechos humanos después de firmar los Acuerdos, demostrando el éxito de la distensión.

choices.text: The Accords were a diplomatic failure because they legitimized Soviet control of Eastern Europe without any real human rights gains.
choices.textEs: Los Acuerdos fueron un fracaso diplomático porque legitimaron el control soviético de Europa del Este sin ningún logro real en materia de derechos humanos.

choices.text: The human rights provisions empowered Eastern European dissidents to use the Accords as a legal basis for challenging communist governments, contributing to the collapse of communism in 1989.
choices.textEs: Las disposiciones de derechos humanos empoderaron a los disidentes de Europa del Este para utilizar los Acuerdos como base jurídica para desafiar a los gobiernos comunistas, contribuyendo al colapso del comunismo en 1989.

choices.text: The Accords established a secret bilateral U.S.-Soviet agreement on human rights that was never shared with other nations.
choices.textEs: Los Acuerdos establecieron un acuerdo bilateral secreto entre EE. UU. y la Unión Soviética sobre derechos humanos que nunca fue compartido con otras naciones.

items.explanation: The Helsinki Accords' human rights provisions (Basket III) proved to have far-reaching consequences that were not immediately apparent. Eastern European dissidents and human rights activists used the Accords as a legal basis for challenging communist governments — forming Helsinki Watch groups (the forerunner of Human Rights Watch) and providing a legitimate framework for demanding freedom of expression and assembly. This grassroots activism, empowered by the Accords, contributed significantly to the eventual collapse of communist governments in 1989. Option A is incorrect because the Soviets did not immediately liberalize — the impact was long-term and indirect. Option B is incorrect because critics argued the U.S. was legitimizing Soviet control of Eastern Europe. Option D is incorrect because the Accords were multilateral, not a bilateral U.S.-Soviet deal.
items.explanationEs: Las disposiciones de derechos humanos de los Acuerdos de Helsinki (Cesta III) demostraron tener consecuencias de largo alcance que no eran inmediatamente evidentes. Los disidentes de Europa del Este y los activistas de derechos humanos utilizaron los Acuerdos como base jurídica para desafiar a los gobiernos comunistas —formando grupos Helsinki Watch (el precursor de Human Rights Watch) y proporcionando un marco legítimo para exigir la libertad de expresión y de reunión—. Este activismo de base, potenciado por los Acuerdos, contribuyó significativamente al eventual colapso de los gobiernos comunistas en 1989. La opción A es incorrecta porque los soviéticos no liberalizaron de inmediato —el impacto fue a largo plazo e indirecto—. La opción B es incorrecta porque los críticos argumentaron que EE. UU. estaba legitimando el control soviético de Europa del Este. La opción D es incorrecta porque los Acuerdos fueron multilaterales, no un acuerdo bilateral entre EE. UU. y la Unión Soviética.

items.stem: The Korean War is often called the 'Forgotten War.' Historically, this perception may reflect —
items.stemEs: The Guerra de Corea is often called the 'Forgotten War.' Historically, this perception may reflect:

choices.text: The American media's deliberate decision not to cover Korean War casualties
choices.textEs: The American media's deliberate decision not to cover Guerra de Corea casualties

choices.text: The war's complete military failure with no strategic objectives achieved
choices.textEs: The war's complete military failure with no strategic objectives achieved

choices.text: Its position between WWII and Vietnam, ending inconclusively without the clear victory Americans expected
choices.textEs: Its position between WWII and Vietnam, ending inconclusively without the clear victory Americans expected

choices.text: The absence of any major military operations throughout the conflict
choices.textEs: The absence of any major military operations throughout the conflict

items.explanation: The Korean War is called the 'Forgotten War' partly because it came between World War II and Vietnam and ended without the decisive victory many Americans expected. B is wrong because the war was not a complete military failure, and D is wrong because it involved major combat. Its ambiguous ending made it harder to fit into a simple national memory.
items.explanationEs: The Guerra de Corea is called the 'Forgotten War' partly because it came between Segunda Guerra Mundial and Vietnam and ended without the decisive victory many Americans expected. B is wrong because the war was not a complete military failure, and D is wrong because it involved major combat. Its ambiguous ending made it harder to fit into a simple national memory.

items.stem: Why do Vietnamese call the Vietnam War the "American War," and what does this reveal?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué los vietnamitas llaman a la Guerra de Vietnam la "Guerra Americana" y qué revela esto?

choices.text: Expanding advocacy for labor rights, educational access, and political representation
choices.textEs: Expanding advocacy for labor rights, educational access, and political representation

choices.text: It reflects different perspectives—Americans left, Vietnamese lived with consequences
choices.textEs: It reflects different perspectives—Americans left, Vietnamese lived with consequences

choices.text: It pushed for workplace, education, and legal reforms addressing gender discrimination
choices.textEs: It pushed for workplace, education, and legal reforms addressing gender discriminación

choices.text: By questioning conformity, consumerism, and traditional authority structures
choices.textEs: By questioning conformity, consumerism, and traditional authority structures

items.explanation: Vietnamese people often call the conflict the 'American War' because the United States left, but Vietnamese communities continued living with the war’s destruction and consequences. Choice A is about expanding advocacy for labor rights, educational access, and political representation and Choice D is about by questioning conformity, consumerism, and traditional authority structures; those options do not match reflects different perspectives—Americans left, Vietnamese lived with consequences. The topic shows how protest, migration, and cultural change reshaped American society after the 1960s.

Choice A is about expanding advocacy for labor rights, educational access, and political representation and Choice D is about by questioning conformity, consumerism, and traditional authority structures; those options do not match reflects different perspectives—Americans left, Vietnamese lived with consequences. The topic shows how protest, migration, and cultural change reshaped American society after the 1960s.

items.stem: Nixon's 'Vietnamization' strategy was designed to withdraw U.S. troops while maintaining South Vietnam's independence. Evaluating this strategy, which of the following represents its most significant flaw?
items.stemEs: La estrategia de 'Vietnamización' de Nixon fue diseñada para retirar las tropas estadounidenses mientras mantenía la independencia de Vietnam del Sur. Evaluando esta estrategia, ¿cuál de las siguientes opciones representa su falla más significativa?

choices.text: It did not address the South Vietnamese government's fundamental lack of popular legitimacy, which no amount of military training could compensate for.
choices.textEs: No abordó la falta fundamental de legitimidad popular del gobierno survietnamita, que ninguna cantidad de entrenamiento militar podría compensar.

choices.text: U.S. military equipment provided to South Vietnam was technologically inferior to North Vietnamese weapons, making it impossible to fight effectively.
choices.textEs: El equipo militar estadounidense proporcionado a Vietnam del Sur era tecnológicamente inferior a las armas norvietnamitas, haciendo imposible combatir eficazmente.

choices.text: Congressional opposition prevented Nixon from providing sufficient funding to train South Vietnamese forces effectively.
choices.textEs: La oposición del Congreso impidió que Nixon proporcionara fondos suficientes para entrenar eficazmente a las fuerzas survietnamitas.

choices.text: North Vietnam agreed to stop fighting after the U.S. withdrawal, so Vietnamization was unnecessary—South Vietnam collapsed due to internal military coups, not external attack.
choices.textEs: Vietnam del Norte acordó dejar de luchar después de la retirada de EE. UU., por lo que la vietnamización fue innecesaria; Vietnam del Sur colapsó debido a golpes militares internos, no a ataques externos.

items.explanation: Vietnamization assumed that sufficient training and equipment could make South Vietnamese forces capable of sustaining an independent war effort without U.S. combat troops. The flaw was that it did not address the fundamental political legitimacy problem: the South Vietnamese government lacked the popular support and institutional cohesion to motivate effective fighting without U.S. backing. When U.S. support ended after the Paris Peace Accords (1973), South Vietnam collapsed within two years. Options B and C identify real issues but are secondary. Option D is factually inaccurate.
items.explanationEs: La vietnamización asumía que la capacitación y el equipamiento suficientes podrían hacer capaces a las fuerzas survietnamitas de sostener un esfuerzo bélico independiente sin tropas de combate estadounidenses. La falla fue que no abordaba el problema fundamental de legitimidad política: el gobierno survietnamita carecía del apoyo popular y la cohesión institucional para motivar una lucha efectiva sin el respaldo de EE. UU. Cuando el apoyo estadounidense terminó tras los Acuerdos de Paz de París (1973), Vietnam del Sur colapsó en dos años.

items.stem: Nixon's SALT I agreement (1972) with the Soviet Union was a landmark arms control treaty. Which of the following best explains a key limitation of the agreement that prevented it from achieving comprehensive nuclear disarmament?
items.stemEs: El acuerdo SALT I de Nixon (1972) con la Unión Soviética fue un tratado histórico de control de armamentos. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor una limitación clave del acuerdo que le impidió lograr un desarme nuclear integral?

choices.text: SALT I only applied to Soviet weapons systems, allowing the United States to continue expanding its nuclear arsenal without restriction.
choices.textEs: SALT I solo se aplicó a los sistemas de armas soviéticos, permitiendo a los Estados Unidos continuar expandiendo su arsenal nuclear sin restricciones.

choices.text: The Soviet Union violated SALT I within one year, rendering the agreement meaningless as a constraint on nuclear proliferation.
choices.textEs: La Unión Soviética violó el SALT I en el plazo de un año, haciendo que el acuerdo fuera irrelevante como restricción a la proliferación nuclear.

choices.text: SALT I froze delivery launcher numbers but did not limit nuclear warheads, allowing both superpowers to multiply their actual destructive capacity by adding MIRVs to existing missiles.
choices.textEs: SALT I congeló el número de lanzadores pero no limitó las ojivas nucleares, permitiendo que ambas superpotencias multiplicaran su capacidad destructiva real añadiendo MIRV a los misiles existentes.

choices.text: SALT I excluded tactical nuclear weapons entirely, only addressing long-range intercontinental missiles while theater nuclear forces grew unchecked.
choices.textEs: SALT I excluyó por completo las armas nucleares tácticas, abordando solo los misiles intercontinentales de largo alcance mientras las fuerzas nucleares de teatro crecían sin control.

items.explanation: SALT I froze the number of strategic ballistic missile launchers but did not limit warheads (Multiple Independently Targetable Reentry Vehicles—MIRVs). Both superpowers continued to add warheads to existing missiles, so the actual destructive capacity of their arsenals continued to grow even as launcher numbers were frozen. This is a fundamental limitation of the treaty's architecture. Options A and B are factually inaccurate. Option D misrepresents what SALT I covered.
items.explanationEs: SALT I congeló el número de lanzadores de misiles balísticos estratégicos pero no limitó las ojivas nucleares (Vehículos de Reentrada de Objetivos Múltiples Independientemente Dirigibles—MIRV). Ambas superpotencias continuaron añadiendo ojivas a los misiles existentes, por lo que la capacidad destructiva real de sus arsenales siguió creciendo aunque el número de lanzadores estuviera congelado.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"China in 2021 is the world's second-largest economy, the leading exporter, and has the fastest-growing military. This is not the China of 1972 that Nixon opened relations with. Our strategy toward China must change." — National Security Council Memorandum, 2021

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of U.S.-China relations, which of the following best analyzes the long-term consequences of Nixon's opening to China in 1972?

choices.text: Nixon's opening helped integrate China into the global economy, but China's subsequent rise as a great power created new strategic challenges that the original policy never anticipated.
Nixon's opening prevented China's economic development by bringing it into a Western trade system that favored American businesses.
Nixon's opening directly caused the Soviet Union's collapse by isolating it from both the United States and China simultaneously.
China's military growth is a direct and immediate consequence of Nixon's 1972 opening, which the national security community predicted at the time.

items.explanation: Nixon's opening to China in 1972, designed to exploit the Sino-Soviet split, contributed to China's eventual integration into the global economy — a process accelerated by subsequent trade agreements and China's admission to the WTO in 2001. However, China's economic growth made it a potential strategic rival rather than a balance against the Soviet Union (which no longer exists). The 2021 memo captures how the strategic rationale that justified Nixon's opening has been overtaken by China's rise as a great power. What was a Cold War masterstroke had the long-term consequence of facilitating the rise of a potentially rival power. Option B is incorrect because Nixon's opening helped China integrate into the global economy. Option C is incorrect because the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, not as a direct result of Nixon's China policy. Option D is incorrect because China's military growth was decades in development, not an immediate result.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows Germans at the Brandenburg Gate in November 1989 after the fall of the Berlin Wall.

(Photograph, November 1989.)

To what extent did the end of the Cold War, symbolized by the event in this photograph, reshape the United States' role in global affairs?
items.stemEs: ¿En qué medida el fin de la Guerra Fría reformuló el papel de EE. UU. en asuntos globales?

choices.text: The U.S. immediately withdrew from all international commitments and adopted a policy of strict isolationism
The end of the Cold War had no effect on U.S. foreign policy because new threats immediately replaced the Soviet Union
The U.S. emerged as the sole superpower, leading to debates about humanitarian intervention, military engagement, and the role of democracy promotion
The U.S. and Russia formed a permanent military alliance that prevented all future international conflicts

items.explanation: The end of the Cold War left the United States as the world's sole superpower, prompting new debates about American foreign policy — including humanitarian interventions in the 1990s (Bosnia, Somalia), NATO expansion, and the promotion of democratic governance worldwide.
items.explanationEs: El fin de la Guerra Fría dejó a EE. UU. como la única superpotencia, generando debates sobre intervención humanitaria y promoción de la democracia.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph captures the Challenger disaster, January 28, 1986.

(Photograph, January 28, 1986. NASA.)

How does the Challenger disaster illustrate the tension between technological ambition and institutional accountability in American government programs?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo ilustra el desastre del Challenger la tensión entre la ambición tecnológica y la responsabilidad institucional?

choices.text: It shows that government agencies always prioritize safety over schedule pressures
It reveals how organizational pressure to meet launch schedules can override engineering concerns, with catastrophic consequences
It proves that private companies are always safer than government agencies at managing complex technology
It demonstrates that public support for space exploration was already declining before the disaster

items.explanation: The Rogers Commission found that NASA engineers had warned about O-ring failure risks in cold weather, but management pressured to launch on schedule. The disaster exposed how institutional culture and political pressure can compromise safety in complex government programs.
items.explanationEs: La investigación reveló cómo la presión institucional puede comprometer la seguridad en programas gubernamentales complejos.

items.stem: Explain how McCarthyism and the Red Scare of the 1950s both protected and threatened American democracy. Provide specific evidence for each side of this tension.
items.stemEs: Explique cómo el macartismo y la Amenaza Roja de los 1950 tanto protegieron como amenazaron la democracia americana.
items.correctAnswer: Protection argument: Some Soviet espionage was real (Alger Hiss, Rosenbergs); vigilance against infiltration had legitimate national security basis. Threat argument: McCarthy's tactics violated due process, destroyed careers based on accusation alone, chilled free speech and political dissent, targeted innocent people, and used fear to consolidate political power. The greater threat to democracy came from McCarthyism itself — it demonstrated that fear could be weaponized to suppress democratic freedoms.
items.explanation: Real Soviet espionage cases such as Alger Hiss and the Rosenbergs gave anti-communism some legitimate national security basis, so a strong response should acknowledge why many Americans feared communist infiltration. A strong answer must also explain that McCarthy's accusations, blacklists, and loyalty investigations often ignored due process, ruined careers, and chilled free speech. The best responses use specific evidence on both sides and then judge whether protecting the nation ever justified methods that weakened democratic rights.
items.explanationEs: Los estudiantes deben analizar ambos lados de una tensión histórica con evidencia específica.

items.stem: Senator Joseph McCarthy made his first public claim of communist infiltration in the State Department in February 1950 — just months after the Soviet atomic test and the Chinese Communist revolution — and his accusations quickly resulted in the firing of experienced East Asia specialists. What does the timing and political impact of McCarthy's charges reveal about the relationship between foreign policy setbacks and domestic political culture?

choices.text: McCarthy's success demonstrates that American democratic institutions were fundamentally unprepared to resist demagogy during Cold War anxieties, since the executive and legislative branches failed to challenge his accusations despite the absence of corroborating evidence for his most sweeping claims.

The timing of McCarthy's rise reveals that anticommunism served as a tool for political entrepreneurs to pursue partisan objectives under cover of national security, with the substance of his claims mattering less than their instrumental value for attacking the Truman administration's foreign policy record.

The McCarthyite period demonstrates that citizens in democratic societies will consistently sacrifice civil liberties during national security crises, as the broad public support for McCarthy's investigations showed that most Americans prioritized security over the constitutional protections they theoretically endorsed.

Foreign policy setbacks created an environment of public anxiety in which McCarthy's charges could gain political traction regardless of their evidentiary basis, illustrating how genuine external security threats can be exploited to generate domestic political power through the systematic manipulation of fear rather than through accurate threat assessment.

items.explanation: The direct temporal connection between the Soviet atomic test, the Chinese Communist victory, and McCarthy's first accusations illustrates the mechanism: genuine foreign policy reversals created authentic public anxiety that McCarthy could exploit by offering a simple explanation — domestic betrayal — that was emotionally satisfying even if factually unsupported.

items.stem: The Soviet launch of Sputnik in October 1957 led directly to the National Defense Education Act (1958), which provided unprecedented federal funding for science, math, and foreign language education in American public schools. How does the American response to Sputnik illustrate the relationship between Cold War competition and domestic policy development in ways that would not otherwise have occurred?

choices.text: Sputnik demonstrated that Cold War ideological competition had direct domestic policy implications — the perception that Soviet scientific achievement threatened American security created political conditions in which federal education investment became achievable, even though domestic educational reformers had been unable to achieve comparable funding on educational merit alone.

The American response to Sputnik was primarily a Soviet propaganda victory, as the United States' disproportionate reaction to a single satellite launch exposed the anxious insecurity underlying the confident consumerist prosperity it presented to the world during the Eisenhower 1950s.

NDEA passage demonstrated that Cold War bipartisan consensus could overcome ideological opposition to federal education spending that had blocked previous legislation, suggesting that national security framing could provide a political work-around for persistent disagreements about the proper scope of the federal government.

The Sputnik crisis shows that technological Cold War competition was more politically motivating for Congress than domestic economic competition, which explains why NASA received substantially greater federal investment in the late 1950s than any domestic social program including federal education assistance.

items.explanation: Sputnik's domestic policy significance lies in demonstrating that external competitive pressures can unlock domestic policy change that interest group politics and ideological disagreement would otherwise prevent — federal education funding was transformed from a politically contested domestic issue into a bipartisan security imperative.

items.stem: Which best explains why the Korean War is described by historians as a 'limited war' in the context of Cold War military strategy?

choices.text: The United States limited its military involvement because Congress refused to formally declare war, restricting the president's legal authority to escalate.
The United States deliberately chose not to use its full military capability, including nuclear weapons and direct attacks on China, to prevent the conflict from escalating into a wider war.
American military commanders deliberately minimized casualties to preserve public support for a conflict that had no formal congressional authorization.
The United Nations' policy of using minimum necessary force defined the constraints on American military operations throughout the conflict.

items.explanation: President Truman's firing of General MacArthur in April 1951 is the defining illustration of 'limited war' doctrine: MacArthur wanted to bomb Chinese supply lines and potentially use nuclear weapons; Truman prioritized avoiding a direct war with China and the Soviet Union.

items.stem: Which best explains the lasting impact of McCarthyism on American political culture during the 1950s?

choices.text: McCarthyism permanently strengthened the authority of congressional committees to conduct unrestricted investigations of the executive branch.
McCarthyism demonstrated that public accusations of disloyalty, even without substantive evidence, could destroy careers and chill political dissent.
The Army-McCarthy hearings ultimately produced public demand for stronger due process protections that were codified in federal law.
McCarthyism led directly to legislation prohibiting political parties from advocating socialist or communist economic platforms.

items.explanation: The central legacy of McCarthyism was its demonstration that the political and social costs of being labeled disloyal — even falsely — were so severe that many Americans and institutions self-censored. This chilling effect on dissent is McCarthyism's most durable historical lesson.

items.stem: Which best explains why the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution of 1964 represented a significant expansion of presidential war-making authority?

choices.text: The resolution formally declared war on North Vietnam, bypassing the traditional Senate ratification process required for military treaties.
The resolution established a permanent military alliance between the United States and South Vietnam requiring automatic American military response to any attack.
The resolution transferred all congressional oversight of Vietnam operations to a joint executive-legislative committee that operated outside Senate procedures.
The resolution authorized the president to use military force in Southeast Asia without a formal declaration of war, setting a precedent for open-ended presidential military action.

items.explanation: The Gulf of Tonkin Resolution authorized the president to take 'all necessary measures' to repel attacks and prevent further aggression — broad language used as the legal basis for massive escalation of American military involvement without a formal declaration of war.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from Senator Joseph McCarthy's speech to the Senate, June 14, 1951, Congressional Record — a U.S. government document available through the National Archives:

"How can we account for our present situation unless we believe that men high in this government are concerting to deliver us to disaster? This must be the product of a great conspiracy, a conspiracy on a scale so immense as to dwarf any previous such venture in the history of man... What is the objective of the great conspiracy? I think it is clear from what has occurred and is now occurring: to diminish the United States in world affairs, to weaken us militarily, to confuse our spirit with talk of surrender in the Far East and to impair our will to resist evil."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of McCarthyism and the Second Red Scare (US.64), write a CER response that analyzes how McCarthy's tactics both reflected and intensified the ideological anxieties of the Cold War. Your response must assess the long-term damage McCarthyism inflicted on civil liberties and democratic institutions, and connect the Red Scare to the broader ideological conflict between the United States and the Soviet Union (US.59) that made such rhetoric politically powerful.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del discurso del Senador Joseph McCarthy ante el Senado, 14 de junio de 1951, Registro del Congreso — un documento del gobierno de EE. UU. disponible a través de los Archivos Nacionales:

"¿Cómo podemos explicar nuestra situación actual a menos que creamos que hombres con alto cargo en este gobierno están conspirando para entregarnos al desastre? Esto debe ser el producto de una gran conspiración, una conspiración de una escala tan inmensa que empequeñece cualquier empresa anterior de este tipo en la historia del hombre..."

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento del macartismo y la Segunda Caza de Brujas Roja (US.64), escribe una respuesta CER que analice cómo las tácticas de McCarthy reflejaron e intensificaron las ansiedades ideológicas de la Guerra Fría. Tu respuesta debe evaluar el daño a largo plazo que el macartismo infligió a las libertades civiles y las instituciones democráticas.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — McCarthyism exploited the genuine anxieties produced by Cold War ideological conflict to create a domestic culture of suspicion that systematically violated civil liberties, ultimately undermining the very democratic institutions the U.S. claimed to be defending against Soviet communism. EVIDENCE — (1) McCarthy's accusation of State Department Communist infiltration (February 1950, Wheeling, WV) with numbers that shifted from 205 to 57 to 81 — demonstrating evidence-free accusations as political weapon; (2) HUAC investigations and Hollywood blacklist (hundreds of careers destroyed without due process); (3) Army-McCarthy Hearings (1954) and Joseph Welch's 'Have you no sense of decency?' moment; (4) Federal Employee Loyalty Program (Truman, 1947) as institutionalization of political surveillance; (5) Smith Act convictions of Communist Party leaders; (6) Senate censure of McCarthy (December 1954) as institutional self-correction. REASONING — McCarthy's effectiveness was rooted in the Cold War's ideological binary: in a world divided between freedom and communism, any accusation of communist sympathy was existentially threatening. The student should reason that McCarthyism was paradoxically self-defeating — its suppression of dissent, due process violations, and guilt-by-association tactics replicated the very authoritarian methods the U.S. opposed in the Soviet Union, revealing the tension between security imperatives and constitutional values.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.59, US.64 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Claim identifies the paradox of McCarthyism (defending democracy through anti-democratic means). Evidence includes at least three specific examples (Wheeling speech, HUAC, Army-McCarthy hearings, loyalty programs, Hollywood blacklist). Reasoning develops the Cold War ideological context that made McCarthyism viable AND the long-term institutional damage. CER fully integrated.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim about McCarthyism's damage to civil liberties. Two specific evidence points. Reasoning connects McCarthyism to Cold War anxiety but may not develop the paradox or institutional analysis.
2 - Developing: General claim about McCarthyism being bad or unjust. One specific evidence point. Reasoning is mostly descriptive.
1 - Beginning: Vague claim. Generic references to McCarthyism with no specific evidence. No analysis.
0 - No response or off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Wheeling, WV speech (Feb. 1950); Federal Employee Loyalty Program (1947); HUAC and Hollywood blacklist; Smith Act prosecutions; Army-McCarthy Hearings (1954); Joseph Welch; Senate censure resolution (Dec. 1954); Rosenberg executions (1953) as context for spy-anxiety; Edward R. Murrow broadcast critique.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: La afirmación identifica la paradoja del macartismo (defender la democracia mediante medios antidemocráticos). La evidencia incluye al menos tres ejemplos específicos. El razonamiento desarrolla el contexto ideológico de la Guerra Fría que hizo viable el macartismo Y el daño institucional a largo plazo.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara sobre el daño del macartismo a las libertades civiles. Dos puntos de evidencia específica.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación general sobre el macartismo. Un punto de evidencia específica. El razonamiento es principalmente descriptivo.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga. Referencias genéricas al macartismo sin evidencia específica.
0 - Sin respuesta o fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Discurso de Wheeling, WV (febrero 1950); Programa de Lealtad de Empleados Federales (1947); HUAC y la lista negra de Hollywood; Audiencias Army-McCarthy (1954); Joseph Welch; resolución de censura del Senado (diciembre 1954).

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President Dwight D. Eisenhower's Farewell Address to the Nation, January 17, 1961 — a U.S. government document available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School, and the National Archives:

"In the councils of government, we must guard against the acquisition of unwarranted influence, whether sought or unsought, by the military-industrial complex. The potential for the disastrous rise of misplaced power exists and will persist. We must never let the weight of this combination endanger our liberties or democratic processes. We should take nothing for granted. Only an alert and knowledgeable citizenry can compel the proper meshing of the huge industrial and military machinery of defense with our peaceful methods and goals."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of Cold War defense policy (US.67, US.60, US.65), write a CER response that evaluates the accuracy and long-term significance of Eisenhower's warning about the military-industrial complex. Your response must connect the growth of defense spending during the Cold War to specific Cold War events that drove it, and assess whether Eisenhower's warning was heeded or ignored in the decades that followed his presidency.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del Discurso de Despedida del Presidente Dwight D. Eisenhower a la Nación, 17 de enero de 1961 — un documento del gobierno de EE. UU. disponible a través del Proyecto Avalon de la Escuela de Derecho de Yale y los Archivos Nacionales:

"En los consejos del gobierno, debemos protegernos contra la adquisición de influencia inmerecida, buscada o no, por parte del complejo militar-industrial. El potencial para el auge desastroso del poder mal orientado existe y persistirá. Nunca debemos permitir que el peso de esta combinación ponga en peligro nuestras libertades o los procesos democráticos."

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la política de defensa de la Guerra Fría (US.67, US.60, US.65), escribe una respuesta CER que evalúe la exactitud y la importancia a largo plazo de la advertencia de Eisenhower sobre el complejo militar-industrial.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — Eisenhower's warning about the military-industrial complex was prescient and largely unheeded: Cold War competition consistently elevated defense spending, fostered structural alliances between government, military, and private contractors, and created political incentives that made demilitarization difficult even after the Cold War ended. EVIDENCE — (1) NSC-68's recommendation to quadruple defense spending as a direct precursor to the complex Eisenhower warned against; (2) the Space Race (US.65) — NASA's creation (1958) and Apollo program's $25 billion cost — as an area where military research and civilian prestige intertwined; (3) defense contractor growth during Korea and Vietnam: McDonnell Douglas, Lockheed, Boeing, Grumman becoming major political stakeholders; (4) the defense budget's growth from ~$13 billion (1950) to over $400 billion (1980s peak during Reagan buildup, US.69); (5) Eisenhower's own 'New Look' defense strategy as context — massive retaliation and reliance on nuclear deterrence actually fueled the very complex he warned against. REASONING — The student should reason that Eisenhower's warning was paradoxical because his own presidency accelerated the MIC through the 'New Look' policy and the Space Race. The long-term significance is that the Cold War created a structural dependency between the U.S. economy, political system, and defense industry that persisted after 1991, suggesting the warning was accurate about the danger but underestimated how deeply embedded the complex would become.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.67, US.60, US.65 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Claim addresses both accuracy and long-term significance. Evidence includes at least three specific details connecting Cold War events to defense spending/MIC growth. Reasoning develops the paradox of Eisenhower's own role and the structural persistence of the MIC post-Cold War. CER fully integrated.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim about the warning's significance. Two specific evidence points. Reasoning connects Cold War events to MIC growth but may miss the paradox or structural persistence.
2 - Developing: General claim about defense spending during the Cold War. One specific evidence point. Reasoning is mostly narrative.
1 - Beginning: Vague claim. Minimal evidence. No analytical reasoning.
0 - No response or off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: NSC-68 defense buildup; 'New Look' and massive retaliation policy; Sputnik (1957) and NASA creation (1958); Space Race costs; defense contractor growth during Korea/Vietnam; Reagan defense buildup (1980s); post-Cold War defense spending persistence; 'revolving door' between Pentagon and defense industry.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: La afirmación aborda tanto la exactitud como la importancia a largo plazo. La evidencia incluye al menos tres detalles específicos que conectan los eventos de la Guerra Fría con el crecimiento del gasto en defensa/MIC. El razonamiento desarrolla la paradoja del propio papel de Eisenhower.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara sobre la importancia de la advertencia. Dos puntos de evidencia específica.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación general sobre el gasto en defensa durante la Guerra Fría. Un punto de evidencia específica.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga. Evidencia mínima.
0 - Sin respuesta o fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Reconstrucción de defensa del NSC-68; política de 'Nueva Apariencia' y represalia masiva; Sputnik (1957) y creación de la NASA (1958); costos de la Carrera Espacial; crecimiento del contratista de defensa durante Corea/Vietnam; reconstrucción de defensa de Reagan (años 80).

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from the Helsinki Accords (Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe, Final Act), August 1, 1975 — a multilateral international agreement available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School:

"The participating States will respect each other's sovereign equality and individuality as well as all the rights inherent in and encompassed by its sovereignty... They will also respect each other's right freely to choose and develop its political, social, economic and cultural systems as well as its right to determine its laws and regulations... The participating States regard as inviolable all one another's frontiers as well as the frontiers of all States in Europe."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of détente and arms control (US.68), write a CER response that evaluates the Helsinki Accords as both an achievement and a limitation of détente. Your response must analyze what the Accords accomplished in practical terms, identify the tensions embedded in the human rights provisions versus the recognition of Soviet-controlled borders, and assess how the Helsinki process ultimately contributed to the erosion of Soviet control in Eastern Europe (US.70).
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento de los Acuerdos de Helsinki (Conferencia sobre Seguridad y Cooperación en Europa, Acta Final), 1 de agosto de 1975 — un acuerdo internacional multilateral disponible a través del Proyecto Avalon de la Escuela de Derecho de Yale:

"Los Estados participantes respetarán la igualdad soberana e individualidad mutua, así como todos los derechos inherentes a ella y comprendidos en ella... También respetarán el derecho de cada uno a elegir y desarrollar libremente sus sistemas políticos, sociales, económicos y culturales..."

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la distensión y el control de armamentos (US.68), escribe una respuesta CER que evalúe los Acuerdos de Helsinki tanto como un logro como una limitación de la distensión.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — The Helsinki Accords were a double-edged instrument of détente: they gave the Soviet Union what it wanted (recognition of post-WWII European borders) while embedding human rights commitments that Eastern European dissidents and Western critics used to delegitimize Soviet control, ultimately becoming a long-term catalyst for the collapse of communist regimes in 1989–1991. EVIDENCE — (1) The Accords' three 'baskets': security (border recognition), economics, and human rights — the Soviets prioritized Basket I while underestimating Basket III; (2) the emergence of Helsinki Watch Groups in the USSR, Poland, Czechoslovakia, and Hungary (1976–1977) — civil society organizations that monitored Soviet compliance and publicized violations; (3) Solidarity movement in Poland (1980–1981) citing Helsinki human rights provisions; (4) Charter 77 in Czechoslovakia as a direct Helsinki-inspired document; (5) the SALT I and SALT II context as the arms control backbone of détente; (6) Reagan's abandonment of détente framing but continuation of arms control negotiations eventually producing INF Treaty (1987). REASONING — The student should reason that the Helsinki Accords reveal the fundamental asymmetry of détente: the Soviet Union pursued détente primarily to achieve strategic parity recognition and economic access, while the West's inclusion of human rights language created a legitimacy framework that empowered internal opposition. This made the Accords a long-term strategic victory for the West even though they appeared to legitimize Soviet dominance of Eastern Europe in the short term.

items.explanation:

Evidence includes at least three specific details: the three baskets structure, Helsinki Watch Groups, Solidarity, Charter 77, or SALT context. 1 - Beginning: Vague claim. Minimal evidence. No analytical reasoning.

4 - Ejemplar: La afirmación identifica la naturaleza de doble filo de Helsinki. La evidencia incluye al menos tres detalles específicos. El razonamiento desarrolla los efectos asimétricos y la contribución a largo plazo al colapso soviético.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara sobre la distensión y Helsinki. Dos puntos de evidencia específica.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación general sobre la distensión como un período de tensión reducida. Un punto de evidencia específica.
